title: Explicit texture release: expose Rml::ReleaseTexture through the facade and C++
description:
THE SMALL HALF, AND IT SHIPS BEFORE ANY POLICY. RmlUi already has the two calls; VaCuus
simply never exposes them:

  Rml::ReleaseTexture(source, match_render_interface)  Core.cpp:397
  Rml::ReleaseTextures(match_render_interface)         Core.cpp:386

Both reach FileTextureDatabase (TextureDatabase.cpp:151-166, :168-178). A game that knows
its own screens can then drop a catalogue's icons when the catalogue closes, which is the
90% case and needs no heuristics at all.

RELEASE IS SELF-HEALING, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE. FileTextureDatabase::ReleaseTexture
assigns `texture = {}`, clearing the handle AND load_texture_failed; EnsureLoaded then sees
!texture_handle, finds load_texture_failed false, and re-runs LoadTextureEntry
(TextureDatabase.cpp:117-129). So a released-then-redisplayed image reloads transparently
and the Rml::Texture objects elements hold stay valid -- they carry a TextureFileIndex,
not a handle. VERIFY THIS RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE PARAGRAPH: release a visible image and
assert it comes back.

SHAPE
  - C++: on the subsystem or the view, taking the VFS source path; per-view because the
    RenderManager is per render interface (VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.h:27)
  - JS: on the vacuus host object, so a screen's own onUnload can drop what it loaded.
    Everything added there has to go into vacuus.d.ts and `vacuus manifest` or the
    conformance test fails BOTH ways (the file's own header says so)
  - THREAD: these must run on the UI thread like every other RmlUi call. From C++ that
    means enqueueing, not calling.

TWO HAZARDS WORTH WRITING DOWN AT THE CALL SITE
  - Textures are shared by SOURCE across every document in a view. Releasing what a
    still-open document is drawing is legal (it reloads) but costs a synchronous probe
    plus a fresh decode on the next frame that needs it -- a hitch, not a bug.
  - EnsureLoaded recovers the source from the index with a std::find_if LINEAR SCAN over
    texture_map (TextureDatabase.cpp:121). Cheap once, O(N) per reload on a database with
    a thousand entries. This is a real constraint on the eviction policy in VaCuus-dqs.3
    and the reason that bead is not just "add an LRU".

ACCEPTANCE
  Pinned by the census from VaCuus-dqs.1: load N, release one by source, assert the count
  drops by exactly one and that re-displaying it brings it back.
notes:
2026-08-13 (b1e156d): the API landed on all three surfaces -- UVaCuusView::ReleaseTexture/ReleaseAllTextures, vacuus.releaseTexture(source)/releaseTextures(), and vacuus.ReleaseTextures [delay] for headless. One implementation behind them: IVaCuusDocumentHost::ReleaseTextures -> Rml::ReleaseTexture(source, recorder).

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PLAN: RenderManager::ReleaseTexture/ReleaseAllTextures are PRIVATE despite looking public at RenderManager.h:98-99; Core.cpp reaches them via its friend RenderManagerAccess. The supported door is Rml::ReleaseTexture(source, render_interface) (Core.h:156,161), and handing it this host's recorder is what makes the release per-view.

Needed a second process-wide slot mirroring GVaCuusActiveScriptHost, because the traffic now runs both ways across the module edge: VaCuusJs cannot see VaCuusRender, so a facade thunk reaches the per-view document host through FVaCuusUIThread::ReleaseTexturesForView. JS acts immediately rather than enqueueing -- the thunk is already on the UI thread and a script wants the boolean, since a mistyped source is the likeliest bug there.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE API. Releasing art the view is STILL DRAWING frees NOTHING: the next frame reloads every handle just dropped (elements hold a TextureFileIndex; EnsureLoaded re-runs LoadTextureEntry, TextureDatabase.cpp:117-129). Measured, one -game run, release between two vacuus.TextureStats beats: 13 textures / 1.50 MiB before, 13 / 1.50 MiB after. It is the safety property seen from the other side, and it is now in both headers.

DIRECT CONSEQUENCE FOR VaCuus-dqs.3: eviction MUST key on what was recently DRAWN, not on what is merely cached, or it burns decodes in a loop and frees nothing. The recorder's per-frame handle set is exactly that signal, which is what that bead already proposes -- this measurement is the evidence for it.

STILL OPEN: this bead's stated acceptance was 'assert the count drops by exactly one'. Not demonstrated, and deliberately not faked: it needs a view that has STOPPED showing the art. A headless toggle swapping one live document for another does not produce that (tried: vacuus.RefHud -> vacuus.M2Demo spawned View 2 and the release hit five still-drawn textures). The honest vehicle is VaCuus-dqs.4's catalogue with a real screen change; suggest landing that assertion there and closing this bead with it.

Semantics ARE pinned: VaCuus.Js.Host.TextureStats now asserts false for an uncached source, TypeError on '' and on a non-string, and that releaseTextures() is callable. Full suite 232/232.
close_reason:
Acceptance met (b24dcf6). It needed a view that had STOPPED drawing the art, which vacuus.LoadBlank now produces -- Toggle could not, because it tears the view down for a different document and takes the replayer, and therefore the census, with it.

ONE RUN, ONE VIEW, 1280x720, the 200-icon catalogue from VaCuus-dqs.4:

    catalogue up                     200 texture(s)   44.85 MiB
    document replaced with an empty  200 texture(s)   44.85 MiB
    vacuus.ReleaseTextures             0 texture(s)    0.00 MiB

The middle line is the epic's premise, shown rather than argued: a screen the player has left keeps every image it ever showed. The last line is this bead's acceptance.

BOTH HALVES OF THE API ARE NOW DEMONSTRATED, and they only make sense together: releasing art still on screen nets to ZERO (measured earlier: 13 textures before and after, because RmlUi reloads on next use), and releasing art the view has stopped drawing frees all of it. That is the safety property and the usefulness in one sentence, and it is what VaCuus-dqs.3's eviction policy must key on -- recently DRAWN, never merely cached.

Shipped surfaces: UVaCuusView::ReleaseTexture/ReleaseAllTextures, vacuus.releaseTexture(source)/releaseTextures(), vacuus.ReleaseTextures [delay] [source], vacuus.LoadBlank [delay]. Semantics pinned by VaCuus.Js.Host.TextureStats. Full suite 232/232. Commits b1e156d, b24dcf6.

title: Resident texture census: count and bytes, readable from a test and a console command
description:
THE OBSERVABLE, AND IT COMES FIRST BECAUSE NOTHING ELSE IN THIS EPIC CAN BE PROVED
WITHOUT IT. Today there is no way to ask "how many UI textures are resident and what do
they cost". What exists is per-buffer DELTAS -- FVaCuusCommandBuffer::NewTextures /
ReleasedTextures -- plus the replayer's private TMap<FVaCuusTextureHandle,
FTextureRHIRef> Textures (VaCuusReplayRenderer.h:227). A delta cannot answer a question
about a total, and a private map cannot answer one at all.

WHAT TO EXPOSE
  - live texture count and summed bytes (sum of W*H*4 over resident payloads), owned by
    the replayer because it is the side that actually holds the RHI refs
  - the same pair per view, since a RenderManager is keyed on the render interface and
    VaCuus gives each view its own (VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.h:27)
  - reachable from THREE places, because each has a different reader:
      * a console command (`vacuus.TextureStats`) for a human with a build in front of
        them
      * an automation-test accessor, because that is what pins the other three beads
      * vacuus.stats() or a sibling, so a demo screen can draw it -- this is what makes
        the atlas demo's claim legible to a client rather than to a log reader

WATCH THE THREAD. The counts live on the render thread; every existing readback in this
plugin that crosses to the game thread does it through a last-sample store rather than a
lock (the vacuus.stats() pattern, VaCuusJsHostApi.cpp:437-462, documented as reading zero
until its scopes have run). Follow that, do not invent a second mechanism.

BYTES ARE COMPUTED, NOT MEASURED. Report W*H*4, and say so in the command's own output:
the RHI may pad row pitch, so this is the logical footprint and not a VRAM figure. A
number that quietly claims to be VRAM and is not is worse than no number.

ACCEPTANCE
  Restore-the-bug standard: a test that loads three distinct images and asserts the count
  goes 0 -> 3, then releases one and asserts 2. Break the accounting deliberately (drop
  the decrement) and watch that test fail before trusting it.
notes:
2026-08-13 (4d21c68): the observable half landed. FVaCuusReplayRenderer::GetResidentTextureCount/Bytes, derived by summing the Textures map rather than accounted at Add/Remove -- a sum cannot drift from the map, and the callers are never a draw. Bytes read each texture's own extent and GPixelFormats; the header states they are the LOGICAL footprint, since RHI row-pitch padding is invisible from here.

VaCuus.Render.Texture.Census pins both halves at 213x276, the owner's own icon size, so the test asserts the epic's own number (235,152 B). Restore-the-bug both ways: with bytes ignoring the extent, the two BYTE assertions fail and BOTH COUNT ASSERTIONS STILL PASS -- which is why bytes are asserted at all; with the retire loop dropped, 'retiring one leaves two: expected 2, but it was 3'. Restored green, full suite 231/231.

REMAINING, and it is two thirds of this bead:
  - the console command. Blocked on a decision, not on code: the replayer lives per Slate element, so a global vacuus.TextureStats has to say WHICH view it addresses (all of them? the focused one?), and a buyer's views are not the demo's. Worth settling before writing it.
  - the JS reader. Needs vacuus.d.ts plus `vacuus manifest`, which the conformance test walks both ways -- editing the .d.ts without re-running the extractor fails the node-side staleness check.
2026-08-13 (4b477e7): the console reader landed. vacuus.TextureStats [delaySeconds] sums every live replayer.

THE 'WHICH VIEW' QUESTION THAT BLOCKED THIS IS ANSWERED: all of them, because there is no one tree to walk. Two unrelated owners hold a replayer BY VALUE -- FVaCuusSlateElement (screen) and FVaCuusWorldSink (world panel) -- so the replayer now enrols itself in a locked process-wide list and the command knows about neither owner. The lock is real and not defensive: both owners are MakeShared'd on the GAME thread while the walk is on the render thread. Copy/move deleted with it, since the registry stores 'this'.

The delay argument is load-bearing for headless recipes: -ExecCmds dispatches at frame 0, before any document exists. Measured in one -game run: frame 0 = 0 textures / 0 replayers / 0.00 MiB; after vacuus.RefHud +8s = 13 textures / 1 replayer / 1.50 MiB.

SumLiveTextures is deliberately un-asserted by any test -- process-wide, so another test's replayer is legitimately part of the answer. The deterministic assertion stays on VaCuus.Render.Texture.Census's own replayer. Full suite 231/231.

LAST PIECE OF THIS BEAD: the JS reader. vacuus.d.ts is load-bearing for VaCuus.Js.Preact.Conformance, which walks the generated manifest BOTH ways, so the .d.ts edit and 'vacuus manifest' have to land in the same change or the node-side staleness check (vacuus manifest --check, run by Web/smoke.mjs) fails.
close_reason:
All three readers landed and each is pinned by a test that has been watched to fail.

THE OBSERVABLE (4b477e7's parent, 4d21c68): FVaCuusReplayRenderer::GetResidentTextureCount/Bytes, DERIVED by summing the Textures map rather than accounted at Add/Remove -- a sum cannot drift from the map, and no caller is ever a draw. Bytes read each texture's own extent and GPixelFormats; every reader states they are the LOGICAL footprint, since RHI row-pitch padding is invisible from here.

READER 1, the test: VaCuus.Render.Texture.Census, at 213x276 -- the owner's own icon -- so it asserts the epic's own 235,152 B and a transposed extent cannot pass. It now also asserts that the published total tracks its own walk in both directions, so the lock-free number and the walked one cannot disagree.

READER 2, the console: vacuus.TextureStats [delaySeconds]. The 'which view' question was answered 'all of them' via a locked process-wide registry the replayer enrols itself in -- two unrelated owners hold one BY VALUE (FVaCuusSlateElement, FVaCuusWorldSink), so there was no tree to traverse. Measured: frame 0 = 0/0/0.00 MiB; after vacuus.RefHud +8s = 13 textures / 1 replayer / 1.50 MiB.

READER 3, JS: vacuus.textureStats() -> {count, bytes}. A published snapshot, because reading the render thread's maps from the UI thread would mean FlushRenderingCommands per call. Storage sits in FVaCuusPerfLog because VaCuusJs does NOT depend on VaCuusRender -- that module edge, not taste, decided the design. vacuus.d.ts and the manifest landed together; conformance walks it both ways and smoke is green.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, four times, each rebuilt and re-run:
  - bytes ignoring each texture's extent: both BYTE assertions fail while BOTH COUNT assertions still pass -- the argument for asserting bytes at all.
  - the ReleasedTextures retire loop dropped: 'retiring one leaves two: expected 2, but it was 3'.
  - bytes crossing to JS as int32: 3 GiB came back as -1073741824, and ONLY the 2^31 assertion failed.
  (the fourth is the count/bytes pair above sharing one break)

Full suite 232/232. Commits 4d21c68, 4b477e7, 7011cb6.

title: UI texture memory: census, release, eviction, atlases
description:
Owner's question 2026-08-13: a weapon catalogue with 213x276 PNG icons -- how much
memory do they cost in a build, and are they padded to 512x512 like a GL texture?

ANSWER, read out of source rather than assumed. A PNG never stays a PNG and is never
padded:

  FileTextureDatabase::InsertTexture dedups by SOURCE STRING, so N elements sharing an
  src cost one texture (ThirdParty/RmlUi/Source/Core/TextureDatabase.cpp:93-104).
  Loading is nominally deferred, but GetDimensions goes through the same EnsureLoaded
  (:139) and layout needs the dimensions -- so LAID OUT == LOADED, on-screen or not.

  FVaCuusRecordingRenderInterface::LoadTexture reads the bytes, whitelists PNG/JPEG/
  UEJPEG, probes the size synchronously and decodes on a worker with
  GetRaw(ERGBFormat::RGBA, 8) (VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:260).

  MakeUITextureDesc issues Create2D(name, Size, PF_R8G8B8A8) with ShaderResource only
  (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:146-151). Size is the IMAGE's size -- no power-of-two
  rounding anywhere -- and NumMips is left at the FRHITextureCreateDesc default of 1
  (Engine RHIResources.h:1893). IsWellFormedPayload pins the payload at exactly W*H*4.

  So 213 x 276 x 4 = 235,152 B ~= 230 KiB per icon. A 512x512 POT texture would have
  been 1 MiB, i.e. 4.5x worse. NOT MEASURED: RHI row-pitch alignment may round each
  852-byte row up (256-byte pitch would cost ~20%); that is API/driver territory and
  nothing in this plugin decides it.

THE SIZE IS NOT THE PROBLEM. THE LIFETIME IS.

FileTextureDatabase has NO EVICTION OF ANY KIND. texture_list only grows; an entry is
cleared only by an explicit Rml::ReleaseTexture(source) (RenderManager.cpp:252-255) or
ReleaseAllTextures (:257-261, also run from ~RenderManager at :41, i.e. Rml::Shutdown).
VaCuus CALLS NEITHER -- grepped the whole plugin outside ThirdParty; there is the
RmlUi-facing override and tests, and no call site. The recorder's own comment says it
outright (VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:1436): "Closing a document or destroying
the element does NOT release them."

So a catalogue the player pages through accumulates for the life of the UI thread:

    100 icons   22 MiB        500 icons  112 MiB
    250 icons   56 MiB       1000 icons  224 MiB

Sibling of VaCuus-wgq (long lists never virtualize): that one is per-frame CPU for rows
nobody can see, this one is resident VRAM for images nobody is looking at. A thousand-
item store hits both at once.

FOUR CHILDREN, IN THIS ORDER, and the order is the point: the census comes first because
none of the other three can be shown to work without it. This project has already
watched an invariant with no observable rot once (CLAUDE.md on M2's cache bug).
close_reason:
Delivered, 4/4. The owner's question -- what does a catalogue of 213x276 PNG icons cost in a build, and are they padded like a GL texture -- is answered end to end.

THE ANSWER: neither. A PNG never stays a PNG and is never padded to a power of two. It becomes an RHI texture at its EXACT size in PF_R8G8B8A8 with NumMips 1: 213x276 = 235,152 bytes = 230 KiB, so 200 icons are 45 MiB. The size was never the problem. The LIFETIME was -- RmlUi's FileTextureDatabase has no eviction, and closing or replacing a document releases nothing.

SHIPPED
  .1 the census, three readers: GetResidentTextureCount/Bytes (derived from the map, so it cannot drift), vacuus.TextureStats [delay], vacuus.textureStats() in JS off a published snapshot.
  .2 explicit release on all three surfaces, plus vacuus.LoadBlank -- the command that made the effect measurable at all.
  .3 the budget: vacuus.TextureBudgetMB, off by default, evicting undrawn file textures coldest-first to an 80% low-water mark, driven by the draw record the recorder already kept.
  .4 the catalogue: Tools/gen_catalog_art.py, 200 icons in two spellings, census on screen.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT CARRIES IT, one run, one view:
    catalogue up                    200 textures  44.85 MiB
    screen replaced with an empty   200 textures  44.85 MiB
    explicit release                  0 textures   0.00 MiB

THREE RESULTS AGAINST THE REFLEX, and the reason this was built rather than asserted: releasing art still on screen frees NOTHING (it reloads the same frame); an atlas costs MORE bytes than loose files when the cells are uniform; and an atlas saves no draw calls here at all. An atlas buys lifetime -- one texture to evict instead of 200 -- and that is the whole of it.

STILL UNMEASURED, named wherever it matters: RHI row-pitch padding, which could reverse the byte comparison. The census reports LOGICAL bytes by construction.

VaCuus-dqs.5 (draw batching) was detached rather than closed: discovered here, measured at a ~0.09 ms ceiling, parked at P3 with reopen conditions. It is not a debt this epic owed.

Full suite 233/233. Commits 4d21c68, 4b477e7, 7011cb6, b1e156d, 2841db3, 0ebaebe, b24dcf6, af44cf5, cce34c1.

title: Docs wrongly say source-only/C++-required: a Fab install is Epic-built binaries into the ENGINE
description: Owner correction 2026-08-12: Fab builds binaries for code plugins itself; the launcher installs into the engine, not the project, and a Blueprint-only project works with zero compiling. The source path (repo or package Source/) still needs a C++ project. Wrong text: setup.md §0/§1, README install paragraph + 'ships as source' line, site landing card 'Source only, so C++ only' + hero eyebrow.
close_reason: Fixed in commit on master: README install paragraph + package note, setup.md §0 (two install channels: Fab->engine with Epic-built binaries, BP-only OK; source->Project/Plugins needs C++), §1 step 1, landing card 4 + eyebrow, owner-handoff §7.3b. title: World-panel touch latch: first touch consumes all input app-wide, forever
description: Found by the mobile research (docs/research/mobile-support.md §0, 'the single biggest surprise: not a mobile bug that needs a device to fix'). MECHANISM per the research: FVaCuusWorldInputProcessor::HandleMouseButtonUpEvent clears its press latch only under MouseEvent.GetPressedButtons().IsEmpty() (VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.cpp:518), which is NEVER true for a touch-sourced pointer event: SlateApplication::OnTouchEnded builds the up-event with bPressLeftMouseButton=true (SlateApplication.cpp:6832-6845) and the touch ctor bakes PressedButtons = FTouchKeySet::StandardSet into the value copy (Events.h:938, Events.cpp:15). The processor holds no Slate capture by design, so no engine safety net fires; every later pointer event in the application is consumed. Affects any touch platform (Android, iOS, Win64 touchscreens) — and desktop stays green because mouse up-events do empty their pressed set. FIX SHAPE: release the latch keyed on the event itself (touch/pointer identity), not on the aggregate pressed-buttons set. PROOF STANDARD: restore-the-bug — a test that drives a touch press+release pair through the processor and asserts the latch clears and later events pass; watch it fail on the current predicate, restore, green. Open the cited engine lines before coding — per project convention.
acceptance_criteria: A touch press+release on a world panel leaves the processor consuming nothing afterwards; the new test fails when the fix is reverted; the existing mouse-path tests stay green; all engine citations opened and verified.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of VaCuus-61d, which was filed AND fixed 2026-08-03 (commit 64b703d) — the latch now records the exact presses it consumed, keyed {UserIndex, PointerIndex, EffectingButton}, released per-press; MakeTouchEvent fixture and the touch regression test shipped with it (198/198). I re-derived the bug from the research doc's §0 table, which records the state at research time — always check bd search for the bead a research finding filed before re-filing it. No code change needed.

title: Port VaCuus to UE 5.6 (engine build + compat fixes + 5.6-authored content)
description:
Owner request 2026-08-10: /w/Unreal/UE5.6 has 5.6.1 set up; port the plugin to it.

DONE. Full write-up: docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-shim1-results.md.

RESULT
  5.6.1 editor target: Succeeded, 0 errors, 0 warnings from plugin sources
  5.6.1 monolithic game target (WITH_EDITOR=0): Succeeded, 0 errors, 0 warnings
  5.6.1 Automation RunTests VaCuus: 227 performed, 227 Success, 0 Fail
  5.8.1 re-run after the port: editor + game targets clean, 227/227 -- unregressed

THE EXPERIMENT'S CENTRAL PREDICTION WAS WRONG, which is the main result. All four
hotspots VaCuusEngineCompat.h ranked as likeliest to drift are IDENTICAL in 5.6.1 and
5.8.1. Every real break was elsewhere, four of seven outside VaCuusRender entirely, so
the 'a version port is one edit to THIS file' promise now holds as a PAIR: the render
seam there, everything else in the new Source/VaCuus/Public/VaCuusCoreCompat.h.

SEVEN BREAKS (three found statically before the first build, by diffing the plugin's 478
includes and its identifier set against both engines' full public-header corpora):
  1 IPooledRenderTarget -> include the umbrella RendererInterface.h (no guard)
  2 FCookDependencyContext -> #if __has_include
  3 UE_FORCEINLINE_HINT -> #ifndef fallback
  4 GetMaterialResource / GetRelevance_Concurrent: feature level -> shader platform.
    The ONLY genuine version guard, UE_VERSION_OLDER_THAN(5,7,0), boundary cited from
    5.8's own UE_DEPRECATED(5.7) text. Two call sites, two modules
  5 FTickableGameObject(ETickableTickType) absent on 5.6 -> macro; no behaviour change
    (GetTickableTickType already answers Never until bInitialized)
  6 FProperty ctors: 5.6 REQUIRES EObjectFlags, 5.8 DEPRECATED it -> overload ranking
  7 UStringTable auto-registers every non-CDO table on 5.6 vs only IsAsset() on 5.8 ->
    ask the registry first. This was a hard checkf that KILLED the run after 214 tests;
    no API diff could have found it -- the registry function is byte-identical and the
    difference is in the caller

CONTENT WAS HALF THE WORK, and nothing in the SHIM-1 page anticipated it: all 8 .uasset
files carried FileVersionUE5=1018 vs 5.6's ceiling of 1017, and IsFileVersionTooNew
refuses them SILENTLY. Re-authored on 5.6 (forward compatibility does the rest):
  - M_VaCuusWorldPanel: committed script re-run
  - the six Spike/* : had NO committed script; written now as
    m5-t5-material-spike/author_spike_materials.py and verified on 5.8 -- authoring into
    /Game/SpikeGen reproduces all six with ZERO structural differences, and a perturbed
    copy is caught with exactly the two planted diffs
  - DevUIBundle: vacuus.Bundle.CreateAsset
  Restore-the-bug: with the 5.8-saved Opaque back in place it alone is refused while its
  six 1017 siblings load in the same process.

THE 5.8 CONTROL EARNED ITS KEEP: finding 6's first fix compiled green on 5.6 and produced
six -Wdeprecated-declarations on 5.8 whose text ends 'otherwise your project will no
longer compile'. A port verified only on the target engine would have shipped it.

NOT CLAIMED: RunUAT BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes on 5.6 (VaCuus-93v's acceptance line is
still unmet for 5.6), Win64/macOS on 5.6, and 5.7 (no SDK here).

WHERE THE WORK IS: uncommitted in the 5.6 build clone /w/Unreal/VcHost56/Plugins/VaCuus
(19 paths), mirrored into the 5.8 clone /w/Unreal/VcHost/Plugins/VaCuus for the control
run. Not committed and not merged to canonical -- conservative profile.

title: Foundation: snapshot tag, change delegate, UStringTable bridge
description:
Spec section 4 plus the tag from section 2.

- FVaCuusTranslationSnapshot gains an FString Tag; SetTable/SetTranslationTable take it. The plugin NEVER interprets the tag, only carries it -- it is what turns the JS callback from 'something changed' into 'the language is now ru'.
- A BlueprintAssignable dynamic multicast on UVaCuusSubsystem, broadcast synchronously inside SetTranslationTable on the game thread. This is the single hanging point for re-pushing FText-bearing models, instead of every buyer rediscovering FInternationalization::OnCultureChanged.
- SetTranslationTableFromStringTable(UStringTable*, Tag): FStringTable::EnumerateKeysAndSourceStrings (StringTableCore.h:157) for keys, FText::FromStringTable(TableId, Key).ToString() (Text.h:510) for culture-resolved values. Makes the engine .locres pipeline work with no buyer glue.
close_reason:
Shipped and proven. Snapshot carries an FString Tag; SetTable/SetTranslationTable take it (defaulted, because a new required pin on a shipped BlueprintCallable would break every existing graph). FOnVaCuusTranslationTableChanged lives on the REGISTRY, not the subsystem, so a C++ caller reaching SetTable directly cannot change the language behind Blueprint's back; UVaCuusSubsystem forwards it to a BlueprintAssignable via AddWeakLambda, removed in Deinitialize.

Broadcast order matters and is commented: the snapshot is enqueued to the UI thread FIRST, then the delegate fires, so a handler's re-pushed model lands BEHIND the snapshot that motivated it in the FIFO -- broadcasting first would apply a model against the OLD table for one frame.

SetTranslationTableFromStringTable gained a guard the test found: FText::FromStringTable resolves through the process-wide registry, and a table absent from it yields the literal '<MISSING STRING TABLE ENTRY>' for EVERY key -- a full, well-shaped, completely wrong table with no error anywhere. UStringTable only auto-registers when IsAsset() (StringTable.cpp:401). Now refused with a named Error.

Tests: VaCuus.Translation.Signal, VaCuus.Translation.StringTableBridge. Both green.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the optional [VaCuus] TranslationStringTable config auto-bridge. It was flagged in the design as the first thing to cut; nothing depends on it. File a bead if wanted.

title: The live route: a translation variable in every data model
description:
Spec section 1. The core of the milestone.

FORCED SHAPE: a separate i18n data model does NOT work. Element.cpp:2203-2218 -- an element inherits data_model from its parent unless it declares data-model=NAME, which switches the whole subtree. One model per subtree, so {{ i18n.x }} inside <body data-model=hud> resolves against hud. Translation must therefore be an extra TOP-LEVEL VARIABLE in every model VaCuus creates.

- Custom VariableDefinition (DataVariable.h:55 Child() is virtual) via RegisterCustomDataVariableDefinition (DataModelHandle.h:136), resolving any child name at lookup time -- no key pre-registration.
- Bound as 't' in every bound model, plus a standalone per-context model named 'vacuus' holding only t, for documents with no game model ({{ }} does nothing without a data-model in scope).
- Dotted keys: ParseAddress splits on '.' (DataModel.cpp:9-42) so Child() is called once per segment; accumulate the prefix and look up the joined key at the leaf.
- Dirty on install: DataExpression::GetVariableNameList returns address[0].name only (DataExpression.cpp:1145-1154), so one DirtyVariable('t') re-evaluates every {{ t.* }}. Rides the existing path (VaCuusBoundModel.cpp:345,387).
- 't' is RESERVED: a bound struct with a top-level field named t gets a named refusal, not a silent overwrite.

KEY SHAPE IS RESTRICTED and this is why live is opt-in per string: IsVariableCharacter (DataExpression.cpp:315-330) allows first char a-zA-Z then a-zA-Z0-9_. only. No hyphens, spaces, colons, leading digits. A key that does not fit stays parse-time. As a global mode that character table would constrain every key in the project.
close_reason:
Shipped, and the restore-the-bug proof was run in both directions.

Built as designed: FVaCuusTranslationVariable is a custom Rml::VariableDefinition bound as the reserved top-level name 't' into every model VaCuusData::BindModelVariables creates, plus a standalone per-context model named 'vacuus' created in AddView for documents that bind no struct. Key paths are interned (DataVariable is exactly (definition*, void*) with no room for a string); dotted keys accumulate a prefix across Child() calls. Dirty happens in the SetTranslationSnapshot drain, over every bound model plus the standalone ones.

Two things the source forced that the design predicted:
- a separate i18n model is impossible (Element.cpp:2203-2218, one model per subtree)
- keys must match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]* (DataExpression.cpp:315-330), which is exactly why live is opt-in per string

One thing the RUN forced: the standalone handles must also be dropped in FVaCuusUIThread::Exit step 1c, not only in RemoveView -- a graceful stop closes documents and goes straight to Exit, so RemoveView never runs and every normal shutdown left dangling handles. Caught by ReleaseAll's own error on the first run.

RESTORE-THE-BUG (both directions observed): commenting out VaCuusTranslationVariable::Dirty in FVaCuusBoundModel::DirtyTranslations leaves section 1 passing and fails section 2 with 'Expected the flat key now shows the NEW language to be Здоровье, but it was Health'. Restored -> green.

Tests: VaCuus.Translation.Live (flat key, dotted key, identity on miss, standalone model, NO reload via NumDocumentsLoaded, replacement-not-merge live, interned-pool count == 5 exactly as predicted) and VaCuus.Translation.ReservedName.

title: Seamless language switching: the plugin owns what only the UI thread can do
description:
Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-vacuus-seamless-localization-design.md (approved 2026-08-09).

Today a language change costs ClearAssetCachesAndReloadAllViews, which re-mounts JS from module top level -- fresh context, fresh state. The screen that changes language IS the settings screen, so the reload destroys exactly what the player is looking at.

Dividing line, forced by FVaCuusUIThread::Enqueue being private (VaCuusUIThread.h:419, below private: at :372): anything needing the UI thread is the plugin's job because no project can build it; content and policy stay the project's.

Five children, in order. Live re-translation is OPT-IN PER STRING -- plain markup keeps the parse-time fast path.
close_reason:
6/6 children closed. A language change now reaches open documents without reloading them.

WHAT SHIPPED: the live route (a reserved 't' variable in every data model plus a standalone per-context model), both change signals with their ordering contracts, the runtime font door with replay across a UI-thread restart, the UStringTable bridge, RmlUi patch #5 making a missing glyph visible, a demo, and docs/buyer/localization.md.

THE DIVIDING LINE HELD ALL THE WAY THROUGH and is worth keeping: FVaCuusUIThread::Enqueue is private, so anything needing the UI thread is the plugin's job because no project can build it -- content and policy stayed the game's. Every piece here landed on the plugin side of that line for a reason stated in its own header.

THE ONE DESIGN CALL WORTH REMEMBERING: live is opt-in PER STRING, not a mode. RmlUi's expression tokenizer restricts keys to [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.]* (DataExpression.cpp:315-330); as a global mode that character table would have become a naming rule for every key in every buyer's project. Opt-in confines it to the strings that actually need it, and plain markup keeps the parse-time fast path.

Four restore-the-bug proofs, each seen fail and then pass. 226/226 automation tests; editor and monolithic targets build. Visual acceptance photographed in three languages.

STILL OWED, and named rather than left implied:
- no proof that the replacement-glyph count goes flat once a covering face is registered -- the repo ships one .ttf and it has no Cyrillic, so that needs a font asset and a licensing decision
- the optional [VaCuus] TranslationStringTable config auto-bridge was cut, as the design said it would be if it read as hidden magic; nothing depends on it
- patch #5 should go upstream with the VaCuus-7ym.1 batch

title: Async upload handover breaks when two pending buffers carry the same texture handle
description:
Found 2026-08-07 while running vacuus.LobbyDemo in the VaCuusDemo project. PRE-EXISTING, not from VaCuus-9b3: it reproduces identically on the stale 2026-08-03 build of VaCuusRender that the demo project was accidentally running, i.e. it predates today's world-sink change and lives in the SCREEN path akj.6.25 shipped.

SYMPTOM, on the lobby's first frames:
  Ensure condition failed: VaCuusReplay::IsWellFormedPayload(Data)
  [VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:638] Texture 1 payload mismatch: 1024x1024, 0 bytes
  UploadNewResources <- Replay <- FVaCuusSlateElement::Draw_RenderThread's pass lambda
  (VaCuusSlateElement.cpp:163), frame 4.

'0 bytes' means the payload was MOVED, and only BeginAsyncTextureUploads moves payloads --
so the async half ran for that buffer and the handover through PendingAsyncTextures did
not find the parked texture.

LIKELY MECHANISM (to be confirmed by a test before any fix): PendingAsyncTextures is keyed
by handle alone. Draw_RenderThread calls BeginAsyncTextureUploads for EVERY pending buffer
before the pass. If buffers N and N+1 both carry the same handle, N+1's park OVERWRITES
N's map entry; then UploadNewResources(N) installs and REMOVES it, and UploadNewResources
(N+1) finds nothing while its own payload is already gone -> ensure. The header comment on
PendingAsyncTextures says installing straight into Textures caused 'the buffer-ordering
bug', and the park-then-install fix does not cover the same handle appearing twice in one
drain.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: VaCuus.Render.Upload.AsyncPayload drives ONE buffer per pass, and
VaCuus.World.AsyncUpload (new today) does the same. Neither has two pending buffers, which
is the state the Slate element's queue exists to hold. The observable already exists (the
route counters plus the ensure itself); what is missing is the two-buffer-one-handle case.

FIRST STEP: write that case as a test at the replayer level -- two buffers, same handle,
both begun before either is consumed -- and watch it reproduce, before touching the fix.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
PLATFORM DATUM, 2026-08-07: does NOT reproduce on Win64/D3D12.

The lobby demo now builds and runs on the Windows box (VaCuusDemo project, own plugin clone,
D3D12 SM6, -game -RenderOffscreen, vacuus.LobbyDemo + .Nav). Across that whole run the log
carries ZERO 'Handled ensure' lines. On Linux/Vulkan the same command fires
'IsWellFormedPayload ... Texture 1 payload mismatch: 1024x1024, 0 bytes' on EVERY run, at frame
4, without fail.

This supports the hypothesis already written on this bead rather than complicating it: the
trigger is two PENDING buffers carrying the same texture handle in one Draw_RenderThread drain.
That is a queue-timing state, not an unconditional defect -- so a venue where the widget paints
promptly enough that the queue never holds two buffers at once simply never enters it.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE FIX AND ITS TEST: do not chase an RHI difference. The reproduction
should be built at the replayer level, where the queue state can be constructed by hand (two
buffers, same handle, both begun before either is consumed) rather than raced into. A test
written that way will fail on all three platforms; a test that drives the real widget may only
fail on Vulkan, which would make it look flaky and get muted.

Also worth recording: the venue that DOES show it is the cheaper one to iterate in.

title: 2d6demo: Shipping Win64 package — bundle wiring first, then build on the Win machine
description:
Owner wants a Shipping Win64 package of the demo, built on kinder@192.168.2.13, and the path to run it from.

BLOCKER, confirmed: the demo has NO bundle wiring. Config/*.ini has no Bundle/DirectoriesToAlwaysCook lines and there is no Content/Bundles. In cooked Shipping the plugin mounts the BUNDLE ONLY — VaCuus.Build.cs:138-146 adds the loose Content/DevUI RuntimeDependencies globs only when Target.Configuration != Shipping — so a Shipping package would launch with no UI at all. VcHost/Config/DefaultGame.ini:9-22 is the working reference.

SECOND TRAP: Demo2d6.Target.cs does not set bUseLoggingInShipping. Stock Shipping compiles logging out entirely, so there would be no log file to read the bundle-mount verification line from ('N open(s) served by mounted bundles, M by loose roots'; M must be 0 in Shipping). VcHostTarget.cs sets BuildEnvironment=Unique + bUseLoggingInShipping deliberately for exactly this reason.

MACHINE SURVEY (done): Windows 11 Pro, PowerShell 5.1, C: 71.3 GB free. Engine is a LAUNCHER build at 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8', version 5.8.1 changelist 56057345 — same version as the Linux source build. Visual Studio Community 2022 17.14.37516.0 present. C:\VaCuusWin64Test\VcHost\Binaries\Win64 exists, so the machine has built UE C++ before. C:\Demo2d6 does not exist. The plugin is a source drop under the project's Plugins/, so it will compile there rather than use delivered binaries (RulesCompiler.cs:402).

SSH quoting: nested shells mangle quotes; base64 -EncodedCommand (UTF-16LE) is the reliable route.
close_reason:
Built and run. C:\Demo2d6\Saved\Archive\Windows\Demo2d6.exe, 2026-08-06 16:00 on the owner's Launcher UE 5.8.1 -- it starts and draws the HUD.

Both blockers this bead named were cleared before the build, in Demo2d6 5faf536 + cd5572c: the bundle wiring (marker asset, DirectoriesToAlwaysCook, BundleAssetPath, and DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS for the seven scene plates the VFS never sees) and bUseLoggingInShipping -- the latter GUARDED on the engine not being Installed, which is what makes the Launcher engine package at all rather than throw at rules validation.

NO LOG, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN, NOT A MISS. %LOCALAPPDATA%\Demo2d6\Saved\Logs exists and is empty: bUseLoggingInShipping carries [RequiresUniqueBuildEnvironment] and an Installed engine resolves BuildEnvironment to Shared even for a monolithic game target, so the guard skips it there. The teardown line '0 by loose roots' is therefore unavailable on Win64 and the gate is the STAGING MANIFEST instead. Checked over ssh, Manifest_UFSFiles_Win64.txt, 2270 entries:

  Demo2d6/Content/Bundles/Demo2d6UIBundle.uasset
  Demo2d6/Content/Bundles/Demo2d6UIBundle.m.ubulk
  Demo2d6/Content/DevUI/2d6/scene/plate_*.png   (seven, and nothing else under DevUI)

No .rml, no .rcss, no .js, no UI .png anywhere in the package -- so a running build that draws the HUD has no source for it except the cooked bundle. Same statement Linux makes with a counter, made by absence.

Recorded in Demo2d6 README.md under 'Win64, and the one thing that differs' (which also had the staging directory wrong -- it is Saved/StagedBuilds/Windows, only the file name says Win64).

title: 2d6demo: HUD blocks anchor to the stage's 16:9 box instead of the screen's real corners
description:
Owner request: the ship/subsystems panel should hug the TOP-RIGHT corner, the status bar and icon rail the BOTTOM-RIGHT, and the radar should be CENTRED.

CAUSE: .stage (components.rcss:40-48) is a FIXED 120rem x 67.5rem box — exactly 16:9 — and every HUD block is positioned by an offset from its corners:
  .hud-ship       left: 73.375rem; top: 0.625rem     (should be top + right)
  .hud-grid       left: 0.375rem;  top: 54.5625rem   (should be left + bottom)
  .hud-radar      left: 53.6875rem; top: 51.9375rem  (should be centred + bottom)
  .rail-fixed     right: 0.875rem; top: 44rem        (right is correct; top is not)
  .statusbar-fixed right/bottom                       (already correct)

applyScale sets the root font-size from min(w/1920, h/1080), so on any aspect other than 16:9 the stage is letterboxed inside the view and its edges stop coinciding with the screen's. Elements pinned by a left/top offset then float away from the corner they belong to.

FIX has two halves: the stage must FILL the view rather than be a fixed 16:9 box, and the blocks must anchor to the edges they belong to. The scale itself should stay min(w/1920, h/1080) so element sizes do not change.

The risk is in the other screens: the lobby and section compositions are laid out against the same stage, so they must be re-checked at a non-16:9 aspect too — that is where a mistake would hide, since everything looks identical at 16:9.
close_reason:
FIXED in Demo2d6 68aa2ec. `.stage` is `100%/100%` and every block anchors to the edge it
belongs to; the scale stays min(w/1920, h/1080).

NEW ANCHORS (all of them the same edge at 16:9 as the offset they replace):
  .hud-caps       left 73.375rem  -> right 0.4375rem          top+right
  .hud-ship       left 73.375rem  -> right 0.3125rem          top+right
  .hud-tabs-top   left 73.375rem  -> right 0.3125rem          top+right
  .hud-tabs-bot   top  53.25rem   -> bottom 12.9375rem        left+bottom
  .hud-grid       top  54.5625rem -> bottom 0.6875rem         left+bottom
  .hud-ctx        top  36.375rem  -> bottom 28.125rem         left+bottom
  .hud-tooltip    top  40.1875rem -> bottom 19.6875rem        left+bottom
  .hud-radar      left 53.6875rem -> left 50% / margin-left -6.3125rem / width 12.625rem
                  top  51.9375rem -> bottom 2.9375rem         centre+bottom
  .rail-fixed     top  44rem      -> bottom 3.71875rem        right+bottom
  .statusbar-fixed unchanged (right/bottom already)
  .screen-stub    left 41.25rem   -> left 50% / margin-left -18.75rem
  .lobby-divider  width 100%      -> width 120rem (kept on the authoring surface)

RADAR CENTRING, no calc(): left 50% plus half the plot's authored 12.625rem as a negative
margin (-6.3125rem). Measured on the captures, plot centre against view centre:
  1920x1080  cx 959.5 vs 959.5   (+0.0)
  2560x1080  cx 1279.5 vs 1279.5 (+0.0)
  1600x1200  cx 799.0 vs 799.5   (-0.5, half a pixel of rounding)

16:9 REGRESSION TEST: lobby, section and all three catalogue benches diff to ZERO pixels
before vs after. The turrets HUD diffs to zero with the simulation frozen (slomo + no
radar wave); with it running the residual is 1,970 px in 13 clusters, every one of them a
simulation readout (both heat gauges, two turret cards' ammo, the radar blips) and none of
them a block edge -- two runs of the SAME build differ the same way. Every measured block
bbox is identical to the before-shot, including the rail's 704..1017.

THE RAIL NEEDED THE DIFF TO SETTLE IT. `bottom: 3.875rem` (the honest 62px) put it 2.5px
high: the last button's gap margin collapses out of `.rail` but not out of `.rail-fixed`,
because an absolutely positioned box establishes its own formatting context. 59.5px is the
offset to the wrapper's margin edge. Restore-the-bug in both directions: 62 -> rail at
702..1015 and 3,843 differing px on both the lobby and the section screen; 59.5 -> zero.

OFF-ASPECT (turrets, after): 2560x1080 ship cluster right-gap 5, rail 14, status plate 5,
turret plate left 6 / bottom 10, plot dead centre -- against a before-shot where all three
right-hand blocks stopped 640px short and the plot sat 420px left of centre. 1600x1200

GATES: vacuus lint clean (18 files); 12/12 Demo2d6.* automation tests Success; both
Demo2d6Editor and Demo2d6 (monolithic) build; 0 "Syntax error parsing property
declaration" and 0 "did not resolve to a readable file" in the run logs.
docs/img/*.png NOT refreshed -- 16:9 is unchanged, so there is nothing to refresh.

title: 2d6demo: the game loses the mouse after leaving fullscreen until alt+Enter is toggled twice
description:
Owner report: 'иногда игра целиком теряет мышь. я вышел из полноэкранного режима -- и хоп, перестало ловить мышку, пока я не передерну через alt+Enter туда-сюда.'

FIRST SUSPECT, and it is ours: ADemo2d6HudActor::BeginPlay applies FInputModeGameAndUI + SetShowMouseCursor(true) EXACTLY ONCE (Demo2d6Hud.cpp:115-119) and nothing ever re-applies it. A fullscreen<->windowed transition reconfigures the viewport window and its capture state; a one-shot input mode is not re-asserted afterwards. That the defect clears when the mode is toggled twice fits: the state is lost on one transition and restored on another.

The plugin's own comment says why this matters at all — 'NOT A NICETY. Under the default FInputModeGameOnly the viewport holds mouse capture, so FSlateApplication routes every pointer event straight to the captor (the SViewport) and never runs a hit test' (VaCuusRender.cpp:122-144). Losing the mode means losing every click into the UI, which is exactly the symptom.

SECOND SUSPECT, and it would be buyer-facing: SVaCuusWidget takes mouse capture on a press over an interactive region (SVaCuusWidget.cpp:567-568) so a drag that leaves the widget keeps being delivered. If a window-mode change lands mid-capture, the capture or the focus state could be left stale. There is handling around OnFocusLost (:1382) and a 'belt and braces' clear at :1240, so it may already be covered — establish which rather than assume.

Reproduction needs an interactive windowed session, which a headless run cannot provide. A cited mechanism plus a defensive re-apply is an acceptable outcome, but the fix must state what was proven and what was reasoned.
close_reason:
Fixed in Demo2d6 a45a0b7, with an honest split between what was proven and what was reasoned.

WHAT WAS PROVEN, by measurement on a real display (Linux/XWayland, 2026-08-06):
- The bead's own premise is FALSE. A real fullscreen round-trip (TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN, the
  command Alt+Enter itself runs; 1280x720 windowed -> 2560x1440 windowed-fullscreen ->
  back) left EVERY field of the input mode intact, both directions. The four flags
  FInputModeGameAndUI writes go on the UGameViewportClient (PlayerController.cpp:6409-6412)
  and that object outlives the transition. The one-shot half (ReleaseMouseCapture,
  ReleaseMouseLock, drained and reset at LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:5261-5264) genuinely is not
  re-asserted -- but releasing a capture nobody has taken is a no-op, so its absence is
  only observable once something HAS taken one.
- The second suspect is CLEAR for this case. SVaCuusWidget overrides OnMouseCaptureLost
  and resets both halves of its capture state unconditionally (SVaCuusWidget.cpp:725-741);
  every engine path that drops capture funnels through FSlateUser::ReleaseCapture, which
  always notifies (SlateUser.cpp:314); VaCuusSlateRoutingTest.cpp:550-560 asserts it.
  Two unrelated residual gaps found and filed as VaCuus-86x. Nothing in /w/Unreal/VaCuus
  was modified.
- THE OWNER'S SYMPTOM WAS NOT REPRODUCED. Filed as VaCuus-3yl with the exact interactive
  steps, because a real Alt+Enter with a held modifier and exclusive fullscreen (Win64)
  is the one configuration left untested.

WHAT SHIPPED, proven end to end rather than argued:
- demo2d6.InputState -- the readback that did not exist. Prints the four viewport-client
  flags, bShowMouseCursor, and who holds Slate pointer capture, as INTACT or DRIFTED with
  every reason named.
- ADemo2d6HudActor re-asserts the mode on FViewport::ViewportResizedEvent, gated on that
  same readback so nothing writes unconditionally and no other owner of the input mode
  gets stamped on. Unbound in EndPlay, paired like RegisterCalmCommand. The event was
  chosen over ToggleFullscreenDelegate (Alt+Enter path only) and OnSceneViewportResizeDel
  (single-cast, would displace another listener); both arguments are in the .cpp.
- PROOF: vacuus.M1HUD 0 hands the controller FInputModeGameOnly (VaCuusRender.cpp:165-166)
  -- a real external system doing exactly what the guard exists for. INTACT -> DRIFTED on
  four counts INCLUDING 'captor=SViewport (THE GAME VIEWPORT) buttonsDown=0', which is
  precisely the state in which no click is hit-tested and the UI is deaf -> the resize
  logs 'the input mode did not survive it' -> INTACT. The second toggle finds nothing to do.
- RESTORE-THE-BUG: with the binding removed, the identical sequence stays DRIFTED across
  two full fullscreen toggles and logs nothing. Restored, it repairs on the first.
- Also confirmed the sizeof static_assert on FInputModeReadback fires, by breaking it.

TWO TRAPS, now in the README:
- -RenderOffscreen never performs a window-mode change at all. No headless run can
  exercise any of this; use -windowed on a real display.
- TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN belongs to the viewport client, which GEngine->Exec does not reach --
  only ULocalPlayer::Exec (LocalPlayer.cpp:1594). Staged the other way it silently does
  nothing, with no 'not recognized' line anywhere. demo2d6.After routes through the
  player controller for this reason.

New commands: demo2d6.InputState, demo2d6.After, demo2d6.Reactivate.
Gates: Demo2d6.* 11/11 green. Config/DefaultEngine.ini's AndroidFileServer injection reverted.

title: 2d6demo: the HUD tooltip's own box is not the comp's either
description:
Found while measuring VaCuus-a4g's action menu, and deliberately NOT fixed there: that
bead's table enumerates six differences and every one of them is the MENU's. The tooltip
underneath it has three of its own, all from one mis-read.

`.tooltip`'s comment says '260x96 is the comp's 626x270 comp-pixels at this scale'. 626 is
the RIGHT EDGE of `Tooltips копия 9` (27,1535 -> 626,1808), not a width — the width is 599.
Measured on the raster `1_Common` of UI_Design_Subsystems.psd, which draws the same card:

  comp box     x 29..624, y 1537..1806  ->  596 x 270 comp px  ->  249.5 x 113.0 px
  ours         x 11..296, y 643..765    ->  286 x 122 px

  - WIDTH: 286 against 249.5, i.e. 36px / 14% too wide. `.tooltip` sets width 16.25rem with
    NO box-sizing, so RmlUi's content-box default adds the 12px padding twice and the 1px
    border twice on top of the 260.
  - HEIGHT: 122 against 113, from min-height 6rem + the same padding.
  - PADDING: the comp's title ink sits 20 comp px (8.4px) inside the box; ours is 12 + 1 =
    13px.
  - RADIUS: the comp's corner arc settles over ~6 comp px (2.5px, i.e. --r-sm); `.tooltip`
    carries --r-lg (8px). Same measurement method as the action menu's, which agreed with
    its comp to 0.4px.

Not a one-line change, which is why it is here rather than folded into a4g: the title is
deliberately set at --fs-md (14px) against the comp's floor-raised 11, so shrinking the box
needs the padding and both type steps re-derived together and the catalogue re-shot.

ALSO WORTH A DECISION, and bigger than this card: every panel stroke in the comps is a
BRASS (105,93,57) — sampled identically on the tooltip and on the action menu's container —
where the project draws `--stroke` #3a3a38. That is one token and every panel in the demo,
so it is the owner's call, not a bug fix.
close_reason:
The tooltip's box is the comp's now. Demo2d6 Content/DevUI/2d6/components.rcss.

RE-MEASURED FIRST, off 1_Common of UI_Design_Subsystems.psd, by scanning for the 1px stroke rather than reading a layer bbox (a bbox includes the layer's shadow):

  box    x 29..624, y 1537..1806  ->  596 x 270 comp px  ->  249.5 x 113.0 px
  corner arc 4 comp px wide at the first row, closed by the fifth -> ~1.8px
  title  ink x 20, y 18, cap 19 comp px  ->  8.37 / 7.54 px in, 7.95px cap
  body   ink x 22, y 69, cap 15 comp px  ->  9.21 / 28.89 px in, 6.28px cap

This CONFIRMS the bead's 596x270 exactly and SETTLES the type question the old comment got wrong: it claimed the title 'was authored at 15'. tokens.rcss derives max(11, round(cap/2.3887/0.72)) -- the title's 19 comp px give 11.05 -> 11, the body's 15 give 8.7 -> floor 11. Both are --fs-xs. Nothing in these comps is set at 15.

THE FIX: box-sizing border-box (the whole width bug -- 260 authored became 260+2*12+2*1=286), width 15.59375rem, min-height 7.0625rem, border-radius --r-sm not --r-lg, padding 4.5px top / 7px elsewhere, title --fs-xs with letter-spacing 0.0625rem like every other Orbitron label in the sheet, body --fs-xs, title margin-bottom 8.5px.

The asymmetric padding is measured rather than computed: at a uniform 7px the title ink landed 10px down against the comp's 7.5, and the missing 2.5 is the face's internal leading, which nothing on this side of the font engine predicts.

CATALOGUE RE-SHOT AND RE-MEASURED (1920x1080, demo2d6.UI 2d6/2d6-catalog.rml):

                    comp      ours    was
    box           249.5x113   250x113  286x122
    title ink L     8.37       9        13
    title ink T     7.54       7        13
    title ink W   111.8      108        --
    body  ink L     9.21       9        13
    body  ink T    28.89      29        --

Every geometric number inside 0.7px, which is the standard the action menu's re-derivation set. The caps render 9 and 8 against 7.95 and 6.28, and the body ink runs 213px against 182.9 -- that is the 11px type floor, expected and documented in the block.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY, AND FILED SEPARATELY: the brass stroke. Sampled (105,93,57) on all four sides of this box and identically on the action menu's container, against this project's --stroke #3a3a38. One token, every panel in the demo, owner's call.

title: 2d6demo: MENU returns to the lobby, and the HUD action menu matches its own design
close_reason:
Both requests shipped in Demo2d6 104614b.

1. MENU RETURNS TO THE LOBBY. pickStatus in Web/apps/2d6/src/nav.ts turns the MENU
button into the ordinary 'nav' emit; no C++ change, so SetScreen's change gate and back
stack are inherited verbatim. On the lobby it is a free no-op (SetScreen compares first).
It RECORDS itself, like RETURN and unlike ESC, so lobby->HANGAR->MENU->ESC lands back in
the HUD; the walk out is finite because GoBack pops without pushing.
Demo2d6.Sim.ScreenHistoryGoesBack now pins both, and both new assertions were watched to
FAIL against deliberate breaks (GoBack routed through SetScreen; SetScreen pushing
ungated) and restored.

2. THE HUD MENU IS ITS OWN COMP's. Split ContextMenu (section screen, unchanged) from a
new ActionMenu (.actmenu): a 226x111 comp-px bordered container with its own gold notch,
ABOVE the tooltip at (15.1, 581.9) with a gap, holding two 210x35 comp-px pill rows each
with its own border and radius, text only, no icons; resting = grey border + dim label,
active/hover = gold border + rgba(gold,38) + gold text. Every number measured off
1_Common of UI_Design_Subsystems.psd rendered alone with psd_tools. Placement corrected:
48px of container fits above the card (ends 630, card starts 643).

Verified: side-by-side against the design crop at matched scale (every box within ~1.5px);

title: 2d6demo: sections take damage in waves and repair, so the dial rings animate in a loop
description:
Owner request: damage should arrive periodically and then recover, so the seven subsystem rings visibly animate in a cycle rather than sitting at 100.

Today StepState ticks heat, ammo and reload; section integrity only ever changes via the demo2d6.Damage console command, so the dials are static in an unattended run.

THE TRAP THIS MUST AVOID, and it is a lesson already paid for once (VaCuus-szf): a continuously-varying float bumped into a revision counter defeats the idle gate. Ship heat did exactly that — it cooled proportionally, changed every step, bumped ShipRevision every step, and re-rendered ~250 elements per frame to move a bar by a hundredth of a pixel; measured 2.9% withheld until it was quantised to the gauge's own pixel, after which 93.9%. Seven dials driven the same way would cost more.

So integrity must be quantised to the resolution at which it is DISPLAYED before it reaches SectionsRevision. The ring has 24 segments (100/24 = 4.17 units) but the needle is continuous over a 270-degree sweep, so the needle is the finer consumer; at the dial's ~81px size one degree is about 0.35px at the tip. The implementer should measure and choose, not guess.

The calm posture (demo2d6.Calm 1) currently measures 93.9-94.4% withheld and is a headline number for the plugin. Whatever cycle ships must not quietly cost it.

DONE — commit cea44b2 in /w/Unreal/Demo2d6 (master, not pushed).

RHYTHM. One salvo every 8 s hits ONE section, on a fixed order that is not the row order, so
each of the seven is hit once per 56 s and no two are in phase. Seven different hit sizes
(28..52) give seven different bands. Repair is PROPORTIONAL, dI/dt = k(100-I), k=0.045 --
a constant rate has no attractor against a periodic hit, so a section would either park at
100 or clamp at 0, and both are the static screen this replaces. Measured over ten simulated
minutes the dials live between 43 and 98 and touch neither stop. bPowered (hysteretic 55/75)
and Alerts (0-3 severity ladder) are derived from Integrity, so they ride an existing publish
and cost nothing.

QUANTUM = 1.0 integrity unit, chosen against the four consumers, not defaulted:
  ring, 24 segments                      4.167 units  (coarsest)
  needle, r=29px through a 270deg sweep  0.73 units/px = 1.37 px of tip travel per unit (finest)
  hub readout Math.round(value)          1.0
  subsystem stat row Math.round()        1.0
One unit is the two TEXT readouts' resolution, and text is the expensive path (geometry
released + recompiled, ElementText.cpp:425-428 -- resource traffic the hash gate cannot
withhold). Below one unit the extra publishes buy needle motion only; and under ambient the

title: var() inside transition or animation is fatal and completely silent
description:
A transition or animation whose value contains var() NEVER RUNS, with no warning, no log line and no visible diagnostic of any kind. Found in the 2d6 demo, where EVERY transition in the project used var(--t-fast|--t-mid|--t-slow) for its duration — so not one of ~30 transitions had ever run, across four component batches, three screens and a component catalogue that was screenshot-reviewed at every step. Nobody noticed, because the failure mode is 'the element simply snaps'.

MECHANISM, both halves opened:
- PropertySpecification.cpp:260-267 — ParsePropertyValues returns ContainsVariable for any value containing var(, and the property is stored as Property{value, Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION}, i.e. the raw unparsed string. This is correct and deliberate: var() is resolved at COMPUTE time (ElementStyle.cpp:162-243).
- ElementStyle.cpp:389-393 — the transition path reads the LOCAL property before computed values exist ('We get the local property directly here to intercept property changes even before the computed values are ready') and then does: if (transition_property->value.GetType() != Variant::TRANSITIONLIST) return;  A VAR_EXPRESSION is a String variant, so it returns. Silently.

So var() works for every other property precisely because it is resolved late, and transition/animation are the two that are read early. That asymmetry is invisible from the outside and there is nothing in the docs about it.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR A BUYER: docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md now documents var() as the theming layer (there is no calc(), so it is the only one). A buyer who follows that advice and puts their timing tokens in custom properties — which is the obvious thing to do — gets a UI where nothing animates and nothing says why.

ASKS: (1) emit one warning when a transition or animation property is dropped because it is still a VAR_EXPRESSION — this is the same class as the existing per-type latched warnings for unsupported filters and unknown shader keys; (2) document it in gotchas.md next to the existing easing-keyword trap, which is the other silent way to lose a whole transition declaration; (3) consider resolving var() for these two properties before the early read, if that is tractable without reordering compute.
close_reason:
FIXED in the vendored tree, not just documented. Vendored patch #4 (Source/ThirdParty/RmlUi/Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp, TransitionPropertyChanges): a PURE INSERTION of 36 lines, zero upstream lines touched, resolving Unit::VAR_EXPRESSION on the transition property with upstream's own ResolveVariablesWithShorthandExpansion before the TRANSITIONLIST test. Safe there specifically, and not assumed: upstream's SubstituteVariableOnce comment (ElementStyle.cpp:227-230) names TransitionPropertyChanges as the case it was written for, and the same function already calls that helper on every transitioned property's start and target value.

THE REPORT'S ANIMATION HALF IS WRONG for this vendored commit (0ae381e) and is now pinned as such. 'animation' with var() has always worked: it is read through ComputedValues::animation(), which resolves (ComputedValues.cpp:8-16). Measured with patch #4 fully reverted -- #anim-variable still animates. Both PropertySpecification.cpp:260-267 and ElementStyle.cpp:389-393 in the report matched the file exactly.

Ask (1), the latched warning: DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED, and the reasoning is in VENDORED_TAG.txt. After the fix the '!= TRANSITIONLIST' branch is unreachable for a var() value, so a warning there is dead code, and it would live in the same vendored function -- a re-vendor that dropped the patch would drop the warning with it. The automation test is the guard instead. The residual failure modes (undefined variable, a substitution that will not parse) were already loud: RmlUi logs LT_ERROR naming the variable or the value.
Ask (2), docs: gotchas.md #3b, next to the easing-keyword trap; rcss-matrix.md via Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py (generator edited, matrix regenerated).
Ask (3), resolving early: done -- that IS the fix.

New test VaCuus.Core.Style.TransitionVariable (Source/VaCuus/Private/Tests/VaCuusStyleVariableTest.cpp). RESTORE-THE-BUG, seen both ways 2026-08-06: patch reverted -> '#variable, transition with var() in its duration STARTS rather than snapping (6gj): expected opacity 1.0000 (+/-0.0100), got 0.2500' and 'has barely moved after 250 ms: expected 0.9500 (+/-0.0600), got 0.2500', every control still passing including '#anim-variable ... opacity 0.2500'. Patch applied -> all nine readings as designed. Suite 207 -> 208, 208/208 green; monolithic VcHost target also builds. Commit 7fbc0b6.

title: 2d6demo: shared chrome remounts on screen change, and entry animation flashes before it starts
description:
Owner report, three symptoms, two causes.

1. THE TOP MENU JERKS when moving between screens. TabBar is rendered INSIDE Lobby.tsx and Section.tsx separately, so a screen change swaps <Lobby/> for <Section/>, preact sees different component types, unmounts one and mounts the other, and the shared chrome is destroyed and rebuilt — replaying its entry animation. The chrome (TabBar, IconRail, StatusBar) must live above the screens in a persistent shell that never unmounts.

2. THE HUD IS VISIBLE IMMEDIATELY, THEN JERKS. RmlUi has NO animation-fill-mode. motion.rcss:255-260 gives .enter-2..enter-6 delays of 0.04..0.20s, and during a delay the element sits at its BASE value — final position, fully opaque — then snaps to the keyframe's start (translateY(1.125rem), opacity 0) when the animation begins. enter-1 has delay 0 and does not flash; the later blocks do, for progressively longer. Task 10 observed this and recorded it as 'correct no-backwards-fill behaviour' without noticing it is visible.
   Fix: transition instead of animation. Base rule holds the START state, a class added on the frame after mount transitions to neutral, and transition's own delay token reproduces the stagger. During a transition delay the element holds its current value, which is the offset state — the behaviour animation cannot give without fill-mode.

3. THE DIAL SEGMENTS DO NOT ANIMATE and still look pixelated. Not animating: they are lit by a class toggle with no transition. Pixelated: converting the ring from a conic-gradient to 24 rotated elements (VaCuus-275) moved it OFF the gradient path that VaCuus-sw1 had just antialiased and ONTO the geometry path, which has no antialiasing at all on a single-sampled RT. The aliasing half is VaCuus-3tg, not this bead.
close_reason:
Fixed in Demo2d6 7501200. Three symptoms, three causes (one more than reported).

1. TAB BAR REMOUNT. TabBar/IconRail/StatusBar were rendered inside each screen; a screen change swaps component types and preact unmounts the subtree. main.tsx now has a persistent Shell above the screen switch with three static-block slots (chrome-top / screen-body / chrome-bottom) whose DOM order reproduces the old paint order exactly -- RmlUi hoists positioned descendants of a static block into the ancestor stacking context in DOM order (Element.cpp:2470-2479, stable sort :2340-2344). EnterGroup keys decide what replays: screen:<name> per screen, tabs:<bool> only when the bar appears/disappears (so lobby<->section never remounts it), chrome:<bool> for the rail/plate. EVIDENCE: two shots across a section -> ESC(2.0s) -> lobby change, the second 234ms into the incoming screen's entry; magick compare over the tab-bar rows = 0 differing pixels, whole frame = 57,437. The only diff in the top 90 rows is the lobby's own divider fading in.

2. ENTRY FLASH. Confirmed as diagnosed (no animation-fill-mode). Replaced with a transition: start state in the base rule, .is-in on an ancestor a frame later, delays unchanged. Element::StartTransition writes the start value immediately (Element.cpp:2690) and UpdateAndGetProperty returns empty while dt<=0 (ElementAnimation.cpp:747-749), so the delay holds the OFFSET state. THE HARD PART WAS 'a frame later': Context::Update is called from RecordAndPublishFrame, which is gated on HasView() (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:1149-1178) while the JS pump is not. In a -game run the document loads, renders, flushes effects and hops rAF with ZERO Updates behind them; vacuus.view reads 1x1 (not recordable) at that point, so a width>0 gate fires just as early as no gate. Proven with a deliberately slowed 3.00s entry: tab bar/rail/plate measured 144.2/148.3/140.3 mean luminance at 20 recorded frames, digit for digit their at-rest values. The working gate is vacuus.stats().updateMs/renderMs > 0 -- the only facade observable for 'a UI frame has been recorded'. EVIDENCE: section screen at 10 recorded frames, before vs after: sec-panel 154.4 -> 127.6, rail 148.3 -> 127.5, statusbar 140.3 -> 127.5 (127.5 = empty). Later blocks now invisible during their delay instead of fully drawn.
GATING: entry stays behind body.ambient, and now on BOTH ends -- the start state is gated too (specificity 0,3,1 vs 0,2,1), so calm mode shows a screen at rest from its first laid-out frame with not even one frame of offset.
EXITING PATH: DELETED, with kf-exit. Nothing ever added .exiting (it appeared in motion.rcss and nowhere else in the repo), and it cannot be made to work by adding the class: preact destroys the outgoing tree in the same commit that mounts the incoming one, so no element survives to carry it. A real exit needs the router to hold the old tree mounted, which is a different feature.

3. DIAL SEGMENTS. The reported cause was wrong in an interesting way: .dial-seg HAD a transition. It had never run. Every transition in the project was written 'var(--t-*)', and a var() anywhere in a transition declaration is fatal and silent -- stored as an unparsed VAR_EXPRESSION string (PropertySpecification.cpp:264-267), and TransitionPropertyChanges returns unless it is already a TRANSITIONLIST (ElementStyle.cpp:388-393). So has every hover in this UI. .dial-seg and .dial-needle are now literals at a matched 0.45s. The other 27 were DELETED rather than repaired: literals were measured first and took calm idle from 94-95% per steady-state window to 87-93%, entirely from the sim-driven ones (20 turret cards changing state while the guns fire). Split filed as VaCuus-9ak.1.

4. NOT REPORTED, FOUND BY THE FIX. RmlUi has no group compositing: opacity is an inherited property, so an element setting its OWN opacity stops inheriting an ancestor's. .mx-icon and .hud-ship-view did, and photographed as 18 fully-lit hardpoint glyphs and 3 ship renders floating over a turret plate at opacity 0. Both moved to image-color, which ElementImage multiplies BY the inherited opacity (ElementImage.cpp:178). Re-shot: gone; at rest 1.5/20.5 pixels differ over the two regions (sub-1/255 rounding). motion.rcss's two sweeps still have the property and now say so -- a ~30x10px radar ping arc can show on an invisible plot for part of one entry.

PERF, turrets HUD, 130s each, vs baseline:
  ambient  0.0% idle, 713.5 draws/frame  (baseline 0.0%, 713.6)
  calm    93.9% idle, 712.8 draws/frame  (baseline 94.0%, 712.8)

title: 2d6demo: HANGAR opens the combat HUD, and ESC goes back
description:

ESC must be handled in C++, not JS: EKeys::Escape is in the widget's DefaultPassThroughKeys (SVaCuusWidget.cpp:144-145), so the UI answers Unhandled by design and the key bubbles to the game. The demo currently binds no input at all.

title: 2d6demo: replace the stage transform with a rem-driven root font-size
description:
Owner report: the UI is blurry in fullscreen and every element has ragged edges.

CAUSE, and it is a defect in the demo's own architecture, not the plugin. main.tsx:52 computes s = min(view.width/1920, view.height/1080) with no upper bound, and .stage is a FIXED 1920x1080 box carrying transform: scale(s). So the entire UI is laid out and rasterised at 1920x1080 and then MAGNIFIED. At 2560x1440 s=1.333; at 3840x2160 s=2.0. Text glyphs come out of the font atlas at their layout size (11px, 14px) and get stretched — that is the blur. Border-radius arcs are tessellated in 1920-space and their facets magnify with everything else — that is the raggedness, on top of the already-known single-sampled RT (VaCuus-3tg).

The spec claimed the transform 'lifts everything back toward the comp's own appearance' on a 1440p or 4K display. True for SIZE; it magnifies an already-rasterised result rather than re-laying-out.

FIX: express every dimension in rem and drive the DOCUMENT's font-size from JS instead of a transform. Verified in the vendored engine: ComputeProperty.cpp:61 resolves Unit::REM as value.number * document_font_size, and ElementDocument::OnPropertyChange:560-562 dirties every rem property recursively when the document's font-size changes. So layout happens at native resolution, glyphs rasterise at true size and arcs tessellate at true radius.

SIDE EFFECT LARGER THAN THE FIX: removing the root transform re-enables scissor clipping document-wide. ElementUtilities.cpp:174 disables it only while a transform is active on the clipping chain, and the clip mask that would replace it is skipped in v1 (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:741-753). With no transform, overflow works again and the whole 'nothing clips' constraint that shaped Tasks 8, 9, 16 and 17 retires. VaCuus-buk's demo-side impact goes away (the plugin-side limitation stands for anyone who does use a transform).

Scope: ~600 lines across components.rcss and tokens.rcss, mechanical (px/16), plus the type ramp, plus img width/height attributes that are px attributes rather than CSS. Then re-verify all three screens and the three catalogue benches at 1080p AND at a higher resolution, which is the case that exposed this.
close_reason: Closed
