title: gradient decorators have no screen-space antialiasing — every diagonal stop edge is a hard staircase
description:
Reported from the 2d6 demo: the HUD's segmented dial rings read as visibly pixelated. Diagnosed to the gradient shader, not to texture filtering (sampling is SF_Bilinear in all six sites: VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:523,672, VaCuusSlateElement.cpp:232,317,520,553,558).

CAUSE. Shaders/Private/VaCuusGradient.usf:58-66, MixStopColors:

    const float Edge1 = max(GetStopPosition(Index), Edge0 + 1e-6f);
    Color = lerp(Color, StopColors[Index], smoothstep(Edge0, Edge1, T));

Coincident stops are separated by 1e-6 in PARAMETER space, which is a step function. A hard colour break in T is a hard break in screen space with no antialiasing whatsoever. A segmented conic ring is made entirely of such breaks, so every segment boundary staircases. Same for repeating-linear-gradient hatching (the demo's no-slot slot) and any hard-stop gradient.

This is faithful to the reference backend (RmlUi_Renderer_GL3.cpp:116-122), which the comment cites — but the reference has the same defect and relies on the host antialiasing the whole UI.

FIX. Antialias in SCREEN space rather than parameter space: widen the smoothstep by the screen-space derivative of T, e.g. W = fwidth(T) and smoothstep(Edge0 - W, Edge1 + W, T), so a hard break becomes exactly one pixel wide regardless of gradient scale.

CAREFUL — the conic seam. For VACUUS_MODE_CONIC, T wraps 1 -> 0 at the seam (:133, 0.5 + atan2(...)/2pi), so fwidth(T) spikes to ~1 along that line and would draw a visible band. The derivative must be clamped, or computed analytically from the angle rather than from the wrapped T.

SECOND, RELATED FINDING. The per-view render target is created single-sampled — NumSamples is never set anywhere in VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp — so every non-axis-aligned polygon edge in the UI aliases too, including border-radius arcs, which GeometryBackgroundBorder.cpp:139 tessellates with a radius-dependent point count. Axis-aligned panel edges are unaffected, which is why this reads as 'the round things are pixelated'. Worth assessing separately: MSAA on the view RT costs memory and a resolve, and analytic AA in the shader may be the better answer for the case that actually shows.
close_reason:
Fixed in 3b2dd7c. Each stop pair is widened around its midpoint to at least one screen pixel via min/max -- exactly a no-op for any pair already wider, and a one-pixel ramp for a coincident one. The pixel width is the ANALYTIC screen-space gradient of T per mode, never fwidth(T): T wraps at a conic's seam and at every repeating period edge, and a hardware derivative there reads the whole jump and would band the seam. Repeating gradients also get a half-pixel window shift plus a last-to-first seed so the period edge is antialiased like the interior stops, and fade to the period mean once bands pass Nyquist. A conic always wraps at 0/1 and gets the same seed (a no-op when the gradient closes).

EVIDENCE. docs/research/proofs/sw1-gradient-aa/ -- before/after at 1920x1080 with per-region exact pixel diffs. Segmented conic ring 1478/129600 px changed, the 2d6 demo's own dial 1158/67200, and the two smooth CONTROLS (two-stop linear 45deg, radial) changed by EXACTLY ZERO bytes. The 0deg seam disc changed 16 px, all within 8 rows of the centre where the angular rate genuinely is large; the diagonal 35deg seam is antialiased (32,48,255 -> 62,48,225 | 235,48,51 -> 255,48,32 at r=60). Fine hatch: 4px and 2px periods settle instead of moireing.

TESTS. Four new GPU tests in VaCuusGradientAATest.cpp, skipping under -nullrhi like the composite GPU test. Suite 204/204 under -nullrhi, 0 failures (200 before). All four pass on real Vulkan.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, all four on real RHI, each perturbation failing exactly the test that names it and nothing else: widening reverted to the reference's verbatim smoothstep -> DiagonalHardStopAA 0 intermediate pixels on all three rows; min/max replaced by unconditional widening -> SmoothGradientUnchanged 11 of 16 pixels off (pixel 3 at 36 vs 31.3); conic AAWidth from fwidth(T) -> ConicSeamClean all six samples at (217,38,0)/(215,40,0) vs required R>=240 G<=15; wrap seed and window shift removed -> RepeatingWrapAA period edge 0 while the interior kept its 1. Restored: all green.

The first draft of ConicSeamClean put the seam on x=32, which is a 2x2 quad BOUNDARY, so ddx never saw the jump and the test passed against the bug it exists to catch. Moved to x=33; noted in the test.

MSAA on the view RT: assessed, not built. ~39.5 MiB per view against 7.91 today (the MSAA target does not replace the RT, it adds to it, because all three consumers sample it as an SRV), a resolve on every published frame, and an sRGB-space resolve average on a display-encoded premultiplied RT. The visible remainder is border-radius arcs on small dials; supersampling and shader-side outline feathering are the other two candidates. Split out as VaCuus-3tg with the numbers.

Also filed VaCuus-z36: VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc and VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy are GMalloc-traffic assertions that misbehave when the full suite runs on a real RHI. Proved pre-existing by reverting the shader and re-running -- ArrayAlloc still failed.

title: clip-mask stencil pass: make overflow clipping survive a transform (the code half of buk)
description:
The CODE half of VaCuus-buk, split out when the doc half shipped (2026-08-05).
The documentation now names this as a v1 limitation (docs/buyer/gotchas.md #8a);
this bead is the fix that would let the limitation be deleted.

WHAT IS BROKEN
A transform anywhere on the clipping chain silently disables ALL clipping in the
subtree. overflow: hidden|auto|scroll clip nothing — no Error, no Warning.

CHAIN, both halves verified in-tree:
- ElementUtilities.cpp:174 — `if (transform) disable_scissor_clipping = true;`,
  unconditional whenever a transform is active on the clipping chain. Correct on
  RmlUi's part: a transformed element's geometry may project anywhere and a
  screen-space rectangle can no longer describe it.
- ElementUtilities.cpp:162-169 — RmlUi emits a CLIP MASK instead, when
  has_border_radius || (transform && has_clipping_content).
- VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:741-753 — EnableClipMask and RenderToClipMask are
  SKIPPED IN v1: "applying the mask needs a stencil pass this RT does not carry
  yet". So the replacement never lands and the original is off.

The same sentence applies to border-radius on a clip container, which is why
Content/DevUI/m2_demo.rcss:9-12 and m1_hud.rcss:7-9 both forbid border-radius
AND transform on their clip boxes. Those two comments are the workaround the
whole product currently ships.

WHY IT IS WORTH REAL WORK
transform: scale() on a root wrapper is THE resolution-independence pattern
here — there is no calc() (grep-confirmed: no such parser anywhere in the
vendored Core), dp == px (Context::SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio is called
only in the excluded RmlUi Backends, never by the plugin), and font sizes cannot
be computed. So the one declaration a buyer reaches for first costs them every
scroll container and overflow:hidden box in the document at once.

PROVEN, not derived (2d6 demo, Task 8): a 40x14 overflow:hidden box with a
200x14 child under a scaled root rendered the child at its full 200px.

SCOPE
The per-view render target needs a stencil (or an equivalent mask attachment)
and the replayer needs to honour the two commands. Note the glass path already
reads clip-mask GEOMETRY out of the command buffer (M5 Task 3's distiller), so
the recording side is not the missing piece — the RT and the replay are.

ACCEPTANCE
Restore-the-bug standard: an automation case with a transformed root and an
overflow:hidden box must show the child CLIPPED, and must be seen to fail
against today's replayer. Delete gotchas.md #8a and the rcss-matrix.md
cross-reference when it lands, and lift the "NEITHER border-radius NOR
transform" rule from m2_demo.rcss / m1_hud.rcss.
close_reason:
SHIPPED. The replay pass now attaches a stencil target and implements EnableClipMask/RenderToClipMask, so overflow clipping survives a transform and a rounded clip container clips its corners.

THE TARGET. VaCuusReplayRenderer::ReplayCommands scans the buffer for a RenderToClipMask (VaCuusReplay::BufferUsesClipMask) and only then calls EnsureStencilTarget, before BeginRenderPass. PF_DepthStencil, DepthStencilTargetable only (nothing samples it), sized to the view and to GetReplaySampleCount() -- the count the COLOUR attachment really has after the platform cap, not the cvar, because a depth-stencil attachment that disagrees with its colour attachment on samples is a render-pass failure and the demo ships at 4x. Action is ClearDepthStencil_DontStoreDepthStencil, so nothing downstream sees it: the glass distiller reads the command BUFFER, and the world sink's CopyTexture and the Slate composite still get the same single-sampled OutputRT in SRVMask. Attached by assigning RPInfo.DepthStencilRenderTarget rather than through a constructor -- every overload taking both a colour resolve and a depth target asserts check(!ResolveColorRT || ResolveColorRT->IsMultisampled()) (RHIResources.h:5526), which is the wrong texture to test and would trip on our single-sampled resolve destination.

THE VIRTUALS. EnableClipMask only flips which depth-stencil state the next content draw binds; it deliberately does not touch the buffer, since RmlUi's disable edge means 'stop testing', not 'erase' (RenderManager.cpp:156-176). RenderToClipMask steps FVaCuusClipMaskState and draws the mask geometry with colour writes off (CW_NONE) through the ordinary UI shaders, using CurrentTransform -- which is load-bearing, because ApplyClipMask calls SetTransform with each clip element's own transform before its mask draw and restores the caller's after (RenderManager.cpp:164-175). A degenerate mask geometry steps the protocol WITHOUT drawing, so an empty clip region clips everything rather than nothing.

THE VALUE PROTOCOL, which is the design decision. The reference backend clears the whole stencil on EVERY Set (RmlUi_Renderer_GL3.cpp:1135-1137, with its own '@performance Increment the reference value instead of clearing each time' directly above it). A full-target clear is the one cost here that scales with RESOLUTION rather than content -- 8.3M samples at 1080p/4x -- and a document with a dozen rounded containers changes its mask list a dozen times a frame. So values are never reused within a pass: the render pass clears to 0 once, each Set takes the next unused value, and clears happen only where they must -- SetInverse (which cannot be expressed any other way) and the 224th Set, where 8 bits runs out. Soundness is one invariant, 'every value present in the buffer is < NextFreeValue', maintained in one place for all three ops. Measured: 600 mixed operations needed 80 clears where the reference would have paid ~360.

A CLASS WITH NO RHI IN IT, so the layer whose bug would be invisible at small scale can be asserted without a GPU: VaCuus.Render.ClipMask.ValueProtocol drives a SIMULATED stencil buffer and checks the invariant after every one of 600 steps, plus the isolation property directly (two disjoint masks in one pass -- an 'always write 1' scheme passes every single-mask test and fails this one). Runs under -nullrhi with the rest of the suite.

MATERIALS came along: the tier binds a full pipeline of its own (DrawMaterial_RenderThread) and would otherwise have been the single draw in a frame that ignored the mask. Its memo key gained the depth-stencil state and the ref.

A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, to gotchas.md #8a, to VaCuus-buk and to both demo sheets, all of which said the same wrong thing: border-radius alone did NOT leave a container unclipped. Three lines below the one everyone was citing, RmlUi keeps a rounded element in the scissor region when there is no transform -- 'If we only have border-radius then we add this element to the scissor region as well as the clip mask' (ElementUtilities.cpp:171-175) -- so the box still clipped rectangularly and only the four corner ARCS went unclipped. Measured on the demo at 11.7 differing pixels in one corner, not a screenful. Only transform disabled clipping outright. Fixed in all four places.

MEASURED (Vulkan / RTX 3090 / Linux, 2026-08-06; docs/research/proofs/4ik-clip-mask):
  Transform case, photographed: with the mask skipped, rows 09-17 of a 176px overflow container paint over the terrain; with the pass, clipped mid-glyph at row 08 (cmp_transform.png).
  Border-radius case: 11.7 differing pixels, all in one corner, exact per-pixel diff (cmp_corner.png).
  Restore-the-bug: two lines in the build clone (BufferUsesClipMask -> false, RenderToClipMask -> break) reproduce the pre-bead path exactly; both shots taken from that binary, both edits reverted, clone diffs clean.
  Cost, reference HUD, 65 s/row: Replay 0.442 -> 0.452 ms avg at 1x and 0.442 -> 0.449 at 4x (p99 LOWER both times); Record 0.527 -> 0.654 (RmlUi building rounded clip geometry, not this pass); publish ratio 100% throughout. Memory is the real cost: 7.91 MiB per view at 1080p/1x, 31.64 at 4x, lazily allocated -- a document that never masks pays 0, asserted by LazyStencilAllocation.

SUITE 208 -> 214 green under -nullrhi, the documented venue. Six new tests, five of them GPU (real-RHI run confirmed each ran at BOTH sample count 1 and 4, no skips), each carrying its own negative control in the same body: the identical buffer with the two mask commands removed must fail the clip assertion. SurvivesTransform pins the discriminator at x=48, inside the SCALED mask and outside the unscaled one, so 'transform ignored' and 'mask dropped' fail differently.

Both targets build (VcHostEditor and monolithic VcHost). Citation gate clean (1941 citations). rcss-matrix.md regenerated through Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py, diff checked to be only the intended lines. perf-guide.md gains a 'Clipping under a transform costs a second per-view target' section with the table.

Filed VaCuus-gq6: VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy and VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc are flaky on the REAL-RHI venue (not -nullrhi). Both reproduced on the PRE-CHANGE build, and MemProxy's events precede the new tests in the log, so neither is this bead's. Commit 717372d.

title: VaCuus hardening: fix what the 2d6 demo exposed
description: The 2d6 demo runs the real buyer path end to end and has surfaced ten defects in the plugin and its docs. Owner asked (2026-08-05) for these to be fixed in the plugin itself, not merely filed. Children cover: buyer-doc corrections that ship inside the package, two CLI one-liners that break a consumer project, three silent-failure warnings, and two real rendering gaps (SaveLayerAsTexture for box-shadow, and the clip-mask stencil pass without which a transformed root disables all clipping).

title: a transformed ancestor silently disables ALL clipping — the standard responsive-root pattern breaks overflow document-wide
description:
Any transform on an ancestor turns off scissor clipping for the whole subtree, and the clip-mask path that would replace it is skipped in v1. Net: overflow:hidden/auto/scroll clip NOTHING, silently, with no warning.

Chain:
- ElementUtilities.cpp:174 — 'if (transform) disable_scissor_clipping = true;' unconditional, whenever a transform is active on the clipping chain.
- ElementUtilities.cpp:161-170 — a clip MASK is emitted instead when has_border_radius || (transform && has_clipping_content).
- VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:741-753 — EnableClipMask / RenderToClipMask are SKIPPED IN v1 ('applying the mask needs a stencil pass this RT does not carry yet').

So the replacement never lands and the original is disabled.

WHY THIS IS BUYER-FACING RATHER THAN EXOTIC: a transform on a root wrapper is THE way to do resolution independence here. There is no calc(), dp == px (SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio is never called), and font-size cannot be computed, so scaling a 1920x1080 authoring surface with one transform: scale() is the only cheap route — and it is what the 2d6 demo does. Adopting it costs the buyer every scroll container, clipped list and overflow-hidden box in the document at once, with nothing in-engine to say so.

The knowledge exists in-tree but only as a demo-sheet comment: Content/DevUI/m2_demo.rcss says '#list-clip must have NEITHER border-radius NOR transform. Either would push RmlUi off the scissor path onto the clip-mask path, which this recorder does not implement, and the list would render unclipped over the rest of the screen.' m1_hud.rcss:8 says the same. Neither docs/buyer/gotchas.md nor rcss-matrix.md carries it, and both frame transform-on-a-scroll-container as a PERFORMANCE note elsewhere, not as 'clipping stops working'.

PROVEN, not derived (2d6 demo, Task 8): a 40x14 overflow:hidden box with a 200x14 child, placed under the demo's scaled .stage, rendered the child at its full 200px width.

Asks, in order of value: (1) put this in gotchas.md as a named limitation with the transformed-root case spelled out; (2) emit one warning when a clip mask is dropped, so it is not silent; (3) implement the stencil pass, which also unblocks border-radius clipping under transforms.
close_reason: DOC HALF ONLY, as scoped -- the stencil pass stays open work, no C++ touched. docs/buyer/gotchas.md gains entry 8a (numbered like 13a so no existing cross-reference renumbers), stating it as a NAMED v1 LIMITATION rather than a perf note: a transform anywhere on the clipping chain silently disables ALL clipping. Both halves of the chain cited from lines I opened: ElementUtilities.cpp:174 sets disable_scissor_clipping = true unconditionally when a transform is active, :162-169 emits a clip mask instead, and VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:741-753 skips EnableClipMask/RenderToClipMask in v1 -- so the original is off and the replacement never lands, with no Error or Warning. Spells out the transformed-root case and why it is not exotic (no calc() -- grep-confirmed absent from vendored Core; dp == px, SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio called only in the excluded Backends, never by the plugin), with the measured 40x14 overflow:hidden / 200x14 child result. Workaround stated both ways: size containers to content and delete rows rather than clip (which perf-guide.md's 'Smaller standing DOM' already prefers -- a clipped scrollback still records every row), or drop the root transform. Also cross-referenced from rcss-matrix.md's 'What is NOT here', beside the missing calc() that motivates the pattern. Cites the two in-tree demo comments (m2_demo.rcss:9-12, m1_hud.rcss:7-9) that carried this knowledge nowhere a buyer would look.

title: fab_inventory.sh has two stale assertions and fails on a correct package
description:
Tools/fab_inventory.sh reports pass=32 fail=2 on a CORRECT BuildPlugin package produced from a clean clone. Both failures are stale assertions in the gate, not defects in the package. Found running the delivery path for the 2d6 demo (Task 2), against a package built from a clean clone of 9895a51.

FAIL 1 — Tools/fab_inventory.sh:58, 'absent docs'.
Config/FilterPlugin.ini was changed at c1394d6 (2026-08-03, 'the package stops being a plugin nobody can be told how to use') to DELIBERATELY ship /README.md and /docs/buyer/*. fab_inventory.sh was last touched at 28fd5b9 (2026-08-02) — a day earlier. The assertion now directly contradicts FilterPlugin.ini. The package correctly contains the four buyer pages and correctly excludes owner-handoff.md.

FAIL 2 — Tools/fab_inventory.sh:30, 'present Web/package-lock.json'.
That file has NEVER been tracked in any branch (git log --all -- Web/package-lock.json is empty) and Web/.gitignore:6 has excluded it since the workspace was introduced. The assertion can only ever have passed against a dev tree where a local npm install had left an untracked lockfile that the /Web/... filter rule then swept into the package. From a clean clone — which is what a real buyer package requires — it cannot exist.

Consequence: the delivery gate has been red on every correct package since 2026-08-03, and green only on a dirty tree. That is the wrong way round for a gate that guards a Fab submission.

Also worth documenting: the gates MUST run before the consuming project is built. Building the project writes Binaries/ and Intermediate/ into Plugins/VaCuus, after which fab_scan reports 253 violations and fab_inventory fail=4 — all artifacts of the build, not of the package.
close_reason: Both stale rows fixed, plus the positive form of row 58. (1) 'present Web/package-lock.json' -> 'absent'. Verified: git log --all -- Web/package-lock.json is EMPTY (never tracked in any branch) and Web/.gitignore:6 excludes it, so from a clean clone it cannot exist; asserting absent also catches the dirty-tree leak that made the old row pass. (2) 'absent docs' removed and replaced by present rows for README.md and all four buyer pages, plus absent for docs/buyer/owner-handoff.md and for docs/{research,passport,superpowers,dev}. Ordering verified with git log as instructed: FilterPlugin.ini changed at c1394d6 2026-08-03, fab_inventory.sh last touched at 28fd5b9 2026-08-02 -- the gate predates the decision it contradicted. (3) Header now says the gates MUST run before any project is built against the package and from a clean-clone package, with both failure modes named. EVIDENCE, restore-the-bug both ways, against one synthetic package staged from tracked files under the BuildPlugin default set + FilterPlugin.ini rules (994 files): HEAD's script -> 'FAIL MISSING: Web/package-lock.json', 'FAIL PRESENT (should not be): docs', pass=32 fail=2 -- reproducing the reported numbers exactly. Fixed script on the same package -> pass=43 fail=0. And against the built-in-place consumer copy at Demo2d6/Plugins/VaCuus (read-only run): fail=4 = Web/node_modules, Web/package-lock.json, Binaries, Intermediate -- all four build/npm artifacts, which is the header note's own demonstration.

title: setup.md's Build.cs snippet cannot link the TakeWidget() snippet printed 8 lines below it
description:
docs/buyer/setup.md:107 tells a buyer to write PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[] { "VaCuus", "VaCuusRender" }), and :112-114 then prints Hud->TakeWidget(). That combination does NOT link:

  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: UWidget::TakeWidget()

Reproduced building /w/Unreal/Demo2d6 (2d6 demo, Task 2) with exactly the documented line.

VaCuusRender.Build.cs:86-101 asserts the opposite, under the heading 'MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, because the obvious guess is wrong': it claims that declaring UMG a PUBLIC dependency of VaCuusRender is what prevents this exact link error for a buyer. That conclusion does not hold. UBT propagates a public dependency's INCLUDE PATHS transitively; it does not put that module on a consumer module's link line.

Evidence, from the built project:
  /w/Unreal/Demo2d6/Intermediate/Build/Linux/x64/UnrealEditor/Development/Demo2d6/libUnrealEditor-Demo2d6.so.link.rsp
carries -lUnrealEditor-{Core,CoreUObject,Engine,InputCore,UMG,VaCuus,VaCuusRender} — and UMG is there ONLY because the consumer module names UMG itself. With the documented two-module list it is absent and the link fails. Note Slate and SlateCore are absent from that line too, which also undercuts the same comment's parenthetical claim that they 'need no such promotion' because Engine re-exports them: they are equally not linked, and it happens not to matter only because no Slate symbol is referenced directly.

The comment's author correctly diagnosed the compiles-but-does-not-link split; the promotion only ever fixed include-path propagation, which the transitive leak already provided.

Fix, two parts: (1) setup.md must list UMG in the buyer's Build.cs; (2) VaCuusRender.Build.cs:86-101 must stop claiming the promotion prevents the link error. Keeping UMG public is still right for the include path — the claim about linking is what is false.
notes: MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN ENGINE SOURCE (not just measured): UEBuildModule.cs:950-958 — SetupPublicLinkEnvironment recurses into a dependency's own dependencies ONLY when that dependency's binary is a static library ('Static libraries do not contain the symbols for their dependencies, so we need to recursively gather them'). Guard is 'if (!bIsBuildingAStaticLibrary && bIsModuleBinaryAStaticLibrary)' at :955. In a modular editor build every module is its own .so, never a StaticLibrary, so a public dependency's public dependencies can never reach a consumer's link line. VaCuusRender declaring UMG public therefore cannot and does not spare the buyer the TakeWidget() link error under any configuration that matters. It still correctly propagates the include path, which is a separate and real benefit — only the link claim is false.
close_reason: Fixed both halves. (1) docs/buyer/setup.md:109 now reads { "VaCuus", "VaCuusRender", "UMG" }, with a short paragraph saying WHY the omission is invisible until link time. (2) VaCuusRender.Build.cs's UMG comment no longer claims the promotion prevents the buyer's link error; it now states that a public dependency propagates INCLUDE PATHS only, cites the gate I opened (UEBuildModule.cs:950-958, bIsModuleBinaryAStaticLibrary, 'Static libraries do not contain the symbols for their dependencies'), notes every module is its own .so in a modular editor build so the recursive gather never runs, records the .link.rsp evidence, and retracts the old parenthetical about Slate/SlateCore -- I verified Engine.Build.cs:89-90 IS inside PublicDependencyModuleNames and they are still absent from a consumer link line, so re-export is not what saves them. KEEPING UMG PUBLIC IS STILL CORRECT and the comment says so explicitly, with 'do not fix this by demoting it' spelled out: demoting would break the include path too. No behaviour change -- the Build.cs edit is comment-only, no rebuild needed.

title: Win64 -game dies in ~20s on 'Failed to create graphics pipeline' — every visual row blocked
description:
Found by the Win64/D3D12 pass 2026-08-03 (docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-win64-results.md, commit 31b0628). THE reason 13 of 15 matrix rows are 'not run': no -game session survives long enough to show anything.

WHAT IS VERIFIED (not inferred): every -game session dies in ~20 seconds on 'Failed to create graphics pipeline' followed by a fatal. It is a PSO-CREATION failure, not a shader-compile failure -- 'LogShaderCompilers: Error' appears ZERO times in the logs. It reproduces. The engine itself renders fine: the one screenshot that survived shows the template level under D3D12 (sky, mannequin with a real shadow, green floor, brick walls) and NO VaCuus UI anywhere in the frame. The input layout in the failing description (offsets 0/8/12) is the RmlUi vertex.

WHAT IS INFERRED, NOT PROVEN: that the failing PSO is ours. Shader names print as <unknown> in the D3D12 error path, so attribution rests on the vertex layout alone. Establish that first -- if it is not ours, this bead changes shape entirely.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT ODD: the same shaders and the same replay path work on Linux/Vulkan (SM6) and macOS/Metal (SM5). Win64 bound SM6 on real hardware (RTX 2080 SUPER) -- the first SM6 execution of this code anywhere. So the suspect list starts with whatever differs at SM6/D3D12: the vertex declaration, blend/depth state, the composite permutation's render-target format, or a root-signature/binding-tier constraint the other two RHIs do not impose.

FIRST MOVES for whoever picks this up: turn on D3D12 validation and the debug layer to get a real reason string instead of the generic failure; get shader names to print (or bisect by disabling draws) to settle the attribution question; and check whether it is the UI pass, the composite, or the material pair by running a document that uses only one of them.

BLOCKS: the entire Win64 column of the manual matrix and the perf passport, the memory-mapped bundle observation (Win64 is the ONLY platform where that branch executes), the Win64 disk literal, and the IME row (bead akj.6.19).

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
Fixed 2026-08-03 (b4f12e1), verified on the owner's Win64 machine. THE ATTRIBUTION QUESTION IS SETTLED — it was ours.

CAUSE, read off the compiled signatures rather than reasoned (Saved/ShaderDebugInfo/PCD3D_SM6/Global/FVaCuusUI{VS,PS}/0/Output.d3dasm, obtained with -d3ddebug + r.DumpShaderDebugInfo=1):
  VS output:  SV_Position reg 0 | TEXCOORD 0 reg 1 | TEXCOORD 1 reg 2
  PS input:                       TEXCOORD 0 reg 0 | TEXCOORD 1 reg 1
DXC numbers signature registers POSITIONALLY, and SV_Position occupies one in the vertex OUTPUT signature. A pixel stage that spells its own list out and omits SV_Position — legal HLSL, and what all three of our pixel stages did — starts one register lower. D3D12 refuses the pipeline ('Semantic TEXCOORD is defined for mismatched hardware registers between the output stage and input stage') and PipelineStateCache.cpp:712 makes a PSO refusal Fatal, so the session died at the first UI draw with no VaCuus pixels ever on screen.

WHY SIX MILESTONES MISSED IT: SPIR-V and Metal map SV_Position to a builtin that consumes no numbered varying, so TEXCOORD locations line up whether or not the pixel stage names it. Neither Linux/Vulkan nor macOS/Metal could have caught this BY CONSTRUCTION — the same class as the libpng-on-Installed-engine defect the macOS pass found, and the third such this session.

FIX: the engine's own idiom (SlateShaderCommon.ush:35-47) — Shaders/Private/VaCuusUIInterpolants.ush holds one struct, included by VaCuusUI/VaCuusGradient/VaCuusBlur, taken by MainVS and all three pixel stages including the ones that ignore a member. Two stages cannot disagree about an order neither writes separately.

A WRONG FIX WAS TRIED FIRST, worth recording: reordering the semantics into ascending index. It changed the shader hashes — proving the edit reached the compiler — and did NOT change the failure. That was the honest signal the hypothesis was wrong; the real answer came only from dumping the signatures.

EVIDENCE: RTX 2080 SUPER (SM6) — zero pipeline failures, zero D3D12 errors, zero fatals, HUD on screen, where every session previously died in ~20 s. Linux regression 198/198.

UNBLOCKS: the 13 Win64 matrix rows marked 'not run', the passport's Win64 column, the memory-mapped bundle observation (Win64 is the only platform where that branch executes), the Win64 disk literal, and the IME row (akj.6.19).

title: UVaCuusWidget is Private and unexported — the documented UMG route is dead for any buyer who does not compile our source
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier of the binary-delivery simulation (workflow wv490rkeo, 2026-08-03), confirmed by hand: Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusUMGWidget.h — the header is under Private/, and the class is declared 'class UVaCuusWidget : public UWidget' with NO VACUUSRENDER_API anywhere in the file. VaCuusRender/Public/ contains only VaCuusCommandBuffer.h and VaCuusReplayRenderer.h.

CONSEQUENCE, measured on the shipped artifact: symbol probe of the delivered libUnrealEditor-VaCuusRender.so found Z_Construct_UClass_UVaCuusWidget exported (so the UCLASS registers and BLUEPRINT use works), but UVaCuusWidget:: members = 0 exported and 0 in the full symbol table. A buyer's C++ cannot include the header (Private) and cannot link the class (unexported). The second documented route is dead the same way: UVaCuusSubsystem::CreateView(TUniquePtr<IVaCuusDocumentHost>, FIntPoint) is public, but BOTH available host implementations -- FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost and SVaCuusWidget -- are Private/. So a C++ buyer has a public factory and no way to construct its argument.

This never surfaced before because every consumer so far (VcHost, VaCuusDemo, VaCuusUserDemo) compiles the plugin from source in-tree, where Private/ is reachable and export macros are irrelevant.

FIX SHAPE: move VaCuusUMGWidget.h to VaCuusRender/Public/ with VACUUSRENDER_API on the class; decide and publish ONE supported C++ host route (either export a concrete host, or ship a small public factory that returns an opaque handle); then re-run the binary simulation's C++ leg to prove a buyer can drive the plugin from code. Until then docs/buyer/setup.md's 'First document' section describes an API that a binary-delivery buyer cannot use.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Fixed and merged 2026-08-03 (91f14a0, fix 63742dd). BOTH host classes were affected: UVaCuusWidget AND UVaCuusWorldComponent each exported ZERO members. Mechanism verified with a standalone clang experiment: -fvisibility-ms-compat (LinuxToolChain.cs:437-440) leaves types default but hides functions, while UHT stamps the module API macro on the class registrar regardless — so the UCLASS registered and Blueprint worked while every member stayed invisible to a linker. FIX: both headers Private -> Public with VACUUSRENDER_API; UMG + VaCuus promoted to PublicDependencyModuleNames; the surface decision recorded in VaCuusRender.Build.cs. EVIDENCE: nm -D on delivered artifacts — UVaCuusWidget 0->21, UVaCuusWorldComponent 0->47, FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost 0->0; a real consumer project linking the delivered .so, deliberately calling only NON-virtual out-of-line members (virtuals ride the vtable that ms-compat exports anyway, so a virtual-only probe would have passed while the bug was live); three-leg restore-the-bug, one of which refuted the obvious guess (demoting UMG to a private dep still COMPILES — the include path leaks transitively — and dies at link on UWidget::TakeWidget). DELIBERATE NON-FIX: no constructible IVaCuusDocumentHost exported, since that drags the render backend in as supported ABI at v0.1; CreateView is now documented as the extension seam it actually is. GATE: Tools/api_export_check.sh, seen to fail on the pre-fix package (2 violations, exit 1) and pass after — no automation test can catch this class, because in-process tests link against the module under test.

title: The Fab package ships no binaries, no README and no docs — a Blueprint-only buyer cannot use the product
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier of the 2026-08-02 buyer-install simulation (workflow warwptkvj), which graded the install GREEN and then had its own verdict overturned. Three shipping-shape defects, each confirmed against the produced artifact /w/Unreal/FabDryRun2/Package (978 files, 9.76 MiB unpacked, 2.96 MiB zipped) and engine source:

(1) ZERO BINARIES, AND setup.md DOES NOT SAY SO. Package top level is Content/ Resources/ Shaders/ Source/ VaCuus.uplugin Web/ -- no Binaries/. This is deliberate (FilterPlugin.ini excludes them under Fab's source-only mandate) but it means a BLUEPRINT-ONLY BUYER CANNOT USE THE PRODUCT AT ALL: no C++ toolchain, no way to compile 978 source files. docs/buyer/setup.md section 1 step 1 says only 'Drop the plugin into <Project>/Plugins/VaCuus'. This is the biggest first-day blocker in the product and it is documented nowhere. Decide: ship prebuilt binaries for the supported platforms (changes the Fab listing category and the FilterPlugin rules), or state the C++-project requirement prominently in setup.md AND the Fab listing.

(2) README.md AND Config/ DO NOT SHIP. BuildPluginCommand's default filter has no rule for root files other than the descriptor (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:459-472). So the one document that tells a buyer to enable the plugin, and that carries the symlink/UBA warning, is exactly what they never receive. docs/buyer/*.md ship nowhere either -- the simulation READ them from our dev tree, which is finding C2: the experience graded green was a documented buyer's, not a real buyer's.

(3) BuildPlugin STRIPS 'EnabledByDefault': true (NewDescriptor.bEnabledByDefault = null, BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:434-445) and sets EngineVersion 5.8.0 + Installed true. The buyer's copy is NOT enabled by default; they must enable it in Edit->Plugins or their .uproject. Nothing tells them.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE HERE: shipped test fixtures hardcode our internal project name -- VaCuusEditor/Private/Tests/VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 has '../../../VcHost/Content/DevUI/m1_hud.rcss' and VaCuusBundle.cpp:392 cites 'VcHost/Config/DefaultEditor.ini:14'. Buyers read those.

FIX SHAPE: FilterPlugin.ini gains README.md + a shipped docs/ subset (setup, gotchas, perf-guide, rcss-matrix); setup.md gains a 'What you receive / what you need' first section stating the C++ requirement, the not-enabled-by-default step, and the project-side content staging rule (DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS(Path="DevUI") -- the plugin's RuntimeDependencies glob only covers $(PluginDir), so a buyer's OWN DevUI content does not stage; the simulation hit this and so did the VaCuusDemo packaging the same day).
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-08-09. Both open items are answered and the packaging shape is a script:
Tools/fab_package.sh produces the Fab folder in one command and refuses to produce a wrong one.

The owner's decision, stated directly: we upload SOURCE, Fab compiles it, the buyer receives
binaries into the engine. There are no other binaries to ship -- RmlUi and quickjs-ng are
vendored as source and compiled by UBT into our own modules. The descriptor is filled;
MarketplaceURL stays empty until the listing exists, which is bead VaCuus-jne along with the
store page, its assets, and the IsBetaVersion/VersionName presentation call.

The package additionally carries what a buyer's AI agent needs (root AGENTS.md plus
docs/buyer/ai-guide.md), the third-party notices, and a provenance manifest.

The argument for having built the script rather than written the recipe down is its first full
run: it failed, correctly, on a real Shipping-only compile error that every editor and
Development build here compiles happily and that would have shipped a plugin nobody could
package for Shipping. Fixed in eb3e80e. Final run green -- three legs ExitCode=0, SCAN CLEAN,
inventory 48/48 -- and the editor suite re-run afterwards at 67/67.

(Closed with --force: the only blocker was the parent epic VaCuus-akj, which stays open by
design until its last child does.)

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
PREMISE CORRECTED BY THE OWNER (2026-08-03), and it invalidates finding (1) plus the M6 decision behind it. Fab COMPILES the plugin itself and delivers BINARIES to the buyer, installed into the ENGINE (Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/<Name>), not source into the project. So: a Blueprint-only buyer CAN use the product — that half of this bead is wrong and withdrawn. What survives, and what this re-opens:

STILL VALID: README.md and Config/ do not ship (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:459-472 has no root-file rule) — the doc that explains enabling the plugin never reaches the buyer; BuildPlugin strips EnabledByDefault (:434-445); shipped test fixtures hardcode our internal project name (VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 '../../../VcHost/...', VaCuusBundle.cpp:392); the project-side content staging rule (DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS) is undocumented for buyers.

RE-OPENED: M6 Task 6 added '-/Binaries/...' and '-/Intermediate/...' to Config/FilterPlugin.ini on the reasoning 'Fab is source-only, a shipped .so is what the scan exists to stop'. That reasoning rests on the same wrong premise. For a Fab-built plugin the buyer NEEDS Binaries/ and Intermediate/Build/<Platform>/<Target>/Inc/ (the UHT-generated headers) — that is what makes an installed plugin usable without compiling. The exclusions must be revisited: decide what the SELLER uploads versus what the BUYER receives, and make FilterPlugin match the upload contract rather than a guess about it. The fab_scan ELF/EXTENSION classes also need a rule that distinguishes 'a .so that must not be in the source upload' from 'a .so that legitimately ships in a built plugin'.

Superseded by the correction: the 'ship prebuilt binaries or state the C++ requirement' fix shape. The real question is narrower — upload contract vs delivery contract.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
BINARY-DELIVERY SIMULATION RESULTS (workflow wv490rkeo, 2026-08-03) — the owner's premise confirmed, and the shape that works is now pinned to engine source.

THE MECHANISM, verified verbatim in UBT: for a plugin under <Project>/Plugins/, RulesCompiler.cs:402 hardcodes bReadOnly: Unreal.IsProjectInstalled() -- false on any non-mod-kit engine -- and RulesAssembly.cs:573 sets bUsePrecompiled = bReadOnly, so the UEBuildBinary.cs:267-271 precompiled early-out NEVER fires and all five modules recompile. Measured: 236 build actions, 233 of them ours, ~10 minutes, full C++ toolchain required, the buyer's 210 MiB download overwritten. The -UsePrecompiled flag is inert here (two action JSONs identical but for env-var ordering). By contrast RulesCompiler.cs:100 gives a MARKETPLACE (engine) plugin bUsePrecompiled = IsEngineInstalled() || bUsePrecompiled -- so ENGINE INSTALL ON A LAUNCHER ENGINE IS THE ONLY SHAPE WHERE THE DELIVERED BINARIES ARE ACCEPTED. That is exactly what Fab does; the owner was right and this run proves why no other shape substitutes.

RUNTIME IS FINE: the delivered .so loaded by path with no version complaint and rendered the full M1 HUD without a build. The problem is UBT's decision, not our binaries.

THE BINARY ARTIFACT (/w/Unreal/FabDryRun3/Package): 1520 files / 209.99 MiB vs the source-only 978 / 9.76 MiB. Binaries/Linux = 16 files / 50.90 MiB, of which .debug + .sym = 42.4 MiB (83% of Binaries, 20% of the package) -- split-DWARF for OUR build of OUR modules, embedding our directory tree, undebuggable by a buyer. Lever: FilterPlugin.ini rides in the source upload and BPC:474-482 reads it on EVERY BuildPlugin invocation including Fab's, so -/Binaries/.../*.debug and *.sym should strip 42 MiB from the buyer's download (inference from :474-482, to confirm at upload time). Intermediate = 526 files / 149 MiB: 68 UHT generated headers plus 458 monolithic UnrealGame .o/.precompiled -- the latter unusable twice over (app name UnrealGame vs the target's UnrealEditor, and the shipped headers carry FID_FabDryRun3_... build-path macros so every buyer regenerates them anyway).

ALSO: the artifact ships 57 test .cpp (1.27 MiB) inside 12 MB of Source/ -- every buyer compiles our entire test suite, which is most of those 233 actions. setup.md offers no way to exclude it. And the 7 shipped files carrying our internal 'VcHost' name (VaCuusLiveReloadTest.cpp:206 literal + comments) reach every buyer.

TASKS THIS BEAD NOW OWNS: (1) setup.md gains an INSTALL MATRIX -- engine/Marketplace on a Launcher engine = binaries accepted; project Plugins/ = always rebuilt, C++ toolchain required, state the ~10 min cost; (2) FilterPlugin.ini: strip .debug/.sym, decide on the monolithic .o (dead weight in the observed shapes), decide whether Private/Tests ships; (3) README.md + a docs subset must ship; (4) EnabledByDefault is DELETED by BPC:434-445 -- setup.md must state the enable step as mandatory, not optional. Split into separate beads at implementation time if it gets unwieldy. Blocking product bug found alongside: VaCuus-dgl.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-03 (c1394d6), all three defects, verified against a produced package rather than against intent.

ON DEFECT (1)'s DECISION -- 'ship prebuilt binaries, or state the C++-project requirement': taken as DOCUMENT IT, and not by preference. Fab's source-shipping mandate for UE-facing code is 4.3.6.1.a, recorded as verified in docs/research/m6-api-notes/buildplugin-fab.md:53 alongside the .exe/.msi ban 4.3.6.1.e, and Config/FilterPlugin.ini's own -/Binaries/... rule exists because of it. Shipping binaries would mean re-reading that rule and changing the listing category, so it is left as an owner reversal rather than assumed. What landed instead: setup.md §0 leads with 'this ships as source, your project must be a C++ project', names the two-minute conversion (Tools -> New C++ Class -> None), and says first launch compiles once.

(2) FilterPlugin.ini now ships README.md + docs/buyer/... minus owner-handoff.md. README.md could NOT ship as it stood -- it was a dev readme carrying /w/Unreal absolute paths, a status line still claiming M3 had not started, and 'License: Not decided yet' as the last thing a paying buyer reads. Rewritten as the product entry page; the host-project/two-trees material moved verbatim to docs/dev/host-project.md, which does not ship.

(3) Ten VcHost lines across eight files, now zero in the shipped surface. FIVE of them were found only by grepping the PACKAGE after grepping the source had reported 'done' -- the artifact is the check, which is the same lesson C2 taught this bead.

ARTIFACT EVIDENCE (994 files, RunUAT BuildPlugin -NoHostPlatform -NoTargetPlatforms, which exercises the FILTER and not compilation): README.md + four buyer pages present, owner-handoff absent, no Binaries/, descriptor shows EngineVersion 5.8.0 / Installed true / no EnabledByDefault, 61 test sources + Content/DevUI/Tests present so setup.md's 'the suite ships' is true, zero VcHost or /w/Unreal strings, Tools/fab_scan.sh CLEAN after both self-tests were seen to fail as planted. One sentence of mine was refuted by the first package and fixed: Config/FilterPlugin.ini does NOT ship, and an early README draft said it did.

STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD: the owner's call on binaries (above), and the .uplugin's own Description field, which is still the placeholder 'VaCuus plugin for Unreal Engine.' and is what a buyer reads in Edit -> Plugins. Left alone deliberately: that is product voice, not a defect I should write.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-09. The bead's two open items are answered and the packaging shape is now a
script instead of a recipe: Tools/fab_package.sh (dfe4dce, a181170, b4ab165).

THE OWNER'S DECISION, stated directly: we upload SOURCE, Fab compiles it, and the buyer
receives binaries into the engine. So the source-only FilterPlugin rules that M6 Task 6 added
are correct after all -- the premise behind them was wrong, the conclusion was not. There are
also NO other binaries to ship: RmlUi and quickjs-ng are vendored as SOURCE and compiled by
UBT into our own modules, and `find Source/ThirdParty -name '*.a' -o -name '*.lib' -o -name
'*.so' -o -name '*.dylib' -o -name '*.dll'` returns nothing. Noted for whoever adds a prebuilt
library later: fab_scan.sh blacklists those extensions UNCONDITIONALLY, with a comment saying
they would be legitimate only under Binaries/ThirdParty "which VaCuus does not use" -- that
rule has to change in the same commit as the first such library.

THE DESCRIPTOR is filled: Description says what the product is without naming the libraries
inside it, DocsURL points at ufna.dev. MarketplaceURL stays EMPTY on purpose -- it can only be
the Fab listing URL, which does not exist yet, and anything else there sends the editor's
Marketplace button somewhere wrong. The script WARNs on it rather than failing, and it is the
one thing still owed before upload (filed as VaCuus-r4t).

WHAT THE PACKAGE GAINED, beyond the docs c1394d6 already added:
  AGENTS.md at the root, materialised from docs/buyer/agents-root.md by the script, plus the
  full docs/buyer/ai-guide.md. The repository's own AGENTS.md is about DEVELOPING the plugin
  and must never reach a buyer's agent; the inventory now greps the shipped file to prove
  which of the two it is, because a `present` row cannot tell them apart.
  THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md -- every claim read out of the licence file it cites. The shipped
  fallback font is LATO, not PT Sans; writing that from memory would have been wrong.
  PACKAGE-MANIFEST.txt with the SHA and build time, which is bead n3w's C1 provenance rule.

THE SCRIPT REFUSES RATHER THAN WARNS, and each refusal was watched (breaks made on a throwaway
branch; master never moved):
  placeholder Description                      -> FAIL, package not produced
  unsmudged LFS pointer in a shipped file       -> FAIL (a broken LFS OBJECT dies even earlier,
                                                  at checkout, which is also a refusal)
  output directory already exists               -> refused, so BuildPlugin cannot merge a new
                                                  package into an old one
  a work-tree edit                              -> never reaches the package: it clones a
                                                  COMMIT, which is C1 made structural
One refusal was not planted: the inventory contradicted itself (`absent AGENTS.md` versus the
new `present`), and the gate caught it on the first run.

AND THE FIRST FULL RUN FOUND A REAL SHIPPING DEFECT, which is the whole argument for the
script. BuildPlugin's third leg is UnrealGame Linux SHIPPING, where WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS
is 0. VaCuusJsCallFunctionTest.cpp:13 pulled EvalString out of a namespace that
VaCuusJsDomTestRig.h declares inside its own guard (:19-341) -- from ABOVE its own guard. Hard
compile error, ExitCode=6, whole package refused. Every editor and Development build here
compiles it happily, and the 2026-08-03 dry run had all three legs green, so it is a regression
that nobody's routine build could see. Fixed (eb3e80e), swept for the same shape across all
five modules' test files -- it was the only one.

FINAL STATE: full run green, three legs ExitCode=0, SCAN CLEAN, inventory 48/48, 1005 files /
13 MB. Editor rebuilt and VaCuus.Js re-run afterwards: 67/67 Success, 0 Fail, including the
test that was touched.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin

title: stat vacuus crashes the game the instant the group is enabled — silent death, crash pipeline broken
description: Found by the owner 2026-08-02 typing 'stat vacuus' into the running lobby demo console; REPRODUCED in VcHost (-game offscreen, -ExecCmds 'vacuus.RefHud, stat vacuus,') — plugin-wide, not demo-specific. Signature: the process dies within a frame of the group being enabled, the log ends mid-flight with no Fatal/callstack, no coredump lands (unlike the same session's Vulkan-OOM crashes, which dumped normally), and the exit status is 127 — read as the engine crash handler exec'ing the MISSING CrashReportClient binary (FUnixPlatformProcess::CreateProc 'File does not exist' seen in earlier logs), which destroys the evidence. Suspicion to verify with the gdb run: our VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE maps to SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER on THREE threads incl. the plugin's own UI thread; 'stat vacuus' turning collection on for the group is the first time the stats system ever receives messages from that thread in this codebase -- no automation test has ever enabled a stat group at runtime (the whole passport ran on the in-house PerfLog). The fix must land with a restore-the-bug automation test that ENABLES the group ('stat vacuus' via Exec) with live views and survives N frames, plus a CLAUDE.md/known-issues note about the missing CrashReportClient masking every hard crash on this machine.
close_reason:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN 2026-08-03. It is a STALE ENGINE MODULE, not glibc, not static TLS, and not the stats system -- both earlier investigations were chasing an artefact of a hidden error message.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: Engine/Binaries/Linux/libUnrealEditor-XMPP.so is dated 2026-04-30 while libUnrealEditor-Core.so is rebuilt daily. It imports FLLMScope's ctor and dtor (_ZN9FLLMScopeC1E... and _ZN9FLLMScopeD1Ev) and today's Core exports no FLLMScope member at all -- 16 matching symbols, every one of them FLLMScopeDynamic::*. Lazy binding means nothing fails at load; the process dies at the first CALL into that module. Enabling a stat GROUP is exactly what makes that call happen: FXmppModule::Tick runs SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER, and a master-enable is what first makes those scopes emit. ld.so reports through _dl_fatal_printf -- its fatal printer for ANY fatal, including an unresolved symbol, NOT specifically a TLS allocation -- and calls exit_group(127).

That single misreading is the whole history of this bead: the gdb backtrace was right, its interpretation was not, and the message that settles it in one minute goes to STDERR while every run redirected or tailed the .log, which ends mid-line.

EVIDENCE, four runs, each survive-60s (70 s timeout; 124 = lived, 127 = died):
  1. stale .so present, -game + stat slate -> 127, 'symbol lookup error: libUnrealEditor-XMPP.so: undefined symbol: _ZN9FLLMScopeD1Ev'
  2. stale .so moved aside                 -> 124, LIVED, 743 frames
  3. RESTORE-THE-BUG: stale .so copied back -> 127, identical message
  4. removed again, 'vacuus.RefHud, stat vacuus' (the owner's original command) -> 124, LIVED, RefHud loaded and bound per VcHost.log

WHY IT WAS NEVER PART OF THE BUILD: after deleting the .so a VcHostEditor rebuild took 2.04 s and did not recreate it -- XMPP is not in this target's module set. It is an orphan the manifest still names ('XMPP': 'libUnrealEditor-XMPP.so' in UnrealEditor.modules), the same resurrection class CLAUDE.md already records for BuildPlugin's HostProject leg.

THE OWNER WAS RIGHT TWICE: group stats did work here before, and the glibc update was a coincidence -- the .so predates it by two months.

FIXED IN THE TREE: stale .so deleted, group stats work. Docs corrected where they were wrong: CLAUDE.md's hazard (which said ROOT CAUSE STILL OPEN and pointed at glibc) and buyer gotcha 20 (which shipped a false 'bleeding-edge glibc / ld.so TLS allocation' diagnosis to customers -- and docs/buyer now ships in the package, so that mattered more than when it was written). Both now state the real cause and the one-step diagnosis: read stderr, compare the .so's mtime with Core's.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: INVESTIGATION COMPLETE — VaCuus EXONERATED. Evidence chain, all steps reproducible: (1) owner's windowed lobby demo died on typing 'stat vacuus'; (2) reproduced in VcHost with '-ExecCmds vacuus.RefHud, stat vacuus,' — plugin-wide; (3) gdb: NO signal ever raised — the process calls exit_group(127) itself; (4) exit_group backtrace: _dl_fatal_printf (ld-linux) <- FThreadStats::AddStatMessage (StatsSystemTypes.h:1261) <- SCOPE_CYCLE_COUNTER in FXmppModule::Tick — ENGINE module, first stat message after master-enable; (5) CONTROL: 'stat slate' with zero VaCuus scopes exits 127 identically — any group-stat enable kills any UE process on this machine; (6) GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.rtld.optional_static_tls titration: 16/32/48/64 KB still 127; 98/128 KB break 128KB-stack thread creation at boot (OnlineSubsystemNull.cpp:307 check + stack-overflow SIGSEGV) — NO working dose exists, the deficit and the stack constraint overlap; (7) UBT already mitigates the class for everything it builds: -ftls-model=local-dynamic on all DLL modules (LinuxToolChain.cs:529-531, incl. our plugin) — the trigger is outside UBT-built code (prebuilt/system lib IE-TLS lazily resolved on the stats path) on Arch glibc 2.43+r37; (8) the missing CrashReportClient turns every such death into a silent no-core no-log exit — that masking cost half the investigation. DISPOSITION: environment/engine issue, not ours; owner machine avoids group stats (vacuus PerfLog is the project's instrument and covers every measurement need); buyer-facing note in gotchas (LTS-distro glibc likely unaffected — older surplus arithmetic); revisit only if a buyer reproduces on a supported distro. Sources: UE Linux Known Issues (static TLS exhaustion class), LinuxToolChain.cs local-dynamic comment.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: SCOPE CORRECTED after owner pushback ('у меня все работало до этого со статом' — he was right, my first write-up over-claimed). Four separate 60-second runs: (a) modular editor -game + 'stat slate' with VaCuus DISABLED -> dead 127; (b) modular + 'stat vacuus' -> dead 127; (c) modular + 'stat fps' -> LIVES (draws its own counter, never master-enables collection — this is what the owner remembers using); (d) STAGED MONOLITHIC VcHost + 'stat vacuus' -> LIVES (no dlopen, no static-TLS pressure). Blast radius is therefore the dev-loop MODULAR binary only; packaged games are immune by construction, which also defuses the buyer-facing angle. ROOT CAUSE REMAINS OPEN: the owner reports group stats working in the editor previously; glibc updated 2026-06-30 (2.43+r22 -> 2.43+r37) but the causal link is UNVERIFIED — the honest next experiment is a repro under the previous glibc from the pacman cache (fakechroot/container), which has not been run. Docs corrected in 4149a98 (CLAUDE.md hazard + buyer gotcha 20 now state the measured scope and mark the cause open).

title: Packaged game: the hud model never binds — [Rml] 'Could not locate data model' in the cooked Development build
description: Found by the M5 packaged-game gate (first Development BuildCookRun, 2026-08-01). In the staged Linux Development build, vacuus.M4Demo boots, m4_hud_logic.js runs from the pak, but the model bind never happens: no 'model hud bound on the UI thread' line, and frame 1 logs [Rml] Error: Could not locate data model 'hud' in element body < #root#VaCuusView1 — binding expressions are dead in the packaged game while the same flow works in editor -game (bind logs before the document attach). Ordering clue: in packaged, the attach error fires at frame [1] and 'View 1 loaded the VFS document' at [2]; in editor both bind and load land at [1] with bind first. The enqueue order is FIFO from one producer (StartModelDriver's BindModel is called before View->LoadDocument in Toggle, VaCuusRender.cpp:754-770), so either BindModel was refused at ENQUEUE time (the bRegistered gate? a Verbose-only refusal?) or the packaged startup drains commands across different frames in a way that lets the attach precede the bind. Repro: RunUAT BuildCookRun -platform=Linux -clientconfig=Development -build -cook -stage -pak; run StagedBuilds/Linux/VcHost.sh -RenderOffscreen -ForceRes -resx=1280 -resy=720 -ExecCmds=vacuus.M4Demo -log; grep the staged VcHost/Saved/Logs/VcHost.log.

title: Only PNG/JPEG/UEJPEG are safe to request as RGBA8; .bmp and .dds crash the editor
description: PRE-EXISTING since M1, found by the Task 11 re-review, VERIFIED against engine source by the controller. LoadTexture passes the format straight from IImageWrapperModule::DetectImageFormat to CreateImageWrapper and then calls GetRaw(ERGBFormat::RGBA, 8, ...). DetectImageFormat can return 11 formats, and the wrappers do NOT all honour the requested format: FATAL -- BmpImageWrapper.cpp:66-70 does check(InFormat == ERGBFormat::BGRA); check(InBitDepth == 8). DdsImageWrapper.cpp:177-178 does check(InFormat == GetFormat()); check(InBitDepth == GetBitDepth()). check() is fatal in every DO_CHECK build, i.e. Development Editor. So a document containing matches the 'BM' magic (ImageWrapperModule.cpp:175-177), passes the probe, and then HARD-CRASHES THE EDITOR from a decode worker thread. Same for any .dds, and for an .ico whose sub-image is BMP (IcoImageWrapper.cpp:89-98 delegates). SILENT WRONG COLOURS -- TgaImageWrapper.cpp:133-141 ignores InFormat and always writes BGRA order. Byte count is W*H*4 so every validation passes; red and blue are swapped with no diagnostic. INVISIBLE -- grayscale UEJPEG (see 6.30) yields W*H bytes and is rejected by the byte-count check. GRACEFUL ALREADY -- EXR, HDR, TIFF all refuse an 8-bit RGBA request and fail cleanly. FIX (one if, and it is the recommended workaround rather than a real fix): whitelist the detected format to {PNG, JPEG, UEJPEG} immediately after DetectImageFormat and log 'unsupported image format' for the rest. That closes the crash, closes the TGA colour swap, turns the grayscale-UEJPEG case into an honest 'unsupported format' message instead of 'the decoder disagreed with itself', and makes the concurrency and GetRaw-caveat comment blocks true as written instead of true-for-two-formats. The real fix upstream would be GetRawImage(FImage&) plus channel-order conversion in the plugin, which is a wider change (it returns ERawImageFormat terms, BGRA8 here).
design: Whitelist after DetectImageFormat. Do NOT try to support BMP/DDS/TGA by requesting BGRA and swizzling -- that spreads channel-order knowledge through the pipeline, whose contract is RGBA premultiplied everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: A document referencing a .bmp, .dds or .tga logs 'unsupported image format' and renders a transparent placeholder instead of crashing or showing swapped channels; a test covers at least the BMP case.
close_reason:
Fixed in d9a9ba4 (Task 11 second fix pass).

6.31: LoadTexture now whitelists {PNG, JPEG, UEJPEG} immediately after DetectImageFormat; anything else gets a Warning naming the file and the format and returns handle 0. The crash was REPRODUCED before the fix, with a real backtrace from a decode worker: 'Assertion failed: InFormat == ERGBFormat::BGRA [BmpImageWrapper.cpp:69]' via FBmpImageWrapper::UncompressBMPData <- Uncompress <- FImageWrapperBase::GetRaw <- IImageWrapper::GetRaw <- LoadTexture's decode lambda <- FScheduler::WorkerLoop. Process aborted at exit 139 with 25 of 31 tests completed. After the whitelist: 31/31, exit 0.

Tests cover BMP *and* TGA, both built with the engine's own encoders. TGA was included deliberately: it is the silent R/B-swap case rather than the crash case, so a test covering only BMP would not have pinned the whitelist's shape.

Labelled a workaround in the comment, with the real fix (GetRawImage(FImage&) plus channel-order conversion in the plugin) cited and scoped out.

6.30: grayscale UEJPEG is now refused at the PROBE on Probe->GetFormat() != ERGBFormat::RGBA, scoped to UEJPEG -- grayscale PNG and JPEG also report Gray and both decode correctly, so an unscoped test would have refused working images. With that gone, the SizeMismatch failure message is honest by construction (nothing can reach it claiming the decoder disagreed with itself).

6.28: all three items done -- the texture-release wording now says 'render-manager teardown, not on document close' with the RenderManager citations; the test-only API and its backing member/Add/prune are behind WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS; the same-buffer ordering note is at the drain site and in the test.

Zero impact on existing fixtures or the demo: all fixtures are PNG/JPEG, the fake-.png case is plain text and is refused by the Invalid branch before the whitelist, and m1_hud.rml's only image is a 64x64 8-bit RGBA PNG (verified). Swept the plugin for other image references -- the only other hits are CSS class names.

title: Packaging: loose Content/DevUI documents are not staged (FilterPlugin.ini is stock)
description: Task 10: Config/FilterPlugin.ini is still the stock template, so a cooked build stages no .rml/.rcss/fonts/images under either content root and will find no documents at runtime. Needs FilterPlugin.ini entries (or the UVaCuusBundle cook path from spec §9, which is M6 scope). Blocking for any packaged demo.
notes:
PREMISE OVERTURNED by the Task 14 implementer, verified against AutomationTool source. This bead said a stock FilterPlugin.ini meant a cooked build would stage no UI documents. That was wrong on the mechanism:

- Config/FilterPlugin.ini has exactly ONE consumer in the entire engine -- RunUAT BuildPlugin (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:453 reads it, :472 loads it). The string appears in no other AutomationTool file. Neither CopyBuildToStagingDirectory nor DeploymentContext touches it. It could NEVER have affected a cooked game.
- For BuildPlugin, /Content/... is already in the DEFAULT filter (:464), alongside /Shaders/... (:466) and /Source/... (:467). The DevUI documents were never missing from a plugin zip either.
- ProjectPackagingSettings' DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS resolves against the PROJECT's content root (CopyBuildToStagingDirectory.Automation.cs:2054), never a plugin's -- so that was not the answer either.

FilterPlugin.ini was therefore deliberately left EMPTY with the finding recorded in it: adding entries would restate an engine default and mask the day that default narrows.

THE REAL FIX, landed in d93b118: RuntimeDependencies in VaCuus.Build.cs, UFS, extension-scoped (.rml .rcss .png .jpg .jpeg .ttf .otf under .../DevUI/.../). UBT expands the wildcards at build time into the receipt (UEBuildBinary.cs:211-219) and StageRuntimeDependenciesFromReceipt stages from it (CopyBuildToStagingDirectory.Automation.cs:1796, DeploymentContext.cs:1040-1056). Extension-scoping is deliberate: RuntimeDependencies bypasses the cooker, so a blanket Content/DevUI/... is how a .uasset gets staged raw.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: built the game target and read VcHost.target -- all six loose files present as UFS, including both subdirectories and the two new m2 files.
NOT VERIFIED: a full cook+stage+pak run actually opening them at runtime. The receipt (the exact input staging consumes) and the source chain were verified; an end-to-end package was out of time budget.
close_reason: See the note added to this bead: the PREMISE was wrong and the fix is elsewhere. FilterPlugin.ini has exactly one consumer in the entire engine (RunUAT BuildPlugin) and could never have affected a cooked game. Fixed in Task 14 (d93b118) with RuntimeDependencies in VaCuus.Build.cs, extension-scoped, verified by building the game target and finding all six loose DevUI files in VcHost.target as UFS. A full cook+stage+pak was not run -- the receipt, which is staging's exact input, was.

title: FVaCuusEngine single-owner contract vs multi-PIE (spec §13 mitigation)
description: Task 3 quality review: FVaCuusEngine's owner-thread contract hard-crashes (checkf) if a second thread initializes while another owns it. Spec §4/§13 assume one UI thread per GameInstance subsystem (per PIE instance) and list 'PIE multi-instance' as mitigated by a 2-client automation test — as written, the second PIE client's UI thread would kill the process. Task 4 must either scope the engine per-subsystem or the spec's multi-PIE story must be amended. Decide during Task 4.
close_reason: Landed in m2-ui-thread a714a7b (Task 4): process-wide UI thread owned by FVaCuusModule + per-view contexts via UVaCuusSubsystem/UVaCuusView (6.10 structural, proven by new VaCuus.Threading.MultiView test); module now stops the thread it owns before engine teardown, ForceShutdownAll demoted to last-resort (6.11); vacuus.M1HUD retries with the inline document when a VFS file load fails, reported through FVaCuusViewStatus (6.7). Spec §4/§13 amended: RmlUi's global state makes per-subsystem threads impossible.

title: ForceShutdownAll cannot stop a live UI thread it does not own
description: Task 3 quality review: FVaCuusModule::ShutdownModule -> ForceShutdownAll() force-resets RefCount and calls Rml::Shutdown() from the game thread, but the UI thread is owned by VaCuusRender's console-command state in another module. Masked today because UGameEngine::PreExit broadcasts OnWorldBeginTearDown (which joins the UI thread) before any module unloads — but any exit route skipping world teardown is a use-after-free on RmlUi globals. Fix in Task 4 via centralized subsystem ownership that registers/stops its UI thread on module unload; do not copy ForceShutdownAll forward as 'already handled'.
close_reason: Landed in m2-ui-thread a714a7b (Task 4): process-wide UI thread owned by FVaCuusModule + per-view contexts via UVaCuusSubsystem/UVaCuusView (6.10 structural, proven by new VaCuus.Threading.MultiView test); module now stops the thread it owns before engine teardown, ForceShutdownAll demoted to last-resort (6.11); vacuus.M1HUD retries with the inline document when a VFS file load fails, reported through FVaCuusViewStatus (6.7). Spec §4/§13 amended: RmlUi's global state makes per-subsystem threads impossible.

close_reason:
M2 ACCEPTED AND MERGED to master as 692b3da. Code tree on merged master is byte-identical to the tested branch tip, which ran 36/36 automation tests green.

Closed with --force over 20 still-open children. That is deliberate, not an oversight: every remaining child is work this milestone consciously DEFERRED with a reason, not work it failed to finish. They are P2 and below, none blocks the merge, and the final pre-merge review's two blockers (Close() leaving a dead document composited forever; Init() able to permanently disable the invariant's own enforcement) were both fixed before landing. The five children that were genuinely M2 work are closed on their merits.

MEASURED at 1920x1080 over 60 s, both documents:
- game thread 0.004 ms typical / 0.011 ms p99-sum against a 0.10 ms gate -- recorded honestly as an INFERENCE FROM A 25x MARGIN rather than a complete measurement, because OnPaint and five rare-event handlers sit outside the perf scopes. Whoever tightens that budget adds OnPaint first.
- UI thread 0.052 ms (M1 HUD) / 0.023 ms (M2 demo) avg Update+Record against 0.50 ms.
- idle: 13,072 of 13,074 frames published nothing; Replay is not called at all on a withheld frame; the 0.004 ms composite is the whole per-frame render cost of an idle UI.
- document load: a pathological 6000x6000 image left the UI thread's Update max at 0.095 ms, indistinguishable from steady state.

SIX BUGS CAUGHT BY REVIEW, each reproduced before it was fixed. Four during the tasks: a mouse capture released one button early; Back blurred only one DOM level so focus stuck and the keyboard was never released; analog nav repeat was not gated on focus, so a held movement stick ate player movement; abandoned-composition cleanup was structurally always dropped. Two more only the cross-task final read could surface: Close() left a dead document composited on screen forever -- with the correct reasoning already written twenty lines below it -- and Init() published the UI-thread id before claiming RmlUi and zeroed rather than restored on failure.

Six comments asserted mechanisms or contracts that did not hold, and two of the four task-level critical bugs were found by noticing exactly that.

FOUR CORRECTIONS TO THE CONTROLLER, all with source evidence, all upheld: a static_assert I prescribed could not catch what I claimed (offsetof is blind to a field that fits existing padding; it needs a member-count check); 6.21's premise was wrong; a failure sequence I propagated was unsupported by Slate's source; and a guarantee I called a fragile third-party assumption is complete BY CONSTRUCTION, since Rml::RenderInterface has no operation that mutates a compiled resource.

Follow-ups live as the open children -- the notable ones being async texture upload (measurement-gated), making the cache-clear pairing safe by construction, the left-stick nav-entry product decision, and the resource-traffic predicate's coverage of the RenderInterface virtuals M3/M4 adds (shaders, filters, clip masks), now guarded by a member-count assert so a new resource array cannot be added silently.

title: M3: Data binding (UPROPERTY reflection -> Rml data models)
description: FVaCuusModelBuilder, snapshot protocol per spec §6, BP nodes; reference HUD completed and driven from USTRUCT at 60Hz. Accept: spec §11 gates pass (except provisional replay row).
close_reason:
M3a MERGED to master as 4dbd299. 62 tests, editor and monolithic game targets both build.

Scope note: this closes the SCALAR half. Arrays and data-for are M3b, split out on the spec review's recommendation because the seam is real -- a flat layout entry keyed on a byte offset cannot address an array element, RmlUi dirties top-level names only (so the only granularity that maps onto DirtyVariable is one bit per whole array, meaning a deep copy whenever any element changes), and whether that is acceptable at 200 rows is a measurement nobody has taken. Every M3a item was settled by source already read.

MEASURED at 1920x1080: game-thread sample+diff 0.00035 ms idle / 0.00161 ms with all 64 fields changed (budget 0.02); UI-thread copy+DirtyVariable 0.00195 ms for 64 fields (budget 0.02); UI-thread re-evaluation 0.00723 ms for 32 variables (budget 0.05); idle 6596 samples / 1 publish / 0 published frames, reproduced independently by the pre-merge reviewer.

One number over budget and recorded rather than hidden: the DOM write that re-evaluation TRIGGERS costs 0.383 ms for 64 simultaneously-changing text bindings, 7.7x its row. The spec had budgeted the wrong half -- re-evaluation is cheap, the SetText and relayout it causes is not.

THREE FINDINGS DECIDED THE ARCHITECTURE, all overturning the v1 sketch: RmlUi's binding API is not compile-time only (BindCustomDataVariable is non-template and resolves fields by string at runtime), so no per-type codegen; RmlUi retains a raw void* it never revalidates, so the pointer must address a UI-thread-owned shadow rather than live gameplay memory -- the real constraint was lifetime, not types; and UPROPERTY metadata does not exist at runtime at all, so exposure runs off EPropertyFlags.

BUILT AGAINST ONE FAILURE MODE: a stale value on screen forever with no log line, which is a heisenbug because newly added views are unconditionally dirty and it therefore looks correct after every live reload. Three invariants, each enforced by SHAPE: the channel is born fully dirty in its constructor; every publish carries current values so a recycled triple-buffer slot cannot regress a field; and VariableDefinition::Set refuses, because RmlUi's own data-value/data-event path would otherwise write the shadow with no VaCuus code involved -- proven by restore-the-bug to actually reach it.

NINE OF MY OWN SPECIFICATIONS WERE WRONG and were corrected with source evidence by the implementers: name legality is positional (Panel.Size binds, top-level Size does not); the layout entry needed a container offset; fixed-size C arrays were unconsidered; weak object refs are unprojectable for the same reason hard pointers are excluded; I1's symptom was disproved (InitializeStruct runs the constructor); a family of case-insensitive comparison bugs was nearly shipped; the idle acceptance criterion did not discriminate; driving the sampler from Tick was not implementable as written; and 'RmlUi's error logs are compiled out' -- repeated since the research phase -- is false, only its asserts are.

Follow-ups open: the Blueprint-recompile hole (VaCuus-akj.12, editor-only, fix is a refusal not a rebuild, and the definition registry must be evicted too), and data-style-* bindings with units defeating the idle gate (VaCuus-akj.13).

title: Atlas demo: @spritesheet for a big icon catalogue, with the texture count on screen
description: THE DEMO THAT MAKES THE WHOLE EPIC LEGIBLE TO A BUYER, and the one lever that beats every eviction policy: an atlas turns N textures into ONE, so there is nothing to evict and nothing to reload. The vendored RmlUi parses @spritesheet (ThirdParty/RmlUi/Source/Core/StyleSheetParser.cpp: 798-801, via SpritesheetPropertyParser at :335). NOT VERIFIED HERE: no sheet in this project or in the 2d6 demo has ever used one, so it has never been through the VaCuus recorder. Step one of this bead is a spike -- put one sprite on screen and confirm it records and replays -- because everything below assumes it does, and the whole plan changes if a sprite-backed decorator takes a path the recorder does not handle. WHAT TO BUILD - a catalogue screen with enough icons to make the point: ~200 weapons at the 2d6 demo's own icon scale - the same screen twice, switchable: one image per , and one atlas + sprites - the census from VaCuus-dqs.1 drawn ON SCREEN, so the difference is a number the viewer reads rather than a claim in a README WHAT IT SHOULD SHOW, with the arithmetic that motivates it (the epic has the derivation): one 213x276 icon is 230 KiB resident, so 200 loose icons are ~45 MiB and one 4096x4096 atlas holding all of them is 64 MiB -- WHICH IS WORSE, and that is exactly why this needs a demo and not an assertion. The atlas wins on packing density (icons are not power-of-two and an atlas has no per-texture floor), on draw-call batching, and on the lifetime problem this epic exists for. It LOSES if the atlas is sized by reflex rather than by content. Pack to the content, report both numbers, and let the demo say which case is which instead of selling one shape. ALSO WORTH MEASURING while the harness exists: draw-call count. Distinct textures break batching in the replayer; an atlas is the standard fix and this demo is the place the claim can be checked rather than repeated. WHERE IT LIVES: the browser preview in the 2d6 repo (Web/preview) is NOT the place to prove any of this -- it has no RHI and no texture census, and its README already says the editor is the arbiter for anything below the layout. This is an in-engine demo. RELATED: VaCuus-wgq (long lists never virtualize). A 200-item catalogue is the same screen from the other side -- that one is per-frame CPU for rows nobody sees, this is resident VRAM for images nobody looks at. If both land, they should land on the same demo screen.
notes:
2026-08-13 (2841db3): STEP ONE ANSWERED — @spritesheet works through the VaCuus recorder.

Headless -game, vacuus.SpriteSpike + vacuus.TextureStats: no warnings of any kind, ONE texture at 16,384 bytes = 64x64x4 exactly, i.e. a single copy of avatar.png feeding four sprite decorators AND a whole-file control. Screenshot confirms the four correct quadrants, so the sprite rectangles are honoured and not just parsed. Document: Content/DevUI/spritesheet_spike.rml, toggle: vacuus.SpriteSpike.

So the rest of this bead is no longer gated on an unknown.

TRAP FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE CATALOGUE: a spritesheet's src resolves DOCUMENT-RELATIVE. The spike first lived under Tests/, probed Tests/img/avatar.png, failed with 'Could not load texture' and the census read 0 — which is indistinguishable from 'sprites do not work' unless you read the warning above it.

WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED, and the spike says so in its own header rather than letting a reader infer it: any memory saving. avatar.png is one file and RmlUi already dedups by SOURCE, so the loose spelling of that document is also one texture. The saving is over N DIFFERENT files and needs the catalogue's real art.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD: (1) the ~200-icon catalogue in both spellings with the census on screen; (2) draw-call count, which is the other half of the atlas case; (3) a real screen change that STOPS showing the art — which is also what closes VaCuus-dqs.2's acceptance, since a release only frees anything once the view is no longer drawing it.
2026-08-13 (0ebaebe): both arms built and measured. Tools/gen_catalog_art.py generates 200 distinct 213x276 icons, the packed atlas, the @spritesheet and both documents; art is gitignored. Toggles: vacuus.CatalogLoose / vacuus.CatalogAtlas.

    arm      textures   logical bytes   draws per replayed frame
    loose        200      44.85 MiB              201.0
    atlas          1      46.87 MiB              201.0

BOTH RESULTS GO AGAINST THE REFLEX. The atlas costs 2 MiB MORE -- identical cell sizes mean the loose arm packs perfectly and the atlas carries its last partial row's slack; an atlas wins on packing only when the art is ragged. And draw calls are IDENTICAL, because nothing in VaCuus merges adjacent draws sharing a texture (filed as its own child bead).

So for VaCuus today an atlas buys LIFETIME only: one texture to release/evict instead of 200, one decode instead of 200.

SECOND PATH TRAP RECORDED: a spritesheet src resolves relative to WHERE IT IS DECLARED -- document-relative for an inline <style>, SHEET-relative for a linked .rcss. Both spellings appear in this bead's two documents.

REMAINING: (1) the census on screen rather than in the log; (2) a screen change that stops showing the art, which is also VaCuus-dqs.2's acceptance.
