title: Auto-eviction: a texture budget the recorder can drive, because it already sees every draw
description:
THE POLICY HALF. Owner asked for auto-unload on screen close; the answer is that
"on close" is the WORSE of the two automatic shapes available, and the better one is
already sitting in the recorder for free.

WHY NOT ON DOCUMENT CLOSE. RmlUi keeps no per-document ownership of a file texture --
FileTextureDatabase is keyed on the source string alone and shared across every document
in the view (TextureDatabase.cpp:93-104). "Release what this document used" is therefore
not a question the database can answer. It could be reconstructed by walking the still-open
documents, collecting their sources and releasing the difference, and that is a legitimate
option B: bounded, runs only on close, no heuristics. Its cost is a full-tree walk per
close and it does nothing at all for the case that actually hurts -- ONE long-lived
catalogue document the player pages through, which never closes.

WHY THE RECORDER IS THE RIGHT PLACE. RenderGeometry(handle, translation, texture) already
carries the texture handle of every draw (VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:235), and
Context::Render runs on EVERY recorded frame -- publication is what the idle gate withholds,
not recording. So "the set of textures drawn this frame" costs one insert per draw and needs
no change to RmlUi at all. Evict what has not been drawn for N recorded frames, under a byte
budget.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION HAS TO GET RIGHT

  1. ONLY FILE TEXTURES. Font atlases arrive through GenerateTexture and live in the
     CALLBACK database, not the file one; Rml::ReleaseTexture(source) cannot touch them,
     but a policy keyed on drawn HANDLES would see them and try. Keep the handle -> source
     map that LoadTexture is already in a position to build, and consider only handles that
     are in it. Evicting a font atlas would be a spectacular, intermittent bug.

  2. RELOAD IS NOT FREE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS. Coming back costs a synchronous
     size probe on the UI thread plus a worker decode -- and EnsureLoaded recovers the
     source from the index with a std::find_if LINEAR SCAN over texture_map
     (TextureDatabase.cpp:121), which is O(N) on the very database that got big enough to
     need evicting. Thrash is therefore super-linear. Hysteresis is not optional: evict in
     batches down to a low-water mark, never one-in-one-out at the budget line.

  3. THE CLOCK IS RECORDED FRAMES, NOT PUBLISHED ONES. A static HUD records thousands of
     frames per publication; keying the age on publications would evict everything on a
     screen nobody is touching, which is exactly backwards.

  4. UI THREAD ONLY. Rml::ReleaseTexture is an RmlUi call like any other. Run the sweep
     between frames on the UI thread, never from the render thread that noticed the budget.

  5. OFF BY DEFAULT, behind a CVar budget. A plugin that silently unloads a buyer's art
     because of a heuristic is a support ticket. Ship it opt-in with the budget in the
     console command from VaCuus-dqs.1 so the number can be tuned against a real screen.

ACCEPTANCE
  Restore-the-bug: with a budget set below the working set, page through a catalogue and
  assert the census plateaus instead of climbing. Then set the budget above it and assert
  it climbs -- a plateau that would have happened anyway is not evidence. Separately assert
  a font atlas survives a sweep that evicts every image around it.
close_reason:
Landed (cce34c1). vacuus.TextureBudgetMB (0 = off) + vacuus.TextureEvictIdleFrames; the sweep evicts undrawn file textures, coldest first, to a low-water mark at 80% of the budget.

THE RECORDER ALREADY HAD THE SIGNAL, as this bead predicted: RenderGeometry carries every draw's texture handle and Context::Render runs on every RECORDED frame, so the drawn-set costs one hash lookup per draw and needs no RmlUi change. Clock is recorded frames, never published ones.

ONLY FILE TEXTURES TRACKED, which is what keeps font atlases safe -- they arrive via GenerateTexture into the callback database and have no source to name. Verified in the catalogue: a sweep that evicted 165 left 36, i.e. 35 icons plus the font atlas to the byte.

MEASURED, 200-icon catalogue, budget 10 MiB:
  on screen                   201 textures / 44.91 MiB, nothing evicted
  screen changed, art undrawn evicted 165, down to 36 / 7.91 MiB
  control at 100 MiB          201 / 44.91 MiB, nothing evicted

The control is not optional -- a plateau that would have happened anyway is not evidence, which this bead's own acceptance said.

THE KNOB PROVES ITS OWN PREMISE: vacuus.TextureEvictIdleFrames 0 with the catalogue ON SCREEN does 7,864 evictions in one run, 165 per frame, tracked total stuck at 44.85 MiB throughout. That is what any policy not keyed on 'recently drawn' produces, and it is the dqs.2 measurement seen at speed.

VaCuus.Render.Texture.EvictionPolicy pins the policy. Restore-the-bug: with the drawn-gate dropped, 'a just-loaded texture is never evictable' and 'a threshold nothing has reached yields nothing' both fail at 3 -- it nominates everything on screen. Restored, green.

OFF BY DEFAULT, as this bead required. Full suite 233/233.

title: Mobile runtime gaps: IVirtualKeyboardEntry text entry and RmlUi ProcessTouch drag-scrolling
description: The two gaps that keep Android/iOS labelled short of 'done', extracted from docs/research/mobile-support.md now that both platforms build+cook+render (Android emulator 2026-08-11, iPhone 11 Pro on-device 2026-08-12): (1) TEXT ENTRY — mobile has no ITextInputMethodSystem; the whole-value push API is IVirtualKeyboardEntry, unimplemented, so a text field never summons the keyboard (mobile-support.md input/text table, GenericApplication.h:550). (2) TOUCH SCROLLING — only scroll path is ProcessMouseWheel (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:194); RmlUi's own ProcessTouchStart/Move/End/Cancel (Context.h:209-230, drag-to-scroll+inertia in Context.cpp:922-1014) are never called, so a finger drag over a scrollable list does nothing. Closing these flips the honest platform wording from 'supported with two named gaps' to plain supported.

title: gotchas.md: a project's first document gets no input until the game sets FInputModeGameAndUI
description: Building the HelloVaCuus example from a blank C++ project surfaced a gap: a project with no input mode set leaves the default FInputModeGameOnly in place, the game viewport holds mouse capture, and FSlateApplication routes every pointer event to the captor without a hit test -- so a viewport-hosted VaCuus document is completely dead to input with no error anywhere. The plugin knows this (VaCuusRender.cpp SetUIInputMode carries the evidence) and its own demos call it, but a buyer following setup.md §2 gets the AddViewportWidgetContent snippet with no mention of it. Add it to gotchas.md, and consider one line in setup.md §2 next to the teardown snippet.
notes:
Added gotchas.md #23 in a new 'Hosting and input' section, plus a pointer in setup.md §2 right after the AddViewportWidgetContent snippet.

Every mechanism claim was read in the engine source, not recalled (5.6 lines; each line checked to be identical in 5.8):
- UInputSettings ships bCaptureMouseOnLaunch=true and DefaultViewportMouseCaptureMode=CapturePermanently_IncludingInitialMouseDown (InputSettings.cpp:40,49); UGameViewportClient::Init copies it (GameViewportClient.cpp:535). So a project that never calls SetInputMode still ends up captured -- ApplyInputMode has exactly one caller, APlayerController::SetInputMode.
- ProcessMouseButtonDownEvent takes the target from GetCaptorPath and routes to that path's LAST widget (SlateApplication.cpp:5125-5128).
- FInputModeGameAndUI::ApplyInputMode is what fixes it, via ReleaseMouseCapture() + SetMouseCaptureMode(CaptureDuringMouseDown) (PlayerController.cpp:6260,6265).

CORRECTED AN EXISTING COMMENT while verifying. VaCuusRender.cpp SetUIInputMode said 'under the default FInputModeGameOnly ... and never runs a hit test'. Two imprecisions: (a) the default is no SetInputMode call at all, not GameOnly -- GameOnly merely asks for the same capture explicitly; (b) the move path DOES hit-test (ProcessMouseMoveEvent calls LocateWindowUnderMouse) -- it just does not matter, because RoutePointerMoveEvent then routes with FToLeafmostPolicy(MouseCaptorPath) at :5610,5630. The conclusion the comment drew was right and was observed; only the mechanism was stated loosely. Comment rewritten with the lines, and mirrored to the /w/Unreal/VcHost clone so the trees stay identical (comment-only, no rebuild needed).

Same imprecision was copied into the HelloVaCuus example (HelloVaCuusScreen.cpp comment and README); both fixed there too, and the example's bundled plugin copy got the three changed files so its 'gotchas.md #23' reference resolves.

title: The missing glyph is silent: RmlUi substitutes U+FFFD and logs nothing
description:
SPLIT OUT OF VaCuus-sg2.4, which shipped everything else. This is the half that needs a VENDORED RmlUi PATCH, which is why it is its own bead: it should travel with the four patches VaCuus-7ym.1 is offering upstream, not be smuggled in beside a feature.

THE DEFECT, in RmlUi not in VaCuus: FontFaceHandleDefault::GetOrAppendGlyph, having failed in the styled face AND every fallback face, sets character = Character::Replacement and returns it (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:386-393). No log at any level. So a game that switches to Russian or Chinese without loading a covering face renders a screen of U+FFFD with a completely clean log, and the only way to find out is to look at the screen.

Measured coverage of the shipped face (fc-query on Content/DevUI/fonts/LatoLatin-Regular.ttf): 20-7e, a0-17f plus symbols. No Cyrillic, no CJK. This is the default every buyer starts from.

WHAT TO ADD: a substitution COUNTER plus one latched Warning naming the first missing character and the face that wanted it. A counter and not a per-glyph log, because this path runs inside text layout and a per-glyph line would flood at frame rate.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DIAGNOSTICS: without it the font half of localization has no observable, so it cannot be tested and will rot -- the project's own rule. The registry half already has one (FVaCuusFontRegistry::GetNumFacesLoaded_UIThread, asserted by VaCuus.Font.RegistryReplay); this is the missing partner.

ACCEPTANCE: the counter rises when Cyrillic text is laid out with only the Latin face loaded, and stays flat once a covering face is registered through UVaCuusSubsystem::LoadFontFace. Independently upstreamable -- offer it with the 7ym.1 batch.
close_reason:
Patch #5 landed, documented in VENDORED_TAG.txt with its re-vendoring check, and proven by reverting it.

SHAPE, chosen for upstreamability not convenience: a virtual GetNumReplacementGlyphs on the PUBLIC FontEngineInterface defaulting to 0, overridden by FontEngineInterfaceDefault over a counter on FontProvider, incremented at the one call site in FontFaceHandleDefault::GetOrAppendGlyph. Reports a COUNT rather than a bool on purpose: an engine that cannot answer and an engine with nothing to report must not be the same value by construction. The warning is latched to one line per Rml::Initialise because the site runs inside text layout; counter and latch are instance members of the provider, so both reset with the library.

WHY NOT AT THE VaCuus LAYER (the question the ledger convention demands): glyph lookup happens inside the default font engine during layout, FontEngineInterface has no hook near it, and FVaCuusSystemInterface::LogMessage can only forward what RmlUi says -- which was nothing. Replacing the whole font engine for one counter is not proportionate.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, both directions on 2026-08-09: commenting out the single call site fails VaCuus.Font.MissingGlyph with 'Expected uncovered text is COUNTED instead of silently becoming U+FFFD to be true' while the LATIN CONTROL still passes -- that control is what stops the claim passing on a counter that incremented per glyph. Restored -> green. The passing run prints the warning naming U+0417, the first character of the test string, which is what proves the latch reports the first offender.

NOT ASSERTED and deliberately: that the count stays flat once a covering face is registered. The repo ships one .ttf and it has no Cyrillic, so there is nothing to register -- that half needs a font asset, i.e. a licensing decision, not a code change.

FVaCuusFontRegistry::GetNumReplacementGlyphs_UIThread is the plugin door, reached through the interface so a game swapping the font engine still compiles.

226/226 green; editor and monolithic targets build. Offer with the VaCuus-7ym.1 batch: it costs an int, changes no rendering behaviour, and is worth having in RmlUi regardless of VaCuus.

title: Prove the seamless switch end to end, then write it down
description:
Spec section 5, and the close-out of VaCuus-cii against what actually shipped.

Restore-the-bug table from the spec:
- {{ t.key }} changes with no reload after a push | drop DirtyVariable -> text stays stale
- dotted {{ t.menu.settings.title }} resolves
- a hyphenated key is diagnosed, not silent
- a struct field named t gets a named refusal | drop the check -> silent overwrite
- vacuus.translate inside the callback sees the new table | fire before install -> sees the old
- the font registry survives a UI-thread restart | drop PublishToUIThread -> faces gone
- the replacement-glyph counter rises on Cyrillic with no face

New counters as observables: dirty count on t, callback fire count, faces replayed, glyphs substituted.

VISUAL ACCEPTANCE, done not read: in VcHost push a Cyrillic table, load a face through the new door, switch language with a settings-like document open, and screenshot BEFORE and AFTER showing the text changed and the JS state did not reset.
close_reason:
Proven end to end, on screen and in the suite.

VISUAL ACCEPTANCE, the part this bead existed for. Three headless runs at 1280x720 driving the new vacuus.LocDemo through vacuus.LocDemo.Lang:
- en  -> LIVE panel 'Health' / 'Settings'; PARSE-TIME panel 'Health'
- fr  -> LIVE panel 'Sante' / 'Parametres'; PARSE-TIME panel STILL 'Health'
- ru  -> LIVE panel rendered as replacement boxes, log naming U+0436 once

The fr frame is the deliverable: the same key, one panel moved and the other did not, with no reload anywhere in the run. The ru frame is the font trap photographed, and it is also patch #5 working outside a test.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, all four, each seen fail and then pass:
- drop VaCuusTranslationVariable::Dirty      -> live text keeps the old language
- hoist the JS dispatch above InstallSnapshot -> the handler reports the previous state
- drop FVaCuusFontRegistry::PublishToUIThread -> zero faces after a UI-thread restart
- drop the patch #5 call site                 -> the glyph counter stays flat on Cyrillic while the Latin control still passes

Six tests carry it: VaCuus.Translation.Live, .ReservedName, .Signal, .StringTableBridge, VaCuus.Js.LanguageChanged, VaCuus.Font.RegistryReplay and .MissingGlyph. 226/226 green; editor and monolithic game targets build.

WRITTEN DOWN in docs/buyer/localization.md (VaCuus-cii), which the screenshots above are the evidence behind.

NOT COVERED, and named so nobody assumes otherwise: no run proves the count stays flat once a COVERING face is registered, because the repository ships one .ttf and it has no Cyrillic. That needs a font asset, i.e. a licensing decision.

title: Runtime font faces: a registry, a door, and the glyph that fails silently
description:
Spec section 3.

DOOR: UVaCuusSubsystem::LoadFontFace(VfsPath, bFallbackFace) -> queue -> Rml::LoadFontFace(path, fallback_face) (Core.h:108). UI thread, so no project can do this itself.

REGISTRY, not just a door: fallback faces are consulted IN REGISTRATION ORDER (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:367-383) and the font provider is process-global inside Rml::Initialise/Shutdown. Same shape as the style and translation registries -- ordered, deduped, plus PublishToUIThread for replay after a UI-thread restart (VaCuusTranslation.h:83 is the precedent). Without replay a restart silently loses the Cyrillic face.

THE SILENT FAILURE: when no face has the glyph, RmlUi substitutes Character::Replacement and logs NOTHING (FontFaceHandleDefault.cpp:386-393). Russian text under the shipped LatoLatin is a screen of U+FFFD with a clean log. Measured coverage of Content/DevUI/fonts/LatoLatin-Regular.ttf via fc-query: 20-7e, a0-17f plus symbols -- no Cyrillic, no CJK.

An invariant with no observable cannot be tested and will rot, so: a substitution COUNTER plus one latched Warning naming the first missing character (per-glyph logging would flood at frame rate). This is a FIFTH vendored RmlUi patch on top of the four VaCuus-7ym.1 is offering upstream -- independently useful, goes up in the same batch.
close_reason:
The registry, the door and the replay shipped and are proven. The silent-glyph diagnostic split out to VaCuus-sg2.6 because it needs a vendored RmlUi patch and belongs with the VaCuus-7ym.1 upstream batch.

SHIPPED: FVaCuusFontRegistry (ordered, deduped by (path, fallback flag)), a LoadFontFace command kind on the UI queue, UVaCuusSubsystem::LoadFontFace(VfsPath, bFallbackFace) as the BlueprintCallable door, existence resolved through the same ordered DevUI roots the default face uses so the diagnostic can name them, and PublishToUIThread replay wired into both GetOrStartUIThread paths.

THE REPLAY IS THE POINT AND IT IS PROVEN: RmlUi's font provider lives inside Rml::Initialise/Shutdown, so a restarted UI thread comes back with only the shipped Latin face. Commenting out FVaCuusFontRegistry::PublishToUIThread makes VaCuus.Font.RegistryReplay fail at 0 faces on BOTH the first boot and the restart; restored -> green.

Test note worth keeping: the probe recorded nothing until it was given a document -- the per-view record loop is gated on HasView(), which wants a non-degenerate size AND a document. Same gate the sizeless view in VaCuus.Model.Apply exists to demonstrate.

Test: VaCuus.Font.RegistryReplay. Full suite 225/225 green; monolithic game target builds.

title: vacuus.onLanguageChanged, and its ordering contract
description:
Spec section 2.

The vacuus.onUnload shape verbatim: initialised to JS_NULL (VaCuusJsViewContext.cpp:186), read at dispatch under FVaCuusJsEntryGuard (:271-290), so === null feature-tests and reassignment works.

ORDERING IS THE CONTRACT, and it is the thing to test by breaking: the callback fires AFTER the snapshot is installed and AFTER DirtyVariable, so vacuus.translate inside it already sees the new table. Fire it before install and a handler that repaints reads the OLD strings -- which is the bug this ordering exists to prevent.

Argument is the tag from the foundation child. Needs a fire-count observable (the GetNumListenerRefs precedent).
close_reason:
Shipped with its ordering contract proven by breaking it.

vacuus.onLanguageChanged(tag) follows the vacuus.onUnload shape exactly: seeded JS_NULL so === null feature-tests, read through the property chain at dispatch time so reassignment and clearing work, guard-wrapped, exceptions to the sink, counted (GetNumLanguageCallbacksRun). Dispatched from IVaCuusScriptHost::OnTranslationTableChanged -- a defaulted no-op on the interface so a non-scripting host stays valid -- fanned out over every materialized view context.

RESTORE-THE-BUG: hoisting the ScriptHost dispatch above FVaCuusTranslationRegistry::InstallSnapshot makes the handler report 'fr:vl_hello' -- the untranslated identity, i.e. the PREVIOUS state -- instead of 'fr:vl_bonjour'. Restored -> green.

Also caught by an existing guard, which is the guard working: VaCuus.Js.Preact.Conformance failed with 'present-but-untyped onLanguageChanged' until the slot was added to Content/DevUI/Tests/vacuus-api-manifest.json. .d.ts updated too.

Test: VaCuus.Js.LanguageChanged.

title: Localization is shipped and tested but documented nowhere a buyer can read
description:
The localization contract exists and is tested, but it lives ONLY in headers. A
buyer reading docs/buyer/*.md finds the word "localization" exactly zero times
(grep over docs/buyer + docs/dev: no hits). Everything below is real, shipped
behaviour a buyer must be told about, and none of it is derivable from the
public API surface alone.

WHAT THE DOC HAS TO CARRY

1. The seam. UVaCuusSubsystem::SetTranslationTable (VaCuusSubsystem.h:230,
   BlueprintCallable) publishes ONE process-wide key->string table, whole-table
   replacement with a monotonic version (FVaCuusTranslationRegistry,
   VaCuusTranslation.h). There is no per-call game handler and that was
   REJECTED, not deferred: translate() answers synchronously during JS
   execution on the UI thread. The game's "handler" IS the push.

2. Two readers with DIFFERENT timing, which is the whole reason a language
   switch is three steps and not one:
     - RML text -> FVaCuusSystemInterface::TranslateString
       (VaCuusSystemInterface.cpp:119), run ONCE at text instancing
       (RmlUi Factory.cpp:336). The key is the literal text in the markup.
     - JS -> vacuus.translate(key, params?) (VaCuusJsHostApi.cpp:346), every
       call, always the newest table. `{name}` params substituted in one
       left-to-right pass; single braces on purpose (RmlUi arms data binding on
       `{{` only), so an unsubstituted token renders literally instead of
       going live.
   Misses are identity on both paths, quietly. The one named refusal is "no
   table was ever published" -- one Verbose per context.

3. THE LANGUAGE-SWITCH RECIPE, all three steps, because skipping any one of
   them fails silently:
     a. SetTranslationTable(new table)            -- JS half answers at once
     b. ClearAssetCachesAndReloadAllViews(...)    -- RML half, VaCuusSubsystem.h:122
     c. re-push every model carrying FText        -- VaCuusView.h:352-365
   Step (c) is a contract, not advice: an FText field is stored in the shadow
   as FText::AsCultureInvariant(Live.ToString()), resolved once on the game
   thread, so the UI thread never touches FTextLocalizationManager -- that is
   what makes the design thread-safe at all. The projection has an empty
   TextId, so CanUpdateDisplayString returns false (TextHistory.cpp:940-943)
   and it can never re-resolve itself. A culture change is invisible until the
   next UpdateModel, with no log line, because nothing on that path is wrong.
   Hang the re-push off FInternationalization::Get().OnCultureChanged()
   (Internationalization.h:201), or call UpdateModel every frame.

4. NO UE-LOCALIZATION INTEGRATION, said plainly. No .locres reading, no
   per-culture files, no OnCultureChanged subscription inside the plugin. The
   game builds the table from whatever it likes. A buyer who assumes FText
   "just works" through the UI will ship the wrong language.

5. FONTS, the trap with the widest blast radius. The plugin loads
   fonts/LatoLatin-Regular.ttf (VaCuusEngine.cpp:138). Measured charset:
   20-7e, a0-17f plus symbols -- NO Cyrillic, NO CJK, no Greek beyond a few
   math glyphs. Any non-Latin language needs the project's own face, and the
   only route is @font-face in RCSS whose src is ROOT-relative, not
   document-relative like <link>/<script src> (gotchas.md #5). Mixed-script
   text wants -rmlui-fallback-face: true (StyleSheetParser.cpp:306), which
   RmlUi supports and VaCuus does not configure for you.

6. What reload costs: it re-mounts JS from module top level -- fresh context,
   fresh state (VaCuusJsWebDxTest.cpp, case E-P7). Open tab, scroll position,
   timers: gone. A settings screen that switches language in place should
   drive its text through vacuus.translate and repaint itself instead.

Proof for all of the above is VaCuus.Js.Translate (VaCuusJsWebDxTest.cpp:568+):
identity before any table, lookup after, replacement-not-merge across two
pushes, both readers through the same snapshot, and the adversarial params case
(a param value carrying another param's token stays literal -- killer/victim in
a killfeed are user data).

ACCEPTANCE
- docs/buyer gains the localization coverage (its own page, or a section in an
  existing page -- author's call), carrying items 1-6 with the three-step
  recipe as copy-pasteable code.
- A buyer following the page alone can switch language in a running game and
  get Cyrillic or CJK on screen. Verify by DOING it in VcHost, not by reading:
  push a table with a non-Latin string, load a face via @font-face, switch,
  screenshot.
- gotchas.md gets an entry if the font trap is not already reachable from
  there.
close_reason:
docs/buyer/localization.md written, and its acceptance met by DOING rather than reading.

The page carries all six items the bead asked for: the one call and its whole-table-replacement rule; the two readers and their DIFFERENT timing as a table (the section everything else follows from); the live route with its key-shape restriction and the standalone 'vacuus' model; both change signals; the FText re-push contract; the fonts section with measured Latin-only coverage; plus a pre-ship checklist.

Verified on screen through vacuus.LocDemo -- see VaCuus-sg2.5 for the three frames.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE WRITING FORCED, both in gotchas.md #5. It asserted 'There is no public C++ font-loading API' -- true until UVaCuusSubsystem::LoadFontFace landed this session, and left standing it would have sent a buyer down the only route it knew about. And it never said the shipped face is Latin-only, which is the single fact deciding whether a second language renders at all.

Also added: gotchas #21 (a switch moves some strings and not others) and #22 (FText in a model shows the old language); the finding count corrected 20 -> 22 in both index tables; ai-guide symptom lines for boxes-after-switch and half-a-screen-changed; index rows in agents-root.md and ai-guide.md.

title: Long lists: nothing virtualizes, so a 1000-item store costs 1000 rows every UI frame
description:
Owner's question 2026-08-09: "a normal UI has very large item lists that you page through and
draw efficiently -- imagine a thousand items in a shop. Do we have that already?"

ANSWER: a long list WORKS today and is NOT optimised. Nothing in VaCuus or in the vendored
RmlUi virtualizes, windows or recycles rows. Checked in source rather than assumed:

  DataViewFor::Update materialises ONE REAL ELEMENT PER ITEM -- it loops to the array size and
  InsertBefore()s a fresh clone for every index (Source/ThirdParty/RmlUi/Source/Core/
  DataViewDefault.cpp, DataViewFor::Update). 1000 items is 1000 subtrees in the DOM.

  Element::Render() walks the ENTIRE stacking context with no viewport culling. The
  `if (ElementUtilities::SetClippingRegion(this))` gate skips only the element's OWN
  background/effects/OnRender; the `for (Element* element : stacking_context)` loop that
  recurses into children sits AFTER that block and always runs. So a row scrolled far out of
  view is still visited every recorded frame.

  Element::Update() recurses into every child unconditionally (Element.cpp:146-147, already
  cited in VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp's header for the animation case).

  The interactive-region snapshot is a per-frame FULL-TREE walk by construction
  (VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.cpp).

SO THE PER-FRAME COST IS O(TOTAL NODES), NOT O(VISIBLE NODES). The idle gate does not save
this: it withholds PUBLICATION when the content hash is unchanged, which spares the render
thread, the replay and the composite -- but Context::Update() and Context::Render() still run
on the UI thread every frame, and those are the two that scale with node count.

WHAT THAT MEANS AGAINST OUR OWN BUDGET. The reference HUD is 1,732 nodes at 1.077 ms
Update+Record average, against a ≤1.2 ms worst-case row (docs/buyer/perf-guide.md:23). A
1,000-item store list at a conservative ~5 nodes per card is ~5,000 nodes -- roughly 3x the
reference HUD, i.e. ~2.5x over the budget row that already represents our worst case. It is on
its own thread, so it is not a game-thread hitch; it is a UI thread that stops keeping up.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS, so this is a performance bead and not a functionality one: overflow-x /
overflow-y accept auto and scroll (docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md:61-62), the widget forwards wheel
input, and RmlUi draws its own scrollbars. A thousand-row list scrolls correctly today.

THE CHEAP IDIOM THAT EXISTS RIGHT NOW, and should be written down for buyers whatever we
decide: bind only a WINDOW of the array to the model and have the host swap the slice as the
user scrolls. data-for handles that unchanged -- it rebuilds to the bound array's size -- so
paging costs nothing new and caps the node count at the window. It is not virtual scrolling
(the scrollbar must be faked or the window must be large), but it is the difference between
5,000 nodes and 50.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD DO, in order:
  1. MEASURE FIRST. There is no number for this anywhere: the largest data-for exercised by any
     test today is 200 rows (VaCuusDataForTest.cpp:701). Build a bench document at 100 / 1,000
     / 5,000 rows and record Update, Record, snapshot-build and first-layout separately, so the
     decision is made against the shape of the curve rather than against a guess about it.
  2. THEN decide, and the forks are real: (a) document the host-side windowing idiom and ship
     nothing -- cheapest, and honest for v1; (b) cull off-screen children in the RECORDER, which
     is our code and would help every long document, not just lists; (c) a real virtualized
     data-for, which is an RmlUi-level feature and the largest by far.
  3. A TEST BELONGS TO WHICHEVER LANDS, not before it. A test written now would only record
     that a big list is slow, which is what step 1 is for -- and per the project's own rule, an
     assertion with no chosen invariant behind it rots.

NOT A REGRESSION AND NOT URGENT UNLESS A CUSTOMER ASKS: no shipped demo has a list anywhere
near this scale (the store screen has 7 cards, the collection 5 thumbs), which is exactly why
nobody has hit it.
notes:
2026-08-13: VaCuus-dqs is this bead's memory-side sibling — a big catalogue costs resident VRAM per icon with no eviction, where this one costs per-frame CPU per row with no culling. A thousand-item store hits both, and VaCuus-dqs.4's demo screen is the natural place to land them together.
2026-08-13 (3a96f5a): THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL ESTIMATE IS WRONG, measured rather than argued.

Tools/gen_catalog_art.py --cards N + vacuus.CatalogNodes: N cards of five plain divs, no images, no text -- so Update/Render/snapshot is the only thing measured. Five nodes per card is this bead's own assumption made literal.

    cards   nodes   Update   Record   Update+Record
      200   1,000    0.040    0.128       0.168 ms
    1,000   5,000    0.172    0.629       0.801 ms
    2,000  10,000    0.369    1.254       1.623 ms

Linear to within noise (~0.163 ms per 1,000 nodes).

THE PREDICTION HERE WAS ~2.5x OVER THE 1.2 ms BUDGET ROW for a 1,000-item store at 5 nodes/card. Measured: 0.801 ms, comfortably UNDER it. The estimate scaled the reference HUD (1,732 nodes at 1.077 ms), which costs ~0.62 ms per 1,000 nodes against these cards' 0.163.

SO NODE COUNT IS NOT THE DRIVER; NODE CONTENT IS, by about 4x. These are the cheapest nodes that can exist -- flat boxes, no text, no decorator, no effect, no transition -- so the figures are a LOWER BOUND. The reference HUD's nodes carry all of those. This bead's conclusion is right for a realistic store row and wrong for the reason it gave.

NEXT STEP BEFORE ANY VIRTUALIZATION IS BUILT: the same curve for a row WITH text and a decorator. That is where the 4x lives, and it decides whether virtualization is needed at 1,000 rows or at 5,000. Building a windowing scheme against the wrong number would be the expensive mistake here -- the analysis in this bead's description (DataViewFor materialising one element per item, Render walking the whole stacking context, the snapshot's full-tree walk) is all confirmed and unchanged; only the magnitude was off.

Everything else in the description stands: the idle gate does not help, because it withholds PUBLICATION while Update and Render run every frame.

title: The Fab listing itself: store page, assets, and the MarketplaceURL that closes the loop
description:
Split out of VaCuus-avu at its close, 2026-08-09. The PACKAGE is now producible by one command
and passes both gates; what is left is the STORE PAGE, which no script can write.

MarketplaceURL IS THE ONE MECHANICAL ITEM, and it is circular on purpose: the descriptor field
can only hold the Fab product URL, and that URL does not exist until the listing does. So the
order is listing first, then set the field, then re-run Tools/fab_package.sh so the shipped
descriptor carries it. fab_package.sh WARNs on the empty field today rather than failing --
deliberately, because failing would make the first package unbuildable.

WHAT ELSE A LISTING NEEDS and this repository does not have:
  - the store description and feature copy (the .uplugin Description is one paragraph for the
    editor's plugin browser, not a product page);
  - screenshots and a thumbnail. The plugin's own demos are the honest source -- vacuus.RefHud
    (the 1,732-node reference HUD), vacuus.M5Deco (the decorator gallery), vacuus.M5Glass, and
    the VaCuusDemo project's five lobby screens, all of which render headless at 1920x1080;
  - the category and tag choices, which decide who ever sees it;
  - a decision on whether the listing states UE 5.8 only. Today it must: BuildPlugin has only
    ever run on 5.8 (bead VaCuus-93v), so any wider claim is unverified.

WORTH SETTLING AT THE SAME TIME, both currently true and both buyer-visible: the descriptor
says IsBetaVersion true and VersionName "0.1". Beta puts a warning in the buyer's plugin
browser. Both are accurate for what the matrix can still not show (VaCuus-cob) -- so this is a
product call about how to present that, not a defect.

title: BuildPlugin has only ever run on 5.8 — the '3 engine versions' acceptance line rests on one
description:
Split out of VaCuus-akj.10 (M6) at its close, 2026-08-09, so the milestone does not carry an
unmet acceptance line silently.

THE LINE: arch spec §14's M6 accept says "RunUAT BuildPlugin passes on 3 engine versions".
WHAT HAS ACTUALLY RUN: 5.8 only -- the Linux leg (docs/research/m6-api-notes/
buildplugin-fab-dryrun.md) and the Win64 -StrictIncludes leg (bead akj.10.8). 5.6 and 5.7 have
never been attempted anywhere, because no 5.6/5.7 SDK exists on the dev machine.

THE SEAM IS ALREADY BUILT, which is why this is a run and not a design: every drift-suspect
engine call goes through Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusEngineCompat.h -- four hotspots,
each documenting what 5.8 does with opened citations and what to CHECK on the older engine.
Ground truth for "zero version guards exist today": grepping all five modules for
ENGINE_MINOR_VERSION|ENGINE_MAJOR_VERSION|UE_VERSION|VERSION_NEWER_THAN|VERSION_OLDER_THAN
returns only that header's own comments. The project conventions forbid speculative #if guards
asserting header shapes nobody here has read, so the guards get written FROM the failures this
run produces, not before it.

THE PROCEDURE IS WRITTEN AND UNEXECUTED: docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-shim1.md has it
per-engine, including the clean-clone rule (the esbuild ELF must never enter the copy; verify
Content/Bundles/DevUIBundle.uasset is a real package and not a ~130-byte LFS pointer) and the
-StrictIncludes shape (no PCH, no unity -- BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:133-137 -- because
Fab recompiles on compilers we do not run).

BLOCKED ON HARDWARE/SDK: needs a machine with 5.6.x and 5.7.x installed. Until it runs, the
honest claim is "BuildPlugin passes on 5.8, Linux and Win64", and anything the Fab listing or
the buyer docs says about older engines is unverified.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
5.6 LEG NOW DONE (2026-08-10, Linux). RunUAT BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes passes on 5.6.1 via Tools/fab_package.sh --engine /w/Unreal/UE5.6: clean clone at 3918c99, 3660 compile actions, 0 errors; fab_scan self-test-fails on the 6 planted fixtures then reports CLEAN; fab_inventory pass=48 fail=0. Artifact: /w/Unreal/VaCuusPackage-5.6 (+ .zip, 3.3 MB), BuildPlugin stamped EngineVersion 5.6.0 / Installed true into the packaged descriptor.

SCORE AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE LINE: 2 of 3 engines. 5.8 (Linux + Win64) and 5.6 (Linux). 5.7 still has no SDK here. Win64 on 5.6 is NOT covered -- BuildPlugin's host filter drops Win64 SILENTLY on a non-Windows host (BuildPluginCommand.Automation.cs:499-508), so it needs a Windows machine.

BLOCKER WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ANYONE REPEATS THIS: RunUAT on a fresh 5.6.1 tree dies in ~2 s with 'AutomationTool encountered an error before a log file was set' and nothing useful on stdout. The cause is UAT's OWN C# script modules failing to build -- NuGet's audit flags Magick.NET-Q16-HDRI-AnyCPU 14.7.0 in Gauntlet/AutomationUtils and NU1901/1902/1903 are Warning-As-Error, 314 errors. Time-dependent, not a broken checkout: the advisories postdate 5.6.1. Fix without touching the engine: NuGetAudit=false in the environment. Memory: ue56-runuat-nuget-audit-blocks-buildplugin

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: Owner 2026-08-12: runtime on 5.7 is tested and OK (demo project ran with only project-side Target.cs updates: DefaultBuildSettings V6, IncludeOrderVersion Unreal5_7). Docs/site/listing now claim 5.6/5.7/5.8 tested. This bead's axis is unchanged: BuildPlugin packaging has still only ever run on 5.8 — the 5.6 and now also 5.7 BuildPlugin legs remain to run before the LISTING claims those engine versions for the package.

title: vacuus.LobbyDemo has no automation coverage at all since it left the plugin
description:
Found 2026-08-08 while fixing VaCuus-pwu.

Commit 562bf45 ('the lobby demo leaves the plugin, and takes the API gap with it') deleted
Source/VaCuusRender/Private/Tests/VaCuusLobbyDemoTest.cpp along with the demo, and the
VaCuusDemo project has NO test target and NO Tests directory -- 'find Source -name *Test*'
returns nothing. So the lobby demo, its router, its brain and its five screens are today
verified only by reading a headless log by hand.

THAT IS WHY VaCuus-pwu SURVIVED. The attribution was wrong for every content click for as
long as the router has existed, and nothing could fail: the two tests that went away asserted
the REFUSAL path (VaCuusLobbyDemoTest.cpp:42,53 per the macOS passport), which is exactly the
part that did not need a human to notice it.

WORTH TESTING, in rough order of value per line:
- The router's press attribution: chrome snapshot covers -> Chrome; chrome declines and
  content covers -> Content; neither -> Game; router never called -> the count guard holds.
  This is now observable (EPressTaker + the press count) which is what makes it testable.
- The router's Unhandled-reaches-no-sibling contract: the reason chrome is the only
  hit-testable widget (HittestGrid.cpp:214-226) is asserted in a comment and nowhere else.
- OnMouseButtonUp's bChromeHeldCapture rule: a chrome-captured press must not send an up to
  the content view.

FIRST QUESTION TO ANSWER, and it is a project-shape one rather than a test one: does
VaCuusDemo get a test module, or do these tests belong back in the plugin against a synthetic
two-view stack (no DevUI content, so no host-content dependency)? The second is cheaper and
runs in the plugin's existing suite; the first tests the thing that actually shipped.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-08-09. VaCuusDemo f67e26a adds VaCuus.Demo.LobbyRouter; it passes, and each of its
three central claims has been watched to fail with the defect reinstated.

THE PROJECT-SHAPE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, and the bead's second option turned out to rest on a
wrong premise worth recording. "Tests belong back in the plugin against a synthetic two-view
stack" cannot test this router: SVaCuusLobbyRouterWidget is VaCuusDemo code and the plugin has
no trace of it (grep -rn LobbyRouter over all five modules returns nothing), so a plugin-side
stack would assert against a REIMPLEMENTATION of the thing under test. The tests therefore live
in the demo project, next to what shipped.

No new module or target was needed for that: UBT compiles TP_ThirdPerson/VaCuus/Tests/*.cpp with
the rest of the module, WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS guards it out of a shipping build, and the
suite runs from VaCuusDemo.uproject like any other. The only build change is one
PrivateIncludePaths entry so Tests/ can include the header a level up by name.

AND IT IS THE FIRST EXTERNAL USER OF THE PLUGIN'S PUBLIC SEAM, which is worth more than the
tests themselves: UBT hands an Internal/ directory only to modules in the same
Rules.Context.Scope (UEBuildModule.cs:736-740), so this module cannot reach
VaCuusTestDocumentHost or any of the plugin's own fixtures -- exactly like a buyer. The rig is
built from VaCuusSlateView::MakeElement/MakeDocumentHost, FVaCuusViewStatus, UVaCuusView and
FVaCuusUIThread alone. If that surface ever stops being sufficient, this test stops compiling.

WHAT IS ASSERTED: all four attribution states (Chrome / Content / Game / the count guard that
says a press never reached the router); the capture rule in BOTH directions -- a chrome-captured
press sends no up to the content, an uncaptured one does, and the second is what makes the first
evidence rather than a tautology; and the tie-break the one-widget design exists to produce, a
point both snapshots claim going to chrome (the modal-dim-over-a-content-button misroute in its
smallest form). The fixture itself is asserted before anything is routed, and that guard earned
its keep on the first run by catching a missing PollStatus() -- without it every point would
have answered Game correctly while proving nothing.

WHAT IS NOT, deliberately and in the test's own words: the Unhandled-reaches-no-sibling contract
is Slate's (FHittestGrid::GetBubblePath, HittestGrid.cpp:214-226), and a test that invokes
handlers directly cannot observe it either way. Our half of that bargain -- Unhandled for a point
neither snapshot covers -- is asserted; the bubble itself stays with the in-game matrix rows.

title: vacuus.LobbyDemo.Click blames THE GAME for every content-view click the UI actually handled
description:
Found 2026-08-08 while running the VaCuus-a1k checklist, and it matters because it is
an INSTRUMENT defect: an acceptance run reads this line and records the wrong answer.

WHAT HAPPENS. vacuus.LobbyDemo.Click prints, for every click that lands in the CONTENT
view, "the press was taken by THE GAME (VaCuus declined, so it bubbled past us to
SViewport)" -- while the click demonstrably reached the UI. Same session, both halves:

  Left click at (577, 412)  -> "THE GAME (VaCuus declined ...)"
  Left click at (1888, 114) -> "THE UI (VaCuus captured the mouse)"

(577,412) is a measured CONTENT rect, (1888,114) a measured CHROME rect. Content clicks
were proven to reach the UI three separate ways in this run set: a menu click produced
"navigating to career ('career.rml')"; the EQUIP click changed the button's MEASURED
geometry (1418,690)-(1848,738) -> (1407,689)-(1855,743); a tab click swapped the whole
collection screen (screenshot evidence, RIFLES -> KNIFES).

WHY, and it is the design working as written rather than a routing bug. The lobby has
ONE hit-testable widget: SVaCuusLobbyRouterWidget on the CHROME view, with the content
widget HitTestInvisible (VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp:48-58 gives the reason -- FHittestGrid::
GetBubblePath walks the ancestor chain, HittestGrid.cpp:214-226, so an Unhandled reply
from an overlay never reaches a covered SIBLING). The router answers Slate from the
CONTENT snapshot when chrome's snapshot declines (:1243-1248). But the attribution is
sampled from SVaCuusWidget::GetMouseCaptureHolder_Debug() (VaCuusLobbyDemoInput.cpp:211),
and CAPTURE is taken on the chrome path only. So for a content-routed press the holder
is empty and the line blames the game.

THE CODE PREDICTED THIS EXACT SYMPTOM. SVaCuusWidget.h:29-30 already says an attribution
that stopped tracking a capture site "would report 'THE GAME' for a press the UI took --
the exact wrong conclusion for an acceptance run to record". The mechanism differs (no
site stopped tracking; the router forwards without capturing) but the wrong conclusion
is the one that was foreseen.

COST ALREADY PAID: a1k's run-1 comment (2026-08-07) recorded the attribution as
trustworthy -- "reports honestly" -- on the strength of a single CHROME click, the one
case where it happens to be right.

FIX SHAPE (the demo's harness, VaCuusLobbyDemoInput.cpp, not the plugin): the message
must distinguish three states, not two -- chrome took it (capture held), content took it
(the router answered from the content snapshot), the game took it (neither). The router
already knows which of its two snapshots answered; the honest fix is to ask IT rather
than to infer ownership from a capture flag that only one of the two paths ever sets.
Until then the line should not claim "VaCuus declined" when it cannot know.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-08, Linux/Vulkan headless 1920x1080, VaCuusDemo working tree.

THE SHAPE, and it is the one the bead asked for: the ROUTER observes which of its two doors
answered and the command reads that observation, instead of the command inferring ownership
from a capture flag that only one door ever sets.

  SVaCuusLobbyRouterWidget::EPressTaker { Chrome, Content, Game } + RecordPress(), called on
  BOTH branches of OnMouseButtonDown (VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp). One writer for the taker and the
  press count together -- the FVaCuusMouseCaptureState::Set shape -- so a future press path
  cannot update one and forget the other.

  DescribeWhoTookThePress(PressesBefore) turns it into words. The count is sampled BEFORE the
  press so the readout can say 'not my press': a click that never reaches the router leaves the
  PREVIOUS click's taker standing, and reporting that would have been the same defect wearing a
  new costume. Deliberately does NOT ask the snapshots what they WOULD do -- a query answers
  'who would take it', which is the question that was already wrong.

  ClickWhereThePointerIs no longer decides the attribution at all; the caller supplies it,
  sampled between press and release (that ordering stays load-bearing for any capture-based
  answer). The plugin's one-widget copies keep their two-answer form, which is exact for them.

FOUR STATES, ONE SESSION, MEASURED RECTS:
  (5000,5000) outside the window -> NOBODY THIS COMMAND CAN NAME (never reached the router)
  ( 960, 300) covered by neither -> THE GAME (bubbled past the router to SViewport)
  ( 577, 412) content[4]         -> THE UI, CONTENT  <- the bug: used to say THE GAME
  (1888, 114) chrome[10]         -> THE UI, CHROME
  demo off, (577,412)            -> THE GAME (vacuus.LobbyDemo is not up)

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, same log, 8 ms apart: click (263,202) -> 'THE UI, CONTENT' then
'vacuus.LobbyDemo: navigating to battlepass' and View 1 swaps to battlepass.rml. The
attribution and the navigation now agree; before, the same click read THE GAME.

RESTORE-THE-BUG. Forced RecordPress(EPressTaker::Game) on the content branch, rebuilt, re-ran:
(577,412) went back to 'THE GAME (neither snapshot covered the point...)' while (1888,114)
stayed 'THE UI, CHROME' -- the original signature exactly, chrome right and content wrong.
Restored, rebuilt, re-ran: the four answers above.

ALSO IN THIS CHANGE
- Removed a dead 'namespace VaCuusM1HUD' forward-declaration block at the top of
  VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp. It claimed external linkage into VaCuusRender.cpp 'same module' -- false
  since akj.25 moved the demo into the project; unused, so it never broke the link.
- Three comments still said the input helpers are shared 'by forward declaration'. They are
  shared through VaCuusLobbyDemoInput.h; corrected.
- docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-macos-plan.md:239 told a macOS runner to use
  vacuus.LobbyDemo.Click for 'did the UI actually take it' and quoted the two-answer token.
  That command is no longer in the plugin at all and no longer prints that string; corrected in
  place, with the new four-answer form named.

BUILDS: VaCuusDemoEditor (10 s) and the monolithic VaCuusDemo game target (87 s), both clean.
NOT COMMITTED -- conservative profile.

title: VaCuus.Js.Cost.CombinedChurn is flaky on Apple silicon -- its tolerance lands on the boundary
description:
Measured 2026-08-07 on the Mac (M1 Pro, 10 cores, 16 GB, macOS 26.5.2, installed UE 5.8, -nullrhi).

THE TEST STRADDLES ITS OWN THRESHOLD. Three consecutive runs of the SAME binary, same commit
(0354c52), nothing else started between them:

  run 1  Success   p99 4.61838 ms, max 10.03617
  run 2  Success   p99 4.95346 ms, max 15.35596
  run 3  FAIL      p99 5.39417 ms, max 11.88838

The assertion is 'the combined p99 stays inside 10x the gate', i.e. p99 <= 5.00 ms against a
stated GATE of p99 <= 0.50 ms. So the platform sits at 92-108% of the pass line and the outcome
is a coin flip.

NOT A REGRESSION, and this is worth stating because it first showed up in the same suite run as
the akj.24 fix. The measurement is JsPump + Update + JsGC with Record==0 -- no recorder, no
replayer, no texture upload -- and akj.24 changed only FVaCuusReplayRenderer's async-upload park
key. There is no path between them. It also passed on this same Mac earlier the same day
(217/217, 0 failures, commit 0e1f470), which is exactly what a boundary-straddling gate does.

CONTRIBUTING BUT NOT CAUSAL: the first failing run was polluted -- a 136 MiB git-lfs clone was
running concurrently on the same machine (my error) and it read p99 12.60, max 48.95. Re-running
on a quieter machine gave 6.14, and the three isolated runs above gave 4.6-5.4. So load makes it
worse; it is marginal even without.

Linux passes comfortably (218/218) and Win64 passed at 217/217 before this test existed in the
delta -- so the tolerance was calibrated on Linux and never re-checked on Apple silicon.

TWO SHAPES FOR THE FIX, and this repo already contains the precedent for the second:
 1. Scale the tolerance per platform, or raise it to a number M1 Pro clears with margin.
 2. Make it a MEASUREMENT rather than a gate off Linux. VaCuus.Render.Upload.Cost does exactly
    this and says why in its header: 'a wall clock on a shared build box is evidence, not a
    gate'. A cost test that fails half the time gets muted, which costs more than it protects.

Whoever takes it: decide which, do not just bump the number without saying what it is calibrated
against and on what hardware.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move LobbyDemo out of the plugin into the VaCuusDemo project
description:
Owner direction 2026-08-07, superseding a1k's premise: the M1-M5 demos STAY in the plugin; the lobby is 'our example content' and belongs to the VaCuusDemo project, which just uses the plugin.

WHAT MOVES: Source/VaCuusRender/Private/VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp (2107 lines) and
Private/Tests/VaCuusLobbyDemoTest.cpp. The CONTENT is already outside -- chrome.rml plus
the five screens and the PT Sans faces live in /w/Unreal/VaCuusDemo/Content/DevUI and are
served through the project document root, which the plugin already lists second
(VaCuusContentPaths.h). Nothing about the content needs to change.

WHAT BLOCKS IT, and it is an API decision rather than a file move. LobbyDemo is not written
against the public surface; it reaches four PRIVATE headers of VaCuusRender:

  SVaCuusWidget.h          -- SUBCLASSED (SVaCuusLobbyRouterWidget, :1241) to own the
                              stack's single hit-testable widget and route input.
  VaCuusSlateElement.h     -- MakeShared<FVaCuusSlateElement>() x3 (:1624, :1625, :1787),
                              one per stacked view, wired to widgets by hand.
  VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.h  -- MakeUnique<FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost>(Element) wrapped in the
                              demo's own IVaCuusDocumentHost decorator (:1628-1631, :1790).
  VaCuusDemoModel.h        -- UVaCuusDemoWriteListener, bound to UVaCuusView::OnJsEvent.
                              Shared with the M1-M5 demos, so it STAYS; the lobby needs its
                              own listener UCLASS in the demo module.

Everything else it uses is already public (VaCuusView, VaCuusSubsystem, VaCuusUIThread,
VaCuusDocumentHost, VaCuusGameBridge, VaCuusInputEvent, VaCuusContentPaths, VaCuusDefines).

THE CASCADE, measured: publicizing VaCuusSlateElement.h drags VaCuusEngineCompat.h,
VaCuusFrameSink.h and VaCuusGlassDistiller.h public with it -- a public header cannot
include a private one from another module. VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.h drags
VaCuusUnsupportedTally.h. SVaCuusWidget.h includes only engine headers and is clean.

TWO SHAPES, both real, owner's call:
 (a) Publicize the six headers and add VACUUSRENDER_API. Fast, low ceremony -- and it makes
     the glass distiller, the frame-sink interface and the engine-version seam part of the
     product's public API on the way to Fab.
 (b) Export a narrow facade: SVaCuusWidget public (subclassing genuinely needs the type),
     plus factory functions returning opaque handles for 'compose this view into Slate' and
     'give me the default document host to decorate'. FVaCuusSlateElement,
     FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost, the distiller and the compat seam all stay private.

THE PRIZE either way: once the lobby compiles in another module, the compiler answers 'is
the public surface enough to build a real UI' -- a question this project currently cannot
ask, because its flagship demo lives inside the module it is supposed to be exercising.

NOT A BLOCKER ANY MORE: the demo project builds and runs the plugin fine -- see the
corrected diagnosis on VaCuus-a1k (the trap was orphan .so copies in <Demo>/Binaries).

title: 2d6demo: owner decision — turn the six simulation-driven fades on, and pay 4-5pp of idle?
description:
Left by VaCuus-9ak.1, which restored the eighteen pointer-driven transitions (measured free: 3,624 published UI frames against the empty sheet's 3,636) and held these back:

  .meter-fill, .vgauge-fill, .vgauge-cap   the meters and the heat gauge
  .item-card, .item-card-pip               twenty turret cards, state and ammo
  .dial-badge                              seven power lights

THE TRADE, measured on the turrets HUD under demo2d6.Calm 1: all twenty-seven took the steady-state idle ratio from 94-95 % per window to 87-93 %. .dial-badge ALONE costs 19 % more published frames (4,331 against 3,636 over 130 s, same session, same command line). The others are the twenty turret cards whose state and ammo change while the guns fire: each change now buys 0.12-0.18 s of published frames where it used to buy one.

WHAT IS BEING TRADED: a UI that fades instead of snapping, against the headline idle figure docs/perf.md is built on and the demo's economics story is told with. Neither is wrong; it is a product decision.

PARTIAL ANSWERS EXIST and are cheaper than the whole: the heat gauge alone is one element (and is already quantised to its own pixel, so a fade on it is bounded); the turret cards are the expensive twenty. Turning on the gauges and leaving the cards snapping is a real middle.

Restoring any of them is one line each at the rule, with a literal duration -- the sites and the durations (fast 0.12s / mid 0.18s / slow 0.45s) are in the header of Demo2d6 Content/DevUI/2d6/components.rcss. Do NOT write var(--t-*): the demo's plugin drop (00497b7) predates the fix at 7fbc0b6 and a var() transition is silently inert there.

Можно было бы сделать, но демка сдана.

The measurement survives here for whoever picks it up. All twenty-seven cost 4-5 pp of steady-state idle; .dial-badge alone costs +19 % published frames.
