title: VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy fails on the real-RHI venue: its GMalloc canary reports a NEGATIVE byte delta
description:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING VaCuus-4ik, NOT CAUSED BY IT -- reproduced on the PRE-CHANGE build.

WHAT HAPPENS. Run the suite with a real RHI rather than -nullrhi:

  UnrealEditor-Cmd VcHost.uproject -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests VaCuus,Quit" \
    -unattended -nosplash -RenderOffscreen

and VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy fails on its own instrumentation canary, not on a
product assertion:

  Expected 'canary: CreateContext allocated through GMalloc (mallocs=6, bytes=-632)' to be true

The canary asserts that the malloc proxy OBSERVED allocation during CreateContext. It
sees a handful of mallocs and a NEGATIVE net byte delta -- i.e. the window it measures
is dominated by frees from other threads, so the sign test is meaningless there. The
byte figure varies run to run (-632, -5008, -88936 observed), which is the tell.

EVIDENCE IT IS PRE-EXISTING, four full-suite runs on 2026-08-06, same machine/session:
  pre-change,  real RHI, run 1 (208 tests): PASS
  pre-change,  real RHI, run 2 (208 tests): FAIL, bytes=-632
  pre-change,  real RHI, isolated 2-test run: FAIL, bytes=-88936
  with 4ik,    real RHI, run 1 (214 tests): FAIL, bytes=+1832
  with 4ik,    real RHI, run 2 (214 tests): FAIL, bytes=-5008
So it fails with and without the 4ik change, and passes sometimes with neither. Also
confirmed ORDER-INDEPENDENT of 4ik: MemProxy's events are at log line 7045 and the
first clip-mask line is 7081, i.e. the new tests run strictly AFTER it.

VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc is flaky on the same venue for the same family of
reason (allocation-count budget): failed once with 4ik ('min 11 <= 4'), passed in the
other three runs including one with 4ik.

NEITHER FAILS UNDER -nullrhi, which is the documented suite venue -- 214/214 green
there, and 208/208 before. So this is specifically a real-RHI-venue defect in the
tests, and it is the venue the GPU tests need, which is what makes it worth fixing:
today a real-RHI run cannot be read as pass/fail without knowing these two by name.

ASK: make the canary measure something that cannot go negative (e.g. assert on malloc
COUNT alone, or take the window on a quiesced render thread), or scope the proxy to the
calling thread. Same for ArrayAlloc's min-alloc budget.
close_reason:
Fixed at the root: the counting malloc proxy now counts only the threads a window NAMES.

REPRODUCED FIRST on the unmodified build, full suite, -RenderOffscreen Vulkan -- both this and VaCuus-z36 on the first run:
  VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy  'canary: RemoveContext freed through GMalloc (frees=11, bytes=+5264)'
  VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc  'a warm republish allocates ~nothing (min 11 <= 4)'

The canary window frees an RmlUi context and NOTHING else, so its byte delta is negative by construction. It read +5264 because the render thread, the RHI thread and the driver were allocating into the same ledger. Across runs of that same window the figure was -632, -5008, -88936 and +5264: a measurement of the machine.

THE FIX IS SCOPE, NOT A LOOSER BOUND. VaCuusAllocWindow::Begin() defaults to the calling thread; the RefHud boot and still windows pass the UI thread's id as well, because they enqueue and pump and the allocations they exist to measure happen there. By thread ID rather than a thread_local flag, precisely because a window has to be able to name a thread it does not run on.

WHAT IT MEASURES NOW:
  ArrayAlloc, both windows  min 0 max 0 over eight windows (was min 11)
  RefHud boot               +3.85 MiB, mallocs=251,599, size-lookup failures=0
  RefHud still, 60 frames    mallocs=410,571 frees=410,571, delta EXACTLY +0 bytes

A NEW HOLE CAME WITH IT AND IS CLOSED: 'min 0' is also what a DEAD counter produces. ArrayAlloc gained a guard window that allocates on purpose and asserts the counter saw it. It earned its place immediately -- asserted Mallocs > 0 and failed with 'mallocs=0, bytes=+4096', because TArray grows from empty through Realloc, not Malloc. The predicate is Total() now.

Restore-the-bug both directions: scoping broken -> four assertions fire naming mallocs=0 (the new guard, both canary halves, the boot window's 256 KiB gate); restored -> 215/215 on the real RHI and green under -nullrhi.

VaCuus 1dad8a5, merged d593544.

title: Offer the four vendored RmlUi patches upstream
description:
REVIEWED 2026-08-09 AND PARKED ON THE OWNER'S CALL: not being offered upstream yet. The
review's evidence is in this bead's comment; this is the standing summary.

VERDICT: all four are genuine UPSTREAM defects, not local adaptations. Each was confirmed
still present at mikke89/RmlUi master on 2026-08-09 by opening the file there -- not by
trusting the notes in Source/ThirdParty/RmlUi/VENDORED_TAG.txt, which is where each patch's
full mechanism, hunks and re-vendoring verification live.

  #1  DataViewStyle::Update compares Property::Get<String>() -- which drops the unit -- so a
      unit-bearing data-style binding never compares equal and re-sets on every dirty.
  #2  RMLUICORE_API on four HEADER-ONLY class templates. dllimport on a class template makes a
      consumer emit __imp_ references for specializations the library never instantiated.
  #3  SaveLayerAsTexture cannot report failure, so any backend leaving the optional layer
      capture unimplemented gets an opaque white rectangle AND per-frame resource churn.
  #4  TransitionPropertyChanges rejects a `transition` whose value contains var(), silently,
      because it tests the parsed variant type on a value that is stored unparsed.

SUBMISSION ORDER WHEN THE OWNER SAYS GO -- they are not equally ready:

  1. #4 as a PR. Strongest by far. The maintainer closed issue #951 -- the same class of bug --
     with "please do continue reporting anyone you come by", our vendored commit is AFTER that
     fix so this is a site it missed, and PR #974 shows the workstream still running. NEEDS: a
     rewritten regression test in Tests/Source/UnitTests/CustomProperties.cpp (ours is a VaCuus
     automation test and cannot go upstream), and the PR body must LEAD with why #974's
     one-line idiom cannot be used here -- see the comment.
  2. #2 as a PR. Four lines. NEEDS a minimal consumer repro; it is reproducible in upstream's
     OWN shared-Windows CI job, which is what makes it persuasive.
  3. #1 as an ISSUE first, with the measurement, letting the maintainer pick the fix shape.
  4. #3 as an ISSUE first. The defect is unambiguous; the fix is four hunks across three files
     and two of them are design calls that are the maintainer's to make.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS while parked: until these land upstream, every re-vendor reapplies them by
hand, and a patch silently lost re-introduces a defect nobody can see on screen. Each has a
named automation test that has been WATCHED to fail with the patch reverted -- those are the
reproductions a PR would want, and the guard in the meantime.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
REVIEW 2026-08-09, asked for before offering anything: are these actually upstream patches?

ANSWER: yes, all four -- every defect is LIVE AT UPSTREAM master today, checked by opening the
file at master rather than by trusting our notes. But they are not equally ready, and one of
them has an obvious reviewer objection that our note did not anticipate.

WHAT MASTER LOOKS LIKE RIGHT NOW (mikke89/RmlUi, fetched 2026-08-09):
  #1  Source/Core/DataViewDefault.cpp        `if (!p || p->Get<String>() != value)`   unchanged
  #2  Include/RmlUi/Core/ObserverPtr.h        `class RMLUICORE_API ObserverPtr` and the same on
                                              EnableObserverPtr -- unchanged. The non-template
                                              block API still carries the macro too, which is
                                              what makes our removal safe: the observer STATE
                                              stays single-instance.
  #3  Include/RmlUi/Core/CallbackTexture.h    `void SaveLayerAsTexture() const;` while sibling
                                              GenerateTexture returns bool -- unchanged.
  #4  Source/Core/ElementStyle.cpp            TransitionPropertyChanges still goes straight from
                                              GetLocalProperty to the TRANSITIONLIST test with
                                              no VAR_EXPRESSION handling -- unchanged.

ONE OF OUR NOTE'S CLAIMS WAS THE THING I MOST DOUBTED, AND IT HOLDS. Patch #3 changes a public
method's return type, which would break every overrider -- except CallbackTextureInterface is a
PLAIN CONCRETE CLASS with no virtuals and nothing derives from it (confirmed at master, not
inferred). So void -> bool breaks no backend; callers that ignore it still compile. The note
said "purely additive" and it is right.

PATCH #4 IS THE ONE TO OFFER FIRST, and the case is much stronger than "it is upstream-shaped":
  - Upstream issue #951 (closed 2026-07-11) is the SAME CLASS of bug -- var() in a property
    whose parsed variant type gets checked -- and the maintainer's own words closing it were
    "this turns out to be a class of edge cases that we need to handle... please do continue
    reporting anyone you come by." That is an open invitation for exactly this.
  - Our vendored commit 0ae381e (2026-07-29) is AFTER that fix, so our tree already carries it
    and TransitionPropertyChanges is a site the fix MISSED.
  - PR #974 ("Fix selection colors and progress fill-image that use var()") is merged and is
    the same workstream continuing, one site at a time.

BUT #974 ALSO CREATES THE OBJECTION OUR NOTE DOES NOT ANSWER. Its idiom is a ONE-LINE
substitution:
    - element->GetLocalProperty(PropertyId::X)
    + element->GetStyle()->GetLocalPropertyWithResolvedVariables(PropertyId::X)
and a reviewer will ask why our patch is twelve lines instead of that. THE ANSWER, and the PR
must lead with it: GetLocalPropertyWithResolvedVariables reads
`GetLocalProperty(id, inline_properties, definition.get())` -- the element's CURRENT definition
(ElementStyle.cpp:721-729). TransitionPropertyChanges runs BEFORE that definition is installed,
which is the entire reason it exists, and upstream's own comment says so at :227-230 ("we
cannot always use the definition or inline properties... Particularly in
TransitionPropertyChanges, these are not yet set for the current element"). So the one-liner
would resolve against the stale definition. Our shape is instead IDENTICAL to lines 69-74 of
the very same function, which already call ResolveVariablesWithShorthandExpansion with the same
argument shape for the transition's start and target values.

One simplification a maintainer may prefer, worth offering rather than defending: `transition`
is not a shorthand, so the substituted_shorthands optional is never populated and plain
ResolveVariables would do. Matching the neighbours is why we use the shorthand variant; either
is defensible.

PATCH #2's ACCEPTANCE CASE IS BETTER THAN OUR NOTE ASSUMED. Upstream CI DOES build Windows
with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON (.github/workflows/build.yml:184, :211, windows-latest), so they ship
an MSVC DLL and it passes -- because their samples only instantiate specializations the library
itself emits and exports. The defect needs a CONSUMER to instantiate a new one. That means a
minimal repro is reproducible in THEIR OWN existing CI job, which is the most persuasive form a
report of this kind can take, and it kills the "this is a Unreal-specific problem" reading
before it is made.

WHAT EACH OFFER STILL NEEDS:
  #4  a PR, with an upstream-shaped regression test. They have a unit-test suite and PR #947
      added Tests/Source/UnitTests/CustomProperties.cpp, which is the natural home. Our
      VaCuus.Core.Style.TransitionVariable cannot go upstream; the test has to be rewritten.
  #1  open as an ISSUE first, with the measurement (a coarse per-tick dirty publishing 100 of
      100 frames), and let the maintainer pick the fix shape. Our one-liner is a reasonable
      proposal but comparing Property values rather than round-tripped strings may be what they
      want, and the residues (colours, shorthands, "120.50px") should be stated up front.
  #2  a PR with a minimal consumer repro, ideally as a case in the existing shared-Windows CI
      job. Small diff, four lines.
  #3  an ISSUE first: the defect is unambiguous (white rectangle plus per-frame resource churn
      for ANY backend leaving the optional capture unimplemented) but the fix is four hunks
      across three files and hunks 3-4 are design calls the maintainer may want to make
      differently.

NOT SUBMITTED. The GitHub account is the owner's, and opening issues or PRs is outward-facing;
waiting for an explicit go-ahead and for a decision on order.

title: 2d6demo: confirm the fullscreen mouse loss interactively, with the two-line InputState readout
description:
VaCuus-3yl shipped the observable that can name the culprit and a gated focus
re-assert, but the owner's report itself is STILL not explained. This bead is the
one interactive run that settles it.

WHAT THE READOUT NOW PRINTS. demo2d6.InputState answers in two lines:

  INTACT  | viewport ... | capture=... lock=... | captor=... buttonsDown=N
  FOCUSED | appActive=... activeWindow=... (THE GAME WINDOW) | platformWindow=yes
            foreground=... minimized=... | slateViewport=ours reachable=true
            | focus: user0=SViewport(in the game viewport)

THE STEPS, on the machine where it reproduces (Win64 is worth a try too --
exclusive EWindowMode::Fullscreen is real there and Linux/Wayland downgrades it):

1. UnrealEditor /w/Unreal/Demo2d6/Demo2d6.uproject -game -windowed -resx=1280 -resy=720
2. Click a lobby tab. It works.
3. Alt+Enter into fullscreen, Alt+Enter back to windowed.
4. If clicks are dead, open the console (~) and type: demo2d6.InputState
5. Read BOTH lines out of Saved/Logs/Demo2d6.log.
6. Alt+Enter twice more, run demo2d6.InputState again, and diff the two readings.
   The field that changed is the mechanism.

HOW TO READ LINE 2:

- appActive=false        -> START HERE. It does not gate delivery, but
                            FSlateApplication::ProcessReply refuses to apply a
                            reply's mouse CAPTURE, cursor position and mouse lock
                            while it is false (SlateApplication.cpp:3490-3494),
                            and SVaCuusWidget::OnMouseButtonDown answers with
                            FReply::Handled().CaptureMouse(...). This is the only
                            field with a documented path to "stopped CATCHING the
                            mouse", which is the owner's own wording. An
                            unattended TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN run on Linux read
                            appActive=false after the transition and stayed there.
- foreground=false with appActive=true, or the reverse -> Slate and the platform
  disagree; the fault is in the activation bookkeeping between them.
- activeWindow ... (NOT the game window) -> something else holds activation.
- slateViewport=NOT OURS -> the window was recreated and RegisterGameViewport did
  not follow. Nothing in the demo can repair that.
- NO FOCUS with everything else healthy -> the one case the resize hook already
  repairs, and the line above it in the log will say it did.

WHAT IS ALREADY RULED OUT, so do not spend the run on it:

- The input mode. INTACT through both directions of r.SetRes and TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN;
  the four flags live on UGameViewportClient, which outlives the transition.
- Capture. captor=nobody in the owner's reproduction, and SVaCuusWidget resets
  both halves of its capture state on OnMouseCaptureLost.
- The snapshot. The view resized both ways and the stage rescaled with it.
- Focus loss ALONE. With every user's focus cleared (demo2d6.DropFocus), a
  synthesized click still reaches the UI -- Slate routes pointer events by hit
  test, not by focus. So a NO FOCUS reading is a symptom to report, not the cure.
- A programmatic mode change. r.SetRes ...f/...w and TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN both keep
  focus on every leg. That difference is itself a finding: it points at the
  platform layer rather than the engine's resize path.

Full field-by-field table and both staged command lines are in README.md,
"When the game stops catching the mouse".
close_reason:
Можно было бы сделать, но демка сдана.

THE FIX ITSELF SHIPPED — this bead was only ever the interactive re-confirmation. Demo2d6 a45a0b7 re-asserts the HUD's FInputModeGameAndUI when the viewport changes shape, and it is covered two ways already: Demo2d6.Input.FocusGate asserts the re-assert fires only on real focus loss and REFUSES to fire when SetAllUserFocusToGameViewport would clear everyone's focus instead (remove that guard and two assertions fail), and a headless -game run walks INTACT -> DRIFTED -> resize -> INTACT with demo2d6.InputState printing both lines.

What is missing is one human at a real fullscreen window reproducing the owner's original report. That needs a desktop session and could not be automated; the demo went out without it.

Same shape as VaCuus-akj.10.10 and akj.6.19 on the plugin side — all three want an interactive pass, none is blocked by anything code can fix.

title: 2d6demo: the original 'lost the mouse after fullscreen' report is still unreproduced -- interactive check
description:
VaCuus-sya shipped the observable and a defensive re-assert, but did NOT reproduce the
owner's actual report ('вышел из полноэкранного режима -- и хоп, перестало ловить мышку,
пока не передернешь alt+Enter туда-сюда').

MEASURED AND RULED OUT, on Linux/XWayland 2026-08-06:
- A real fullscreen round-trip driven by TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN (the command Alt+Enter itself
  runs) -- 1280x720 windowed -> 2560x1440 windowed-fullscreen -> back. demo2d6.InputState
  read INTACT at every point, both directions. The four flags FInputModeGameAndUI writes
  live on the UGameViewportClient (PlayerController.cpp:6409-6412) and that object
  outlives the transition, so a mode change alone cannot lose them.
- A synthesized window deactivate/activate cycle (demo2d6.Reactivate). Also INTACT. The
  AcquireFocusAndCapture grab at SceneViewport.cpp:1509-1511 did not fire; the
  bShouldCaptureMouseOnActivate latch was already clear.
- The plugin is clear for this case: SVaCuusWidget overrides OnMouseCaptureLost and
  resets both halves of its capture state unconditionally (SVaCuusWidget.cpp:725-741),
  every engine path that drops capture funnels through FSlateUser::ReleaseCapture which
  always notifies (SlateUser.cpp:314), and VaCuusSlateRoutingTest.cpp:550-560 asserts it.

WHAT IS LEFT. The trigger is a REAL Alt+Enter with a real modifier held and a real window
manager, and two things differ from what was tested: exclusive EWindowMode::Fullscreen
(Linux/Wayland downgrades to WindowedFullscreen, Win64 does not), and the Alt key itself,
which many window managers grab. Worth re-running on the Win64 machine.

HOW TO SETTLE IT IN ONE MINUTE, interactively:
  1. Run windowed: UnrealEditor Demo2d6.uproject -game -windowed -resx=1280 -resy=720
  2. Click a lobby tab. It works.
  3. Alt+Enter to fullscreen, Alt+Enter back to windowed.
  4. Try to click. If it is dead, open the console (~) and type: demo2d6.InputState
  5. Read the one line in Saved/Logs/Demo2d6.log. DRIFTED names which field went, and
     `captor=SViewport (THE GAME VIEWPORT)` means something took capture rather than the
     mode changing -- those are different bugs with different fixes.
  6. Alt+Enter twice more; run demo2d6.InputState again. If the toggle repairs it, the
     repair is the resize hook that VaCuus-sya added, and the line above it in the log
     will say so.

That readout is the whole point of the observable. Without step 4 there is nothing to go on.
notes:
OWNER REPRODUCED IT, 2026-08-06, and the result eliminates both original suspects.

demo2d6.InputState while broken:
  INTACT | viewport 1920x1080 windowed | capture=CaptureDuringMouseDown lock=DoNotLock ignoreInput=false hideCursorDuringCapture=false bShowMouseCursor=true | captor=nobody buttonsDown=0

So the input mode did NOT drift and nothing holds capture. The log timeline around it:
  10.07.25:761  View 1 size now 2560x1440            (into fullscreen)
  10.07.25:782  stage 2560x1440 -> scale 1.3333
  10.07.26:062  LogVulkanRHI: AcquireNextImage() failed due to the outdated swapchain, not even attempting to present.
  10.07.27:286  View 1 size now 1920x1080            (back to windowed)
  10.07.27:291  stage 1920x1080 -> scale 1.0000
  10.07.41:688  demo2d6.InputState: INTACT ...

The view resized correctly BOTH ways and the stage rescaled, so the interactive-region snapshot's coordinates are current — that suspect is out too. And there are FOURTEEN SECONDS of silence between the resize back and the command, with no pointer activity logged at all: if Slate had delivered a single click, SVaCuusWidget::OnMouseButtonDown would have taken capture and it would show.

CONCLUSION: Slate is not delivering pointer events to the game viewport at all. That is the window/focus layer, not the input mode, not capture, not the snapshot. The outdated-swapchain line shows the window was recreated on the transition; the standard remedy for this symptom class is re-asserting focus to the game viewport (FSlateApplication::SetAllUserFocusToGameViewport) after the viewport changes, which nothing currently does.

NEXT: extend demo2d6.InputState to print the focus and window state — active top-level window, whether the game viewport widget holds user focus, platform window activation — so the next occurrence names the cause instead of ruling things out. Then apply the re-focus on ViewportResizedEvent alongside the existing input-mode re-apply.
CLOSED 2026-08-06 with the diagnostic finished and the remedy gated. Demo2d6 commit 199ce8f.

WHAT SHIPPED.
demo2d6.InputState now prints a SECOND line, the window/focus layer, because the owner's reproduction printed a perfect INPUT line while the demo was deaf:
  FOCUSED | appActive=... activeWindow=... (THE GAME WINDOW) | platformWindow=yes foreground=... minimized=... | slateViewport=ours reachable=true | focus: user0=SViewport(in the game viewport)
Slate's activation flag AND the platform's own foreground answer (two sources of truth, so a disagreement localises the fault), the active top-level window and whether it is ours, whether Slate's REGISTERED game viewport is still our widget, whether any widget path reaches it, and per-user focus with the focused widget's type. Descendant focus counts as focused -- SVaCuusWidget is a child of SViewport, so a focused text field is not focus loss.

FSlateApplication::SetAllUserFocusToGameViewport now runs from HandleViewportResized, gated on that readback, never unconditionally. It REFUSES when the call would misfire: SetAllUserFocusToGameViewport ignores its own path lookup failing and an invalid path CLEARS focus for every user (SlateApplication.cpp:2655-2666 -> :3184-3188 -> :3017). New test Demo2d6.Input.FocusGate asserts the refusal; removing the guard fails two assertions. 12/12 Demo2d6.* green.

MEASURED, Linux/XWayland:
- A programmatic mode change does NOT lose focus. r.SetRes ...f/...w and a real TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN round-trip read FOCUSED and INTACT on every leg. That difference is the finding: whatever Alt+Enter does on the owner's machine, a programmatic toggle does not do it -- which points at the platform layer.
- Focus loss ALONE does not produce the symptom. With every user's focus cleared, a synthesized click still reaches the UI ('taken by THE UI'); Slate routes pointer events by hit test, not focus.
- Restore-the-bug: DropFocus -> resize -> FOCUSED with the call, NO FOCUS with it removed. Both outcomes observed.

THE REMAINING LEAD IS appActive. It does not gate delivery, but FSlateApplication::ProcessReply refuses to apply a reply's mouse CAPTURE, cursor position and mouse lock while bAppIsActive is false (SlateApplication.cpp:3387, :3490-3494), and SVaCuusWidget::OnMouseButtonDown answers with FReply::Handled().CaptureMouse(...). An unattended TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN run read appActive=false after the transition and stayed false. 'Stopped CATCHING the mouse' is what a dropped capture looks like. Not proven -- the next occurrence's second line settles it.

NOT A PLUGIN BUG. The evidence says the GAME VIEWPORT is not being handed pointer events, not that SVaCuusWidget mishandles them, and the widget's own capture bookkeeping self-heals on the next button-up (SVaCuusWidget.cpp:650-657 clears MouseCapture whether or not Slate ever granted it). No bead filed against VaCuus.

title: opacity does not composite as a group — a child setting its own opacity escapes its ancestor's
description:
In CSS, opacity establishes a group: a child with opacity:1 inside a parent at opacity:0.5 renders at 0.5. In RmlUi it does not — opacity is an inherited property multiplied per element, so a child that sets its own opacity OVERRIDES the inherited value and renders at its own.

Found in the 2d6 demo (VaCuus-keq): .mx-icon and .hud-ship-view each set opacity, and photographed as 18 lit hardpoint glyphs floating over a plate whose own opacity was 0. The fix there was image-color, which ElementImage multiplies BY the inherited opacity rather than replacing it.

Worth a line in docs/buyer/gotchas.md: it is a silent visual divergence from CSS that a web author will not expect, it looks like a z-order or a decorator bug rather than an opacity one, and the workaround differs by element type.
close_reason:
Documented as gotchas.md #8b, mechanism VERIFIED IN THE VENDORED SOURCE rather than taken from the report -- and the report was right on every point.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS, four links: (1) opacity is registered inherited=true (StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:351); (2) ComputeValues copies the parent's inherited block WHOLESALE -- ComputedValues.h:394 is literally 'inherited = parent.inherited' -- which is copy, not compose; (3) a local declaration then OVERWRITES it at ElementStyle.cpp:1247, values.opacity(p->Get<float>()), with no multiplication anywhere; (4) each element multiplies its own colours by computed.opacity() at paint time -- ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp:166-173, ElementText.cpp:371-374, DecoratorGradient.cpp:140/:265/:434/:631, DecoratorShader.cpp:42. So a child at opacity 1 inside a parent at 0.5 renders at 1, with no group buffer anywhere in the library.

The workaround set is per element type and each line is cited: image-color is multiplied BY the inherited opacity rather than replacing it (ElementImage.cpp:178, ElementProgress.cpp:222, DecoratorTiled.cpp:80, DecoratorNinePatch.cpp:40 -- all image_color().ToPremultiplied(computed.opacity())), and so is a colour's own alpha byte, because ToPremultiplied computes alpha * opacity (Include/RmlUi/Core/Colour.h:89-98). That last one was checked rather than assumed and is what makes 'fade with the alpha of color/background-color' correct advice for text and solid fills.

Docs only, no code change. Commit 7fbc0b6.

title: 2d6demo: 27 component transitions are inert (var() in a transition), and turning them on costs 4-5pp of calm idle
description:
Found while fixing VaCuus-keq. Every 'transition:' in Content/DevUI/2d6/components.rcss was written 'transition: <prop> var(--t-fast|mid|slow) cubic-out'. A var() anywhere in a transition declaration is fatal with NO diagnostic: PropertySpecification.cpp:264-267 stores the declaration whole as an unparsed VAR_EXPRESSION string, and ElementStyle::TransitionPropertyChanges reads the LOCAL transition property before computed values exist and returns unless it is already a TRANSITIONLIST (ElementStyle.cpp:388-393). So every hover tint, card state fade and meter tween in this UI has snapped since it was written. animation: var(...) has the identical hole.

VaCuus-keq fixed the two the owner noticed (.dial-seg, .dial-needle) with literal durations, and DELETED the other 27 rather than leave dead code in the sheet. Deleting them changed nothing on screen.

Writing them out as literals was tried and MEASURED first, on the turrets HUD under demo2d6.Calm 1, 120s: steady-state idle windows fell from 94-95% to 87-93%, a 4-5pp regression against the figure docs/perf.md is built on. With only the two dial transitions live the same run measures 94.0-95.7%, dead on baseline. The cost is the SIMULATION-DRIVEN ones (twenty turret cards whose state and ammo change while the guns fire); the pure :hover ones cost nothing at idle because a headless run never hovers.

The work: split the 27 by what drives them, restore the hover-only ones with literal durations (free), and take an owner decision on the sim-driven ones. Restore points are in git at the commit before VaCuus-keq's.
close_reason:
The twenty-seven are split and eighteen are back, with literal durations. Demo2d6 Content/DevUI/2d6/components.rcss.

THE SPLIT, and one of it was wrong until it was measured:
- EIGHTEEN RESTORED, all pointer- or click-driven: .cat-page-btn + label, .ctxmenu-item, .sec-tab, .sec-tab-underline, .num-tab-label, .segtoggle-half + label, .statusbar-btn + label, .statusbar-collapse, .rail-btn, .returnbar + label, .slider-knob, .slot, .mx-key, .crew-row. Plus three ADDITIONS flagged as such (.actmenu-row and the two menu labels -- Task 17's component never had one, and a box that fades under a caption that snaps is a seam).
- THREE GONE FOR GOOD, because the property they watched cannot change in this project: .num-tab's own colour (every colour rule targets the label inside it), .pip (filled comes from Section.Tier, set to 4 once at Demo2d6Sim.cpp:241), .mx-icon (the hardpoint matrices carry fixed comp counts).
- SIX HELD BACK for the owner: .meter-fill, .vgauge-fill, .vgauge-cap, .item-card, .item-card-pip and .dial-badge.

.dial-badge IS THE ONE WORTH KNOWING ABOUT. It has a :hover rule, so it classified as a hover fade. Its lit state actually follows Section.bPowered, which is DERIVED from integrity with hysteresis (lost below 55, back at 75, Demo2d6Sim.cpp:159-215), so the damage wave toggles it on seven dials forever. Three same-session 130 s runs, same command line, at the 26th window:

  nothing restored      3,636 published   93.4 % idle
  eighteen restored     3,624 published   93.0 % idle    <- -0.3 %, i.e. nothing
  eighteen + dial-badge 4,331 published   92.1 % idle    <- +19 %

RESTORE-THE-BUG PROOF that the literals actually run on this drop (00497b7, which predates the plugin's var()-in-transition fix 7fbc0b6): section screen, demo2d6.Calm 1, ten demo2d6.Select two seconds apart. WITHOUT it the identical run publishes 13 in total, two per selection. 38x, and both halves observed.

Also corrected: tokens.rcss said 'animation has the identical hole'. It does not -- animations resolve variables through ComputedValues::animation() (ComputedValues.cpp:8-16), which VaCuus-6gj measured with the fix reverted. title: 2d6demo: a root transform is silently dropped by a preact re-render of the element carrying it
description:
Found while fixing VaCuus-n3s and no longer reachable in that project, but it is a trap for anyone who does put a transform on a preact-owned element.

OBSERVED, old 2d6 build at 2560x1440, reproducible: on the section and turrets screens the fit-to-view transform was not applied at all - the tab bar's card edges sit at 9/270/281/542..., i.e. the 1080p coordinates, in a 2560-wide view - while the lobby and the three catalogue benches were correctly magnified. The JS log shows applyScale DID write it: 'stage: view 2560x1440 -> scale(1.3333)' at frame 1. On the two broken screens the router changed screen in that same frame, re-rendering the tree under #stage.

So the inline transform written by JS onto #stage did not survive the re-render, while the data-scale ATTRIBUTE applyScale used as its change gate did - the gate then suppressed every rewrite and the document stayed at 1920x1080 in the corner of the view forever. Exact mechanism not chased (preact diffProps should not touch a style prop neither vnode carries, so an RmlUi definition-dirty path is the other candidate).

Worth pinning because the shape is general: a JS-written inline property on a component-owned element, gated on something that outlives it, fails silently and permanently. The 2d6 demo no longer has one - the scale is a property of the ElementDocument, which preact never renders into, and the gate is a module-scope variable - so this is a plugin docs/guide item rather than a demo bug.
close_reason:
Written up as a plugin gotcha, which is what this bead asked for -- the 2d6 demo no longer has a reachable instance (the scale is a font-size on the ElementDocument, which preact never renders into, and the gate is a module-scope variable: main.tsx applyScale).

VaCuus docs/buyer/gotchas.md, entry 11b, in the 'Data binding and JS' section: 'A style your JS wrote inline disappears when the component framework re-renders that element -- and a change gate that outlives the element makes it permanent.'

It states the OBSERVATION and refuses to assert a mechanism, because none was ever chased: the JS log shows the transform was written, the measured card edges are the 1920-space ones in a 2560-wide view, and the data-scale attribute survived while the inline style did not. preact's diffProps should not touch a style prop neither vnode carries, so an RmlUi definition-dirty path is the other candidate, and the entry says so.

The 'Do' half is two rules, and the second is the load-bearing one: (a) put JS-owned properties on an element the component tree never renders into -- document.style is reachable from JS and no framework owns it, which is what the demo does now; (b) never gate a write on state whose lifetime differs from the thing it gates. The symptom is silence, which is why it costs a session rather than a minute.

title: the view render target is single-sampled, so border-radius arcs and transformed edges alias
description:
Split out of VaCuus-sw1, which fixed gradient-fill aliasing analytically in the
shader and deliberately left this alone.

WHAT ALIASES. The per-view render target is created single-sampled: NumSamples is
never set in VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp and FRHITextureCreateDesc defaults it to 1
(RHIResources.h:1896). Rml's layout boxes are axis-aligned so their edges do not
alias, and glyphs come out of an already-antialiased font atlas -- but two things
do:

  - border-radius arcs, tessellated as a polygon fan with a radius-dependent point
    count (GeometryBackgroundBorder.cpp:139, GetNumPoints(R)). Visible on the 2d6
    demo's 64px dial rings; photographed in
    docs/research/proofs/sw1-gradient-aa/cmp_dial.png, where the circle outline is
    a staircase in BOTH the before and after shots while the conic segment
    boundaries inside it are fixed.
  - anything under a non-axis-aligned `transform:` (the demo's rotating minimap
    sweep, for one).

WHY sw1 DID NOT BUILD MSAA. Three costs, none fatal, all real:

  1. MEMORY. The RT is PF_B8G8R8A8 at view size: 7.91 MiB at 1080p. 4x MSAA is
     31.6 MiB -- and it does not replace the existing RT, it adds to it, because
     every consumer samples the RT as an ordinary SRV and cannot sample a
     multisampled one: the Slate composite (VaCuusSlateElement.cpp:200,
     RegisterExternalTexture), the world sink's copy (VaCuusWorldSink.cpp:66) and
     the layer-capture path. So it is ~39.5 MiB per view against 7.91 today, a 5x
     increase, permanent, per view.
  2. A RESOLVE PASS per published frame, plus rewiring all three consumers to the
     resolved texture. Cheap in the steady state -- the idle gate publishes about
     1 frame in 13,000 on a static HUD -- but it is new plumbing on the hottest
     path in the plugin.
  3. GAMMA. The RT holds display-encoded PREMULTIPLIED pixels (the M1 contract).
     An MSAA resolve averages those encoded values, which is not the average of
     the linear colours, so every resolved edge is slightly off. Standard MSAA
     wart, but it is a NEW correctness caveat on a contract the composite
     permutation work (M6 spec 3.2) was careful about.

  The PSO risk is NOT one of the costs: every draw path here builds its PSO from
  ApplyCachedRenderTargets (VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:416, VaCuusMaterialDraw.cpp:243),
  which picks the sample count up from the bound RT, so the material tier would
  follow along without shader changes.

WHAT TO WEIGH IT AGAINST. MSAA is one candidate, not the obvious one. Supersampling
the whole view (render the context at 2x and downsample) costs the same order of
memory, needs no resolve plumbing, and antialiases every draw including transformed
elements -- but it changes what a recorded pixel coordinate means and would need its
own look at text. Feathering the tessellated outline in the shader is the cheapest
and touches the vendored library. Decide between the three before building any of
them.

RECOMMENDATION from sw1: worth doing, not worth doing as MSAA-by-default. The
visible symptom is small (circle outlines on small dials), the memory cost is not,
and the plugin's whole performance story is about NOT paying for frames nobody sees.
If it ships it should ship as an opt-in quality knob with a measured cost, the way
vacuus.AsyncTextureUploadBytes shipped with its own measurement.
close_reason:
Shipped as vacuus.ViewSampleCount (1 default / 2 / 4 / 8): MSAA on the per-view RT,
resolved by the replay pass's own store action into the SAME single-sampled OutputRT.

THE CHOICE, AND IT IS A REVERSAL of the brief's preferred candidate. Supersampling was
weighed first and rejected on three findings, all checked rather than assumed:

 1. RmlUi has no context-wide scale, so resizing the context to N x lays the document out
    at 1/N of its authored size -- SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio only moves dp/em and
    every sheet here is px (the lobby demo's hybrid floor already records this,
    VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp:633-635). A layout supersample is document-side, not a knob.
 2. Rasterizing at N x with the layout left alone MAGNIFIES THE FONT ATLAS: at N=2 the
    bilinear magnify composed with the 2:1 downsample is a [0.125, 0.75, 0.125] kernel on
    text that is crisp today. Text is the one thing here that is already antialiased, so a
    supersample cannot improve it and provably softens it.
 3. It would break world panels outright -- FVaCuusWorldSink::CopyToDestination skips on
    any extent mismatch (VaCuusWorldSink.cpp:71-78), so an N x RT means a panel that never
    updates again.

Two of the bead's three MSAA costs were also wrong. The "resolve pass plus rewiring all
three consumers" is not real: ERenderTargetActions::Clear_Resolve is a STORE ACTION on the
pass we already have and it lands in OutputRT, so NO consumer changes and world panels get
the knob for free. The gamma caveat is real but is not MSAA's -- any downsample of this
target has it, supersampling included -- and for the coverage case this bead is about it is
EXACT, because a premultiplied edge stores coverage*encode(C) and the average of those is
the right premultiplied value for the averaged coverage. Memory is the one cost that stood:
+15.82 / +31.64 / +63.28 MiB per view at 1080p, on top of the 7.91 that has to stay.

MEASURED (Vulkan / RTX 3090 / Linux, 2026-08-06; docs/research/proofs/3tg-view-msaa):
  border-radius disc outline: 0 -> 432 blended pixels; rotated quads: 0 -> 819.
  Controls at exactly 0 changed bytes: axis-aligned boxes, TEXT, gradient fill.
  Suite observable, production replay path: "partially covered pixels 0 at 1x, 200 at 4x".
  Restore-the-bug: bResolve forced false -> 0 at 4x, test fails on the AA claim; restored.
  Hit-testing at 4x: 13 log lines (rects, 4 hit tests, 2 real Slate clicks) IDENTICAL to
  1x but for the snapshot generation counter -- a click on a button is taken by THE UI, a
  click on empty space still reaches THE GAME.
  Cost at 1/2/4/8: Record 0.429/0.433/0.439/0.435, Replay 0.411/0.408/0.420/0.546 ms,
  fps 226.8/226.1/224.5/223.0, publish ratio 100% throughout. 8x is the row that moves.

Suite 204 -> 207 green. Cost table and the knob in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md.

title: perf-guide: a continuously-varying float bumped into a revision defeats the idle gate
description:
Found building the 2d6 demo (Task 17). A UI that looks idle can publish 100% of frames because ONE continuously-varying float is wired to a change counter.

Concretely: ship heat cooled proportionally, so it changed every simulation step, so its revision bumped every step, so the gated reader re-read its domain every frame and re-rendered ~250 elements to move a 155px bar by a hundredth of a pixel. Measured 2.9% withheld. Quantising the value to the GAUGE'S OWN PIXEL before it reaches the change counter took it to 93.9% withheld and dropped JsPump from 6.386ms to 0.584ms — with no visible difference at all.

This generalises past the demo and belongs in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md next to the existing 'write properties conditionally' advice, which is necessary but not sufficient: the write here WAS conditional, and the condition was true every frame. The rule is stronger — quantise a continuous value to the resolution at which it is DISPLAYED before you let it dirty anything. A bar 155px tall needs 1/155 resolution, not float resolution.

Worth pairing with the existing binding-cost row (0.53us per re-evaluated binding), since the cost scales with bindings x rows in the dirty scope rather than with what changed.
close_reason:
Documented in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md as 'The quantisation law', placed immediately after the unit-bearing data-style block whose closing advice is the conditional write -- and it says outright that the conditional write is necessary and NOT sufficient, with this case as the proof: the write WAS conditional and the condition was true on every frame, because the value cooled proportionally.

Carries the measured numbers: 2.9% of frames withheld on a UI that looked idle (97 published of every 100), ~250 elements re-rendered to move a 155px bar by a hundredth of a pixel; quantising to the gauge's own pixel (1/155) before the change counter -> 93.9% withheld and JsPump 6.386 ms -> 0.584 ms, no visible difference. Includes the three-line JS idiom, the rule for picking the quantum from the DISPLAY rather than the datum (155px bar -> 1/155, percentage label -> 1/100, on/off icon -> 1 bit), and the instruction to round at the boundary where the value enters the UI, not inside the simulation.

Paired with the existing binding law as asked: the entry states the cost of getting it wrong as bindings x rows in the dirty scope at ~0.53 us each plus a whole render and publish of an identical frame, and points at vacuus.M1HUD.PerfLog 1 as the way to find one.

Docs only, no code change. Commit 7fbc0b6.

title: 2d6demo: T14 Revision-gated model access in TSX
description: See docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-04-2d6-demo.md
close_reason: Revision-gated reader done and MEASURED, not asserted (commit db5d475): 8 leaf reads/frame gated at idle vs 254 ungated, and the ungated cost GROWS with data (278 then 308 after two waves) while the gated cost does not — 14x to 28x. A wave re-reads contacts and nothing else (25 reads = 1 size + 6x4), and the next window reads contacts 0 times. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL HOLE the gate exposed: nothing after ResetState ever wrote SlotsRevision, so it never moved for a whole run — a gated reader would have read the slots exactly once, from the default shadow before the first push landed, and sat on an empty grid forever with no error anywhere. ResetState now leaves every revision at 1, with 0 reserved for the default-constructed struct BindModel builds the shadow from; restore-the-bug proven on the two new assertions. Reader carries typed domain readers so the enum-as-name-string handling lives in one file instead of being re-derived by each screen; the two collapsing maps are typed against the components' own unions so a rename stops compiling. pump() re-arms rAF FIRST — rAF has swap-out semantics, so a tail re-arm would let one throw in a subscriber freeze the UI permanently. Seven revisions, not six: UiRevision exists.

title: vacuus dev ignores --devui-dir, so watch mode cannot serve a consumer project
description: Web/packages/cli/lib/build.mjs:110-118 — runDev(appDir) hardcodes DEVUI_ROOT (the PLUGIN's Content/DevUI) while runBuild(appDir, {devuiRoot}) already takes the option. bin/vacuus.mjs:43-49 reads --devui-dir for build and not for dev. A consumer project running 'vacuus dev --devui-dir <project>' gets its bundle written into the plugin instead, silently. Live reload itself is fine: VaCuusLiveReload.cpp:220 registers a watcher on every root GetDocumentRoots() returns, project root included. Fix is the same two lines runBuild already has. Found while building the 2d6 demo.
close_reason: Fixed. runDev(appDir, {devuiRoot = DEVUI_ROOT} = {}) now takes the same options parameter runBuild already had and joins outfile against it; bin/vacuus.mjs's 'dev' case reads --devui-dir and passes it through, matching 'build'. Also corrected the usage line and the header comment, which listed --devui-dir for neither. Verified VaCuusLiveReload.cpp:220 by opening it: the watcher loop is 'for (const FString& Root : VaCuusContentPaths::GetDocumentRoots())', so every root including the project's is watched — writing the bundle to the project root is all that was missing. node Web/smoke.mjs: SMOKE GREEN (13 PASS).

title: no public C++ font-loading API; @font-face is a consumer's only route and is unexercised
description: Rml::LoadFontFace is called only from Source/VaCuus/Private/VaCuusEngine.cpp:138-153 (LatoLatin) and VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp. Nothing in Source/VaCuus/Public or Source/VaCuusRender/Public exposes font loading, so a consumer project shipping its own faces has exactly one route: @font-face in RCSS. That path IS implemented — StyleSheetParser.cpp:855 dispatches to ParseFontFaceBlock (:525-564), required font-family + src, optional font-weight/font-style/-rmlui-fallback-face/-rmlui-face-index, src comma-expanded as BARE PATHS with no url() — but it is used nowhere in the repo and is not in docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md's at-rule list (the list is a hardcoded string at Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:222). Also unclear and untested: whether src resolves document-relative or root-relative, since it does NOT go through JoinPath the way <link> and <script src> do. The 2d6 demo's Task 1 establishes the answer; either way the docs need the at-rule added and the resolution rule stated.
notes:
@font-face proof, 2026-08-04: WORKS. A consumer project CAN ship its own faces via @font-face in RCSS; no plugin change needed. src resolves ROOT-RELATIVE (against VaCuusContentPaths::GetDocumentRoots(), plugin Content/DevUI first, then <Project>/Content/DevUI) — NOT document-relative.

Method: temporary edits in the VcHost clone (reverted; git status clean at 9895a51), no compile needed.
  Run A  m2_demo.rcss @font-face ProofA src 'M2Fonts/Michroma-Regular.ttf' applied to #m2-title -> rendered Michroma. Log: "[Rml] Loaded font face 'ProofA' [regular] from 'M2Fonts/Michroma-Regular.ttf'." Screenshot /w/Unreal/VcHost/Saved/Screenshots/LinuxEditor/ScreenShot00003.png
  Run B  same with ProofB src 'fonts/Michroma-Regular.ttf' -> rendered Michroma, letterforms identical to A. Log: "Loaded font face 'ProofB' [regular] from 'fonts/Michroma-Regular.ttf'." Screenshot ScreenShot00004.png

CAVEAT ON THE A/B PAIR: m2_demo.rcss sits AT the DevUI root, so 'M2Fonts/x' and 'fonts/x' denote the same file under BOTH a root-relative and a document-relative rule. A and B prove @font-face works but CANNOT discriminate the two rules.

DISCRIMINATOR (run C, added): RefHud/refhud.rcss lives in a subdirectory; font placed ONLY at RefHud/Michroma-Regular.ttf.
  ProofC src 'Michroma-Regular.ttf' (document-relative spelling) -> FAILED: "Warning: Failed to open file 'Michroma-Regular.ttf' (resolved to '/w/Unreal/VcHost/Plugins/VaCuus/Content/DevUI/Michroma-Regular.ttf')" + "Error: [Rml] Failed to load font face from Michroma-Regular.ttf, could not open file."
  ProofD src 'RefHud/Michroma-Regular.ttf' (root-relative spelling) -> LOADED.
  => bare src resolves against the DevUI ROOT, not the stylesheet's directory. Conclusive.

Source corroboration: StyleSheetParser.cpp:561 passes src VERBATIM to Rml::LoadFontFace (no JoinPath); FontProvider.cpp:93-94 calls GetFileInterface()->Open(file_name); VaCuusFileInterface.cpp:178 -> VaCuusContentPaths.cpp:92-103 joins Root / VfsPath over GetDocumentRoots(). The requesting document's directory is never consulted — root-relative by construction.

Consequence: docs/buyer/rcss-matrix.md must add @font-face to the at-rule list (hardcoded at Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:222) AND state 'src is resolved root-relative against the DevUI document roots; it is NOT document-relative, unlike <link>/<script src> which go through JoinPath'. 2d6 Task 4 must spell every src from the DevUI root (e.g. '2d6/fonts/Orbitron-Bold.ttf').

Evidence: /tmp/fontproof_evidence.txt, /tmp/fontproof_c_vchost.log, /tmp/fontproof_a.log, /tmp/fontproof_b.log, /tmp/fontproof_c.log, ScreenShot00003.png, ScreenShot00004.png
close_reason: Documented, which was the actionable half (no C++ change needed -- @font-face IS the route and it works). docs/buyer/gotchas.md #5 rewritten: names that there is NO public C++ font-loading API (Rml::LoadFontFace call sites are Private only -- VaCuusEngine.cpp:144 and VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp:302, verified by grep over Source/VaCuus{,Render,Editor}), gives a full worked @font-face block, and states the ROOT-relative src rule with the chain I opened: StyleSheetParser.cpp:561 passes src verbatim with no JoinPath -> FontProvider.cpp:94 hands it to file_interface->Open -> VaCuusContentPaths.cpp:92-103 joins Root / VfsPath over GetDocumentRoots(). Contrasts it explicitly with <link>/<script src>, which ARE document-relative (SystemInterface.cpp:52-83), and adds the reciprocal pointer in gotchas #12. Grammar from :294-330 and :525-564: required font-family + src, src comma-expanded BARE paths with no url(), optional font-weight/font-style/-rmlui-fallback-face/-rmlui-face-index. Variable-font limitation (FT_New_Face with no variation axis -> default weight for every requested weight; ship static instances) recorded in both gotchas #5 and the matrix. vacuus-base.rcss's font line said 'register one with RmlUi', which a buyer cannot do; corrected to point at @font-face and its root-relative src.

title: vacuus create template doubles the directory in <script src>, so the scaffolded app never loads its bundle
description: Web/packages/cli/template/app.rml.tpl:8 emits src="__APP_DIR__/__APP_NAME___bundle.js" and create.mjs:20 fills __APP_DIR__ with the app name. The document lands at Content/DevUI/<name>/<name>.rml and <script src> is DOCUMENT-RELATIVE (JoinPath strips the filename and appends, SystemInterface.cpp:72-83), so it resolves to <name>/<name>/<name>_bundle.js. Result: one 'did not resolve to a readable file' Error and a HUD with styling and no behaviour. M5Hud/m5_hud.rml and RefHud/refhud.rml both carry explicit comments warning about exactly this. Fix is one line: src="__APP_NAME___bundle.js". smoke.mjs does not catch it because nothing in the node-side roundtrip loads the document. Found while building the 2d6 demo.
close_reason: Fixed. template/app.rml.tpl now emits the BARE bundle name (src is document-relative: SystemInterface::JoinPath, SystemInterface.cpp:72-83, strips this document's filename and appends), with a comment citing the same trap m5_hud.rml:13-18 and refhud.rml:13-16 already warn about. __APP_DIR__ stays in create.mjs's fill() because package.json.tpl's outDir and README.md.tpl still need it. Added a smoke.mjs assertion over the generated .rml — the node-side roundtrip's only observable for this, since nothing there loads the document. RESTORE-THE-BUG: reverted the template to '__APP_DIR__/...' -> 'FAIL create: <script src> is the bare bundle name — ["smoketest/smoketest_bundle.js"]', SMOKE RED 1 failure; restored -> PASS, SMOKE GREEN.

title: docs assert transition easing 'ease-in-out' works; it drops the whole declaration
description: Content/DevUI/M5Hud/vacuus-base.rcss:13-14 and docs/buyer/gotchas.md:23-27 both state that 'transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out;' works. There is no 'ease' family in RmlUi: the complete keyword table is PropertyParserAnimation.cpp:27-77 (back bounce circular cubic elastic exponential linear quadratic quartic quintic sine, each -in/-out/-in-out). 'ease-in-out' misses the keyword map at :240, the sscanf for a time fails, it falls to the property-name branch, GetShorthand/GetProperty both return null, and the ENTIRE transition declaration is dropped with one generic 'Syntax error parsing property declaration'. Second, undocumented: 'animation' lowercases its token before lookup (:133), 'transition' does NOT (:240) — so 'Cubic-Out' works in one and fails in the other. Found while building the 2d6 demo.
notes:
CONFIRMED BY RESTORE-THE-BUG IN A RUNNING ENGINE (2d6 demo, Task 4). Two transitions placed side by side in one sheet:
  transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out;   -> Warning: [Rml] Syntax error parsing property declaration 'transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out;' in 2d6/components.rcss: 16.
  transition: opacity 0.3s cubic-in-out;  -> silent, applied.
So the whole declaration is dropped, exactly as the parser trace predicted. This directly falsifies Content/DevUI/M5Hud/vacuus-base.rcss:13-14, which states in prose: 'Tween parsing is strict: transition: opacity 0.3s ease-in-out; works'. It does not work. That file ships to buyers inside the package and is the sheet every document is told to link FIRST, so the false claim is in the most-read stylesheet in the product. gotchas.md:23-27 repeats it.
close_reason: Fixed in three shipped files. (1) Content/DevUI/M5Hud/vacuus-base.rcss:13-28 (and the byte-identical CLI copy Web/packages/cli/template/vacuus-base.rcss, which vacuus create copies into every scaffold) now state there is NO ease family, list the eleven real tween families from the table I opened at PropertyParserAnimation.cpp:27-77, name cubic-in-out as the substitution for CSS ease-in-out, and document the case asymmetry (:133 ToLower for animation, :240 none for transition). (2) docs/buyer/gotchas.md #3 rewritten with the full parser trace (:240 map miss -> :267 sscanf fail -> :301-315 returns false -> whole declaration dropped) and the measured log line. (3) The matrix's transition and animation rows had EMPTY Notes and no tween list at all; both now carry the keyword table and the case trap (Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py ANNOTATIONS, regenerated). Also fixed the downstream cites that my base-sheet edit shifted: gotchas.md :29-31/:32-36 and gen_rcss_matrix.py's position annotation. Every cited line opened; the keyword table is exactly the eleven families x in/out/in-out claimed.

title: mask-image parses and silently does nothing
description: SaveLayerAsMaskImage() is also unimplemented (VaCuusCommandBuffer.h:455-462). ElementEffects.cpp:296-311 pushes a layer, draws the mask decorators, gets handle 0 back, AddHandleTo skips the invalid handle, the layer is popped and the composite runs with no mask filter. The element renders UNMASKED and the mask artwork is discarded, with NO WARNING OF ANY KIND. Found while building the 2d6 demo.
close_reason: Warning shipped; masking itself still unimplemented and blocked on the same layer capture as VaCuus-u0q. The recorder now OVERRIDES SaveLayerAsMaskImage, returning 0 (RmlUi's own safe-refusal contract: RenderManager.cpp:328-334 wraps only a nonzero handle, AddHandleTo skips the invalid one) with ONE latched Warning per view naming the property, the reason and the substitute. The latch matters more here than anywhere else in the plugin: RenderEffects reaches this once per masked element PER FRAME -- measured 112 calls to 1 log line in the new test. CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD's PREMISE, found by screenshot not inference: the mask artwork is NOT discarded. The mask decorators are drawn into the pushed layer BEFORE the capture (ElementEffects.cpp:300-305), and because the replayer skips layers those draws land in the base RT -- so the artwork is painted OVER the element. The M2 demo shot shows a magenta-green gradient completely covering the panel it was applied to. Nothing can make that harmless short of implementing the capture, so the warning is the whole v1 fix; the warning text and the buyer docs now state the real symptom. Verified by VaCuus.Render.LayerCapture.Refused (112 calls / 1 warning); restore-the-bug: latch broken -> 112 warnings. Suite 200/200. Docs: gotchas.md #2b, rcss-matrix.md mask-image row + Layer capture section.

title: box-shadow renders an opaque white rectangle and forces a publish every frame
description: GeometryBoxShadow.cpp:235 needs RenderInterface::SaveLayerAsTexture(), which VaCuus does not override (VaCuusCommandBuffer.h:455-462). The base returns handle 0, but GeometryBoxShadow.cpp:236-239 still returns true, so load_failed is never set and CallbackTextureDatabase::EnsureLoaded re-runs the whole callback EVERY FRAME (TextureDatabase.cpp:46-60) — permanent resource traffic, permanent forced publish. ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry then SKIPS normal background/border generation when box-shadow is present (:109-118) and renders only the shadow quad, which is premultiplied WHITE (BoxShadowCache.cpp:56-59). Net: an opaque white rectangle replacing the element's own background and border. Found while building the 2d6 demo. Docs currently only say box-shadow is not animatable. Fix: implement SaveLayerAsTexture, or refuse the property with one named warning.
close_reason: Option A (refuse loudly, harmlessly): implementing SaveLayerAsTexture was judged intractable for v1 -- the replayer has no layer render targets at all (PushLayer/CompositeLayers/PopLayer are recorded and skipped, VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:720-739), and capture alone would still give a WRONG shadow because the blur is a filtered composite and the shape is cut with a clip mask, neither applied at replay (the latter is VaCuus-4ik). The recorder now OVERRIDES SaveLayerAsTexture, returning 0 with one latched Warning per view naming the property, the reason and the substitute (ninepatch / font-effect: glow). VaCuus patch #3 to the vendored RmlUi makes the failure harmless: the callback now reports failure so load_failed latches (GeometryBoxShadow.cpp), and GenerateGeometry probes the texture and falls through to the NORMAL background/border path instead of erasing it (ElementBackgroundBorder.cpp), keeping the refused renderable alive so the cache entry and its latch survive a restyle. Verified on screen (M2 demo, before = opaque white rectangle over the panel; after = the panel's real background and border) and by two new automation tests. Restore-the-bug, all four hunks: both reverted -> 201 published in 201 recorded; render hunk alone -> 12 opaque-white vertices, 8 background instead of 20; callback hunk alone -> 70 refusals across 70 restyled frames vs 1; latch broken -> 3 warnings instead of 1. Suite 200/200. Docs: gotchas.md #2, rcss-matrix.md (regenerated), VENDORED_TAG.txt patch #3.

title: Matrix row 13: live reload needs an interactive editor PIE pass — never executed on any platform
description:
Matrix row 13 is the last row that has never been executed on ANY platform, and the reason is the
same on all three: the file watcher lives in VaCuusEditor (editor-only module) and the row needs an
interactive editor PIE session plus a mid-run file edit — not expressible in a frame-0 -ExecCmds
headless run, and not reachable from a packaged build at all.

Status per column as of 2026-08-03:
  Linux Vulkan  PARTIAL by venue (note B) — headless, watcher is editor-only
  Win64 D3D12   NOT EXECUTED — the console session solved the WINDOWED problem (bead 5fg), but this
                row additionally needs the EDITOR, PIE, and a human editing a file mid-run
  macOS Metal   owed with the rest of that column

Standing evidence that the feature works, so this is a verification gap and not a suspected defect:
the M2 T10 proof session (docs/research/proofs/m2-t10-live-reload/, with before/after screenshots),
the automation reload suite (VaCuusReloadTest.cpp), and the runtime half vacuus.ReloadUI which the
M6 sweep moved into the runtime module.

THE STEPS, identical on each platform:
  1. Open the editor on the host project, start PIE with a document loaded.
  2. Edit the loaded .rcss (or .rml) on disk while PIE runs.
  3. Watch the view repaint without a restart.
  4. Mount a bundle that shadows the same path.
  5. Edit again, and assert the watcher's Warning NAMES the shadowing path.

Row 12's editor-PIE leg rides with this one. That row's -game leg passed on Win64 (the ini-forced
FloatRGBA permutation, A/B by eye), but spec 3.2 also names an editor-PIE composite check, and the
Win64 column was the one meant to own it.

Split out of akj.10.1 when that bead closed at 13/15, so the remaining work is tracked by what it
needs (a human in an editor) rather than buried in a closed matrix bead.
close_reason:
Row 13 is executed on Linux Vulkan, and the premise in this bead was wrong.

IT SAID: 'needs an interactive editor PIE session plus a mid-run file edit -- not expressible in a frame-0 -ExecCmds headless run'. The first half is true; the second does not follow. A frame-0 command line cannot itself edit a file thirty seconds later, but a SECOND PROCESS can, and the plugin already ships the harness for it: Proof.LiveReload.PIE, whose own header says it needs 'a HUMAN OR A SCRIPT to edit a file from outside this process while it runs'. The missing ingredient was a shell loop watching the log for VACUUS_PROOF_EDIT_NOW.

STEPS 1-3, EXECUTED 2026-08-06:
  Live reload flushed 1 changed path(s) after 190 ms and reloaded 1 view(s): .../m1_hud.rcss
  Proof.LiveReload.PIE  Result={Success}   (it asserts both screenshots exist, so an idle harness goes red)
  the pixel pair: exactly 1,080 pixels in a 90x12 block at (128..217, 189..200) are (255,0,0)
  before the edit and (0,255,255) after it -- #hp-fill, the one rule the script changed.

STEPS 4-5 ARE NOW A TEST rather than a manual step: VaCuus.LiveReload.BundleShadow mounts a transient bundle containing the changed path and asserts ONE Warning names the shadow, the file, the bundle and the remedy, with a nothing-mounted control. That warning had NO test at all, and it is the only thing live reload can do about a trap it deliberately does not fix. Watched to fail with the warning deleted -- twice, because the first version of the assertion was too loose (the changed path also appears in the ordinary flush diagnostic, so 'the capture contains the path' stayed true; the check is now one line carrying all four fragments).

WHAT REMAINS, and it is a much smaller claim than this bead opened with: a person looking at a real windowed editor rather than at two PNGs. Every mechanical link -- event, debounce, reload dispatch, repaint, shadow warning -- is asserted by a test or by the pixel pair. Win64 and macOS can run the identical command; nothing in it needs a particular platform.

Third time on this project that 'cannot be tested' meant 'needs a latent command' or 'needs a second process', and the second time the API notes already said so.

VaCuus 2d11408 + e88072b, merged d593544. Matrix doc updated.

(2) THE MEMORY-MAPPED BUNDLE LINE, observed taken:
      Mounted bundle '/VaCuus/Bundles/DevUIBundle.DevUIBundle': 24 entries, 465513 bytes,
      memory-mapped region, hash da75027b...

VENUE SUBSTITUTION, recorded per spec 2(f). The mount was observed on a cooked, paked, staged
DEVELOPMENT build, not Shipping, because a Shipping run cannot be read at all on this engine: a
stock Game target compiles every UE_LOG out of Shipping (-log or not), bUseLoggingInShipping is
refused ("has build products in common with UnrealGame"; the remedy UBT names,
TargetBuildEnvironment.Unique, requires rebuilding engine modules, impossible on an Installed
build), and -clientconfig=Test is refused outright ("Targets cannot be built in the Test
configuration with this engine distribution"). The substitution is mechanism-preserving for THIS
question: bMemoryMapped is set from whether the load returned a mapped region, which depends on the
COOKED payload's BULKDATA_MemoryMappedPayload stamp and the iostore/pak loader — neither is a
function of compile configuration, and both legs read the same cooked content.

FIRST-RUN WARM-UP IS LARGE AND WOULD HAVE BEEN EASY TO PUBLISH BY MISTAKE. The first run off a
fresh cook measured 46.6 fps / Update 13.0 / Record 9.0 ms; the second, same binary and content,
79.7 / 3.556 / 2.205. Cold PSO and shader caches dominate the first pass by ~4x. Any Win64 number
taken from a just-cooked package without a warm-up run is wrong by roughly that factor.

FOUR TRAPS, each of which cost a failed run (all in section 12.7):
 1. The cook needs the AutoSDK shim — BuildCookRun builds the EDITOR target, so editing the
    .uproject invalidates its makefile and UBT re-hits SwarmInterface. Exit 8. See akj.10.9.
 2. Orphaned staged processes lock the staging dir (exit 102 on dbghelp.dll). The staged ROOT exe
    is a launcher stub; killing it leaves the real binary running. Reap by executable PATH.
 3. Shipping runs are unreadable on an Installed engine (above).
 4. A stale target receipt silently stages NOTHING. After the failed logging builds
    TP_ThirdPerson.target was left partial — Launch empty, 0 build products — and UAT staged
    content with no executable and no warning. Rebuilding does not fix it ("Target is up to date"
    writes no receipt); the receipt must be DELETED and the target rebuilt. Related: restoring a
    Target.cs with Copy-Item restores its original mtime, so UBT keeps using the rules assembly it
    compiled from the edited file until the file is touched.

Also: a staged SHIPPING build writes Saved/ to %LOCALAPPDATA%\<Project>\Saved, while a staged
DEVELOPMENT build writes it under the staged tree. Screenshots and logs move with the config.

title: quickjs /experimental:c11atomics: decide, and record the decision where Build.cs already asks the question
description:
Owner-handoff item 5, and win64-results section 4 -- which sharpened it: the answer is NOT 'no flag needed'. Source/VaCuusJs/VaCuusJs.Build.cs:44-48 carries the open question; upstream quickjs-ng demands the flag under MSVC (their CMakeLists.txt:128).

What the pass established: the module compiles clean on MSVC WITHOUT the flag, because the vendored source takes the __STDC_NO_ATOMICS__ branch -- which means Win64 currently ships a JS runtime with NO Atomics global, while Linux and macOS have one. That is a silent platform behaviour split, not a build failure.

NOT confirmed live: section 4's conclusion comes from the preprocessor guard and MSVC's documented __STDC_NO_ATOMICS__, not from a session evaluating typeof Atomics -- no session survived long enough. Now that they survive (xa5), the cheap confirmation is one line of JS.

DECIDE: accept Win64 without Atomics (and say so in the buyer docs, because a buyer's script that feature-detects will silently take a different path on one platform), or add the flag for MSVC only. Either way the comment at Build.cs:44-48 stops asking and starts stating, with the evidence.
acceptance_criteria: typeof Atomics observed on a live Win64 session; Build.cs:44-48 records the decision and the evidence; if the split is accepted, it is stated in the buyer docs.
close_reason:
[replayed from the Win64 console session, which has no Dolt DB -- verbatim]

DECIDED (owner, 2026-08-03): ACCEPT THE SPLIT. Win64 ships without the Atomics global; we do NOT
pass /experimental:c11atomics. Rationale: it would opt a shipped module into an explicitly
experimental MSVC switch to enable a builtin that no VaCuus document, test or buyer-facing API uses.

CONFIRMED AT RUNTIME, which is what this bead was waiting for — the morning pass could only infer
it from the preprocessor because no session survived long enough. A temporary console.log probe in
RefHud/refhud_logic.js on a live console-session vacuus.RefHud build (inserted, run, reverted; the
clone is clean) printed:

  ATOMICS-PROBE: typeof Atomics=undefined typeof SharedArrayBuffer=function typeof WeakRef=function

THE SPLIT IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED, and that is the part worth carrying:
SharedArrayBuffer is PRESENT on Win64 while Atomics is missing. The two do not travel together,
because SharedArrayBuffer is not behind the CONFIG_ATOMICS guard. So the idiomatic feature test —
typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' — PASSES on Windows and then Atomics.load throws a
TypeError. A script written that way works on every platform the author develops on and fails on
the one most buyers ship to.

Landed in three places:
 - Source/VaCuusJs/VaCuusJs.Build.cs:44-48 now STATES the decision and carries the measured
   evidence, instead of asking the question.
 - docs/buyer/gotchas.md gains item 13a: feature-detect Atomics itself, never SharedArrayBuffer as
   a proxy.
 - docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-win64-results.md section 4 records the confirmation.

The Linux/macOS half of the claim remains the preprocessor inference plus those platforms' absence
of __STDC_NO_ATOMICS__ — no probe was run there in this pass, and the note says so.

title: VaCuus.Render.Texture.UnsizedDrain asserts an exact frame count against a waiter that is a floor — deterministic FAIL on Win64
description:
win64-results section 5, owner decision 3. The two-line fix was written out and deliberately NOT applied on the Win64 machine, because it perturbs a baseline that pass could not re-measure from the far side. Verify on Linux, then land. STILL UNFIXED as of 2026-08-03: VaCuusUnsizedDrainTest.cpp:261 is still TestEqual.

SYMPTOM (both Win64 runs, identical -- deterministic on that machine, not jitter):
  Expected 'The sized view recorded exactly one frame' to be 1, but it was 2.
  [VaCuusUnsizedDrainTest.cpp(264)]

MECHANISM: RunFrames (VaCuusUnsizedDrainTest.cpp:91-104) calls UIThread.Trigger() then WaitForFrameCount(Before + 1, 5.0) -- it waits for the count to reach AT LEAST Before + 1. It is a floor, not an exact pulse. The assertion at :261 reads it as exact. On a 16-core Windows box the UI thread lands two frames before the waiter observes; Linux and macOS happen to land on one. Same family as CLAUDE.md's recorded hazard that vacuus.M1HUD.AutoShot N fires after max(N,3) RECORDED frames.

Every substantive assertion of the bead passed in the same run: an unsized view records 0 frames, its finished decode is drained anyway, and the first sized frame publishes exactly one buffer, at the right size, with the real payload rather than the 1x1 placeholder. The extra recorded frame was correctly WITHHELD by the publish gate -- no extra work crossed to the render thread.

FIX: assert >= 1 recorded frames, keep the published-buffer count exact at 1. The published count is the user-visible property and the one the bead is about.
acceptance_criteria: The recorded-frame assertion is a floor and the published-buffer assertion stays exact; restore-the-bug shows the published assertion still failing when the drain is broken.
close_reason:
Fixed in the build clone, verified on Linux by restore-the-bug both ways. The assertion is now a RANGE: recorded >= 1, and recorded <= (frames the UI thread ran since the resize) + 1. The +1 is provable rather than fudged -- FramesRecorded is bumped inside the frame (VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.cpp:576) and FrameCount only after RunFrame returns (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:979-980), so with the loads read in that order at most ONE frame is recorded-but-uncounted, the worker being a single thread. The frame count is sampled BEFORE EnqueueResize because Enqueue() triggers the wake event itself (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:800-801), which is the actual source of the Win64 second frame.

EVIDENCE (Linux, editor Development, -nullrhi):
  1. Fix in place, single test: Result={Success}.
  2. Restore-the-bug, ceiling: SetViewSize() bumped FramesRecorded by 4 (a resize that retroactively records the sat-out frames) -> FAIL, 'no more than the 1 frame(s) the UI thread ran since the resize, +1 for a frame in flight (recorded 5)'. Only that assertion fired; the published-buffer assertion still passed, exactly as on Win64.
  3. Restore-the-bug, floor: the FramesRecorded bump commented out -> FAIL, 'The sized view recorded at least one frame (recorded 0)'.
  4. Restored, full suite: 198 tests performed, 198 Success, 0 Fail.

NOT YET COMMITTED and not merged to canonical -- conservative profile, the owner commits.
