 - Exp-FPS-LAW: I PREDICTED the breach was an artifact of the low frame rate (a time-driven HUD
   doing more work per longer frame) and predicted ~8.1 ms at a 30 fps cap. MEASURED 2.93 ms
   against 3.00 at 80 fps, with JsPump equally flat. PREDICTION REFUTED — per-frame cost is
   frame-rate independent, so the gap is real work on a slower machine.

OWNER CALL RAISED, not decided: as written, the 1.2 ms row 2a budget silently encodes the 7950X3D.
Either it is a per-frame figure that any shipping machine must meet, or it should be stated against
a named reference machine the way row 6's disk literal is stated against a named platform.

STILL OWED: the cooked-Shipping-Win64 leg, and for a documented reason rather than an oversight —
a stock Game target compiles every UE_LOG out of Shipping, and bUseLoggingInShipping cannot be
enabled on an Installed engine (it needs TargetBuildEnvironment.Unique, which requires rebuilding
engine modules). -clientconfig=Test is refused outright by this distribution. See akj.10.3's close
note. A cooked DEVELOPMENT run was measured instead as a cross-check and lands at 79.7 fps /
Update 3.556 — within noise of the editor venue, so the packaged build performs like the editor one
on this workload.

title: Windows SSH sessions cannot open a window — no interactive desktop for GUI processes
description:
Environment blocker found by the Win64 pass 2026-08-03. A process launched over SSH on Windows has no interactive desktop, so any windowed UE session crashes before engine init. Offscreen sessions do boot (which is why the pass produced findings at all), but the manual matrix explicitly requires WINDOWED runs -- half its rows exist to be seen on a real desktop, and the macOS plan established that -RenderOffscreen is not even available there.

CONSEQUENCE: 13 of 15 matrix rows are marked 'not run, because X' on Win64, and the IME line the headless run did produce is a nullrhi artifact that MUST NOT be quoted as evidence on its own.

OPTIONS TO EVALUATE (none tried yet): run the session under the owner's interactive console session rather than the SSH session (PsExec -i, a scheduled task set to run in the console session, or an autologon + startup script); use RDP, which creates a real interactive session; or accept that Win64 visual rows are a hands-on-keyboard job like the macOS interactive rows and schedule them that way.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PASS: the same constraint will apply to every future Win64 visual verification, including the IME row (akj.6.19) and the disk literal's packaged runs. Deciding the mechanism once is cheaper than rediscovering it each time.
close_reason:
[replayed from the Win64 console session, which has no Dolt DB -- verbatim]

ANSWERED, on the first option of the list: run from the PHYSICAL CONSOLE SESSION. No PsExec, no
scheduled task, no RDP and no autologon were needed.

The check is SESSIONNAME=Console (state Active; [Environment]::UserInteractive True). The thing
that has to be true is that the shell issuing the launch is ITSELF in the console session — an
OpenSSH session on Windows is a different session with no interactive desktop, and a windowed
process there dies before engine init at exit 3 with zero VaCuus lines, exactly as the morning
pass recorded.

Recipe, which drove ~15 sessions on 2026-08-03 with zero venue failures:
  UnrealEditor.exe <ABS>.uproject -game -windowed -resx=1920 -resy=1080 -ForceRes -ExecCmds="...,"

Two operational lessons, both learned by doing it wrong first:

 - CLOSE the window (Process.CloseMainWindow), do not Stop-Process. A hard kill leaves no teardown
   tail, and that tail is matrix row 14's entire evidence. Graceful close gives exit 0 plus the
   full tail (UI thread in-band stop, VFS totals, RmlUi shut down, zero unpublished NEW resources).
 - Staged builds add a second trap: the staged ROOT exe is a launcher stub that re-launches the
   real binary out of <staged>\VcHost\Binaries\Win64\, so killing the PID Start-Process hands back
   leaves the GAME running. Two such orphans locked dbghelp.dll and killed a later cook with
   Error_FailedToDeleteStagingDirectory (102). Reap by executable PATH after every staged run.

Recorded in docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-win64-results.md section 12.1; the runner is kept beside
the artifacts as C:\VaCuusWin64Test\run-row.ps1.

This unblocked akj.10.1, akj.10.2 and akj.10.3, and moved akj.6.19 from "blocked on venue" to
"blocked on a human with an IME".

title: World-panel input processor latches all application input on the first touch
description:
Found by the mobile research (docs/research/mobile-support.md, b779983) and REPRODUCIBLE ON LINUX TODAY — no phone needed. Filed separately from the mobile beads because it is not a mobile-only defect.

MECHANISM, from source: FVaCuusWorldInputProcessor takes a latch on press and clears it when the pressed-button set empties. But GetPressedButtons() is baked into the touch event at CONSTRUCTION (Events.h:938, Events.cpp:15, SlateApplication.cpp:6832), so for a touch event the clearing predicate at VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.cpp:518 can NEVER be true. The latch therefore never releases. Worse, the processor deliberately holds no Slate capture, so none of the engine's safety nets fire, and preprocessors run BEFORE all routing — so the stuck latch swallows input for the WHOLE APPLICATION, not just our panel.

WHY IT MATTERS OUTSIDE MOBILE: -faketouches (SlateApplication.cpp:900, 5261, 6092) synthesises real touch events from mouse clicks, and any touchscreen laptop or tablet-mode device produces them natively. So a desktop customer with a touch display can hit this today.

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT: the plugin's test suite has never seen a touch event — every synthesized FPointerEvent in Tests/ uses CursorPointerIndex. That is the coverage gap the fix must close, not just the latch.

FIX SHAPE (to be designed, not prescribed): the clearing condition must not depend on a button set that touch events cannot populate; a touch-index-aware release, or a latch keyed on the same event stream that set it. THE OBSERVABLE IS THE POINT: a test that drives a touch press/release through the processor and asserts the latch releases — the suite currently cannot express that, so the fixture work is part of the bead. -faketouches gives a manual reproduction for the before/after.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
MECHANISM PINNED 2026-08-03 with every line opened, and the reason it looked correct is now known. HandleMouseButtonUpEvent releases the latch only when MouseEvent.GetPressedButtons().IsEmpty() (VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.cpp:518). That can never be true for touch: FSlateApplication::OnTouchEnded constructs the event with bPressLeftMouseButton=true (SlateApplication.cpp:6832-6845) and the touch constructor bakes PressedButtons = FTouchKeySet::StandardSet into the event's VALUE COPY (Events.h:938, Events.cpp:15) — so the set is non-empty regardless of the application's live button state.

WHY IT LOOKED RIGHT: the comment at :509-517 justifying the predicate cites SlateApplication.cpp:6100-6103, which is about the application's LIVE set, not the event copy. The load-bearing justification is wrong — which is exactly the class this project's conventions name as a critical-bug source.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT: the processor holds no Slate capture by design, so no engine safety net fires; the other ClearLatch sites (:390, :446, :601) all require the panel to have died while Tick is empty (VaCuusWorldInputProcessor.h:220); and IInputProcessor offers no touch or capture-lost hook (IInputProcessor.h:26-50). So the first tap consumes every subsequent pointer event in the application, permanently.

REPRODUCES ON LINUX TODAY: -faketouches makes FSlateApplication convert every left click into a real touch event (SlateApplication.cpp:900, 5261-5264, 6092-6095). Recorded as section 0 of docs/research/mobile-support.md.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
Fixed 2026-08-03 (64b703d). Linux regression 198/198 — the count moved 197 -> 198 because this bead's own test is the +1.

THE FIX, by shape rather than by patch: FVaCuusPointerLatch now holds the SET OF PRESSES THIS PROCESSOR CONSUMED and has not seen released, keyed by {UserIndex, PointerIndex, EffectingButton}. That triple covers both device shapes with no branch — a mouse puts every button on CursorPointerIndex so Button separates them; a touch puts every finger on its own PointerIndex with EffectingButton hard-coded to LeftMouseButton (Events.h:939-940) so PointerIndex separates them. The held set is private and every mutator takes an FVaCuusPointerPress, so the type offers NO predicate over a button set to write — the wrong-looking-right alternative is out of reach. TSet not a counter: a re-reported press is idempotent rather than a leaked hold nothing can release.

A CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCOUNT, established by the implementer: the justifying comment did NOT misquote its source. It cited SlateApplication.cpp:6098-6118, and those lines do say what it claimed. The failure was OVER-GENERALISATION — the engine comment's very next clause names the touch exception, and our paraphrase kept the rule and dropped the exception. Same failure class as a wrong citation, different mechanism, and worth distinguishing: 'the citation was wrong' and 'the citation was right and the generalisation from it was not' call for different review reflexes.

THE FIXTURE IS HALF THE DELIVERABLE: MakeTouchEvent(Position, FingerIndex, SlateUserIndex) is the suite's FIRST touch event — before this, every synthesized FPointerEvent under Tests/ used CursorPointerIndex, which is why nothing caught the bug. It passes bPressLeftMouseButton=true for the RELEASE too, because that is what OnTouchEnded does; a fixture quietly passing false would test a device that does not exist. Test VaCuus.World.InputLatchRelease drives a REAL UVaCuusWorldComponent — with a null one every handler takes its panel-died branch and the assertions would pass under the very bug they exist to catch.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, three distinct wrong rules each failing a distinct row set: the original predicate (3 rows), an unconditional Drop (2 rows), and a reset-instead-of-remove (5 rows). That is the evidence the test constrains the RULE and not the one line that was wrong.

ONE SITE LOOKED IDENTICAL AND IS NOT A BUG: SVaCuusWidget::OnMouseButtonUp:638 has the same predicate, but the widget holds real Slate capture and FSlateUser::NotifyPointerReleased force-releases it on every touch end regardless of the reply (SlateUser.cpp:1284-1290), which drives OnMouseCaptureLost and clears the mirror. The engine's net ends a touch drag there — not that line.

title: Re-run the buyer-install simulation as a TRUE cold start: artifact only, no dev-tree docs
description:
The 2026-08-02 simulation (workflow warwptkvj) was graded CONTAMINATED by its own adversarial verifier on two counts that make its GREEN result unearned:

C2 -- the installer read docs/buyer/*.md from /w/Unreal/VaCuus (the protected dev tree). The package ships no docs at all. Its own deliverables prove the reading: the authored myhud.rml cites 'gotchas.md #1' and '#9' and the citations are accurate. So the run measured a DOCUMENTED buyer's experience; a real buyer starts with zero of the five docs.
C3 -- the headless verification recipe (-RenderOffscreen -ForceRes, the -ExecCmds comma rule, kill-by-PID after StopTestSession) came verbatim from our CLAUDE.md and was presented as live discovery. No buyer could reproduce that pipeline from the artifact.

Everything else the verifier checked was CLEAN with strong evidence: no symlinks (find -type l = 0), no hardlinks, distinct inodes, no AdditionalPluginDirectories; zero path leakage into the customer project; the plugin genuinely COMPILED there (228 .o stamped after the copy, .so hashes differ from ours, staged monolith strings show only the customer path); the demo UI was original (md5-unique); the packaged run had no editor and no plugin .so in the stage; 190/190 tests green in the customer's own log.

RE-RUN CONTRACT (after VaCuus-avu ships docs in the package): the installer gets the zip and NOTHING else -- no access to /w/Unreal/VaCuus, /w/Unreal/VcHost, /w/Unreal/VaCuusDemo, and no CLAUDE.md. Every step it cannot take from the artifact alone is the finding. Expect it to be much redder than the first run; that redness is the deliverable. Keep the same adversarial verify phase.

ARTIFACT PROVENANCE RULE (finding C1, already fixed but worth codifying): the first run's package was built from a work tree carrying an UNCOMMITTED include fix, so a package rebuilt from canonical would have FAILED BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes. The fix is now committed (061eb9b, merged to canonical). Rule: build the artifact from a CLEAN CLONE OF CANONICAL at a named SHA, and record that SHA in the run's evidence.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: UNBLOCKED 2026-08-03: the re-run contract said 'after VaCuus-avu ships docs in the package', and c1394d6 does -- a produced package now carries README.md and docs/buyer/{setup,gotchas,rcss-matrix,perf-guide}.md, with owner-handoff.md excluded. So a cold-start installer can read the same five pages a real buyer gets, from the artifact only, and C2 stops being structural. C3 (the headless recipe coming from our CLAUDE.md rather than from the package) is NOT fixed by that and remains this bead's real work: either the package must teach the verification pipeline, or the simulation must run without one and say so.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
C3 CLOSED 2026-08-09 (d56e2de), which was this bead's real remaining work. The re-run itself
is deferred by the owner's call the same day: fix the contamination first, run the simulation
after.

WHAT C3 WAS: the 2026-08-02 installer's headless verification recipe -- comma-separated
-ExecCmds, -RenderOffscreen with -ForceRes, kill-by-PID once StopTestSession appears -- came
verbatim from this repository's CLAUDE.md and was presented as live discovery. The artifact
teaches none of it, so the run measured a pipeline a real buyer does not have.

THE FIX, and it is the "package teaches it" fork rather than the "run without one and say so"
fork: setup.md gains section 4, which ships (Config/FilterPlugin.ini:67-68 carries README.md
and docs/buyer/... minus owner-handoff.md). Two runnable recipes -- the suite under -nullrhi,
and a visual run offscreen at a chosen resolution -- plus the four traps, each attributed to
the engine line that causes it rather than left as advice:
  the comma split, and single-quoted commas as its escape   ParseExecCommands.cpp:27, :11-14
  the -ExecCmds value swallowing every later argument        ParseExecCommands.cpp:63
  -resx/-resy clamped to nothing useful without -ForceRes    GameEngine.cpp:413-419
  Saved/Logs over stdout; kill by PID, never a -f pattern    observed, stated as such
Every citation was opened before it was written.

WHAT THE RE-RUN NOW LOOKS LIKE, when it happens. C2 was already structural-fixed by c1394d6
(the package carries README.md + four buyer pages), and C3 is fixed here, so BOTH contamination

every step it cannot take from the artifact alone is the finding.

TWO THINGS FOR WHOEVER RUNS IT:
  - Build the artifact from a CLEAN CLONE OF CANONICAL at a named SHA and record that SHA
    (the C1 provenance rule; the first run's package came from a tree with an uncommitted
    include fix, so a package rebuilt from canonical would have FAILED -StrictIncludes).
  - The new section 4 is now itself under test. If the installer cannot run the suite from

title: rmlui_dynamic_cast fails across module boundaries in Linux modular builds — VaCuusTextInput casts may be dead
description: Found during M4 Task 4 (commit 4b7d5da): with RMLUI_CUSTOM_RTTI, the type identifier is a function-local static of an inline member (ThirdParty/RmlUi Traits.h:67-91). Under Linux modular builds (-fvisibility-ms-compat / -fvisibility-inlines-hidden, LinuxToolChain.cs:439/:450) each .so gets its OWN copy, so rmlui_dynamic_cast<T> across a module boundary compares two different statics and always fails. Observed directly: every ElementDocument wrapped as a plain element in VaCuusJs until the cast was replaced with the owner-document self-reference test (GetOwnerDocument()==this). SUSPECT SITES: VaCuusTextInput.cpp:238/:243/:334 and the input/text-entry tests — those casts cross VaCuus->VaCuusRml and may be silently taking the failed branch in modular builds while monolithic builds mask it. Fix shapes: (a) audit each cross-module rmlui_dynamic_cast and replace with structural tests; (b) or force the RTTI statics into one home (export the specializations from VaCuusRml). Verify with a modular-build test asserting each cast succeeds.
notes: SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE (M4 Task 6, commit bc958b7): a document subclass whose vtable lived in VaCuusJs.so made rmlui_dynamic_cast<ElementDocument*> answer null INSIDE VaCuusRml.so — the context ctor's cursor proxy wrote through null+0x1b8, SIGSEGV in the first suite run. Fix shape that worked: move the subclass + instancer into VaCuusRml with a key function pinning the vtable there; identify via an instancer membership set, never a cast. The audit of VaCuusTextInput.cpp casts remains open.
close_reason: Fixed in 0eb0033 (M6 Task 1): three VACUUSRML_API non-inline cast helpers home both sides of the identity compare in VaCuusRml's relocations — sound under every load order; all 6 sites converted, zero rmlui_dynamic_cast outside VaCuusRml/ThirdParty; canary test VaCuus.Rml.CrossModuleCast; the load-order-accident evidence (dlopen probe, RTLD_LOCAL scoping) recorded in the helper header.

title: Desc build recurses forever on hand-built circular UUserDefinedStructs (TArray of each other)
description: Found during M3b Task 1: FVaCuusModelArrayDesc builds a plain FVaCuusModelLayout per struct element type; two structs each holding TArray of the other recurse infinitely at desc build. Unwritable in native C++ (declaration order) and the BP editor refuses circular structs, but hand-built UUserDefinedStructs can construct it (VaCuusModelRecompileTest.cpp shows the technique). Fix shape: a visited-set or depth guard in the desc build, one Error naming the cycle.
notes: ESCALATED by the Tasks 1-2 quality review (2026-07-31): the cycle is reachable from LEGAL UHT type graphs, not only hand-built UUserDefinedStructs — UHT refuses only DIRECT self-recursion (UhtArrayProperty.cs:216-222), so mutual recursion FA{TArray<FB>}/FB{TArray<FA>} and intermediate-struct cycles compile cleanly and crash the stack at bind time with no diagnostic. Being fixed in-milestone (build-stack guard + refusal Warning); close when the fix commit lands on m3b-arrays.
close_reason: Fixed in-milestone on m3b-arrays (commit d6c8ab9): build-stack guard refuses the array field on a container cycle with a named Warning; VaCuus.Model.LayoutCycle hand-builds both cycle shapes from UUserDefinedStructs and the red state was an observed SIGSEGV stack overflow. Native cycle fixtures proved unwritable (UHT zero-codegen-hash error), narrowing the reachable surface to UDS — the guard covers both.

title: Blueprint struct recompile dangles every FProperty* in a live layout
description:
ANSWERED BY EXPERIMENT in M3a Task 9 (VaCuus.Model.BlueprintRecompile). The spec's 'strong ref + rebuild' mitigation was half-fictional: the strong ref works, the rebuild exists nowhere.

MECHANISM, from source: CompileStruct's own comment says 'Recompiled UDS keep the same instance' (UserDefinedStructureCompilerUtils.cpp:595) -- so the strong reference to the UScriptStruct holds. But the FIRST thing it does to that instance is CleanAndSanitizeStruct -> DestroyChildPropertiesAndResetPropertyLinks (:512, :225) -> DestroyPropertyLinkedList, a plain 'delete FieldToDestroy' over the whole chain (Class.cpp:2117-2126). Only the DefaultValueChanged change-reason is exempt (:221-232).

So: type object SURVIVES, every FProperty* in the layout DANGLES. Verified by pointer comparison (the test never dereferences the freed property).

FAILURE MODES, worst first:
- FVaCuusModelShadow's destructor runs DestroyStruct on a buffer laid out by the OLD properties using the NEW DestructorLink -- a free of a pointer read from the wrong offset. Heap corruption, not a leak.
- Sample/Publish/ApplyUpdate dereference freed memory every frame.
- Even a correct rebuild would have to run on the UI THREAD, because RmlUi holds a raw void* into the UI shadow and revalidates it never.

SCOPE: editor-only -- FStructureEditorUtils lives in UnrealEd, so a packaged game cannot reach this. Requires a designer editing a Blueprint struct while a view bound over that struct is live.

RECOMMENDED FIX IS A REFUSAL, NOT A REBUILD: have FVaCuusBoundModel register with FStructureEditorUtils::FStructEditorManager (editor-only) and, on a pre-change for its type, log an Error and stop sampling. That converts silent heap corruption into a loud, documented limitation. A real rebuild is M3b or later.
acceptance_criteria: A Blueprint struct recompiled under a live bound model produces a loud Error and a stopped model rather than dangling pointers; a test covers it.
notes: M3b doubles this hazard's surface: an array-of-struct field pins TWO type objects (model root + element type via FVaCuusModelArrayDesc::ElementLayout), and a recompile of EITHER dangles the FProperty*s a live layout holds. The tracked refusal fix must cover element types too (M3b spec §4, 2026-07-31).
close_reason: Fixed in a96ecb4 (M6 Task 2): FVaCuusStructRecompileGuard (INotifyOnStructChanged) fires at PreChange with the old property chain alive; game-thread walk matches root+ElementLayout structs; dead flag, synchronous game-shadow reset, fenced UI-side drop (observed 1.1ms vs 100ms window), Abandon() only on timeout with leaked-bytes Error; the definition registry evicts stale types so re-bind+reload is a real recovery. Two tests incl. real-UDS-rename red run.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: M6 Task-4 quality review, on record per the reviewer: the retirement design (224ffa3: Invalidate() empties the game-side Models map; UI-side refs drain via RemoveView) leaves a residual window -- a recompile whose PreChange walk condemns NOTHING returns without a fence, so a just-retired view's UI-side model refs (awaiting the already-triggered RemoveView drain) could in principle be destroyed after the struct chain is freed. When any live model IS condemned, the FIFO+fence closes the window completely (the pending RemoveView drains ahead of the drops inside PreChange). Accepted trade-off: strictly better than pre-fix, and the nothing-condemned case means no VaCuus model uses the recompiled struct, so the dangling-FProperty hazard the guard exists for is absent by construction; the destructor is thread-agnostic (no CAS, chains alive at that point).

title: M3b: data binding — arrays and data-for
description:
Split from M3 on the spec review's recommendation. The seam is real rather than administrative: a flat layout entry keyed on a byte offset cannot address an array element (its address is FScriptArrayHelper::GetRawPtr(i), valid only for the current Num()), and RmlUi dirties TOP-LEVEL NAMES ONLY, so the only granularity that maps onto DirtyVariable is one bit per top-level array -- meaning the apply deep-copies the whole array whenever any element changes.

Whether that is acceptable at 200 rows is a MEASUREMENT NOBODY HAS TAKEN, which is why this is separate: everything in M3a is settled by source already read, and everything here depends on numbers.

Carries: the array definition including the .size child (RmlUi's own array definition handles it inline; a hand-written one that forgets it breaks {{ Arr.size }} with only a warning); the bit-granularity decision; the shrink cost (RmlUi's view cleanup is self-flagged quadratic, and shrink is the expensive direction while growth appends at the tail); a 200-row budget; and the killfeed end to end.
close_reason: Merged to master f0eb3a6. TArray UPROPERTYs drive data-for end to end (killfeed demo verified on screen); one bit per array shipped on measured evidence (0.423 ms RmlUi re-evaluation vs 0.014 ms copies at 200x4); SyncCopy warm republish allocates exactly zero (counting-allocator proof, restore-the-bug showed 600 reallocs/window through the engine copy); .size child + element definitions + three evaluation counters; idle exact 0/0/0; 80 tests green x4 runs, monolithic build green, SIGTERM teardown clean with live array models.

title: CreateView returns a valid-looking handle even when UI-thread Initialize() failed
description:
Found during M3 research. CreateView returns the UVaCuusView unconditionally. If the host's Initialize() then fails on the UI thread, the host is dropped -- but the handle the caller is holding still reports IsViewValid() == true, forever.

So a caller that correctly checks the handle gets a view that will never render, never accept input and never load a document, with no way to discover this from the API. Every subsequent command it enqueues is dropped by the unknown-view-id path in DrainCommands, which logs at Verbose.

This becomes more visible in M3: a data model bound to such a view will accept updates on the game thread and silently never apply them, which is indistinguishable from the dirty-variable bug M3 must already guard against -- so two different root causes present identically.

Fix shape: the view already has an async status channel (FVaCuusViewStatus) that the load path uses to echo results back; a failed Initialize should travel the same way and flip the handle to invalid.
acceptance_criteria: A view whose UI-thread Initialize fails reports invalid through the handle, and a test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed in 0eb0033 (M6 Task 1): BootState atomic on FVaCuusViewStatus; PollStatus on first Failed logs one Error, Invalidates, fires OnLoadCompleted(false). Restore-the-bug showed the eternal-pending state verbatim (valid forever, callback never). VaCuus.View.BootFailure.

title: Snapshot focusability is an under-approximation, not RmlUi's exact precondition
description: bAnyFocusable is accumulated during the snapshot walk, but Visit returns early for vacuus-passthrough and for an empty child clip, and RmlUi's CanFocusElement (ElementDocument.cpp:30-44) knows about neither. So bTabEntersFocus is a strict UNDER-approximation: a document whose only focusables sit inside a passthrough wrapper, or inside a collapsed overflow:hidden height:0 container, reports 'Tab cannot enter' while RmlUi enters fine -- and the entering key then double-acts. Fails toward the pre-Task-14 behaviour, so not a regression. Filed because VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.h:350 claims the flags are 'EXACTLY RmlUi's OWN PRECONDITIONS, both of them', which they are not. Mirror finding: the walk passes include_non_dom_elements=true while SearchFocusSubtreeChildren uses the default false, so a non-DOM element with tab-index auto would be a false POSITIVE -- no such element could be constructed (only ElementFormControl.cpp:8 sets TabIndex::Auto, and those are DOM).
close_reason:
Done in 6a32d47. bTabEntersFocus now matches CanFocusElement's reachability. Rather than teach the rect DFS about tab rules -- the two concerns are genuinely different traversals -- the question got its own walk mirroring RmlUi 1:1 (CanFocusElement :30-44, SearchFocusSubtree :728-737, SearchFocusSubtreeChildren :739-750), with the comment showing why FindNextTabElement(document, forward, wrap_around=true) reduces to exactly one SearchFocusSubtreeChildren call when the DOCUMENT holds focus (:675, :679-681, :691, :721, :725) -- which also means the document element itself is correctly not a candidate. Runs at most once per frame, only in the state the flag is read in, early-outs on the first target.

Restore-the-bug: reverting only VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.cpp fails VaCuus.Input.TabReach on EXACTLY three of seven cases and no others -- the passthrough wrapper, the collapsed overflow:hidden container, and the non-DOM child. focus:none, display:none and both controls stayed green, so the test is not 'everything true'.

THE PREVIOUS REVIEWER WAS REFUTED on the non-DOM false positive, and it was real. Their premise held (ElementFormControl.cpp:8 is RmlUi's only TabIndex::Auto setter and its subclasses are all parsed from RML) but the conclusion did not: tab-index is an ordinary registered property (StyleSheetSpecification.cpp:375) and non-DOM elements are style-matched like any other, so ONE LINE of author RCSS constructs one. The test does it -- <progress> appends its fill as a non-DOM child (ElementProgress.cpp:24-27), and 'fill { tab-index: auto; }' produced a document the old code called tabbable and RmlUi provably cannot tab into. The mirror now uses GetNumChildren()'s default include_non_dom_elements=false, matching :741, so it is unreachable rather than unlikely.

Also fixed a SEVENTH comment asserting a mechanism that does not hold, found in the same file: the header said EVaCuusRectFlags::Focusable is 'computed with RmlUi's own rule' for click-focus. It is not -- a click resolves through FindFocusElement, which walks up to the nearest ancestor-or-self with focus != none and NEVER looks at tab-index (Context.cpp:607-619, :631-641), so a click on a plain div does take RmlUi focus. The flag's behaviour is right (Slate keyboard focus is the thing being gated, and stealing the player's keyboard on a background-panel click is what D11 prevents); the comment now describes it as the deliberate narrower policy it is. No behaviour changed.

title: Decide: should a digitized left-stick press enter the UI nav grid at all?
description:
Surfaced and ASSERTED (not fixed) by Task 14's acceptance work, deliberately left for a decision with real gamepad hardware.

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: SVaCuusWidget::OnKeyDown enqueues unconditionally, so a Gamepad_LeftStick_Up/Down/Left/Right key is FORWARDED into RmlUi's nav grid and moves UI focus -- but Task 14's new rule does not CONSUME it, so the game sees it too. That is exactly the double-action the new rule removes for the DPad, on the key family where a walking player is most exposed.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED: the only clean suppression mechanism is D12's pass-through FKey set, which is static and cannot be state-dependent. Suppressing the enqueue would mean a pad player can no longer enter a VaCuus menu with the stick AT ALL -- the analog nav path is gated on bWantsKeyboardFocus (the fix for the M2 critical bug where a held movement stick silently re-focused the HUD and ate player movement), so this accident is currently the ONLY stick-based entry into the UI.

So the choice is: 'a walking player can lose the stick to UI focus' versus 'a pad player must use the DPad to enter a menu'. Both are real costs and it is a design call, not a code call.

MITIGATING CONTEXT worth weighing: OnKeyDown only runs while the widget holds SLATE KEYBOARD FOCUS, which arrives only from a click on a focusable rect or from the game deliberately putting it there. So the exposed scenario is narrower than 'player walking around' -- it is 'the UI already has keyboard focus, nothing inside the document is focused yet, and the player pushes the stick'. Most games do let the left stick drive menu navigation, which argues for keeping it.

VaCuus.Input.NavEntry asserts the CURRENT behaviour, so it will fail loudly whichever way this is decided -- the decision cannot be made silently.
design: Revisit with real gamepad hardware in the M6 platform matrix. If suppression wins, it needs a state-dependent mechanism, not the static pass-through set.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded with its reasoning, the test updated to assert it, and the losing option's cost stated in the code comment.
close_reason: Decided + implemented in a96ecb4 (M6 Task 2): digitized left-stick presses do NOT enter the nav grid by default; vacuus.NavStickPress cvar opt-in at the WIDGET site (a map-site gate would starve the analog-repeat clock — recorded); routing test asserts both ways.

title: Task 12 quality review: buffer-level gate blind spot, per-view observability, two dangerous stale comments
description:
From the Task 12 code-quality review. APPROVED WITH MINOR ISSUES -- no demonstrable bug -- but four items worth doing before M2 closes.

I1 (the important one). bHasResourceTraffic hard-codes the four arrays with NO compile-time link to FVaCuusCommandBuffer's member list. This is the buffer-level analogue of the FVaCuusCommand blind spot and it is CLOSER: the command struct is at least pinned by a static_assert; the buffer's member list is pinned by nothing, and the gate names the four arrays 500 lines from where they are declared.

The trigger is concrete, not hypothetical. The recorder overrides 9 of Rml::RenderInterface's 21 virtuals. The 12 it does not include CompileShader/RenderShader/ReleaseShader (RenderInterface.h:131-140 -- how RmlUi 6 renders decorator: linear-gradient), CompileFilter/ReleaseFilter (:122-125 -- filter: and backdrop-filter:), and EnableClipMask/RenderToClipMask (:78-86 -- rounded-corner clipping). A Gameface-class product needs all three, so they are M3/M4 work, not speculation. The moment one lands it brings a NewShaders/NewFilters map; sizeof(FVaCuusCommand) == 112 still holds because the payload is on the buffer; no test fails; and a document with an animated gradient publishes its first frame and then FREEZES.

Fix costs nothing: move the predicate onto the buffer as bool HasResourceTraffic() const, declared immediately below the four arrays with a comment saying a new array must be added to it. A member declared next to that comment is hard to miss.

I2. The per-view publish/skip counters are unreachable from anything but a unit test -- the recorder is only reachable through a Private host with no accessor on IVaCuusDocumentHost and no path onto FVaCuusViewStatus. Worse, this commit REMOVED the per-view publish count that existed (UVaCuusView::GetFramesPublished -> GetFramesRecorded). Concrete cost: two views, A genuinely idle and B wedged, produce one PROCESS-WIDE 'published=1 skipped=13295' line and nothing anywhere tells you which view contributed. Four lines: add std::atomic<uint64> FramesPublished to FVaCuusViewStatus, which already has the atomic block.

I3. No kill switch. The gate's failure mode is a frozen UI with no error, no ensure, no log -- and it is the first thing anyone will suspect when a UI stops updating, yet the only way to test that suspicion is a rebuild. FVaCuusPerfLog::IsEnabled() already establishes the UI-thread-readable cvar pattern. Natural home for the second-cheapest diagnostic too: a Verbose line on each idle<->active TRANSITION (not per frame).

I4 (dangerous). SVaCuusWidget.cpp:39-42 justifies ForceVolatile(true) with 'the UI thread publishes a command buffer per frame that only a paint drains'. That premise is now FALSE (1 publish per 13,296 frames) while the conclusion became MORE critical: since the RT is the only copy of an idle UI's pixels, Draw_RenderThread running every frame is the sole reason an idle UI stays on screen. A maintainer who reads this, knows about Task 12, and correctly concludes the stated reason no longer applies will remove ForceVolatile(true) -- and under Slate Global Invalidation the draw elements get cached, Draw_RenderThread stops being called, and the idle UI DISAPPEARS with nothing to bring it back. Called 'the single most dangerous stale comment in the tree right now'.

I5. VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.cpp:253-255 -- the Hide() comment is now wrong in both sentences. Hide still works (the first hidden frame's empty command list hashes differently, publishes, and Clear_Store wipes the RT), but the comment says the view 'keeps publishing frames, they are simply empty' and warns that 'skipping the frame would leave the last published content in the RT' -- which is precisely what now happens from frame two onward. A reader trusting it concludes either that hide is broken or that hidden views need exempting.

Minors: the header still says RecordAndPublishFrame 'publishes two things per frame' (now one per frame and one per change); the perf-log comment equating skipped with missing Replay samples is not arithmetic (Draw_RenderThread emits one Replay scope per PAINT regardless of how many buffers queued, so a changing UI at 220 Hz UI / 60 Hz paint gives published 220/s, Replay 60/s, skipped 0 -- the difference is coalescing); VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:353's 'one replay per frame' is no longer true; the one perf claim in the diff ('~600 out-of-line calls is a measurable slice of a 0.04 ms Record') is unmeasured and contradicted in direction by the diff's own numbers, so lead with the determinism argument instead; PublishInteractiveSnapshot is the one frame cost in no perf scope, two lines above a comment arguing that hiding costs makes the perf log lie; and the publish/skip counters are plain uint64 behind VACUUSRENDER_API getters with no thread annotation while every other entry point on the class opens with CheckOwnerThread().

Nits: IdleGateTest's 'command count is part of the frame hash' assertion cannot fail (appending a command adds 112 bytes regardless); the 'restarted view' half of the first-frame test is a tautology on a fresh recorder's NSDMI and would need the host path to test what it claims.
design: I1 is the one with a real future trigger -- do it as a member function next to the arrays, not as a better comment at the gate.
acceptance_criteria: Resource-traffic predicate lives on the buffer next to its arrays; per-view publish count observable at runtime; the two stale comments corrected; kill-switch cvar plus idle-transition Verbose line if judged worth it.
close_reason: Done in the Task 12 quality fix pass (982ec06, 1897320, 920965e). I1: the resource-traffic predicate moved onto FVaCuusCommandBuffer next to the four arrays, guarded by a member-count tripwire -- adding a fifth array without touching the predicate now FAILS THE BUILD, proven by adding one and removing it. A second site enumerating the arrays inline (the recorder's destructor) was found and re-pointed. I2: per-view FramesPublished added to FVaCuusViewStatus so an idle view can be told from a wedged one. I3: vacuus.IdleGate cvar plus a Verbose line on each idle<->active transition. I4/I5 and five minors: comments corrected. The I4 finding itself was partly refuted -- see the memory on Slate cached custom elements.

title: Task 12 review follow-ups: hash tripwire blind spot, test controls, RT-is-only-copy comment
description:
From the Task 12 spec review. Three items, the first is a latent hazard of exactly the kind this feature must not have.

1. THE HASH TRIPWIRE HAS A 7-BYTE BLIND SPOT. VaCuusCommandBuffer.h asserts sizeof(FVaCuusCommand) == 112 and offsetof(Geometry) == 8, with a message promising that an unhashed field cannot slip through. It catches a field appended after Transform, or anything that changes sizeof. It does NOT catch a field declared between Type and Geometry that fits the existing padding -- a uint8/uint16/uint32 lands at offsets 1-7, leaves sizeof at 112 and offsetof(Geometry) at 8, passes silently, and goes UNHASHED. That is precisely the 'false unchanged -> visibly stale UI with no diagnostic' failure the assert advertises preventing. Fix: four more offsetof clauses (Texture == 16, Translation == 24, Scissor == 32, Transform == 48).

2. IdleGate.HashPadding's positive controls mutate one representative scalar per field GROUP (Translation.Y, Scissor.Max.Y, Transform.M[3][1]), proving each group participates but not each of the nine scalars. A copy-paste bug of the form Image.Scissor[1] = Command.Scissor.Min.X would leave Scissor.Min.Y permanently unhashed and every assertion in the file would still pass. The nine assignments are correct today -- verified by hand -- but the test does not defend them. Fix: five more one-line mutations (Translation.X, Scissor.Min.X/Min.Y/Max.X, a second matrix cell).

3. A NEW HAZARD THE TASK INTRODUCED, worth a comment even though nothing exploits it today. Before the gate, every frame republished, so any lost or unreplayed buffer self-healed on the next frame. Now, on a static UI the render target is the ONLY copy of the pixels and the recorder will never resend them. FVaCuusReplayRenderer::ReleaseResources() resetting LastConsumedGeneration = 0 is therefore load-bearing in a way it was not before: any FUTURE path that drops the RT without also destroying the recorder, or that discards an unreplayed buffer, becomes a PERMANENTLY blank UI rather than a one-frame glitch. Put that on ReleaseResources().

Also: the comment dismissing Rml::Context::GetNextUpdateDelay as 'a timer hint' is stronger than RmlUi's header justifies -- the header presents it as an on-demand-rendering mechanism (Context.h:284-286). The real reason it cannot serve here is different and worth stating correctly: it is forward-looking, returns infinity when the answer is 'wait for input', and says nothing about whether the frame just recorded differs from the last one.
acceptance_criteria: Four offsetof clauses added so a padding-slot field fails to compile; five more scalar mutations in HashPadding; ReleaseResources carries the RT-is-the-only-copy note; the GetNextUpdateDelay comment states the accurate reason.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 13 (23f3181 exact-EOF Tell, a117ba7 private VaCuusRml dep, df2164b task-10 follow-ups, c82a2ce task-12 follow-ups, 5d0a36b self-correction). 31/31 tests green; both the editor and the MONOLITHIC game target rebuilt Succeeded, and the monolithic target genuinely recompiled Module.VaCuusRender.cpp so the dependency change was exercised rather than assumed.

6.1: verified the clamp at UnixPlatformFile.cpp:177 (FileOffset = NewPosition >= FileSize ? FileSize - 1 : NewPosition) before coding. Rml::FileHandle now carries handle + logical position + cached size; Seek moves only the position and Read re-syncs the handle. RmlUi's contract was checked in the vendored header rather than assumed POSIX. Restore-the-bug: reverting Tell() to the handle gave 4 failures (Tell 15 instead of 16; empty-file EOF reporting 18446744073709551615), and reverting the whole pre-fix pair gave 6, adding 'a read returns 0, not the last byte again'. NEW FACT WORTH KEEPING: the exact-EOF clamp is UNIX-ONLY -- both Windows read handles accept InPos == FileSize and report it -- so this fix makes Unix agree with Windows rather than inventing a third contract.

6.4: premise confirmed before acting -- zero RmlUi includes anywhere under VaCuusRender/Public/, and in fact no Build.cs in the plugin or the host project even names VaCuusRender.

6.32 (task-12 spec review): D1's stated fix WAS WRONG AND THE FINDING IS WORSE THAN STATED. A uint32 between Type and Geometry occupies offsets 4-7 and shifts nothing: sizeof stays 112 and every other member keeps its offset, so offsetof is structurally incapable of seeing it. Verified by building it both ways. What catches it is a MEMBER COUNT check -- FVaCuusCommand is an aggregate, so brace-initialising it with one initialiser too many is ill-formed inside a requires-expression. The four offset clauses were kept anyway for a different reason: they catch REORDERING (swapping Texture with Translation leaves both sizeof and the member count intact). Restore-the-bug: the padding-slot field now fails compilation with 'FVaCuusCommand gained or lost a field'; with the pre-change assert it compiled clean. D2 also got an unrequested restore-the-bug -- the exact copy-paste slip named in review now fails, and passed the whole file before.

6.23: gitignored in the canonical repo.

title: Policy: first nav press is both consumed by the UI and seen by the game
description: Task 7 finding: bWantsKeyboardFocus is false while only the document holds focus (per D9), so the FIRST direction key is enqueued (moving UI focus) AND answered Unhandled (game sees it too) — in a real game the camera twitches on the first DPad press. Same for analog nav, which is deliberately emitted regardless of bWantsKeyboardFocus so the bootstrap press can reach the document. Needs a per-view 'document is up and navigable' policy bit. Decide at Task 14 acceptance, do not widen silently.
close_reason: Decided in M2 Task 14 (c6d7726): the press that ENTERS the UI's focus is consumed and not also given to the game; activation keys (Return/NumpadEnter/Space/FaceButton_Bottom) keep the old rule; digitized left-stick keys are excluded. Implemented by PREDICTING RmlUi's own preconditions rather than approximating them -- two snapshot flags, later refined to a 4-bit direction mask because 'nav' is a Box shorthand, so 'nav: vertical' declares all four directions and acts on two (an ANY-of bool swallows strafe; an ALL-of bool reintroduces the double-action). Activation keys are excluded for a checkable reason: with nothing focused they resolve to the document, which has no tab-index auto, so they do nothing and consuming them would eat a player's jump for free. The remaining left-stick question is split out as 6.35.

title: Verify snapshot-vs-input-dispatch frame ordering empirically on Linux
description: Task 5 review found the documented rationale is backwards on Linux: FLinuxApplication::AddPendingEvent dispatches input synchronously during FPlatformApplicationMisc::PumpMessages (LaunchEngineLoop.cpp:5784) — BEFORE GEngine->Tick (:5859) where PollStatus refreshes the snapshot cache — because GPumpingMessagesOutsideOfMainLoop is only ever set on Windows. So input in frame N sees the cache built in frame N-1, one frame older than VaCuusView.h claims; cursor updates (TickPlatform, later in FSlateApplication::Tick) end up fresher than mouse dispatch. The single-stable-snapshot-per-dispatch-batch property still holds. Verify empirically with log timestamps/Insights once SVaCuusWidget lands in Task 6 and correct the header rationale.
close_reason: Verified empirically on Linux during M2: input dispatches during PumpMessages, i.e. BEFORE GEngine->Tick, so the snapshot a handler reads is one frame old -- observed directly (frame 396 consuming generation 394). That ordering is why the snapshot is cached game-thread-side once per frame: every handler in a frame then sees one stable geometry instead of a moving target.

title: LoadModuleChecked on the UI thread (LoadTexture) — same hazard class as the fixed Engine::Get()
description: Task 4 found that FModuleManager::LoadModuleChecked refuses to serve a module to a non-game thread (assert NotLoadedByGameThread) — FVaCuusEngine::Get() was fixed by injecting the reference. One instance remains: FVaCuusRecordingRenderInterface::LoadTexture calls LoadModuleChecked<IImageWrapperModule>("ImageWrapper") on the UI thread (VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:~121). Works during normal frames but is the same crash class during load/unload windows. Fix by caching the module pointer at boot from the game thread; Task 11 rewrites this path anyway.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 11 (a177662) + fix cycle (4dde61b, eebeb52). Async DECODE only -- the payload arrival travels in band through FVaCuusCommandBuffer::NewTextures rather than out of band into the replayer's map, because an out-of-band arrival would have been installed but never re-replayed once Task 12's idle gate landed. Async UPLOAD deferred to 6.25 with a measurement (~1 ms of render thread per 4 MB).

Proven end to end in a live headless PIE run, not just by unit contract: with a deliberately slow 6000x6000 decode, UI frame 3 shows the transparent 1x1 placeholder and frame 300 shows the real payload, same asset and same command. Decoding 36M pixels cost the UI thread nothing measurable (Update max 0.095 ms, indistinguishable from steady state). Zero ensures fired, including the replayer's unknown-handle ensure under exactly the condition it guards. Evidence in docs/research/proofs/m2-t11-async-texture/.

6.12 folded in: the IImageWrapperModule lookup is now cached once from the game thread in StartupModule via LoadModulePtr. The bug was real but LATENT rather than deterministic -- ModuleManager.cpp:935-939 returns an already-loaded module even off the game thread, so it would only have crashed on a session where ImageWrapper had not yet loaded when the first UI-thread LoadTexture ran.

Follow-ups filed rather than folded: 6.25 async upload, 6.26 module unload racing a decode, 6.27 unsized-view drain window, 6.28 small comment/guard fixes, 6.30 grayscale UEJPEG, and 6.31 -- a P1 that predates M1, where .bmp/.dds in a document hard-crash the editor because those wrappers check() on the requested format.

title: Batch adjacent draws that share a texture — the atlas win VaCuus does not have
description:
MEASURED, NOT SUSPECTED (VaCuus-dqs.4, commit 0ebaebe). The 200-icon catalogue drawn
from 200 separate files and drawn as 200 sprites of ONE atlas issue THE SAME NUMBER OF
DRAWS: 201.0 per replayed frame either way -- one per element plus the background.

So the classic reason to build an atlas does not apply to VaCuus. RmlUi emits one
geometry per element (Element::Render -> RenderManager::Render), the recorder records
one RenderGeometry command per call, and FVaCuusReplayRenderer::Replay replays that
buffer 1:1. Nothing anywhere looks at whether two consecutive draws happen to carry the
same texture handle.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a merge pass over the recorded command stream that concatenates
runs of adjacent RenderGeometry commands sharing a texture (and shader, and scissor
state) into one draw. The recorder is the natural place -- it already owns the command
buffer and the handles -- and the replayer would then issue what it is given, unchanged.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING, and it is bigger than atlases: the SAME merge collapses runs that
share the FONT ATLAS, which is most of the text in any HUD, and runs that share the 1x1
white texture flat-coloured boxes draw with. A 250-element screen is mostly those two.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE BUILDING IT
  - Adjacency is not enough on its own: two draws sharing a texture may be separated by a
    scissor change, a layer push or a transform, and merging across one of those is a
    rendering bug rather than an optimisation. The merge must break on any state command.
  - Vertex indices are per-geometry and would need rebasing into the merged buffer.
  - The idle gate must not be disturbed: the content hash is computed over the recorded
    buffer, so a merge changes what hashes -- deterministically, but it must be
    deterministic, or a static screen starts republishing.

ACCEPTANCE: the catalogue's atlas arm drops from 201 draws to a small number while the
loose arm stays at 201 -- the two arms already exist and already print the figure, so
this bead's evidence is one command away on either side of the change.
notes:
2026-08-13: INVESTIGATED BEFORE BUILDING, and the finding is that this should NOT be built yet. Two things came out of reading the replay path and measuring it.

1. THE DESIGN IS HARDER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED, and for a reason the bead did not name. Per draw the replayer sets TWO batched shader parameter blocks (VS and PS) plus a stream source, and the VS parameter is Projection = Translate * CurrentTransform * Projection -- where Translate comes from THAT COMMAND'S translation. So adjacent same-texture draws do NOT share their parameters, and merging them cannot just skip the redundant work: it requires BAKING EACH TRANSLATION INTO A MERGED VERTEX BUFFER, rebuilt per published frame. Meanwhile the PSO bind is ALREADY redundancy-checked (BindPipeline early-outs on an unchanged PS/DS pair, VaCuusReplayRenderer.cpp:999), so the 'fewer state changes' win people expect from an atlas is partly already there.

2. THE PRIZE IS SMALL. Measured on the 200-icon catalogue -- 201 draws, the most draw-heavy screen this plugin has -- Replay on the render thread is p50 0.090-0.102 ms, avg 0.125 (win) / 0.236 (all). That 0.090 ms is an UPPER BOUND on what batching could recover, and it includes render-pass setup and clears that batching would not remove. For scale, the project's own passport puts the game thread at 0.008-0.012 ms/frame and a 1,732-node reference HUD at 1.05 ms on the UI thread.

AND IT ONLY COSTS ANYTHING ON PUBLISHED FRAMES. A blank document produced ZERO Replay samples in the same run -- the idle gate withheld publication entirely -- so a screen that is not animating pays none of this at all.

So: a per-frame merged-buffer rebuild, in the render path, with index rebasing and a merge that must break correctly on every state command, to recover at most 0.09 ms on a deliberately extreme screen that only pays it while animating. Dropped to P3.

REOPEN WHEN any of these is true: a real screen shows Replay as a material share of a frame budget (the perf log already prints it); element counts reach the thousands, where the per-draw cost stops being linear in something small; or a platform turns up whose draw calls are much more expensive than this desktop Vulkan one -- mobile is the obvious candidate, and VaCuus-ma3 is where that would surface.
2026-08-13: DETACHED from the VaCuus-dqs epic and left standing on its own. It was discovered while measuring that epic's catalogue, not scoped by it -- the epic was about texture MEMORY and delivered that; this is a draw-call optimisation whose own measurement says it is not worth building yet. Keeping it as an epic child would have made a finished epic read as unfinished.

title: PsData adapter: optional glue module/example feeding VaCuus models from a UPsData tree
description:
Optional glue module (or example project) bridging PsData (https://github.com/PushkinStudio/PsData) into VaCuus data binding. NOT a core dependency — the core stays zero-dependency and keeps consuming plain USTRUCTs; this is a convenience + marketing-synergy layer for teams already on PsData (both plugins are Pushkin Studio).

**What it does:** subscribe to DMETA(Event) change events on a UPsData tree, auto-fill a view-model USTRUCT from configured PsData paths (e.g. Game.Battle.Characters -> struct fields), call View->UpdateModel. PsData = source of truth, VaCuus model struct = screen projection (classic model/view-model split).

**Why not core integration (analysis from 2026-08-13 session):**
- Incompatible data shape: VaCuus channel consumes UScriptStruct + plain FProperty; PsData stores values in its own field system (FDataField) inside a UObject graph. A bridge is a new sampler comparable in size to FVaCuusModelLayout/FVaCuusModelSampler, not reuse.
- No real binding optimization: cross-thread cost (struct copy into TTripleBuffer) stays regardless; diff-walk on quiet frames is already avoidable by not calling UpdateModel. The 1000-row store pain (VaCuus-wgq) is fixed by UI-side virtualization, not by the data source.
- Product positioning: hard-coupling Gameface-class middleware to a third-party data model is an anti-feature for buyers.
- PsData public repo is low-activity (last commit 2024-12-27 "Add support for UE5"; .uplugin still says UE4). UE 5.8 compatibility must be verified first — that is step one of this bead.
- Threading: PsData is game-thread-only UObject world (zero IsInGameThread asserts). All event subscription and view-model fill happens on the game thread; the existing VaCuus channel handles the crossing. Never call RmlUi from PsData callbacks.

**Shape options (decide at design time):** separate VaCuusPsData plugin/module with an optional dependency, vs. a documented example in docs/buyer showing the subscribe->fill->UpdateModel pattern by hand. Start with the example; promote to a module only if demand shows up.

**Do by demand** — no current buyer asked for it.

title: Mobile input fine edges: DPI click/scroll threshold, multi-touch capture, iPad hardware-keyboard composition, iOS caret ints
description: The remainder after VaCuus-ujm closed the two headline mobile gaps (touch scroll d7bbe56, virtual keyboard 192a1b8, both verified by finger on iPhone 11 Pro 2026-08-12). (1) SetDensityIndependentPixelRatio never set — TOUCH_CLICK_MAX_DISTANCE*ratio uses 1.0, several times too tight on high-DPI phones (Context.cpp:978); needs per-view DPI plumbing + device tuning. (2) Multi-touch: capture is one bool, every finger dispatches button 0; the touch ledger only decides whom to cancel. (3) iPad+hardware keyboard: RequiresVirtualKeyboard() false and iOS has no ITextInputMethodSystem — OnKeyChar carries typing, composition genuinely unavailable (stated in TickVirtualKeyboard comment). (4) SetSelectionFromVirtualKeyboard declined: iOS's two ints have undocumented index space (IVirtualKeyboardEntry.h:66) — needs on-device research before a caret mapping is trusted.

title: Unity-порт VaCuus: исследование завершено, архитектура переносится
description:
# Unity-порт VaCuus: вторая реализация вокруг общего ядра

Рисеч 2026-08-12 (три параллельных захода: карта нашего кода на 673d574, заголовки Unity 6000.5.8f1 с диска, публичные доки/changelogs Gameface и Noesis). Вывод: архитектура переносится почти один-в-один, ниша пустая, но по объёму это не порт, а вторая реализация — ~половина продакшн-кода заменяется, тестовый корпус заново.

## Почему архитектура выживает

Gameface и Noesis на Unity сходятся ровно на нашей схеме: нативное ядро + C#-обёртка, запись команд на своём треде, реплей на рендер-треде Unity через plugin events, вывод в per-view текстуру, трансляция ввода на стороне движка. Интеграции RmlUi↔Unity не существует (официальный список интеграций RmlUi: Godot/UE4/O3DE/bgfx/…, Unity отсутствует; единственный C#-биндинг — chicken-with-lips/rmlui.net, ~7 коммитов, без рендера).

Несущие конструкции имеют прямые аналоги (проверено по PluginAPI-заголовкам 6000.5.8f1):
- Свой UI-тред: Unity плагинным потокам не мешает; IUnityProfiler.RegisterThread даёт его в профайлер.
- ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND → CommandBuffer.IssuePluginEventAndData (колбэк на рендер-треде).
- Персистентный per-view RT: first-class. Vulkan-интерфейс (IUnityGraphicsVulkan) отдаёт VkDevice целиком и делает layout-переходы за нас (AccessTexture/AccessRenderBufferTexture + PipelineBarrier); D3D12 — command list + fence + RequestResourceState; D3D11/Metal проще. Обёртка: Texture2D.CreateExternalTexture либо рендер прямо в Unity RenderTexture через GetNativeTexturePtr.
- Снапшот-хит-тест переносится дословно: uGUI требует синхронный ответ в ICanvasRaycastFilter.IsRaycastLocationValid (UI Toolkit — override VisualElement.ContainsPoint) — та же проблема, что Slate, наш снапшот — готовый ответ.

Два структурных отличия: (1) ввода/IME на нативном уровне у Unity НЕТ вообще — только C# (legacy Input.compositionString/compositionCursorPos либо InputSystem Keyboard.onTextInput/onIMECompositionChange), заметно беднее ITextInputMethodContext; (2) lifecycle-владелец — C#-обёртка под IL2CPP-ограничениями (AOT, [MonoPInvokeCallback] static, статическая линковка iOS), пульс — PlayerLoop-инъекция.

## Карта нашего кода (673d574)

49k строк продакшна + 39k тестов; vendored ~160k компилируемых (RmlUi+quickjs) переносится как есть (CMake вместо UBT).

- ~13k engine-agnostic, переносится почти без правок: весь VaCuusJs (JsDom.cpp — ноль UE-типов), VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.cpp, IR командного буфера + content-hash гейт, record-only RenderInterface, glass distiller, FileInterface (логика резолва), TranslationVariable, ScriptDocument.
- ~11k тонкий адаптер, механическая замена TArray/FString/FRunnable/TSpscQueue/TTripleBuffer/FEventRef на std-эквиваленты. Сюда входит цикл UI-треда (RunFrame: drain → data apply → JS pump → record → GC — движка не касается).
- ~26k глубоко UE, переписывается: Slate/RHI-слой (реплеер 1.4k + виджеты + RDG glass-цепочка), рефлексия data binding по FProperty (~4.7k: ModelLayout/DataVariable/WriteRouter/ModelSampler), UObject-обвязка (Subsystem/View/Bundle), IME (VaCuusTextInput.cpp 1.6k), BundleMount на FByteBulkData, InputMap (FKey), LiveReload (DirectoryWatcher). Плюс 602 строки .usf (UI/Blur/Gradient/Material) и 2 материальных шейдера.
- 39k тестов привязаны к UE automation целиком.

Утечки UE-типов в «портируемое» ядро, которые придётся вычищать: EMouseCursor::Type в снапшоте (VaCuusInteractiveSnapshot.h:361), FKey в input-событии (VaCuusInputEvent.h:149), FXxHash64Builder в хеше кадра, IImageWrapperModule + UE::Tasks в декодере текстур рекордера. Шрифты — чистые: FreeType внутри RmlUi (RMLUI_FONT_ENGINE_FREETYPE=1), UE-шрифтовая система не используется вовсе; FontRegistry — упорядоченный реплей LoadFontFace, порядок несущий (fallback-порядок RmlUi).

## Новые статьи расходов (чего в UE-версии не было)

1. Реплеер без RHI. Либо нативный бэкенд на каждый API (Vulkan/D3D11/D3D12/Metal — путь Noesis RenderDevice, самая дорогая часть), либо managed-реплей через Unity CommandBuffer/Mesh (путь dear-imgui-unity; у Gameface managed-бэкенд есть как штатная опция). Managed — один код на все API и все SRP; для v1 экономит месяцы. IssuePluginCustomTextureUpdateV2 как pixel-upload путь не годится (нет Vulkan/D3D12).
2. Data binding заново: источник модели — C#-объекты, а не FProperty. C# собирает снапшот модели → маршалит в ядро (blittable + IntPtr, без строк на кадр). Это проектирование, не порт.
3. SRP-налог: Built-in/URP/HDRP — три пути композита; по changelogs Noesis это постоянная статья каждый релиз Unity (injection points, RenderGraph-эра). У Gameface — трифуркация через scripting defines.
4. Итерация в редакторе: Windows-редактор никогда не выгружает нативные DLL; domain reload не сбрасывает нативные глобалы — process-global initialised/CoreData RmlUi должен переживать повторные managed init/shutdown против живой библиотеки. Плюс device-reset события (Initialize/Shutdown/Before/AfterReset) — пересоздание GPU-ресурсов.

## Оценка (для знающего ядро)

- Выделить engine-agnostic ядро в C++-либу с C API (вычистить UE-контейнеры, CMake): 1–1.5 мес
- C#-обёртка: lifecycle, PlayerLoop, ввод, raycast-фильтр: ~1 мес
- Managed-рендер (CommandBuffer) + шейдеры: 0.5–1 мес
- Data binding на C#-моделях: ~1 мес
- IME/текст (потолок платформы ниже UE): 0.5–1 мес
- Bundle/VFS (формат наш) + live reload (FileSystemWatcher): ~0.5 мес

MVP уровня M2-демо (managed-рендер, десктоп): ~5–6 чел-мес. Полный продукт (нативные пер-API реплееры, мобилки, три SRP): 10–12+, плюс постоянный SRP-maintenance, которого в UE нет.

## Первый шаг, окупающийся без Unity

Вынести ~13k engine-agnostic строк в отдельную библиотеку. UE-плагин от этого чище (границы ядра станут проверяемыми), а опция Unity-порта дешевеет радикально. Конкретные первые мишени: EMouseCursor/FKey/FXxHash64/IImageWrapper из ядра, std-эквиваленты в UIThread/Queues/ViewStatus.

Источники: PluginAPI-заголовки 6000.5.8f1 (IUnityGraphics.h, IUnityGraphicsVulkan.h, IUnityRenderingExtensions.h, IUnityProfiler.h, IUnityEventQueue.h), docs.coherent-labs.com (unity-gameface: technicaloverview, rendering, plugin_architecture), noesisengine.com (Unity3DTutorial, RenderingTutorial, changelogs 3.1/3.2), github.com/mikke89/RmlUi/discussions/186, github.com/chicken-with-lips/rmlui.net, github.com/realgamessoftware/dear-imgui-unity, issuetracker.unity3d.com (DLL unload).

title: IME warning names FLinuxApplication on every non-desktop platform — the wording lies on a phone
description: Found during the first on-device iOS run (2026-08-12, iPhone 11 Pro): the predicted IME warning fired, but its last clause reads 'Only FWindowsApplication and FMacApplication implement it; FLinuxApplication does not.' On iOS that sentence names the wrong platform — the CLAIM (no ITextInputMethodSystem here) is right, the wording is misleading anywhere but Linux. Find the warning in Source/VaCuus (VaCuusTextInput area), reword to name the RUNNING platform or drop the platform enumeration; grep for siblings with the same pattern.

Confirmed live on iOS device log 2026-08-12: 'IME: IOS exposes no ITextInputMethodSystem ... Text entry here goes through the platform's virtual keyboard ... FVaCuusVirtualKeyboardEntry in VaCuusRender.'

title: Quest research leg: what stands between the proven Android boot and UI in the headset
description: Follow-on from VaCuus-ma3/-3nl/-2so. WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN: the exact pipeline Quest needs (Android arm64, Vulkan ES3_1) compiles, cooks, packages, boots and renders — the emulator run of 2026-08-11. WHAT QUEST ADDS, each to be answered from source, not assumed: (1) THE HEADSET CANNOT SEE OUR FLAGSHIP PATH — the composite Slate element rides the 2D viewport overlay, which UE renders to the spectator/companion surface, not the stereo eye buffers; in-HMD UI must go through world panels (we have them: UWidgetComponent-pattern quad, stereo-correct by construction as a scene primitive) or stereo layers (we have no integration). (2) Motion-controller ray input for world panels is NOT wired: FVaCuusWorldInputProcessor consumes POINTER events and traces from the cursor; a WidgetInteractionComponent-analogue for VaCuus panels is new work. The touch-latch bug is NOT a blocker — fixed in VaCuus-61d. (3) Mobile Multi-View (instanced stereo) vs our world-panel material path — untested. (4) Glass/backdrop over scene color under the mobile renderer + XR compositor — expect degraded/unavailable; research §glass notes the backbuffer-sampling gate on Android. (5) XR2 perf, UI thread scheduling, and app suspend/resume under VrApi/OpenXR runtime — unknowns from the ma3 list, sharpened by VR frame-timing sensitivity. (6) Toolchain: Quest needs the Meta OpenXR plugin and Android packaging with specific manifest flags — enumerate what the engine's Oculus/OpenXR path pins. DELIVERABLE: research note + implementation beads, mirroring how ma3 was run.

title: gotchas #22 got an observable: the stale-FText detector
description:
Filed AFTER the fact, as the record of a correction rather than as work to do -- it is already implemented and closed with this description.

Owner asked whether the new findings had been FIXED or merely written down. The honest accounting was: gotchas #5's two corrections were real documentation defects and were fixed; #21 (parse-time text does not re-translate) is a design boundary we chose explicitly, with {{ t.key }} as the opt-in escape, so there is nothing to fix; and #22 was the real gap.

#22 is not fixable and that IS the design: an FText field is projected culture-invariant once, on the game thread, inside Sample(), which is what keeps the UI thread away from FTextLocalizationManager. The plugin holds no pointer to the game's live struct so it cannot re-push. But the failure was completely SILENT, and this project's own rule says an invariant with no observable will rot -- the same argument that justified vendored patch #5 for fonts one commit earlier. Leaving one silent and fixing the other was the inconsistency worth removing.

SHIPPED: models carrying FText are stamped on a table change and warned once, by name, if 60 UI frames pass with no applied update. Deliberately generous, because a false accusation is worse than a late one.

THE ASSERTION THAT MATTERS is the second model in VaCuus.Translation.StaleText -- one that publishes every frame and must NOT be accused. A warning that tells a developer their text is wrong must never say that to someone whose text is right; without that half this feature would be noise.

Restore-the-bug both ways: dropping the arming call fails 'the model nobody re-pushed is REPORTED'. 227/227 green; both targets build. gotchas #22 and localization.md updated to quote the warning.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in the same session it was filed; the bead exists as the record, not as a task. Evidence is in the description and in commit e7f9d78.

title: Manual matrix: four cells never executed, and the macOS column was never merged into the table
description:
Split out of VaCuus-akj.10 (M6) at its close, 2026-08-09. The matrix is M6 acceptance line 6;
these are the cells it does not actually have, recorded so the table stops implying it does.

NEVER EXECUTED ANYWHERE (row / platform / why):

  15  macOS   Shipping ignition flags. Packaging was never attempted on the Mac at all.

  (Row 5, IME composition, is NOT in this list on purpose: it is bead VaCuus-akj.6.19, which

THE DOCUMENTATION HALF, and it is the part that misleads a reader today: the macOS pass ran
2026-08-03 and answered 12 of 15 rows, but it wrote its results into
docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-macos-results.md and NEVER MERGED THEM BACK. Every macOS cell in
2026-08-vacuus-manual-matrix.md still reads "owner hw", so the one table anybody consults says
a whole platform is unrun when it is not. A warning paragraph now sits above the table pointing
at the results document; the fix is to fill the 15 cells from it and delete the warning.

TWO THINGS THE MERGE MUST CARRY, or it will overstate what macOS proved:
  - Every macOS visual row is an SM5 row. M1 Pro is GPUFamilyApple7 and the SM6 clause at
    MetalRHI.cpp:255-268 needs GPUFamilyApple8, so SM6 never bound. "Our HLSL survives the
    Metal front-end at SM6" is open and needs an M2-or-later Mac or an SM6 cook.
  - Row 8 (glass) passes there via the BOUNDED-COPY route, not the direct SRV -- Metal does
    not set ShaderResource on the Slate output. Same route as Win64, different reason to
