  - Row 14 passed but NOT via SIGTERM; the results doc's venue note says how it was ended.

title: Repeat the lobby visual + state-model pass on Win64 and macOS
description:
Owner-hardware leg of VaCuus-a1k, split off so that bead can close on what Linux can answer.

WHAT LINUX HAS DONE (a1k runs 1-4): all seven checklist groups. All five screens loaded and
LOOKED AT; navigation proven for all four navigable screens; every body-class family in the
state model exercised with a logged observable; zero RmlUi warnings across every session.

WHAT THE OTHER TWO PLATFORMS HAVE: Win64 ran groups 2 and 3 only (a1k run 2, 2026-08-08 at
9c6ca5a -- 4/4 PT Sans faces, chrome-over-content at 1920x1080, one navigation, chrome loaded
once). macOS has never run the lobby demo at all: the 2026-08-03 pass hit "chrome.rml is not
served by any DevUI root" because the demo still lived in the plugin, and by the time that was
resolved (akj.25 moved it to VaCuusDemo, where its content already was) the pass was over.

WHY IT IS WORTH REPEATING RATHER THAN ASSUMING. The two defects a1k actually found are content
authoring bugs (VaCuus-o7n) and would reproduce anywhere -- but the pass also exercises text
shaping across four PT Sans faces, image decode of 61 PNGs, and the interactive-region
snapshot's measured geometry, and those are the three things a different rasteriser, a
different Metal/D3D12 shader path and a different DPI story could each move. A rect table that
differs by a pixel is a finding; one that differs by 40 is a bug.

WHAT TO RUN, and it is now cheap because the instrument exists:
  vacuus.LobbyDemo.State   NEW in run 4 -- body classes, remembered state, and every marked
                           control's box BY ID. Drives the whole checklist without measuring
                           anything off a stylesheet by hand.
  The seven-family sequence and its exact coordinates are in a1k's run-4 comment; on another
  platform the coordinates are the OUTPUT, not the input -- read them from LobbyBox first.

HARNESS TRAP, from run 4: the scheduled delays run from the GAME's frame 0, not process
start, so a session must outlive boot + last delay + margin. A killed session drops the rest
of the schedule silently, and a missing State line looks exactly like a state that did not
change.

title: Two lobby screens draw text on top of other text: career's level pair, and store's refresh note under chrome's chat bar
description:
Found 2026-08-08 by the first VISUAL pass over all five lobby screens (bead VaCuus-a1k,
run 3, Linux/Vulkan headless at 1920x1080). Both are authoring defects in the demo's own
sheets -- the renderer places every box exactly where the RCSS asks.

(1) career.rcss: THE LEVEL READOUT SITS ON ITS OWN "NEXT LEVEL" LABEL.
    .pc-level  right: 36px; top: 38px;  font-size: 26px   ("LEVEL 42")
    .pc-next   right: 24px; top: 46px;  font-size: 13px   ("LEVEL 43")
    Same right lane, 8px apart vertically, and the 26px line is ~31px tall -- so
    "LEVEL 43" is drawn inside "LEVEL 42" and both are unreadable. career.rml:22-23.

(2) store + chrome: TWO DOCUMENTS CLAIM THE SAME CORNER, and this one is the more
    interesting of the pair because no single stylesheet can see the collision.
    #store-rotation  (store.rcss:285-294, CONTENT view)  left: 40px; bottom: 46px
    #chatbar         (common.rcss:132-140, CHROME view)  left: 40px; bottom: 46px
    Byte-identical anchors in two different documents in two different contexts. On
    screen "STORE REFRESH IN: 2 DAYS 14 H" (26px amber italic) lands on top of the
    "[SQUAD]: ..." bar.

WHY THE EXISTING GATES MISS BOTH: tools/verify_preview.py asserts on the DOM, not on
rendered boxes, so neither overlap is visible to it; and (2) is invisible to ANY
single-document check by construction -- the chrome/content split means nothing owns
"the screen's bottom-left corner". A browser twin renders both the same way; nobody had
looked at the pixels until this run.

NOT A PLUGIN DEFECT either way -- zero RmlUi warnings across all five screens, and the
measured interactive-region snapshot agrees with the sheets. This is content.

FIX IS A DESIGN CALL, deliberately not made here: (1) wants .pc-next moved below the XP
track or onto the left of the lane; (2) wants a reserved chrome-owned bottom band that
content sheets are told not to use (the durable fix), or store's note moved. Worth
stating the reservation as a rule in Content/DevUI/README.md either way, because the
next screen to use bottom-left will collide again.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-08-09, VaCuusDemo 783d86e, both defects fixed and both fixes MEASURED rather than
reasoned. The owner chose the durable option: a written rule plus both moves, not two nudges.

(1) CAREER. .pc-next left top:46px -- inside .pc-level's ~31px line -- for top:104px. The right
lane now has one row per line: LEVEL 42, the XP bar, LEVEL 43, then 12 240 / 18 000 XP, with
.pc-xp moved to 124px to make room. Read off a 1920x1080 screenshot: four separate rows.

(2) STORE + CHROME. The rule first, because the nudge alone would only have moved the problem:
THE BOTTOM 100PX OF THE SCREEN BELONGS TO chrome.rml. It is written in Content/DevUI/README.md
under "The reserved chrome band", with the reason it can never be enforced automatically --
chrome and content are separate RmlUi contexts in separate views, so no document can see the
other's boxes, and verify_preview.py asserts on the DOM anyway -- and restated beside #chatbar
in common.rcss so the next author meets it where they would collide. #store-rotation moved to
bottom: 110px.

AND MOVING IT FOUND A SECOND COLLISION, which is the finding worth keeping. #ft-card is
bottom-anchored too (bottom: 120px, fluid height BY DESIGN), so the note at 110 ran straight
through the card's lower edge -- and because both boxes sit on the same axis, that overlap
happens at EVERY window height rather than at one size. This is the same class of bug as the
original in a new costume, and the first screenshot after the move is what caught it. The card
now ends at bottom: 160px, which it was explicitly built to absorb ("internals are
distributed... so the card fills any window height"). Final layout, bottom-up: chrome band ends
at 100, the note occupies 110..141, the card starts at 160.

EVIDENCE: headless shots of career and store at 1920x1080, plus the store corner again at
1366x768 -- the second resolution is the point, since a bottom-axis fix that only clears at one
height is not a fix. Both read clean; zero RmlUi warnings or errors across every run.

CARRIED: preview/shots/*.png are now stale for these two screens. They need playwright, which is
not installed on this machine. The twins themselves are NOT stale -- preview/*.html <link> these
sheets rather than inlining them, so a browser already renders the fixed layout.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-09 to this bead's closing note, and to the commit message's last paragraph.

I recorded "preview/shots/*.png are now stale... they need playwright, which is not installed
here". Both halves were wrong.

PLAYWRIGHT IS AVAILABLE. The browsers were already in ~/.cache/ms-playwright; what was missing
was only the Python package, and `python3 -m venv /tmp/pwenv && pip install playwright` gets it
in one step -- which is exactly what Content/DevUI/README.md already said ("any playwright
install; /tmp/pwenv works"). I checked for the venv, found it absent, and concluded the tool was
unavailable instead of reading the line that says how to make one.

AND NOTHING WAS STALE IN THE REPOSITORY, because none of it is IN the repository:
.gitignore:46-47 excludes Content/DevUI/preview/*.html and Content/DevUI/preview/shots/
entirely, with the reason written above them -- they are regenerable from the tracked .rml/.rcss
by tools that read nothing outside Content/DevUI. (img/ was deliberately REMOVED from that same
block on 2026-08-08, because prepare_assets.sh bakes it out of the Dawg repo and a fresh clone
could not reproduce it.) So the shots are local output, and a fresh clone regenerates them from
this bead's fix without ever seeing an old one.

BOTH TOOLS HAVE NOW BEEN RUN against the fixed sheets:
  tools/shoot.py preview/shots      14 screen captures (career/career_static and
                                    store/store_static carry the fix; verified by eye)
  tools/verify_preview.py           the ~40-check acceptance suite: ALL CHECKS PASSED,
                                    including the store buy flow and the career route
Only those two tools are current generators; the other ~98 files under preview/shots are
one-off review captures from earlier passes (v2_/v3_/rv*/mx_/res_/app_/hv_) that no committed
tool reproduces. They are local, ignored, and dated -- worth knowing before anyone treats one as
evidence of today's layout.

title: The lobby demo refuses by name for missing DOCUMENTS but not for missing ART
description:
Filed 2026-08-08 from a real incident on the Windows box, at the owner's request.

WHAT HAPPENED. The owner ran the lobby from a desktop shortcut on a fresh clone. It booted,
laid out correctly, and drew every card as a flat colour block. The first hypothesis -- his and
mine -- was a load RACE in the async image-decode path, which is a reasonable guess because that
path exists and had just produced a real bug (VaCuus-akj.24, two queued buffers fighting over one
texture handle). It was not that. Content/DevUI/img/ was gitignored, so the clone had none of the
61 PNGs, and the engine was reporting it honestly the whole time:

  Warning: Failed to open file 'img/hero.png' (resolved to '<plugin>/Content/DevUI/img/hero.png')
  Warning: LoadTexture: failed to read 'img/hero.png'
  Warning: [Rml] Could not load texture: img/hero.png

Three lines per image, ~60 lines, and NOTHING on screen that says the art is missing rather than
broken. The art is committed now (VaCuusDemo 1a373da), so this bead is not about that clone -- it
is about the shape of the failure, which will recur.

THE PRECEDENT TO MIRROR IS ALREADY IN THE SAME FUNCTION. Toggle() checks its DOCUMENTS up front
and refuses by name (VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp:1585-1595):

  for (const TCHAR* RequiredVfsPath : {GChromeVfsPath, GLobbyVfsPath})
      if (VaCuusContentPaths::ResolveExistingDocument(RequiredVfsPath).IsEmpty())
          Error: "'%s' is not served by any DevUI root (%s). This demo needs the VaCuusDemo
                  project's Content/DevUI documents; nothing was created"

That message is exactly right and it is why a missing chrome.rml costs nobody a minute. Art gets
no such check, so a missing image costs an hour.

TWO FAILURE MODES, AND AN EXISTENCE TEST ONLY CATCHES ONE. That is the part worth getting right:

 1. FILE ABSENT -- what happened here. ResolveExistingDocument() returns empty. Easy.
 2. FILE PRESENT AND IS AN LFS POINTER -- what happens on a machine that cloned WITHOUT git-lfs
    installed. The file exists and is ~130 bytes of text beginning
        version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1
    so an existence check PASSES, the open succeeds, and the failure moves to the PNG decoder --
    same blank cards, different log line. This is not hypothetical: the project's own
    lfs-objects-live-on-github-origin memory records 'git-lfs installed BEFORE the clone, else
    the checkout writes pointers and git lfs pull is the repair'.

So the check should sniff the first bytes of ONE representative image rather than merely stat it,
and say which of the two it is -- 'not served by any DevUI root' vs 'is a Git-LFS pointer, run
git lfs pull'. One file is enough; they all arrive together or not at all.

WHERE: next to the existing document loop in Toggle(), same shape, same refusal-before-creation
discipline (nothing is created, the viewport is never asked for).

ALSO WORTH A LINE WHILE THERE: the plugin's own demos reference exactly one image,
Content/DevUI/img/avatar.png (m1_hud.rml) -- audited 2026-08-08, 4/4 references resolve. Same
check, one path, if it is cheap.

NOT URGENT: with the art committed both repos are self-contained today. This is diagnosability,
and the measure of it is that the same mistake should cost one log line instead of an hour.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08, and the sniff earned its keep on the first try: the LFS-pointer
case is one an existence check PASSES, and it was watched passing before the fix.

THE SHARED HELPER, in the plugin: VaCuusContentPaths::ProbeImage(VfsPath, &OutDiagnosis)
-> EVaCuusImageProbe {Ok, Missing, GitLfsPointer, NotAnImage, Unreadable}. It resolves
through ResolveExistingDocument (so bundle-first precedence is not re-derived), reads the
first 64 bytes, and classifies: PNG (RFC 2083 3.1) or JPEG SOI -> Ok; the LFS v1 spec's
mandatory first line -> GitLfsPointer; anything else present -> NotAnImage. OutDiagnosis
carries the full sentence INCLUDING THE REPAIR, so no call site can invent a weaker one.

BUNDLES ARE READ IN PLACE rather than skipped, and this was not optional: a bundle hit
returns the deliberately unopenable `bundle://` pseudo-path, so a naive open would report
Unreadable for every image in a bundle-only Shipping build and turn a healthy package
into a refusal. ProbeImage reads the mounted span via ContainsPath + FindEntry instead.

TWO CALL SITES, TWO CHARTERS, and the difference is deliberate:
 - VaCuusDemo VaCuusLobbyDemo.cpp Toggle(): FATAL, beside the existing document loop,
   same refusal-before-creation discipline. The lobby has no fallback.
 - Plugin VaCuusRender.cpp M1/M2 bootstrap: WARNING only. That demo has an inline
   fallback by charter so a bare project still works; bad art must not stop it. It says
   "The HUD still loads; its avatar box will be empty".

THE REPRESENTATIVE IMAGE IS NOT hero.png, and the first draft that used it was wrong.
SuppressHeroCard() removes `#hero` from the DOM after every load (the overdraw pass,
Content/DevUI/PLUGIN-NOTES.md round 4), so the engine NEVER loads img/hero.png -- the
guard would have gated the whole demo on a file the demo deliberately never asks for.
Worse, that same note says the suppressed subtrees may be "cut for real" on the owner's
word, at which point a healthy install would start refusing to boot. Now probes
img/icon_credits.png: chrome.rml loads it, chrome is persistent across all five screens,
no suppression pass touches it. Caught by LOOKING AT THE RENDERED LOBBY, not by reading
the markup -- the hero is simply absent from the screenshot.

EVIDENCE, restore-the-bug on both failure modes at the real call site (Linux/Vulkan,
-game -RenderOffscreen 1920x1080), each broken deliberately and restored:
  A baseline            -> boots, 4/4 PT Sans, chrome view 2 over content view 1
  B img/ moved aside    -> Error: "'img/icon_credits.png' is not served by any DevUI root
                           (<both roots>) and no mounted bundle carries it ... nothing was
                           created"; no views, no fonts, no documents
  C 130-byte LFS pointer-> Error: "... is a Git-LFS POINTER, not an image -- this tree was
                           cloned without git-lfs installed ... Run `git lfs pull` ...";
                           THE CASE AN EXISTENCE CHECK PASSES
  D restored            -> boots again; `git status Content/DevUI/img/` clean
Plugin side, same pointer planted on img/avatar.png: "Warning: ... is a Git-LFS POINTER
... The HUD still loads; its avatar box will be empty", and m2_demo.rml loaded anyway.

UNIT TEST: VaCuus.Core.ImageProbe (VaCuusFileInterfaceTest.cpp) covers Missing, pointer,
non-image, a real PNG signature, and the shipped img/avatar.png over the real resolution
path; it asserts the pointer diagnosis CONTAINS "git lfs pull", because that string is the
whole difference between a one-line fix and an hour. Watched to FAIL first against a stub
that returned Ok unconditionally -- 5 failures, exactly the rows a stub cannot answer --
then pass. Full suite after the change: 219 tests, 0 failures, exit code 0.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the two overlaps a1k's visual pass found are filed as VaCuus-o7n,
not fixed here.

title: No export-surface gate on macOS -- api_export_check is ELF-only
description:
Found 2026-08-07 during the cross-platform re-verification (docs/passport/2026-08-07-cross-platform-reverify.md).

Tools/api_export_check.sh is ELF-only by construction: it reads nm -D from
libUnrealEditor-<Module>.so. macOS modules are libUnrealEditor-<Module>.dylib and Mach-O, so the
script cannot run there at all. Win64 has a twin (api_export_check_win64.ps1, dumpbin); macOS has
nothing, so the third shipping platform's public C++ surface has never been gated.

The rule PORTS UNCHANGED -- verified by hand on 0e1f470 against
libUnrealEditor-VaCuusRender.dylib and -VaCuus.dylib:

  nm -gU <dylib> | c++filt | grep -c 'Class::'

  SVaCuusWidget 44, UVaCuusWidget 21, UVaCuusWorldComponent 47, UVaCuusView 56,
  UVaCuusSubsystem 38, UVaCuusStyleSet 7; FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost 0, FVaCuusSlateElement 0.

TWO THINGS THE SCRIPT MUST GET RIGHT, both learned the hard way in that hand run:

 1. DEMANGLE BEFORE MATCHING. A raw grep for the mangled class name counts PARAMETER mentions --
    SVaCuusWidget::Construct(..., TSharedRef<FVaCuusSlateElement> const&) and
    VaCuusSlateView::MakeDocumentHost(TSharedRef<FVaCuusSlateElement> const&) both contain
    19FVaCuusSlateElement. The .sh already documents this trap and answers it by matching
    'Class::'; the Mach-O version must do the same.

 2. VTABLES ARE EXPORTED ON MACH-O AND ARE NOT A VIOLATION. 'vtable for FVaCuusSlateElement' and
    'vtable for FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost' are both in the dylib's global symbol table while ZERO of
    their members are. That is not the facade leaking -- the class definitions stay in Private/,
    so nothing outside the module can name either type. The naive count reads 3 and 1 instead of
    0 and 0. Say this in the script, or the next reader files a bug against a non-problem.

nm and c++filt are both in the Xcode command line tools, so there is no new dependency.

Also worth doing in the same change: the .sh's own header says 'A Win64 package needs the same
check written against dumpbin' and never mentions Mach-O. Fix that sentence too.
close_reason: Closed

title: 2d6demo: owner decision — every panel stroke in the comps is BRASS (105,93,57), the demo draws #3a3a38
description:
Split out of VaCuus-9ak.2, where it was found and deliberately not taken: it is one token and every panel in the demo, which makes it a design decision rather than a bug fix.

MEASURED, twice, on two different components in two different comps:
  the tooltip card (1_Common of UI_Design_Subsystems.psd, box x 29..624 y 1537..1806):
      stroke sampled (104,93,56) / (106,94,57) / (105,93,57) / (106,94,57) on the four sides
  the action menu's container: sampled identically (recorded on VaCuus-a4g)

The project draws --stroke #3a3a38 (58,58,56) -- a neutral dark grey. The comp's is a brass
one long step down in value from --gold #efcc27, the same family as the brass the screen
title's name span already uses (#736742, itself derived from a comp sample).

WHAT IT TOUCHES: --stroke is used by essentially every surface in components.rcss -- panels,
tabs, cards, slots, the status bar, the rail, the return bar, the tooltip. Changing the token
changes the whole demo's chrome at once, which is the point and also the risk: the screenshots
in docs/img and the whole component catalogue would need re-shooting, and the three README
captures with them.

CHEAPER MIDDLE, if the whole-demo change is not wanted: leave --stroke alone and give the two
measured components a literal brass, the way .screen-title-name already carries its own
literal with the argument written next to it ('the only brass in the project, and a token with
one user is a lie about how widely it applies'). That comment stops being true the moment a
second user appears, which is exactly the decision here.
close_reason:
Можно было бы сделать, но демка сдана.

The finding stands and is recorded in the sheet: every panel stroke in the comps is BRASS, sampled (105,93,57) on all four sides of the tooltip card and identically on the action menu's container, in two different comps by two independent passes. The demo draws --stroke #3a3a38 on all 28 rules that use it.

ONE CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAD COSTED, and it is why this was never a one-token change: --stroke-hot IS --gold (#efcc27), used in 8 rules. Today a hover is grey -> gold, a large jump. With a brass resting stroke it becomes brass -> gold, the same hue only brighter, and VaCuus-9ak.1 has since put a 0.12s fade on most of those borders — so the hover feedback would get quieter in a way that is easy to ship without noticing. Taking the brass means revisiting --stroke-hot in the same pass.

Cost if re-opened: the token, plus re-shooting docs/img's three captures and the whole component catalogue.

title: 2d6demo: the scene plates ride in the UI bundle for nothing (7.5 MB of 9.9)
description:
Content/DevUI/2d6/scene/*.png is inside <Project>/Content/DevUI, so VaCuusContentPaths::GetDocumentRoots() hands the whole directory to the bundle packer: the cooked Demo2d6UIBundle is 85 entries / 9,911,865 bytes, and ~7.5 MB of that is the seven scene plates that NOTHING will ever open through the VFS.

They cannot be served from the bundle: Demo2d6Scene.cpp:172 reads them with FFileHelper::LoadFileToArray off FPaths::ProjectContentDir(), ordinary file I/O the plugin's VFS never sees. So Config/DefaultGame.ini stages them separately (+DirectoriesToAlwaysStageAsUFS=(Path=DevUI/2d6/scene)) and the same bytes ship twice. On Linux the bundle is a RESIDENT buffer, so it is also 7.5 MB of resident memory at boot.

Fix, if judged worth the churn: move the plates to a root the packer does not walk, e.g. Content/Scene, and stage that instead. Touches Demo2d6Scene.cpp:172 (one string), its comment at :162, Demo2d6Scene.h:103, Tools/assets.json (2 out paths), Tools/build_scene_plates.py's usage banner, README's tree and its Assets section.

Left alone in VaCuus-4ph because it changes a layout decision the file argues for and buys disk, not correctness. The real argument for doing it: it makes the demo a bad advertisement for the plugin's bundle footprint.
close_reason:
Можно было бы сделать, но демка сдана.

The seven scene plates (7.5 MB of the bundle's 9.9) sit inside <Project>/Content/DevUI, so the bundle packer walks them, and they are ALSO staged loose because Demo2d6Scene.cpp:172 reads them with FFileHelper off ProjectContentDir -- ordinary file I/O the VFS never sees. Same bytes twice, and on Linux the bundle is a resident buffer, so it is 7.5 MB of resident memory nothing will ever open from.

The fix is a one-string move to a root the packer does not walk (Content/Scene) plus six follow-on edits: the comment at :162, Demo2d6Scene.h:103, two out paths in Tools/assets.json, build_scene_plates.py's banner, and the README tree. Correct and cheap; it buys disk, not correctness, and the package that shipped works.

Worth re-opening if the demo is ever used as an argument about the plugin's bundle footprint -- as it stands it is a bad advertisement for it.

title: 2d6demo: the DEFENCE matrix overflows the turret plate, and at 4:3 it reaches the screen's last row
description:
`.hud-mx-defence` (top: 6.6875rem) plus `.mx`'s own height exceeds `.hud-grid`'s 12.125rem of content, so the matrix's last cell row is drawn BELOW the plate. Pre-existing and stated in the sheet (nothing on this screen sets overflow), but VaCuus-pa9 moved the plate to the screen's bottom edge, so the overflow now lands in the plate's 11px of bottom clearance instead of on empty stage.

Measured, turrets HUD, demo2d6.Scene 0:
  1920x1080  plate bottom stroke row 1068, lowest ink 1069  -> 1px over
  2560x1080  same
  1600x1200  plate bottom stroke row 1190, lowest ink 1199  -> 9px over, and 1199 IS the
             view's last row: three or four empty defence cells touch the screen edge
  1280x1024  plate bottom stroke row 1016, lowest ink 1017  -> 1px over

Not monotonic in scale, so it is layout rounding rather than a fixed ratio -- the 1px cell
borders do not shrink with the rem lengths, and where the rows round is what decides it.
Nothing is clipped at any of the four aspects measured.

NOT FIXED IN VaCuus-pa9 ON PURPOSE: every candidate fix (moving .hud-mx-defence up, or
shortening .mx) moves pixels at 1920x1080, and that bead's whole regression test is that
1920x1080 is unchanged. Fixing it needs its own before/after on the 16:9 shots.
close_reason:
Можно было бы сделать, но демка сдана.

Not a defect anyone will hit by accident and not fixed: `.hud-mx-defence` plus `.mx`'s height exceeds `.hud-grid`'s content box, so the DEFENCE matrix's last cell row draws below the plate — 1px over at 1920x1080, 2560x1080 and 1280x1024, and 9px over at 1600x1200, where it reaches the view's last row. Nothing is clipped at any of the four aspects measured, and 16:9 (which is what the demo was shot and shown at) is the 1px case.

Left because every candidate fix moves pixels at 1920x1080 and would need its own before/after against the shipped captures. Re-open if the demo is ever shown at 4:3.

title: plugin: SVaCuusWidget can be left believing it has no capture while Slate still routes to it (macOS)
description:
Found while clearing SVaCuusWidget as a suspect for VaCuus-sya. Not that bug, and not
reachable through a window-mode change -- but a real stale-state window, buyer-facing on
macOS.

MECHANISM. FSlateUser::RestoreCaptorPathsByIndex (SlateUser.h:193) assigns the captor map
wholesale and sends NO notification. Its only caller is the PLATFORM_MAC block at
SlateApplication.cpp:5518-5526: it snapshots the captors, calls ActivateApplication()
(which runs ReleaseAllPointerCapture at :7140 and so fires the widget's
OnMouseCaptureLost -> MouseCapture flag goes false), and then restores Slate's capture
behind the widget's back.

RESULT is the reverse of the usual stale-capture bug: Slate still routes captured pointer
events to SVaCuusWidget while the widget believes it holds nothing, so a drag that leaves
the interactive rect starts answering Unhandled at SVaCuusWidget.cpp:537 -- the drag dies
mid-gesture. Needs macOS + a held LMB + an application activation, so it is narrow, but a
buyer on macOS inherits it and the plugin has no way to observe it today.

A SECOND, SMALLER ONE in the same area, all platforms: SVaCuusWidget.cpp:567 sets the
capture flag BEFORE Slate confirms the request. If FSlateUser::SetPointerCaptor fails
(SlateUser.cpp:257-282, when the widget is not reachable from the event path)
ProcessReply only broadcasts a debug warning (SlateApplication.cpp:3576-3580) and no
OnMouseCaptureLost ever arrives, so the widget answers Handled for every move of a
capture it never got. Self-heals on the next mouse-up (:650), so the window is one drag
long.

Both want the same thing to be fixable at all: a way for the widget to reconcile its flag
against FSlateUser rather than trusting its own bookkeeping. Note VaCuus-sya added
`demo2d6.InputState` on the game side, which reads the captor out of
FSlateApplication::GetCursorUser()->GetCursorCaptor() -- the same source a plugin-side
check would use.

DO NOT fix in the demo repo; this is /w/Unreal/VaCuus.
close_reason:
Fixed by moving the question to whoever owns the answer. SVaCuusWidget's routing decision now asks Slate (SWidget::HasMouseCapture) instead of its own bool.

BOTH CITATIONS IN THIS BEAD HOLD, opened and read. RestoreCaptorPathsByIndex really is a one-line setter that assigns the whole captor map and notifies nobody (SlateUser.h:191-193), and Epic's own comment above it is "Unclear why from existing code, but Mac seems to need to cache & restore all mouse captor paths when activating the top level window". SetPointerCaptor really can refuse and really is answered by a WITH_SLATE_DEBUGGING trace only (SlateUser.cpp:261-271).

WHY HasMouseCapture IS THE AUTHORITY rather than a second opinion: it reads the same PointerCaptorPathsByIndex the Mac restore writes -- SWidget::HasMouseCapture -> FSlateApplication::DoesWidgetHaveMouseCapture -> FSlateUser::DoesWidgetHaveAnyCapture. The widget already used it for teardown (ReleaseOwnPointerCapture), so this is existing practice rather than a new idea.

WHAT THE FIX DELIBERATELY DOES NOT TOUCH, and the first draft got this wrong: the press and button-up bookkeeping still read the mirror. "Have we already requested capture for this gesture" and "is the last button up" are questions about OUR presses, not about routing. Asking Slate there re-requested capture on the second button of a two-button drag in any venue that does not process replies, and VaCuus.Input.SlateRouting failed immediately -- which is what that regression test exists for.

THE ADOPT IS ONE-WAY for the same class of reason. "Slate holds it" is a fact, so adopting it is always right. "Slate does not hold it" is not the mirror image: our own press sets the flag before the reply is processed, so clearing on it would tear down a live gesture and hand RmlUi a MouseLeave mid-drag. The ANSWER comes from Slate; the flag is left to the button-up and the notification that own it.

TEST: VaCuus.Input.CaptureReconcile reproduces the macOS shape on any platform -- parent the widget into a real added window, find its path, hand FSlateUser the capture DIRECTLY (which is what the Mac restore does), and require the move to be Handled with the flag still false. Reverted and watched to fail on exactly the two assertions that matter. It is the only test in the file that needs a window, because SetPointerCaptor refuses a widget it cannot find a path to.

THE SECOND, SMALLER HALF is fixed in production by the same line -- the answer comes from Slate either way -- but the test could not REACH that state and says so in an AddInfo rather than pretending: in this venue ReleaseAllCapture notifies the widget, so the flag cannot be left standing. Producing it honestly would need a refused SetPointerCaptor, which is a fixture about Slate's internals rather than about this widget.

Suite 217 -> 218, green on the real RHI (-RenderOffscreen Vulkan). VaCuus 3b4df14, merged.

STILL OWED, and it is the venue and not the code: nobody has held a real drag on macOS across an application activation. What the fix rests on is the engine source above plus the reproduced shape; the macOS column of the manual matrix is where the wild version would show.

title: two allocation-counting tests are unreliable when the full suite runs on a real RHI
description:
Found while running the full suite on a real RHI to exercise VaCuus-sw1's new GPU
tests. The canonical venue is -nullrhi and all 204 pass there, every time; the
real-RHI venue is where these two misbehave.

Two runs of `Automation RunTests VaCuus` under -RenderOffscreen (Vulkan, 2026-08-05),
one with the sw1 shader fix and one with the shader reverted -- so the shader is
ruled out:

  with the fix     : VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc FAIL, VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy FAIL
  shader reverted  : VaCuus.Model.Sampler.ArrayAlloc FAIL, VaCuus.RefHud.MemProxy pass
  the two alone,
  shader reverted  : both pass

So ArrayAlloc fails reproducibly under a real RHI inside the full suite, MemProxy
fails intermittently, and neither fails when the two are run by themselves.

The messages say what they are:

  "a warm SyncCopy allocates ~nothing (min 6 <= 4)"
  "canary: RemoveContext freed through GMalloc (frees=14, bytes=+1368)"

Both are GMalloc-traffic assertions with tight absolute bounds. Under -nullrhi
nothing else is allocating while they measure; under a real RHI the render thread,
the RHI thread and the driver are, and a counter that is process-wide picks that up.
It is the measurement that is venue-dependent, not the code under test.

Worth deciding rather than leaving: either scope the counters so foreign threads
cannot contribute, or state that these two are -nullrhi-only and skip them on a real
RHI the way the GPU tests skip on NullRHI. The current state -- a red full-suite run
on the venue where the GPU tests carry their evidence -- makes that run hard to read.
close_reason:
Same defect as VaCuus-gq6 and fixed by the same change -- see that bead for the mechanism and the numbers.

This bead's own question ('either scope the counters so foreign threads cannot contribute, or state that these two are -nullrhi-only and skip them on a real RHI') is answered by the first option. Skipping them on a real RHI was the wrong trade: the GPU tests carry their evidence on that venue, so a suite that is only readable under -nullrhi is a suite with two answers.

Both named tests now pass on both venues, and the numbers got BETTER rather than merely quieter: ArrayAlloc reads min 0 max 0 across all eight windows for both SyncCopy and republish, against a bound of 4 and a previous floor of 11. 'Zero container reallocations; ~0 element allocations' is finally the literal reading of the instrument rather than a claim inside a noise band.

VaCuus 1dad8a5, merged d593544.

title: Game→JS one-shot calls: add CallJs sugar, replace unsafe Printf interpolation
description:
Game code triggers one-shot imperative UI actions (e.g. "open shop window") via UVaCuusView::ExecuteScript(), which evals raw JS on the UI thread's QuickJS-ng engine. The only idiom in the codebase today is a hand-rolled guard + FString::Printf, e.g. VaCuusRender.cpp:2147-2149:

if (typeof vacuus !== 'undefined' && typeof vacuus.onFreeze === 'function') vacuus.onFreeze(%s);

with the JS side registering vacuus.onFreeze = function(isFrozen) {...} (Content/DevUI/m4_hud_logic.js:188-209).

Two problems with calling this at every site by hand:
1. Boilerplate repeated per call site (the typeof/typeof guard).
2. Arguments are Printf'd directly into the JS source string — a string argument containing a quote or other special character is a code-injection bug into our own JS engine, not just a broken call. This is the more important reason to fix it, not just the boilerplate.

No existing InvokeJs/CallJsFunction/DispatchJsEvent symbol exists anywhere in the tree (confirmed by search) -- this is genuinely open, undecided design space. CLAUDE.md's Conventions & Patterns section does not state a preference between ExecuteScript (imperative) and UpdateModel (declarative, via data-if/data-class) for one-shot UI actions; both are exercised in demos for different purposes today.
design:
Proposal: add a thin helper, e.g. UVaCuusView::CallJs(FName FunctionName, ...args), that:
- builds the typeof-guard automatically instead of hand-writing it per call site
- JSON-serializes arguments instead of raw %s interpolation into the JS source
- check whether FVaCuusJsValue (already used for the reverse JS->game direction on the OnModelWrite/OnJsEvent dynamic multicast delegates, VaCuusView.h:97-138) can be reused or mirrored for outgoing argument serialization, instead of inventing a second value type

Relevant call chain (all confirmed by direct code read, cite file:line):
- UVaCuusView::ExecuteScript -- VaCuusView.cpp:237-252 (asserts game thread, enqueues)
- FVaCuusUIThread::EnqueueExecuteScript -- VaCuusUIThread.cpp:698, pushes FVaCuusUICommand{Kind=ExecuteScript} onto the same SPSC command queue as LoadDocument/SetVisible (EVaCuusCommandKind, VaCuusUIQueues.h:117) -- so ordering vs. other view commands is FIFO-safe already, sugar should preserve that
- UI-thread drain/consume -- VaCuusUIThread.cpp:1306-1324, forwards to ScriptHost->ExecuteScript(...) if a script host is registered, else logs an Error (this is also the only failure surface today -- no error propagates back to the game thread)
- FVaCuusJsScriptHost::ExecuteScript -> View->Eval(Source, SourceName) -- VaCuusJsScriptHost.cpp:636-648, real QuickJS-ng engine (Source/VaCuusJs, Source/ThirdParty/quickjs-ng)

Declarative alternative already in use for state (explicitly NOT in scope for this bead -- different use case, already works fine): UpdateModel + data-if/data-class, e.g. Model.bAlert = Model.Health < 30.f (VaCuusRender.cpp:618) driving data-class-alert="bAlert" (m4_demo.rml). Do not conflate the two -- CallJs is for one-shot actions without persistent state, not a replacement for model-driven show/hide.
acceptance_criteria:
- CallJs (or equivalent) helper added to UVaCuusView, building the typeof-guard and serializing arguments safely (no raw FString::Printf of argument values into JS source)
- At least the existing onFreeze call site (VaCuusRender.cpp:2147) converted to use it, as a worked proof
- Scope explicitly excludes request/response RPC (return values, structured error propagation back to game thread) -- stays fire-and-forget like ExecuteScript is today; that is a separate, larger feature if ever needed
close_reason:
CallJs shipped. UVaCuusView::CallJs(FunctionPath, Args) -- Blueprint-callable, dotted path from globalThis, FVaCuusJsValue arguments.

THE BEAD RANKED THE TWO PROBLEMS AND THE RANKING WAS RIGHT: boilerplate is the small one, injection is the real one, and the fix is structural rather than an escaping scheme. CallJs NEVER BUILDS A LINE OF JAVASCRIPT. The path is resolved property by property from globalThis, each argument becomes a JSValue through the same marshaller vacuus.emit uses in the other direction, and JS_Call takes them as data. There is no parser downstream for a string to escape into.

A SEPARATE COMMAND KIND, not sugar over ExecuteScript, because sugar would still have to build 'f(<args>)' as text. Everything else is ExecuteScript's shape: ahead of the per-view host lookup, unknown view refused by the script host at Error, no-script-host refused by the drain, FIFO after a LoadDocument*.

Design answers the bead left open:
-  is the OWNER of the last segment (vacuus.onFreeze sees this === vacuus, as a written call would); a single-segment path gets globalThis.
- a path that resolves to nothing is ONE WARNING, NO THROW -- the hand-written  guard, now in the API.
- ExecuteScript stays and keeps its job: running SOURCE you wrote. CallJs passes DATA you were handed. gotchas.md 11c says exactly that.

PROOF, not just tests: the one production caller (VaCuusRender's M4 freeze command) converted and driven end to end in a live -game run -- 'm4_hud_logic: frozen (beats paused, rAF inert)' then 'm4_hud_logic: running (beats re-armed)'.

VaCuus.Js.CallFunction.Arguments sends  as a string and asserts the payload did NOT run, arrived as ONE argument, byte for byte -- then puts THE SAME STRING through the old Printf idiom on the same view and asserts pwned === 1. The bug is demonstrated, not asserted. Plus all four value kinds as primitives, , multi-segment paths, and a second string of every character an escaper fears. .Refusals covers the four quiet failures and the one loud one.

Two self-inflicted findings kept in the file: a test named exactly 'VaCuus.Js.CallFunction' silently never ran while '.Refusals' existed (prefix shadowing in the controller's tree, green 66/66 with no skip line), and a log-count assertion written as 3 that is 2.

Suite 215 -> 217, green on the real RHI. VaCuus 053094e, docs 3fc4d8f-ish, merged.

title: The Win64 machine has no .NET Framework SDK — every editor target needs an AutoSDK shim to produce a makefile
description:
win64-results section 2, owner decision 5. Not a plugin defect -- the control settles authorship: a stock TP_ThirdPerson project with no VaCuus at all fails identically in 3.4 s.

  Unable to instantiate module 'SwarmInterface': Could not find NetFxSDK install dir
  (referenced via TP_ThirdPersonEditor -> Launch.Build.cs -> ... -> UnrealEd.Build.cs)

SwarmInterface.Build.cs:29-34 throws outright when Target.WindowsPlatform.NetFxSdkDir is null on Win64, and UnrealEd depends on it. The SDK is genuinely absent, checked four ways: no NETFXSDK under either Windows Kits path, no registry key in either view, no .NETFramework reference assemblies, no mscoree.h or mscoree.lib on the volume. Only the .NET RUNTIME (v4.0.30319) is installed.

The pass did not touch the owner's Visual Studio. It used a sandboxed AutoSDK shim: MicrosoftPlatformSDK.cs:357-367 probes $(UE_SDKS_ROOT)/HostWin64/Win64/Windows Kits/NETFXSDK/<4.6.2|4.6.1|4.6>/Include/um/mscoree.h (UEBuildPlatformSDK.cs:1150 supplies HostWin64), so that path was created under C:\VaCuusWin64Test\autosdk with a stub header and UE_SDKS_ROOT was set PER BUILD PROCESS ONLY, never in the user or machine environment. The shim is demonstrably inert: this Installed engine ships UnrealEditor-SwarmInterface.dll prebuilt, its LastWriteTimeUtc is byte-identical before and after all six builds, no build log contains a SwarmInterface action, and the stub header is #error-ed so an actual include would have failed loudly.

OWNER ACTION: install VS component Microsoft.Net.Component.4.6.2.SDK (or 4.8.SDK) and the shim becomes unnecessary. Everything the pass created lives under C:\VaCuusWin64Test and deletes with it. Until then, every future Win64 editor build on this machine needs the shim re-created, which is a trap for the next session.

notes:

title: VaCuusBundleMount's resident-buffer log asserts a reason that is factually wrong on Windows
description:
win64-results section 9, owner decision 7b. VaCuusBundleMount.cpp:89-94 prints 'resident buffer (FPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() is false on this platform)' whenever the mapping did not take. On Windows that parenthetical is FALSE: WindowsPlatformProperties.h:76-79 returns true. So on the one platform where the memory-mapped path actually exists, a failed mapping explains itself with a reason that cannot be the reason, and whoever reads the log is sent away from the real causes (pak alignment, compression).

The trap is recorded in the pass notes as 'read bMemoryMapped, not the sentence' -- which is exactly the shape of comment CLAUDE.md says to replace with code that cannot lie.

FIX SHAPE: split the message. One line for 'this platform has no memory-mapped files' (query the predicate, do not assume it), another for 'the platform supports it and the mapping still did not take', which is the interesting case and should say so.
acceptance_criteria: The log line's stated reason is derived from the predicate rather than assumed, and the supported-but-unmapped case has its own distinguishable message.
close_reason: Already fixed by 825969f (2026-08-03 16:06, hours after the Win64 pass that reported it). VaCuusBundleMount.cpp:98-108 now branches: the resident line prints 'this platform DOES support memory mapping -- the load returned no mapped region, so the mapping was refused or the payload was not cooked memory-mappable' when FPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() is true, and only claims the property is false when it actually is. The comment above it also corrects the wider premise the pass repeated: 'only Win64 maps' is false -- Win64, Android and iOS all answer true; Linux and Mac inherit false from FGenericPlatformProperties (GenericPlatformProperties.h:258-261). Verified in the tree, commit is an ancestor of master. Filed and closed in the same session because the bead was reconstructed from the pass write-up, which predates the fix.

title: The Win64 export gate exists and passes, but lives in a scratch dir — decide whether Tools/ takes PowerShell
description:
win64-results section 6, owner decision 7a. Tools/api_export_check.sh is ELF-only and says so (bead dgl is why it exists). The Win64 twin was written for the 2026-08-03 pass, run against the built DLLs, and PASSES including its own self-test: 5 supported classes reachable (UVaCuusWidget 27 exported member refs, UVaCuusWorldComponent 53, UVaCuusView 66, UVaCuusSubsystem 39, UVaCuusStyleSet 14), FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost correctly at 0, absent-class self-test reports 0 so the FAIL path works, and exported JS_* symbols = 0 -- confirming vendored patch #1 (hidden quickjs visibility) on PE/COFF, a third binary format after ELF and Mach-O.

The mechanism differs from Linux and the script says so: on Linux -fvisibility-ms-compat lets a class register while exporting zero linkable members; on Windows nothing is exported without the module's _API macro, and UHT stamps that macro on the generated registrar regardless of what the class declares -- so the FAILURE SHAPE is identical and the check is meaningful.

It should be committed as Tools/api_export_check_win64.ps1. The only open question is whether this repo wants a PowerShell script in Tools/ at all, or whether the check should be reshaped (python driving dumpbin, say). Losing it is the bad outcome: it took a pass to write and it guards a shipping-shape property no other check covers.
acceptance_criteria: The Win64 export check is in the repo under a decided form, and runnable from documented steps.
close_reason:
Rewritten and landed as Tools/api_export_check_win64.ps1 (6b82e4a), verified on DESKTOP-590NICV against the very DLLs the pass measured.

THE OWNER'S 'SHIP IT AS-IS' COULD NOT BE HONOURED LITERALLY: the script is NOT in the pass's scratch. C:\VaCuusWin64Test is still on the machine, and a content search for 'dumpbin' across it, %TEMP%, Documents and Desktop returns exactly one hit -- docs/buyer/owner-handoff.md, i.e. a mention, not the file. The pass ran it inline over SSH and it went with the session. So the choice was between losing the check and re-earning it; it was re-earned.

VERIFIED against Binaries/Win64 built 15:19-15:42 on 2026-08-03: 27 / 53 / 39 / 14 member references, FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost 0, self-test 0, exported JS_* 0, totals 385 / 143 / 2 / 1746 / 2. Every number reproduces except UVaCuusView -- 65 here against the pass's 66 -- and the cause is pinned rather than waved: ?GetImeStatus@UVaCuusView@@... names the class twice in its undecorated form (nested return type UVaCuusView::FImeStatus, then the qualified method name). The pass counted occurrences; this counts exported symbols, which is what a buyer can link and what the Linux twin's grep -c already counts.

ALSO CORRECTED: §6's mechanism sentence ('UHT stamps that macro on the generated registrar regardless of what the class declares') contradicts UhtHeaderCodeGeneratorHFile.cs:833, where the generated class body takes Module.Api only for a MinimalAPI class and NO_API otherwise. The check is still meaningful on Windows, for the reason the new header states: registration needs no export of the module's own, so a class with no _API macro registers, works in Blueprint, and cannot be linked -- the same failure shape Linux gets from -fvisibility-ms-compat (LinuxToolChain.cs:439) by a different route.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: OWNER DECISION 2026-08-03: it goes in as-is, at Tools/api_export_check_win64.ps1. PowerShell in Tools/ is accepted rather than rewritten -- the script already ran green against real DLLs including its own FAIL-path self-test, and a rewrite would put an unverified check in the repo. REMAINING WORK IS RETRIEVAL, not authorship: the file lives in the 2026-08-03 pass scratch on the Win64 box (under C:\VaCuusWin64Test), which is the same directory tree the pass says deletes with itself -- so it is one machine wipe away from being lost. title: BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes for Win64 has never been run (the monolithic half is done)
description:
win64-results section 9, two adjacent 'not attempted' rows.

(1) MONOLITHIC / GAME TARGET, not attempted on Win64. The pass notes why it matters and why it would NOT have caught the biggest build finding: B5 (RmlUi's dll-interface on header-only class templates, fixed in 38e1318) cannot fire in a monolithic build because RMLUI_STATIC_LIB makes the macro empty. So the two build shapes are not substitutes for each other in either direction, and only one of them has ever been exercised on this platform. CLAUDE.md already treats the monolithic leg as a pre-milestone gate on Linux.

(2) BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes for Win64, not run. The Linux and macOS legs have it; it is the check that catches a header which only compiles because something else included its dependencies first, and MSVC's two-phase lookup differs from clang's, so this is the platform where it is most likely to find something.

Both are hands-off-keyboard buildable -- neither needs an interactive desktop -- so this bead is NOT blocked on 5fg, unlike most of the Win64 backlog.
acceptance_criteria: A Win64 monolithic game target builds, and BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes for Win64 runs, both with their output recorded.
notes:
[replayed from the Win64 console session -- verbatim]
2026-08-03 console pass: HALF DONE. Scope narrowed to leg (2) only.

(1) MONOLITHIC / GAME TARGET — DONE.
    Build.bat TP_ThirdPerson Win64 Development -project=...\VcHost.uproject
      -> Result: Succeeded, 888 s, 358 actions, TP_ThirdPerson.exe 337,195,008 B.
    It also needed NO AutoSDK shim: SwarmInterface is reached via UnrealEd, and a game target does
    not depend on UnrealEd. UE_SDKS_ROOT was unset in machine, user and process scopes and the
    makefile generated anyway. (That fact narrowed akj.10.9 — and then the cook un-narrowed it; see
    that bead.)

    AND IT EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN, which is exactly what this bead predicted. One warning:
      ...\ThirdParty\RmlUi\Source\Core\Layout\ContainerBox.cpp(141) : warning C4756:
      overflow in constant arithmetic
    ContainerBox.cpp:141 is `available_space.y = HUGE_VALF;`. The overflow is deliberate and lives
    in Microsoft's own header — corecrt_math.h:90-99 defines _HUGE_ENUF as 1e+300 with the comment
    "_HUGE_ENUF*_HUGE_ENUF must overflow", INFINITY as ((float)(_HUGE_ENUF)), HUGE_VALF as
    ((float)INFINITY); narrowing 1e+300 to float overflows on purpose, which is how the header
    manufactures infinity. So the diagnostic is benign.

    WHAT IS NOT BENIGN IS THAT THE MODULAR LEG CANNOT SEE IT. The same TU
    (relay_Core_Layout_ContainerBox.cpp) is compiled by both targets — 190 relay_Core_* actions in
    each — and the modular editor build emits nothing for it; its /experimental:log SARIF sidecar
    for that TU contains ZERO results, so it is not a log-capture artifact. Cause isolated rather
    than inferred: the only substantive difference between the two response files is /fp:precise
    (editor) vs /fp:fast (game), and two lines reproduce it on demand —
        #include <math.h>
        float f() { return HUGE_VALF; }
        cl /c /W4 /fp:precise -> clean ; cl /c /W4 /fp:fast -> warning C4756
    Consequence worth remembering: bWarningsAsErrors is an OR (UEBuildModuleCPP.cs:2669), so the
    day anything upstream turns /WX on for a game target this becomes a build stopper, on Windows
    only, in vendored code, from a flag nobody set deliberately. Recorded rather than silenced,
    because silencing it in the module would also hide any REAL constant overflow.

    This is B5's mirror image and the reason the bead insisted on both shapes: B5 cannot fire
    monolithically because RMLUI_STATIC_LIB empties the macro; C4756 cannot fire modularly because
    the editor target compiles /fp:precise. Neither shape substitutes for the other, in either
    direction. Recorded in docs/passport/2026-08-vacuus-win64-results.md section 12.3.

(2) BuildPlugin -StrictIncludes for Win64 — STILL NOT RUN. It kept getting queued behind the two
    Shipping cooks and the Development re-stage, which claimed the machine for the rest of the
    session. This bead stays open for exactly this and nothing else:
      RunUAT.bat BuildPlugin -Plugin=<clone>\VaCuus.uplugin -Package=<out>
                 -TargetPlatforms=Win64 -StrictIncludes
    Still hands-off-keyboard, so it needs no console session. Note the CLAUDE.md hazard about
    BuildPlugin's HostProject editor leg rewriting UnrealEditor.modules before running it here.
close_reason:
DONE 2026-08-04, and the answer is: nothing found, which is the result this leg existed to produce.

  RunUAT.bat BuildPlugin -Plugin=C:\VaCuus\VaCuus.uplugin -Package=C:\VaCuusStrict\Package
            -TargetPlatforms=Win64 -StrictIncludes
  EXIT=0, 2,687 s, 994 files in the package.

THE FLAG IS VERIFIED IN EFFECT RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because a silently-ignored flag would have produced exactly the same green: the log says 'Building with precompiled headers and unity disabled', UBT is invoked with -NoPCH -NoSharedPCH -DisableUnity on every leg, and 929 of the 936 compile actions name an INDIVIDUAL .cpp. The only seven Module.* translation units are the UHT-generated Module.<X>.gen.cpp, one per module, which exist with or without unity.

THREE LEGS, ALL 'Result: Succeeded':
  UnrealEditor Win64 Development  335 actions  1,080 s
  UnrealGame   Win64 Development  305 actions    911 s
  UnrealGame   Win64 Shipping     305 actions    692 s

FINDINGS: NONE. In 1,059 log lines the only diagnostic is C4756 'overflow in constant arithmetic' at the vendored RmlUi ContainerBox.cpp:141, twice -- once per GAME leg, never in the editor leg -- which is the same benign HUGE_VALF construction the monolithic build already reported on this bead (Microsoft's own corecrt_math.h manufactures infinity by deliberate overflow), and whose editor/game asymmetry is /fp:precise versus /fp:fast, already recorded. So under MSVC with PCH and unity off, no header in this plugin compiles only because something else included its dependencies first. Given that this was the platform most likely to find one -- MSVC's two-phase lookup is stricter than clang's -- that is worth having asked.

THE CLAUDE.md MANIFEST HAZARD DID NOT FIRE: Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor.modules is byte-identical before and after (SHA256 BBE466E4...8747, mtime 2026-08-03 11:13:35), measured by the script rather than assumed. That is an Installed engine; the hazard was recorded against a source engine and this does not refute it.

BONUS, on the artifact rather than on intent: this package comes from a REAL full run, unlike the -NoHostPlatform filter-only run bead avu was verified with. It carries README.md and docs/buyer's four pages, and no Binaries/ -- so avu's fix holds on the actual upload shape produced on Windows.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT ON THIS BEAD:
 1. I said the run 'probably died with the SSH session'. IT DID NOT. The link dropped about four minutes in and the machine then left the network for over an hour; the build ran to completion regardless and wrote its whole log. Windows did not reap the child when the session ended. The 'launch it detached' lesson stands as good practice, but the loss I reported was a loss of VIEW, not of work.
 2. The machine had not rebooted -- uptime at recovery was 1,234 minutes. It was off the network, not restarted.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text:
ATTEMPT 2026-08-04, NOT COMPLETED — the machine went offline mid-build, and the run was not detached, so this is a venue loss rather than a finding.

WHAT GOT ESTABLISHED ANYWAY, so the next attempt does not re-learn it:

BuildPlugin builds the plugin against the HostProject's EDITOR target, which reaches SwarmInterface through UnrealEd, so without UE_SDKS_ROOT=C:\VaCuusWin64Test\autosdk it dies exactly like akj.10.9 says. With it, the editor leg compiled: 'Building UnrealEditor...', MSVC 14.44.35228 toolchain, Windows SDK 10.0.26100, cl.exe running at the 4-minute checkpoint.
 - QUOTE THE UAT ARGUMENTS. Written bare in PowerShell as -Plugin=$Plugin, the token is passed LITERALLY and UAT reports "Plugin 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8\$Plugin' not found" one second in. Build the argument list as an array of double-quoted strings.

WHAT KILLED IT: the process was launched from the SSH session itself. The link dropped ('Connection closed by remote host'), and after that the host stopped answering SSH before the banner AND stopped answering ICMP entirely — so the box went away, not just the shell. A 45-minute waiter timed out without it returning.

Then a dropped link costs the live output and nothing else. The script as shipped (C:\VaCuusSession\strict-includes.ps1) is correct apart from that; only the launch shape changes.

title: Mobile research: what VaCuus actually needs before iOS is a supported platform
description:
RESEARCH ONLY, no implementation — the owner's scope for now is 'only research of tasks within Epic's platforms'. The Mac has the engine's IOS platform extension installed (Engine/Platforms/IOS, Engine/Binaries/IOS, Source/Runtime/Core/Private/{IOS,Apple}), and Xcode 26.0 is present, so the toolchain half is closer than Android's.

Shares most of its risk surface with VaCuus-ma3 (Android) — research them together and only record what genuinely DIFFERS here. The iOS-specific items:

1. JIT IS FORBIDDEN. iOS refuses W^X: no writable-executable pages for third-party apps. quickjs-ng is an interpreter and should be fine, but this must be CONFIRMED from the vendored source rather than assumed — check for any code path that allocates executable memory, and check what our JS_SetGCThreshold/stack handling does. If anything JITs, iOS is blocked outright, and that changes the product's shape.
2. Metal only, and mobile Metal at that (ES3_1-equivalent feature level by default). Our custom pass, the .usf shaders, the composite permutation and the MD_UI material pair all need their ShouldCompilePermutation gates checked against iOS shader platforms. The macOS pass already proved the DESKTOP Metal path works at SM5 and that glass takes the bounded-copy fallback because Metal does not set ShaderResource on the Slate output — mobile Metal is likely stricter still.
3. MEMORY-MAPPED BUNDLE IS LIVE ON iOS: IOSPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() returns TRUE. Same never-executed code as Android — and on iOS the file-mapping and paging rules are their own subject.
4. Touch input and the iOS virtual keyboard — same gap as Android but a different API surface.
5. THE DEDICATED UI THREAD under iOS app lifecycle: backgrounding, suspension, and the OS's willingness to kill a process holding threads. Our UI thread owns every Rml::Context process-wide; what happens on suspend/resume has never been considered.
6. Provisioning/signing and what a plugin must declare to ship through the App Store — plus whether test automation can run on device at all.
7. Bitcode/arm64e, and whether any vendored third party (RmlUi, quickjs-ng, FreeType via the engine) has an iOS-specific build story.

DELIVERABLE: a research note under docs/research/ — per area: works unchanged / needs work with an estimate / blocked, each claim citing engine or plugin source. Then this bead splits into implementation beads.

title: Mobile research: what VaCuus actually needs before Android is a supported platform
description:
RESEARCH ONLY, no implementation — the owner's scope for now is 'only research of tasks within Epic's platforms'. The Mac has the engine's Android platform extension installed (Engine/Platforms/Android, Engine/Binaries/Android, Source/Runtime/Core/Private/Android), but NDKROOT and ANDROID_HOME are unset, so no SDK/NDK toolchain yet.

THE OWNER'S HYPOTHESIS, to be tested rather than assumed: 'apart from mipmap generation and small things, everything should work on mobile'. Several areas suggest it is optimistic; the deliverable is the honest inventory with file:line, not a verdict.

Risk areas to research, each answered from Epic's own platform sources:
1. RHI/feature level — ES3_1 vs SM5 on Android Vulkan/GLES. Our custom replay pass, the .usf shaders and their permutations (VaCuusUIShaders, the composite LinearOutput permutation, VaCuusMaterialDraw's MD_UI FMaterialShader pair): do their ShouldCompilePermutation gates admit mobile shader platforms, and does the mobile renderer even run our ICustomSlateElement path?
2. FGenerateMips on mobile — WillFormatSupportCompute and whether ES3_1 has the compute path at all (the world-panel mips work assumes it).
3. THE MEMORY-MAPPED BUNDLE PATH IS LIVE ON ANDROID. AndroidPlatformProperties::SupportsMemoryMappedFiles() returns TRUE (unlike Linux/macOS, where the generic false sends us down the resident-buffer path). So BULKDATA_MemoryMappedPayload executes for the first time on this platform — code that has never run anywhere.
4. Input — our path is mouse/keyboard/gamepad. Touch does not map today; what does Slate deliver on Android and what would a pointer bridge cost?
5. Text entry — the mobile virtual keyboard is a different model from ITextInputMethodSystem entirely.
6. The dedicated UI thread on a phone: core counts, thread priorities, what UE does about background/foreground transitions and app suspension (our UI thread owns every Rml::Context process-wide).
7. quickjs-ng: interpreter only, no JIT — confirm from the vendored source, and confirm Android has no W^X objection.
8. Glass/backdrop blur: it needs the scene colour; check what the mobile renderer exposes.
9. Packaging/toolchain: what Android needs (SDK/NDK/JDK versions the engine pins), and what the .uplugin/Build.cs must declare — the descriptor currently names no SupportedTargetPlatforms and no PlatformAllowList, i.e. it claims every platform including ones never built.
10. Whether anything in the plugin is Win64/desktop-only by construction (the bundle's mmap branch, VaCuusEditor, the world-panel material preset).

DELIVERABLE: a research note under docs/research/ listing, per area, what works unchanged, what needs work with an estimate, and what is blocked — each claim citing engine or plugin source. Then this bead splits into implementation beads.
notes: 2026-08-11 FULL ACCEPTANCE PROVEN (beads VaCuus-3nl build, VaCuus-2so run): compiles under NDK r27c, cooks ASTC clean, packages APK+OBB, boots on the UE_pixel_6_API_35 emulator under Vulkan (gfxstream/MoltenVK, '-gpu host -feature Vulkan' required) and renders the complete RefHud with live quickjs logic. Remaining before 'supported platform' can be claimed publicly: real-device run, Shipping bundle config, suspend/resume behaviour, touch input (explicitly deferred).

So this bead's acceptance is now: the plugin compiles for Android, cooks, packages, boots, and shows a document. Touch input, virtual-keyboard text entry and hover-dependent behaviour are explicitly OUT of scope until a customer asks.

That reprioritises what the research found. IN SCOPE (blocks 'builds and runs'): the memory-mapped bundle branch, which is LIVE on Android (AndroidPlatformProperties.h:118-121 returns true, unlike Linux/macOS) and has therefore never executed anywhere; the mobile shader cross-compile, which is admitted by our gates but never actually compiled (DXC -> SPIR-V -> SPIRV-Cross for GLES is the untested hop); the SDK/NDK/JDK toolchain, absent on the Mac (NDKROOT and ANDROID_HOME unset); packaging shape (APK/OBB) versus our cooked-bundle story; and the UI thread under application suspend/resume, which nobody has considered and which can kill a process rather than degrade it.

Mipmaps are NOT a problem at all — FGenerateMips gives Android GLES the engine's only dedicated fixed-function branch and Vulkan device-queries the storage bit; all paths degrade, none refuses.

title: World panels: visibility-driven throttle for the UI pipeline (mass in-scene UI)
description:
Filed 2026-08-02 from the owner's question "does an off-screen world panel tick/render?" — the honest answer exposed the gap this bead closes. Matters at MASS in-scene UI scale (name plates, kiosks, terminals: tens-hundreds of panels), where cost scales with panel COUNT, not with visible count.

CURRENT STATE, verified with opened lines:
- The component never ticks by design (VaCuusWorldComponent.cpp:146) — zero tick cost either way.
- The mesh draw IS visibility-culled by the engine: bDrawRelevance = IsShown(View), CanBeOccluded() (VaCuusWorldComponent.cpp:121,130; occlusion query measured 0.47 us in the M5 manual matrix).
- The UI PIPELINE IS NOT: the view Updates + Records on the UI thread every UI frame, JS runs, and each publish drives replay + CopyTexture into the panel RT (+ FGenerateMips as of branch worldpanel-mips, 3da3a82) on the render thread — none of it consults camera visibility. The only throttle is the CONTENT-driven idle gate (WS-COPY-COST, VaCuusWorldComponent.h: 2 publishes / 13,074 recorded frames on a static HUD).
- WORST CASE is a material-decorator document: forced republish clamped to engine rate — such a panel replays+copies+generates EVERY engine frame while completely unseen. This is the biggest single win for the throttle.

DESIGN FORKS to decide (each needs its cost stated):
1. SIGNAL: WasRecentlyRendered(threshold) (engine-maintained LastRenderTime from the proxy, game-thread cheap) vs proxy visibility callbacks (occlusion-precise) vs distance tiers (LOD-style). WasRecentlyRendered is the cheap default; note it goes true from ANY view rendering the panel (shadow/capture passes may count — verify).
2. PAUSE SEMANTICS — the core fork:
   (a) full view pause (Update+JS+Record stop): maximum saving; JS timers freeze and the panel either jumps or visibly catches up on re-show;
   (b) publish-side suspension (Update+JS keep running, Record/publish/copy/mips skipped): saves the render side (~0.4 ms Record at reference scale + replay + copy + mips) and re-shows instantly current — but UI-thread cost remains, so it does NOT solve mass scale;
   (c) rate throttle (e.g. 5 Hz when unseen): bounded staleness, partial saving, no freeze pathologies.
   At mass scale (a) or (c) is the answer; (b) is the safe incremental step.
3. RE-SHOW: the RT is the ONLY copy of the pixels (idle-gate invariant — a dropped publish is permanently stale, see the akj.6.32/6.33 lessons on ReleaseResources). A pause must end with a forced publish-on-wake, and the first frame after re-show is stale until it lands — decide whether that is acceptable (likely yes at distance) and TEST it.
4. INPUT: the world input processor traces against the panel roster; a paused panel should still resolve traces or explicitly refuse — decide and assert (the processor's occlusion rule already handles occluded-but-live panels).
5. THREADING: the visibility signal is game-thread state; pausing the view must cross to the UI thread as an enqueued command per the standing thread invariant. The flag-crossing pattern from SetGenerateMips (worldpanel-mips) is the template.
6. MASS-SCALE ENDGAME (may split into its own bead at implementation time): a global budget scheduler — N panel updates per frame, round-robin over visible panels, unseen panels at floor rate; per-panel RDG builders for mips may want batching at that point.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE (for whoever implements): every fork above gets a recorded decision; the throttle state is OBSERVABLE (per-panel suspended-frame counter + a PerfLog line — an invariant with no observable will rot); tests include the re-show staleness case and a restore-the-bug on the wake-publish; the material-decorator worst case measured before/after; the perf-guide world-panel section gains the numbers.

comments.text:
BLOCKER DIAGNOSED AND CLEARED 2026-08-07. The 2026-08-06 comment above is WRONG on both of its claims -- correcting it here so the next reader does not re-derive a dead end.

CLAIM 1, 'VaCuusDemoEditor.target has an EMPTY Modules map, so UBT built this target
without the plugin'. An empty Modules map in a .target file is NORMAL at UE 5.8:
UnrealPak.target and ShaderCompileWorker.target in the same directory have it too. It is
not a symptom of anything. The real manifest is Binaries/Linux/UnrealEditor.modules, and
the demo project's one lists all five VaCuus modules.

CLAIM 2, 'nothing happens, no module, no view'. The plugin loads fine. A -game run with
-ExecCmds=vacuus.LobbyDemo produces the full boot sequence -- document roots (plugin's
DevUI then /w/Unreal/VaCuusDemo/Content/DevUI), RmlUi init, UI thread, views 1 and 2, the
lobby's chrome-over-content stack, PT Sans faces loaded from the demo project's own fonts.
The earlier run saw nothing because it used VaCuusDemoNoUI.uproject, whose Plugins array
has VaCuus 'Enabled': FALSE. VaCuusDemo.uproject has it true.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is a genuine trap worth keeping: the demo project was
running a FOUR-DAY-OLD plugin. Both VcHostEditor and VaCuusDemoEditor produce an
executable named UnrealEditor, so the plugin compiles into ONE shared intermediate keyed
on that target name (<Plugin>/Intermediate/Build/Linux/x64/UnrealEditor/Development/...)
and links to <Plugin>/Binaries/Linux/. UBT is therefore right to say 'Target is up to
date'. But <Demo>/Binaries/Linux/ still held libUnrealEditor-VaCuus*.so copies from a
2026-08-03 build, the module manager searches the PROJECT binaries first, and both
manifests carry the same BuildId so nothing rejects them. Result: edits to the plugin have
no effect in the demo project, silently, forever.

FIX: delete the orphan libUnrealEditor-VaCuus*.{so,debug,sym} from <Demo>/Binaries/Linux/
(keep the project's own module). Verified -- after the removal the same run loads today's
build. Same family as the CLAUDE.md hazard about BuildPlugin resurrecting stale modules
via UnrealEditor.modules: a stale binary plus a manifest that still names it.

So a1k is NOT blocked on wiring. What remains is the owner's 2026-08-07 direction, which
supersedes this bead's premise: M1-M5 demos stay in the plugin, LobbyDemo becomes part of
the VaCuusDemo project. Filed separately.

title: data-style-* bindings with units defeat the idle gate on every dirty
description:
Found while measuring M3a's acceptance. This is RmlUi behaviour, not ours, but it changes what a HUD author pays and it is invisible to them.

DataViewStyle::Update compares p->Get<String>() against the expression's string (DataViewDefault.cpp:168), and Property::Get<T>() returns the raw variant WITHOUT THE UNIT (Property.h:41-45). So '100' never equals '100%': SetProperty runs on EVERY dirty, layout is invalidated, and the frame republishes even when the bound value did not change.

Consequence for the acceptance numbers, worth recording: this is why one implementer's MarkEveryFieldDirty restore-the-bug run failed the RENDER-level idle gate while an earlier text-only one did not. The spec's claim stands -- for {{text}} and data-attr the render-level test genuinely cannot discriminate, which is exactly why the apply-level assertion exists -- but the render-level test's blindness is VIEW-KIND-DEPENDENT, and that is worth knowing before anyone trusts it alone.

Practical impact: any data-style-* binding whose value carries a unit (%, px, em) costs a relayout per dirty, forever, whether or not the value moved. A HUD with a data-style-bound progress width would never go idle.

Options: document it as a authoring guideline; or normalise the comparison on our side before dirtying; or upstream a fix to RmlUi (the comparison should include the unit).
acceptance_criteria: Either the behaviour is documented where a HUD author will meet it, or the comparison is normalised so a data-style binding with an unchanged value does not relayout.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (42c213e). The code half landed as a ONE-LINE patch to the vendored tree, after the other two options were proven impossible rather than merely undesirable: (1) normalization at our binding layer has NO HOOK — Factory::RegisterDataViewInstancer refuses a duplicate name and warns (Factory.cpp:561-567) so 'style' cannot be shadowed, Element::SetProperty is not virtual (Element.h:177) so no custom instancer can intercept, and DataModel::DirtyVariable takes top-level names only so the coarse dirty cannot be narrowed; (2) an authoring rule + lint CANNOT COVER IT — a percentage bar cannot be written without its unit (the shipped reference HUD itself binds data-style-width="Health + '%'"), and the common shape carries the unit in a UPROPERTY at runtime, invisible to any static check, so the shipped advice 'bind unit-less numbers' was unfollowable. THE FIX: DataViewStyle::Update compares p->ToString() instead of p->Get<String>() — Property::Get<T> forwards to the value Variant (Property.h:41-45) while the unit is a separate member (:50-51), so '120px' read back as '120' and never compared equal. The fork's real danger is a silent re-vendor, so it is recorded the quickjs-ng way: a new Source/ThirdParty/RmlUi/VENDORED_TAG.txt with mechanism, diff, re-vendor procedure and the named verification. VENDORED_SHA.txt deliberately untouched — Tools/gen_rcss_matrix.py:134 reads that whole file and strips it into a generated doc, so a bare SHA is a machine contract. The doc half shipped earlier in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: M6 disposition: carried, doc half landed. perf-guide.md's unit-bearing data-style row (0e1abd7) documents the idle-gate defeat for buyers; the normalization/upstream fix remains v1.x work.

title: RunFrame() has no perf scope: DrainCommands and DrainInput are unmeasured
description:
Found during M3 research. The UI thread's RunFrame() carries no VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE at all, so two substantial pieces of per-frame work are outside every measurement the project has:

- DrainCommands does full document parse and layout on a load
- DrainInput does hit-testing, focus resolution and IME work

This is the UI-thread twin of bead 6.38 (game-thread work outside the scopes), and it matters more now, because M3's per-frame data-model apply lands exactly there. Without a scope, the milestone's own cost cannot be attributed: an apply that costs 0.3 ms would be invisible, and the spec's UI-thread budget row would keep reporting Update+Record only.

Add the scope before M3's apply lands, so the apply's cost is measurable from the first commit rather than retrofitted.
acceptance_criteria: RunFrame's phases are covered by perf scopes; the M3 data apply has its own scope; stat vacuus and the PerfLog distinguish it from Update and Record.
close_reason: Closed as done: RunFrame carries VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE for DrainCommands/DrainInput/DataApply/JsPump/JsGC; stats declared and PerfLog prints every phase (verified in M6 research, p2-sweep.md).

title: RmlUi asserts are compiled out — but its ERROR LOGS are not (premise corrected)
description:
Found during M3 API research, verified through the whole chain:

UBT defines NDEBUG=1 (UEBuildPlatform.cs:1344) -> RMLUI_DEBUG is left undefined (Platform.h:20-21) -> every RmlUi assert is a no-op (Debug.h:45-52). And because RMLUI_LOG_TYPE_ERROR is defined as RMLUI_ERRORMSG (DataTypes.h:74), this silences not just asserts but RmlUi's ERROR-level LOGGING as well.

So in every build we ship or test, the vendored library's entire self-diagnosis is absent. The worst instance found so far is in the data-binding type registry: double-registering a struct returns StructHandle<T>(nullptr, nullptr) SILENTLY, and the next RegisterMember call null-derefs (DataStructHandle.h:125). A crash with no preceding diagnostic, where upstream RmlUi would have told you exactly what you did wrong.

This is not an M3 problem -- it applies to M1 and M2 code already shipped, and to every future milestone. Two things worth deciding:

(a) Should a Development/Debug editor build define RMLUI_DEBUG so the library's own asserts fire during development? That is a one-line Build.cs change, and it would have caught unknown numbers of misuse at authoring time rather than as a crash. Cost: RmlUi's asserts abort rather than ensure, so a misuse becomes a hard stop instead of a wrong picture -- which is arguably what you want in Development.

(b) Independently: anywhere VaCuus calls an RmlUi API whose only failure signal is an assert, VaCuus should check the precondition itself and log through LogVaCuus. Those call sites need finding.

Filed at the plugin level rather than under a milestone because it spans all of them.
design: Prefer (b) for anything already shipped, and evaluate (a) as a development-only define. Do not enable RMLUI_DEBUG in Shipping -- abort-on-misuse is not shippable behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on (a); and the call sites where VaCuus relies on an RmlUi API whose only failure signal is a compiled-out assert are enumerated and guarded.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-07-31 by the M3a pre-merge review, which read Log.cpp rather than inheriting the claim. The original title and description were WRONG on the half that mattered most.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: Rml::Log::Message is an ordinary function that forwards to the registered SystemInterface (Log.cpp:11-31), and VaCuus's own system interface routes LT_ERROR -> UE_LOG(LogVaCuus, Error) and LT_WARNING -> Warning (VaCuusSystemInterface.cpp:73-78). So RmlUi's error and warning LOGGING reaches our log in every configuration.

Only RMLUI_ASSERT / RMLUI_ASSERTMSG / RMLUI_ERROR are compiled out (Debug.h:45-50, gated on RMLUI_DEBUG, which Platform.h:20-21 defines only when NDEBUG is absent).

WHERE THE CONFUSION CAME FROM: the macro RMLUI_LOG_TYPE_ERROR really is defined as the assert macro -- but it exists in only three headers (DataModelHandle.h, DataTypeRegister.h, DataStructHandle.h), i.e. the TEMPLATED type-registration path. M3a's design deliberately bypasses that path entirely via BindCustomDataVariable. So the one place the original claim held is the one place this plugin does not go.

CONSEQUENCE FOR M3a: the milestone's named signature failure is NOT silent. Element.cpp:2218 emits 'Could not locate data model %s in element %s' at LT_ERROR, which lands as 'LogVaCuus: Error: [Rml] Could not locate data model...'. Nine code comments, the M3 spec section 8, and several of my own briefs repeat the false version; being corrected in the M3a fix pass.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND STILL WORTH DOING: RmlUi's asserts are absent, so any API whose ONLY failure signal is an assert still needs VaCuus to check its own precondition. That is now the whole of this issue, hence the priority drop from P2 to P3 -- the diagnostic blackout is far narrower than filed.
close_reason: Decision recorded in a96ecb4 (M6 Task 2) at VaCuusRml.Build.cs: RMLUI_DEBUG stays off in all shipped configs (NDEBUG chain cited); RmlUi's LOGS work, only asserts are gone (the corrected premise); local-debug recipe documented.

title: Test coverage gaps the final review named
description: Four gaps, each of which hid or could hide a real defect. (a) No test drives the idle gate through a real Rml::Context -- all five drive the recorder directly and say so at VaCuusIdleGateTest.cpp:21-31. (b) No test covers live reload THROUGH the gate. (c) The async-decode wake path is tested via GenerateTexture rather than through the decode drain. (d) Close() has no render-side assertion at all -- which is exactly why merge blocker B1 (a closed document staying composited forever) was invisible to every per-task review.
