(a) 'no test drives the idle gate through a real Rml::Context' — ALREADY CLOSED before this session; the cited lines now say the opposite (VaCuus.Render.IdleGate.HoverRecolour drives a real context, VaCuus.Threading.MultiView is the integration check, and there are 7 tests, not the 5 the bead names). (b) 'no test covers live reload through the gate' — OPEN, closed here by VaCuus.Render.IdleGate.LiveReload: real UI thread, real FVaCuusRmlDocumentHost, real FVaCuusSlateElement, observed through the FVaCuusViewStatus counters the game thread actually reads, with the two enqueues an editor live reload really issues. (c) 'async-decode wake tested via GenerateTexture, not the decode drain' — OPEN, and confirmed at the source: ResourceTraffic case 2's own comment claimed the async arrival channel while calling GenerateTexture, the SYNCHRONOUS font-atlas path that never enters DrainCompletedDecodes. Closed by VaCuus.Render.IdleGate.AsyncDecodeWake: real PNG on disk, real LoadTexture, real WaitForTextureDecodes, byte-identical command list across five frames, counters pinned at 3 published / 2 skipped; red leg (swap back to GenerateTexture) fails with 'The drained decode payload wakes the gate to be not null'. (d) 'Close() has no render-side assertion' — ALREADY CLOSED before this session by VaCuusCloseDocumentTest's two tests.

comments.text: M6 disposition: carried. The overlapping gaps landed across M6 (suite 168 -> 186, incl. RefHud.Count/DirtyScope/BlipDriver, MemProxy, LinearOutputSelection/GPU, Js.BundleScript both-ways); the remainder stays per this bead's own list.

title: PerfLog TickLog sorts an unbounded array on the game thread holding the shared lock
description: TickLog appends each window into a Cumulative array forever, then re-copies and re-sorts the WHOLE cumulative array every 5 s for 7 scopes -- on the game thread, holding State.Lock, which is the same lock the UI thread takes in Update/Record and the render thread in Replay/Composite. At 500 input events/s over ten minutes that is roughly a 30 ms sort per window with two other threads stalled behind it. cvar-gated off by default and deliberately outside SlateTick, so the tool's own cost is invisible to the numbers it produces -- which also means 'the measurements already include the lock' is true of the ACQUISITION but not of the contention the tool itself creates.
close_reason: Fixed in 0eb0033 (M6 Task 1): Cumulative[] is a 16,384-sample uniform reservoir (Algorithm R) with exact running Count/Sum/Max; all Summarize() sorts run on private copies after the lock releases. Landed before the M6 passport soaks per the spec's ordering requirement.

title: Game-thread work outside the perf scopes (add OnPaint first)
description: The three scopes added in Task 14 (GameTick, SlateTick, Input) do not cover the whole game-thread path, so the budget gate is met by inference from a 25x margin rather than by complete measurement -- recorded that way in spec 11. Outside all scopes: SVaCuusWidget::OnPaint (per frame, per view, includes an ENQUEUE_RENDER_COMMAND with a lambda allocation), OnMouseEnter/OnMouseLeave/OnMouseCaptureLost (no Input scope), and OnFocusReceived/OnFocusLost (OnFocusReceived does a MakeShared, a global SetNavigationConfig, a ToString() and a nav-direction probe). Add OnPaint first if the budget ever tightens.
close_reason: Closed in M6 (7d54c2f): EScope::OnPaint + STAT_VaCuusOnPaint landed BEFORE the passport soaks per arch §11 row 1's precondition; VACUUS_PERF_SCOPE(OnPaint) in SVaCuusWidget::OnPaint. The five rare-event handlers (OnMouseEnter/Leave/CaptureLost, OnFocusReceived/Lost) remain unscoped by design — recorded in the passport row 1 Method cell and arch §11 amendment as the unmeasured rare-event remainder.

title: Make the cache-clear pairing safe by construction, not by documentation
description:
Follow-on to 6.29's C1, which was resolved by DOCUMENTING the hazard because I scoped restructuring out of Task 13. The Task 13 implementer investigated anyway and reports safe-by-construction is achievable and cheap, so this records the shape.

THE HAZARD: after the C1 fix, the RmlUi stylesheet/template cache clear lives in the EDITOR-ONLY FVaCuusLiveReload::ReloadAllLiveViews, while UVaCuusSubsystem::ReloadAllDocuments() is VACUUS_API and reads as the sanctioned entry point. A runtime reload hook in M3 -- a gameplay debug command, a data-binding hot reload -- that calls ReloadAllDocuments reintroduces the original critical bug verbatim: RML edits apply, RCSS edits silently do not, no error anywhere. Currently guarded only by a warning on the declaration.

THE FIX (implementer's proposal, ~40 lines moved): put the clear-then-fan-out pairing in a static entry point in the RUNTIME module. GEngine->GetWorldContexts() needs only Engine, which VaCuus already depends on. FVaCuusLiveReload::ReloadAllLiveViews then just calls it. ReloadAllDocuments stays the per-instance fan-out and the process-wide door becomes a different, correctly-paired name. Cost: move ~40 lines from VaCuusEditor to VaCuus plus retarget one test.

CHEAPER ALTERNATIVES if that is too much: rename to ReloadAllDocumentsWithoutClearingCaches (ugly but self-documenting at every call site), or give it a mandatory scope enum so a caller cannot omit the decision.

Worth doing before M3 adds the runtime reload hook that this protects against, not after.
acceptance_criteria: A runtime caller cannot reload documents without the cache clear, enforced by the API's shape rather than by a comment.
close_reason:
Done in 65f6cab, and made ENFORCING rather than merely correct. The pairing is a static UVaCuusSubsystem::ClearAssetCachesAndReloadAllViews(const TCHAR*), and ReloadAllDocuments() is now PRIVATE -- a static member reaches a private member without friendship, so the door needs no machinery and nothing outside the class can reach the unpaired half. Proved rather than asserted: temporarily calling Probe->ReloadAllDocuments() from VaCuusRender gave 'error: ReloadAllDocuments is a private member of UVaCuusSubsystem', then reverted. UVaCuusView::ReloadDocument() stays public because 're-read this one view' is a coherent request (the M1HUD fallback re-arm uses it); 'fan out over every view but skip the caches' never is.

The regression test moved with the code: VaCuus.LiveReload.AssetCaches -> VaCuus.Reload.AssetCaches, now in the runtime module, so it guards the door M3 will actually use rather than the editor one.

One change beyond the brief, and it was required: the world-context walk LOST its EWorldType::PIE|Game filter. Its justification was 'a -game process cannot reach this code at all, VaCuusEditor is EHostType::Editor' -- true of the editor module, false the instant the dispatch is Runtime. Rather than keep a comment whose reasoning no longer holds, the filter is gone: the subsystem lookup IS the test, any coarser proxy can only lose views, and it removes the branch the old comment admitted no headless test covered.

title: Task 10 re-review follow-ups (five minor items)
description:
From the re-review of the Task 10 fix commits (fa097c3..4d3d732). Approved with minor issues; these are the five.

1. MOST VALUABLE -- UVaCuusSubsystem::ReloadAllDocuments() is the runtime-facing 'one door' (VACUUS_API) and its doc contract does NOT mention that the RmlUi cache clear is required. After the C1 fix the clear lives one level up, in the EDITOR-ONLY FVaCuusLiveReload::ReloadAllLiveViews. UVaCuusView::ReloadDocument's doc warns about this explicitly; ReloadAllDocuments's does not -- it says 'this is the one door'. So an M3 runtime reload hook (gameplay debug command, data-binding hot reload) that calls ReloadAllDocuments gets C1 back verbatim: RML edits apply, RCSS edits silently do not, and no test catches it because LiveReload.AssetCaches exercises ReloadAllLiveViews. One sentence on the declaration closes it.

2. LiveReload.AssetCaches waits for a FRAME where it should wait for the COUNTER. Trigger() is a coalescing auto-reset latch and FrameCount increments AFTER RunFrame returns, so a leftover latch can give a frame that drains nothing; if that frame passes DrainCommands but not yet the fetch_add when the game thread samples FrameBefore, WaitForFrameCount is satisfied by it and the clear has not been applied -> red on a correct product. Sub-microsecond window, so a rare flake. GetNumAssetCacheClears() is directly observable -- poll IT to a deadline and the race is gone.

3. LiveReload.WatcherEvent writes an untracked probe .rcss into the git-TRACKED Content/DevUI (it must write inside a watched root -- that is the point of the test). git check-ignore says not ignored. Abort the run between write and verify and the probe survives as untracked; a 'git add -A' in this shared worktree commits it. Fix is a .gitignore line, not a path change.

4. I5 only partially closed: DebouncePollSeconds is STILL public under the group comment 'Public so VaCuus.LiveReload.Debounce can assert the timing contract against the same numbers'. QuietSeconds and MaxDeferSeconds genuinely are now; DebouncePollSeconds has exactly two references in the tree -- its own declaration and ArmDebounce. That is the precise defect I5 named, still present for one constant.

5. FlushNow() now has no production caller (M12 made TickDebounceAt call FlushAt directly), reached only from LiveReload.Filter. Its docstring still sells a property for a caller that no longer exists ('safe even when the caller IS that ticker's delegate'). New near-dead code in a commit whose theme was deleting dead code.

Plus nits: 'AutomationTest.cpp:869-870' is off by one at both ends (gate is :870-871, :869 blank); WorldPartitionEditorModule.cpp:719 is the call but the quoted comment is at :717; '~17 callers' of IDirectoryWatcher::Tick is actually 14 external sites and at least three are not one-shot flushes (SlateFileDlgWindow.cpp:1297 is a per-frame widget Tick, UserInterfaceCommand.cpp:117 is UnrealFrontend's main loop); 'FilterPlugin.ini is comments only' -- it does have a [FilterPlugin] section header, just no entries; FVaCuusLiveReload is copyable while handing raw 'this' to an FTSTicker lambda and a CreateRaw delegate (no failure today, one accidental copy from a double-unregister).
acceptance_criteria: Item 1 documented on the declaration; item 2 polls the counter; item 3 gitignored; items 4-5 resolved; nits corrected.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 13 (df2164b). C2 now polls GetNumAssetCacheClears() to a deadline, re-arming Trigger() each poll since WaitForFrameCount does not wake the thread -- and the implementer kept a one-frame barrier AFTER the counter is observed rather than accepting a bare poll-until-1, because two clears land in the same DrainCommands but their counter bumps are a few instructions apart, so a bare poll would have silently discarded the 'one fan-out is ONE clear' half of the test. C3 gitignored by name, and the implementer found the same hole for the .tmptest probe from VaCuus.Core.ContentRoots and closed it too. C4 made DebouncePollSeconds private rather than test-asserted, correctly: TickDebounceAt is judged at times the test chooses, so the poll rate cannot change any answer. C5 deleted FlushNow entirely and folded its self-removal property into FlushAt's declaration.

C1 resolved by DOCUMENTATION only, per my scoping instruction. The implementer investigated safe-by-construction anyway and found it achievable for ~40 lines -- filed as VaCuus-akj.6.34.

All five C-nits corrected with each citation re-opened, plus one the review missed: the .tmptest probe was credited to VaCuus.Core.FileInterface when it belongs to VaCuus.Core.ContentRoots. The '~17 callers' claim is now '14 call sites outside the DirectoryWatcher module', enumerated, with the two genuine counterexamples to 'one-shot flushes' named.

Also worth recording: the implementer found two of its OWN new comments wrong while re-checking them and fixed them in a follow-up commit (5d0a36b) -- IFileHandle::Seek on Windows is not a real SetFilePointerEx, and RmlUi does not close handles it never got.

title: Decodes launched while a view is unsized sit undrained (placeholder stays on screen)
description:
FVaCuusUIThread::RunFrame gates recording on HasView(), and HasView() requires both a non-degenerate ViewSize and a live document (VaCuusRmlDocumentHost.cpp:273). A host that loads a document while its view is still unsized will run LoadTexture (RmlUi resolves images lazily during Show()), launch the decodes, and then record no frame -- so DrainCompletedDecodes() never runs and the finished payloads sit in the TMpscQueue.

Self-healing: the first tick that has a sized view drains them. No leak either -- if the view never gets sized, the sink's destructor destroys the queued payloads. The only visible symptom is that the transparent 1x1 placeholder stays on screen for that window instead of the image.

Filed for airtightness rather than because it bites today: in every current path the view is sized before or with the document load. It becomes reachable if some future caller loads a document before layout.
design: Either drain unconditionally (before the HasView gate) or document that an unsized view defers arrivals. Draining before the gate is probably right -- the drain only touches recorder state and does not need a view.
acceptance_criteria: A document loaded into an unsized view still shows its images once the view is sized, and there is a test or an explicit note covering the ordering.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (b19233f). The bead UNDERSTATED it: its claim 'in every current path the view is sized before or with the document load' is false — UVaCuusWidget::RebuildWidget creates the view at FIntPoint::ZeroValue (VaCuusUMGWidget.cpp:75-76), SynchronizeProperties loads at :121-122, the size lands only on the first SVaCuusWidget::Tick (:253-256), and DrainCommands applies a size only when positive (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:1362-1365), so the shipped UMG route hit this on EVERY auto-loading widget and finished payloads stayed resident for the whole unsized window — indefinitely for a widget never arranged. FIX: IVaCuusDocumentHost::DrainAsyncArrivals(), called by the record loop for every live host BEFORE the HasView() gate. The lobby decorator's forward is enforced at COMPILE TIME by comparing pointer-to-member types of derived and base ([expr.unary.op]/4) — deleting the forward now fails the build with a named static_assert instead of silently reinstating the bug. Restore-the-bug: record-loop call deleted -> exactly one assertion fails ('its finished decode is drained anyway'), FramesRecorded stays 0; restored -> Success. NOTE: the triage's test design was WRONG about absolute img paths (SystemInterface::JoinPath strips the leading slash, SystemInterface.cpp:54-59) and the implementer caught it and worked around it, commented at the call site.

title: Module unload racing an in-flight texture decode (two dangling targets)
description:
Task 11 launches PNG/JPEG decodes with UE::Tasks::Launch from VaCuusRender. The lambda's code lives in libUnrealEditor-VaCuusRender.so. The recorder's destructor sets an atomic abandon flag that the task checks at entry, which closes the common window, but does not eliminate 'task already past the flag check when the module unloads' -- the .so could be unmapped under a running decode.

Not solved in Task 11 deliberately: a proper fix needs a process-wide outstanding-decode counter waited on in ShutdownModule, which is more machinery than bead 6.2 warranted. Note this is the same exposure any UE::Tasks::Launch from a plugin module carries, so if it is worth fixing it is probably worth fixing as a small module-level helper rather than per-call-site.

Hard to hit in practice: module unload happens at editor shutdown or plugin reload, and decodes are sub-millisecond. Filed so it is a known risk rather than a surprise.
design: Process-wide outstanding-decode count, waited on in FVaCuusRenderModule::ShutdownModule. Prefer a reusable module-scoped guard over a bespoke counter, since every UE::Tasks::Launch from this plugin has the same exposure.
acceptance_criteria: A decode in flight at module unload cannot execute code from an unmapped .so; verified by a test or by inspection of the shutdown path.
notes:
EXTENDED 2026-07-30 after the Task 11 spec review: there are TWO things that can dangle in this window, not one.

(a) The task lambda's CODE lives in libUnrealEditor-VaCuusRender.so. If the module unloads mid-decode, the .so is unmapped under a running task.

(b) The cached raw IImageWrapperModule* (new in Task 11 -- the old code re-resolved through LoadModuleChecked on every call). FModuleManager::UnloadModulesAtShutdown can free the ImageWrapper DLL while a decode launched just before teardown is still running, and CreateImageWrapper is a VIRTUAL call through that pointer.

The bAbandoned flag narrows both windows but closes neither, because the recorder's destructor deliberately does not wait (waiting would retract-and-execute the decode on the UI thread -- see TaskPrivate.cpp:246-251 -- which is strictly worse). Zero impact on monolithic builds; requires editor teardown to overtake an in-flight sub-millisecond decode. Arguably the price of caching the module pointer, which was itself the fix for 6.12.

Both are covered by the same fix: a process-wide outstanding-decode count waited on in FVaCuusRenderModule::ShutdownModule.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (b19233f). The two targets had come apart. (a) 'the .so is unmapped under a running decode' is UNREACHABLE in any supported configuration, verified not assumed: UnloadModulesAtShutdown passes bIsShutdown=true (ModuleManager.cpp:1491-1492) and that flag skips InternalFreeLibrary — 'we'll simply abandon it in memory instead' (:1369-1381); the only path that frees a plugin library is FPluginManager::UnmountExplicitlyLoadedPlugin (PluginManager.cpp:3650), refused without bExplicitlyLoaded (:3660), which VaCuus.uplugin does not set. Recorded in FVaCuusTextureDecodeSink with what would make it live again. (b) REAL and now closed by shape: the module OBJECT dies in every unload, shutdown or not ('This will actually destroy the module object', ModuleManager.cpp:1344-1348), so the captured raw pointer dangled even with the code mapped, and CreateImageWrapper is a virtual call through it. LoadTexture now creates the wrapper on the frame-owning thread and hands the instance to the worker; wrapper instances are plain MakeShared (ImageWrapperModule.cpp:79-158) and FImageWrapperModule::ShutdownModule is empty (:529), so teardown cannot reach them. The worker's whole world is a declared struct with a structured-binding FIELD COUNT guard — restore-the-bug: adding the module pointer back fails the build with 'decomposes into 8 elements, but only 7 names were provided'. No wait added: waiting from the destructor retract-and-executes the decode on the UI thread (TaskPrivate.cpp:246-251).

title: Async texture upload for large images (decode is already async)
description:
Task 11 made the PNG/JPEG *decode* async (worker task) but keeps the *upload* in band: the finished RGBA payload travels through FVaCuusCommandBuffer::NewTextures and the replayer uploads it with RHICmdList.UpdateTexture2D on the render thread. For a large atlas (2048x2048 RGBA = 16 MB) that memcpy lands on the render thread's critical path as a one-frame cost at document load.

The out-of-band alternative was deliberately rejected in Task 11 (see the commit body and the plan amendment): worker -> FRHICommandListBase::CreateTextureInitializer -> Finalize on a non-immediate command list -> FRHICommandListImmediate::QueueAsyncCommandListSubmit, installing the FTextureRHIRef straight into FVaCuusReplayRenderer::Textures. Two reasons it lost: (1) it defeats Task 12's idle short-circuit -- a texture arriving while the UI publishes nothing would be installed but never re-replayed, so the placeholder would stay on screen until an unrelated change dirtied the frame; (2) it opens a second resource channel into render-thread-private state, with a weak-pointer lifetime problem across two modules.

If this ever matters, the fix is not to reopen that channel but to keep arrival in band and make the *upload itself* async: hand the payload to a worker command list and have the replayer install the resulting ref, while still publishing a buffer so the re-replay happens. Only worth doing if a measurement shows the render-thread memcpy actually hitching.
design: Keep arrival in band (it is the re-replay signal); make only the RHI upload async.
acceptance_criteria: A measured render-thread cost for a >=2048^2 texture load shows a hitch worth removing, then: upload off the render thread with the in-band arrival preserved, and the idle short-circuit still triggers a re-replay when the real payload lands.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-07-30 in a live headless PIE run, so this is now sized rather than speculative.

Test: temporarily swapped Content/DevUI/img/avatar.png for a synthetic 6000x6000 PNG (36M px, 144 MB decoded, only 150 KB on disk so the read and probe memcpy stay trivial). PerfLog window containing the document load:

  Update    (UI) avg=0.014 p50=0.011 p99=0.053 max=0.095 ms  (937 frames)
  Record    (UI) avg=0.042 p50=0.039 p99=0.105 max=0.438 ms
  Replay    (RT) avg=0.068 p50=0.028 p99=0.066 max=36.567 ms
  Composite (RT) avg=0.003 p50=0.003 p99=0.006 max=0.068 ms

Decoding 36M pixels cost the UI thread NOTHING measurable -- Update max 0.095 ms, indistinguishable from steady state (0.383 ms max over 6456 frames). Task 11 did its job. The hitch moved entirely to the render thread: Replay max 36.567 ms, which is the UpdateTexture2D memcpy of 144 MB, and it never recurs in any later window (subsequent Replay max 0.149 ms).

So the sizing is roughly 1 ms of render thread per 4 MB of texture. A realistic 2048x2048 UI atlas (16 MB) is therefore about 4 ms -- a visible but single-frame cost at document load. Judgement: still not worth the complexity unless a project ships genuinely large UI textures. The number to beat is 4 ms per 16 MB.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (f5eba06), measurement first — and the measurement corrected the bead. The bead priced the upload at '~1 ms per 4 MB' (linear) and set its acceptance gate at 2048x2048. The real curve is NOT linear: ~13 GB/s below 16 MB, ~3 GB/s above. Measured on real Vulkan, render thread, cold/warm: 256^2 0.049/0.041 ms, 512^2 0.074/0.054, 1024^2 0.201/0.169, 2048^2 1.249/0.905, 4096^2 28.385/26.129, 6000^2 36.996/42.432. So a 2048^2 atlas costs 1.25 ms — NOT a hitch worth machinery — and the gate is genuinely met three sizes higher, at 4096^2 = 28 ms (two dropped frames from one ). Also decisive: CreateTexture never exceeds 0.38 ms even at 137 MB; the entire cost is UpdateTexture2D's staging memcpy, which dictated the split — create stays synchronous, only the memcpy moves. TWO OF THE BEAD'S THREE API ASSUMPTIONS WERE FALSE: RHIAsyncCreateTexture2D is UE_LOGF(Fatal, 'not supported') on Vulkan (VulkanTexture.cpp:1571-1576, D3D/Metal only); IRHIUploadContext is an EMPTY class in 5.8 (RHIContext.h:569-570) with RHIGetUploadContext() returning nullptr by default (DynamicRHI.h:823-826) — a placeholder. The one real route is the parallel command list, and the constraint nobody had spotted is that QueueAsyncCommandListSubmit DETACHES and dispatches the immediate list (RHICommandList.cpp:1482-1510), so it cannot be called from inside the RDG pass lambda — it had to go at graph-build time next to EnsureOutputRT, where the engine makes its own such calls (ShadowSetup.cpp:6902, SkeletalMeshUpdater.cpp:437-440). No -onethread guard needed: FScheduler::LaunchInternal runs the task inline when ActiveWorkers is zero (Scheduler.cpp:533, :622-630). END-TO-END, same binary, cvar-flipped, m1_hud with a 6000x6000 PNG, headless PerfLog: Replay (RT) avg 21.651 / p99 41.319 ms BEFORE -> avg 0.722 / p99 1.396 ms AFTER. The load frame went 41.3 ms -> 1.4 ms. The residue was NOT hidden: the async start moved outside the Replay scope, so it was measured directly (0.32 ms for that payload) and stated at the call site so nobody reads the PerfLog delta as bigger than it is. One anomaly reported rather than smoothed: at 2048^2 the async start reads ~2 ms in both runs while larger sizes read 0.29-0.32 ms; it reproduces, so it is not noise — most likely the test's own back-to-back sequencing. The implementer also caught a bug in its OWN first shape before building: installing the texture at graph-build time would have let an older buffer's inline upload overwrite a freshly uploaded image, precisely for the one handle that legitimately appears in two buffers (a late decode records the 1x1 placeholder in one buffer and the real payload in a later one). The ref is now parked and installed by the owning buffer. Restore-the-bug: deleting UpdateTexture2D from the async body fails only 'async payload is byte-exact (first difference at 0 of 4194304)'; restored -> Success.

title: Two VaCuus working trees on disk diverge; live reload only watches one
description: Task 10: /w/Unreal/VaCuus (master) and /w/Unreal/VcHost/Plugins/VaCuus (m2-ui-thread) are separate inodes. All M2 work is in the VcHost clone; inotify watches inodes, so edits in the canonical clone are invisible to live reload. Resolve before divergence accumulates: either merge M2 back and work only in the clone, or make the clone a git worktree of the canonical repo.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-30, all four candidates tested against this engine build rather than assumed. THE DUPLICATION IS NOT FORCED -- AdditionalPluginDirectories is the real fix, verified end to end.

| Symlink into Plugins/ | STILL BREAKS. Reproduced verbatim: 'ASSERT: rename: cross-process rename-while-open ... UbaDetoursSharedPosix.inl:1158', only the plugin's own modules. -NoUBA builds fine. The old note is current. |
| git worktree | NON-FIX. A linked worktree is a separate checkout with its own files -- fixes git divergence, not inotify. |
| Hard-linked content | NON-FIX AND SELF-DEFEATING. Editors save write-to-temp-then-rename (the very shape ShouldTrackChange is built around), which replaces the directory entry and breaks the link. |
| AdditionalPluginDirectories | WORKS, WITH UBA ON. Plugin moved outside the project, full 202-action rebuild with no UBA error, plugin mounted, IPlugin::GetContentDir() AND the watcher both resolved to the external tree, 37/37 green. |

TRAP THAT COMES WITH IT, confirmed in both sources: the entry must name a PARENT of the plugin directory. UBT's EnumeratePlugins only looks inside SUBFOLDERS of the search root (EnumeratePlugins.cs:81-107, its own doc comment says so) while the runtime FPluginManager::FindPluginsInDirectory seeds its queue with the root itself (PluginManager.cpp:1177-1203). Point straight at the plugin and you get the worst of both: the editor mounts it, UBT never builds it.

NOT APPLIED, controller's decision 2026-07-30, deliberately deferred rather than forgotten: it needs VcHost.uproject (outside this repo), a relocation of the canonical checkout, AND a dedicated parent directory -- naming /w/Unreal would pull the entire engine plugin set into the scan. Moving the canonical checkout invalidates paths in the memories, the README, the GitHub clone instructions and every doc, which is real churn mid-project on a working build loop. The silent half of the hazard is now closed (see below), so what remains is convenience rather than risk. Revisit when the tree is quiet -- e.g. at the start of M6, or the next time the build loop is being touched anyway.

MEANWHILE THE FAILURE IS LOUD, which was the actual hazard. The watcher's startup line now states the consequence, not just the roots, and FindSecondWorkingTreeDevUI() names the other tree when one is PROVABLE -- the plugin is a git checkout whose remote url/pushurl is a local absolute path to a directory that has its own Content/DevUI. That is a fact off disk, not a heuristic: upstream remotes are not absolute paths, a bare mirror has no Content/DevUI, and a symlinked plugin resolves to the canonical config whose remote is upstream, so the one arrangement with a single inode set stays quiet. It cannot see two clones that both point upstream, or a cp -r; stated in the comment, and the unconditional log line covers those. Covered by VaCuus.LiveReload.SecondTree, which already earned its keep by catching that FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull KEEPS a trailing slash, so 'url = <this dir>/' compared unequal and the check reported the plugin as its own second tree.

NOTE: there is a THIRD tree in play -- /w/Unreal/VaCuusDemo, the old host project, still has a symlinked plugin and -NoUBA. Fold it into whatever consolidation happens.
close_reason: Closed in M6: the two-tree workflow is codified in CLAUDE.md (canonical git+beads tree vs the VcHost build clone, with the UBA symlink trap and the AdditionalPluginDirectories recipe pointer), and the second-working-tree detector ships in the live-reload path. Disposition table: docs/research/m6-api-notes/bead-dispositions.md (0e1abd7).

Fixed in the Task 10 review cycle (06ad496/d1403f9). Proof.LiveReload.PIE is now gated on an explicit -vacuusproof switch: without it the test logs how to run it and returns in ~17 ms without touching PIE; with it, it additionally asserts both expected screenshots exist, so the harness can now actually FAIL instead of passing while asserting nothing. title: Dedup: mouse-capture release exists in two teardown sites
description: Task 8: capture release now lives in both VaCuusM1HUD::TearDown and UVaCuusWidget::ReleaseSlateResources. SVaCuusWidget::DetachView() is precisely 'this widget is being retired' and is the natural single home — a 3-line dedup for whoever touches SVaCuusWidget next. Not done in Task 8 because the instruction forbade improvising on Task 6/7 code.

title: Test hygiene: five near-identical FProbeHost copies across two modules
description: Task 7: probe hosts duplicated in Snapshot/Routing/SpatialNav (VaCuus) and SlateRouting/MultiView (VaCuusRender). A shared probe cannot live in VaCuus/Private; needs a small public test-only header. Do before another test adds a sixth.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-03 (6d9df17). The bead was wrong about its own size for the third time: not 'five near-identical FProbeHost across two modules' (bead) and not '~26' (triage) — 25 IVaCuusDocumentHost implementations across FOUR modules; the name FProbeHost alone occurred 8 times in two modules. All 25 unified, 0 left standalone, net -1589 lines (25 files, +312/-2271 in existing files, +370 in two new headers).

MECHANISM RATHER THAN WORKAROUND: the fixtures live in Source/VaCuus/Internal/, which UBT auto-discovers (UEBuildModuleCPP.cs:451-455) and hands only to modules in the same Rules.Context.Scope (UEBuildModule.cs:736-740) — this plugin's four modules and nobody else. Zero Build.cs change, and Public/ keeps the meaning the dgl decision record gave it. Two headers, not one: VaCuusTestNullDocumentHost.h deliberately has NO RmlUi include because VaCuusEditor does not link VaCuusRml.

THE HAZARD WAS REAL AND WAS AVOIDED BY SHAPE: Rml::FocusFlag is a required constructor argument with no default, because Show()'s own default is FocusFlag::Auto (focuses the first tabbable element, ElementDocument.h:81) while FocusFlag::Document focuses the document itself (ElementDocument.cpp:347-359) — folding those together silently would have weakened the navigation tests without breaking the build. RecordAndPublishFrame and SetVisible stay PURE virtual: the first IS the measurement bracket in the cost tests (an extra virtual would land inside it), the second is a genuine no-op/Show-Hide split that exactly one test drives.

RESTORE-THE-BUG, two independent breaks in the base, one suite run: 6 fail / 191 pass, and the failures are precisely the dependents — ignoring the per-host FocusFlag fails VaCuus.Input.SpatialNav/.TabReach/.NavEntry/.NavBackNested/.AnalogNavGate; skipping OnDocumentClosing fails VaCuus.Js.Documents.Unload ('after the close, document is a dead wrapper' — expected dead, got alive). The 191 that kept passing prove the breaks were targeted, not blanket. Both restored; suite green. Citation gate CLEAN afterwards (1048 in-repo citations).

title: Build.cs: downgrade VaCuusRml to private dep in VaCuusRender + stale comment
description: After recorder header moved to Private (afce959), no public header of VaCuusRender includes RmlUi; PublicDependencyModuleNames entry for VaCuusRml + its comment are stale. Downgrade to Private, verify build.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 13 (23f3181 exact-EOF Tell, a117ba7 private VaCuusRml dep, df2164b task-10 follow-ups, c82a2ce task-12 follow-ups, 5d0a36b self-correction). 31/31 tests green; both the editor and the MONOLITHIC game target rebuilt Succeeded, and the monolithic target genuinely recompiled Module.VaCuusRender.cpp so the dependency change was exercised rather than assumed.

6.1: verified the clamp at UnixPlatformFile.cpp:177 (FileOffset = NewPosition >= FileSize ? FileSize - 1 : NewPosition) before coding. Rml::FileHandle now carries handle + logical position + cached size; Seek moves only the position and Read re-syncs the handle. RmlUi's contract was checked in the vendored header rather than assumed POSIX. Restore-the-bug: reverting Tell() to the handle gave 4 failures (Tell 15 instead of 16; empty-file EOF reporting 18446744073709551615), and reverting the whole pre-fix pair gave 6, adding 'a read returns 0, not the last byte again'. NEW FACT WORTH KEEPING: the exact-EOF clamp is UNIX-ONLY -- both Windows read handles accept InPos == FileSize and report it -- so this fix makes Unix agree with Windows rather than inventing a third contract.

6.4: premise confirmed before acting -- zero RmlUi includes anywhere under VaCuusRender/Public/, and in fact no Build.cs in the plugin or the host project even names VaCuusRender.

6.32 (task-12 spec review): D1's stated fix WAS WRONG AND THE FINDING IS WORSE THAN STATED. A uint32 between Type and Geometry occupies offsets 4-7 and shifts nothing: sizeof stays 112 and every other member keeps its offset, so offsetof is structurally incapable of seeing it. Verified by building it both ways. What catches it is a MEMBER COUNT check -- FVaCuusCommand is an aggregate, so brace-initialising it with one initialiser too many is ill-formed inside a requires-expression. The four offset clauses were kept anyway for a different reason: they catch REORDERING (swapping Texture with Translation leaves both sizeof and the member count intact). Restore-the-bug: the padding-slot field now fails compilation with 'FVaCuusCommand gained or lost a field'; with the pre-change assert it compiled clean. D2 also got an unrequested restore-the-bug -- the exact copy-paste slip named in review now fails, and passed the whole file before.

6.23: gitignored in the canonical repo.

title: FileInterface: exact-EOF Tell() off-by-one on Linux (FFileHandleUnix clamp)

Linux-only, benign. Options: clamp-and-track position ourselves or document. Address in M2 alongside UI-thread file loading.

6.1: verified the clamp at UnixPlatformFile.cpp:177 (FileOffset = NewPosition >= FileSize ? FileSize - 1 : NewPosition) before coding. Rml::FileHandle now carries handle + logical position + cached size; Seek moves only the position and Read re-syncs the handle. RmlUi's contract was checked in the vendored header rather than assumed POSIX. The four offset clauses were kept anyway for a different reason: they catch REORDERING (swapping Texture with Translation leaves both sizeof and the member count intact). title: FVaCuusWorldSink still uploads textures inline — the async path stops at the screen sink
description:
Follow-up to akj.6.25 (fixed 2026-08-03, f5eba06), named by its implementer rather than discovered later.

The async upload landed on the SCREEN path (FVaCuusSlateElement): the memcpy moved to a parallel command list, taking a 6000x6000 load frame from 41.3 ms to 1.4 ms. FVaCuusWorldSink was deliberately left inline.

WHY IT WAS LEFT: the sink HAS the immediate command list at its publish site, but IVaCuusFrameSink::SetPendingBuffer_RenderThread narrows the parameter to FRHICommandList&, and QueueAsyncCommandListSubmit needs the immediate one (it detaches and dispatches it — RHICommandList.cpp:1482-1510). Widening that interface means changing every implementor and every test host, including VaCuusUnsizedDrainTest.cpp. That ripple did not belong in the same change as the mechanism.

WHY IT IS LOW PRIORITY: a world panel is a DrawSize-pixel surface — a 64 MB texture is even less likely there than on screen, and akj.6.25's measured curve says the hitch only becomes real at 4096x4096 (28 ms). Below 2048x2048 the whole thing costs ~1.25 ms and needs no machinery.

WHEN TO DO IT: if a world panel is ever shown carrying large imagery, or when IVaCuusFrameSink is being changed anyway for another reason — then widen the parameter once and route both sinks through the same path. The observable already exists: the akj.6.25 test shape (VaCuus.Render.Upload.Cost / .AsyncPayload) transfers directly.
close_reason: Closed

title: VaCuus.Model.BlueprintRecompile flake: address-inequality assert defeated by LIFO allocator reuse
description: Observed once during M3b Tasks 1-2 (passed on rerun, identical binaries): the recompiled struct's new FIntProperty was allocated at the freed old property's address, so the address-inequality assertion at VaCuusModelRecompileTest.cpp:145 fails nondeterministically. The test's premise (new property != old address) is not guaranteed by any allocator contract. Fix shape: assert on identity that survives reuse (e.g. a serial/name/flags change), not on pointer inequality.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-03 (3ac0fdb). The address-inequality assert is replaced by UStruct::FieldPathSerialNumber — the engine's own process-wide monotonic generation counter (Class.cpp:636-640), re-stamped by DestroyChildPropertiesAndResetPropertyLinks (Class.cpp:2136), which is exactly what CleanAndSanitizeStruct calls (UserDefinedStructureCompilerUtils.cpp:225). It exists so FFieldPath can detect a stale cached FProperty* (FieldPath.cpp:427-430) — this test's question in the engine's own terms — and it never names an address, so no allocator reuse can defeat it. Also added a CONTROL so the observable is measured both ways: a ChangeVariableDefaultValue edit is the one path where CleanAndSanitizeStruct skips the teardown (:221-232) and CreateVariables finds the existing property (:271-281) — a real compile round trip that must NOT move the serial; asserted, and it holds. Restore-the-bug: rename replaced by a second default-value change -> 'the recompile destroyed the struct's whole FProperty chain: The two values are equal'; restored -> Success. NOTE for the record: the bead's own file path and line numbers were both stale (the file is in VaCuusEditor, not VaCuus — the runtime module cannot name FStructureEditorUtils).

title: Per-element array dirty granularity (open only if M3b §9 measurement fails)
description: Design sketch referenced by the M3b spec §9. If the 200-row measurement shows the whole-array copy pipeline exceeding budget: keep one RmlUi dirty bit per top-level array (that is the entire expressible vocabulary — DataViewFor re-evaluates per root name regardless), and reduce COPY cost only: per-element dirty ranges riding the existing channel protocol (Pending/Unacked become per-(field, element-range)), the slot carries ranges + values, SyncCopy applies ranges instead of the whole container. Prerequisite already in M3b: the capacity-preserving SyncCopy — without it the copy cost story is dominated by destroy/reconstruct churn, not by range width. RmlUi work is NOT reducible from VaCuus (spec §2(b)).
notes: PARKED WITH NUMBERS (M3b §9 measured 2026-07-31, commit 2895ae5): the changed-row cost at 200×4 is 0.423 ms, of which the three SyncCopys contribute ~0.014 ms (store+publish 0.010, apply 0.004) — the rest is RmlUi re-evaluation that no VaCuus granularity can reduce (spec §2(b)). Warm republish already allocates exactly zero. This refinement could shrink only the 0.014 ms; open only if a real HUD shows the copy slice mattering.
close_reason: Closed 2026-08-03 by triage, precondition never met. This bead's own opening condition was 'open only if the M3b section 9 measurement fails'. It did not fail: the two-array scoreboard topology is proven at reference scale — a one-panel change re-evaluates exactly 192 bindings (192 gets / 1 size / 192 childs), both panels exactly 384/2/384 (the exact sum), a scalar plate change 2/0/0 with zero array evaluations (VaCuus.RefHud.DirtyScope, M6 Task 4). The soak half agrees with the 0.53 us/binding law: measured +0.084/+0.120 ms on the bump frame against a ~0.10 ms prediction (Exp-REF-SCALE, passport). Split-along-your-update-boundaries is documented as the shipped idiom in docs/buyer/perf-guide.md. Per-element granularity would buy nothing measurable and would complicate the dirty-scope model that currently has exact, falsifiable counters. Reopen only if a real workload shows an array whose per-row cost cannot be split by topology.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: M6 disposition: carried (parked). The M3b granularity decision stands — two-array scoreboard topology proved at reference scale (192-eval one-panel delta, Exp-REF-SCALE).

title: Inline mode makes IsInUIThread() true on the game thread at all times
description: In inline mode (!SupportsMultithreading()) Init() stores the game thread's id into GVaCuusUIThreadId, so IsInUIThread() is true on the game thread ALWAYS, not only inside RunFrameInline. Every check(IsInUIThread()) therefore passes for a game-thread RmlUi call made outside the inline scope. Inherent to inline mode and no such call exists today, but the assertions no longer mean what their comments say in that configuration. Related: FVaCuusEngine::ForceShutdownAll runs Rml::Shutdown() on the game thread, deliberately skipping the owner-thread check -- a documented error path, unreachable via ordered teardown, but a real Rml:: call on a non-UI thread that no assert would catch.
close_reason: Closed 2026-08-03 (7d76c57): the bead's premise is half wrong, nothing breaks, and nothing runs there. The title claims IsInUIThread() is true on the game thread 'at all times' in inline mode — FALSE, verified in source. FVaCuusInlineUIThreadScope (VaCuusUIThread.cpp:107-117) RESTORES the previous id and brackets exactly three windows: StartInline()'s Init() (:441), each RunFrameInline() (:469), and the destructor's Exit() (:352). Between those windows IsInUIThread() is false on the game thread and every guard still bites. INSIDE them the game thread genuinely IS RmlUi's owner, so the assertion is TRUE, not vacuous — the header already said as much at :55-58. Init()'s durable publication at :912-913 is undone by the scope on the way out, and RmlUi ownership is latched separately by FVaCuusEngine::OwnerThreadId, so nothing is lost. The inline venue is commandlet/-nothreading only; no shipping path and no automation test runs in it. Disposition recorded in the code so the premise is not re-filed.

comments.author: Vladimir Alyamkin
comments.text: M6 disposition: carried. Commandlet/-nothreading venue only; no M6 surface touched it.

title: Grayscale UEJPEG images are unsupported (decode to a transparent placeholder)
description:
PENDING CONFIRMATION by the Task 11 re-review; filed now so it is not lost.

The Task 11 fix-cycle implementer reports that FUEJpegImageWrapper::Uncompress IGNORES the requested InFormat entirely and allocates Width*Height*NumColors (UEJpegImageWrapper.cpp:275-276), with NumColors == 1 for a grayscale UEJPEG (:138-141). It is reachable from LoadTexture because DetectImageFormat recognises the OOJPEG magic (ImageWrapperModule.cpp:171-173).

So a request for (ERGBFormat::RGBA, 8) can come back with W*H bytes instead of W*H*4. Task 11's byte-count revalidation therefore rejects it, and the image degrades to a permanent transparent 1x1 placeholder plus a Warning -- which is the correct failure, and strictly better than the pre-Task-11 behaviour, where the mismatched payload would have reached the replayer and tripped its payload-mismatch ensure.

Two consequences worth recording:
(a) The revalidation added in the Task 11 fix cycle is LOAD-BEARING, not defensive. Under the pre-fix ordering the premultiply pass ran before the length check and would have scribbled over a grayscale buffer treating it as RGBA before rejecting it.
(b) If UEJPEG ever needs to be supported for UI art, the fix is a grayscale->RGBA expansion in the worker, not a wider revalidation.

Low priority: UEJPEG is an engine-internal format, unlikely in UI art, and the failure is graceful and logged.
acceptance_criteria: Either grayscale UEJPEG expands to RGBA in the decode worker, or the limitation is documented at the decode site so the warning is self-explaining.
close_reason:
Fixed in d9a9ba4 (Task 11 second fix pass).

6.31: LoadTexture now whitelists {PNG, JPEG, UEJPEG} immediately after DetectImageFormat; anything else gets a Warning naming the file and the format and returns handle 0. The crash was REPRODUCED before the fix, with a real backtrace from a decode worker: 'Assertion failed: InFormat == ERGBFormat::BGRA [BmpImageWrapper.cpp:69]' via FBmpImageWrapper::UncompressBMPData <- Uncompress <- FImageWrapperBase::GetRaw <- IImageWrapper::GetRaw <- LoadTexture's decode lambda <- FScheduler::WorkerLoop. Process aborted at exit 139 with 25 of 31 tests completed. After the whitelist: 31/31, exit 0.

Tests cover BMP *and* TGA, both built with the engine's own encoders. TGA was included deliberately: it is the silent R/B-swap case rather than the crash case, so a test covering only BMP would not have pinned the whitelist's shape.

Labelled a workaround in the comment, with the real fix (GetRawImage(FImage&) plus channel-order conversion in the plugin) cited and scoped out.

With that gone, the SizeMismatch failure message is honest by construction (nothing can reach it claiming the decoder disagreed with itself).

title: Task 11 small fixes: texture-release wording, test-only API guard, same-buffer ordering note
description:
Three small items from the Task 11 spec review, to fold into that task's fix cycle:

1. VaCuusRecordingRenderInterface.cpp:451-452 says 'RmlUi's own ReleaseTexture retires the 1x1 when the source goes away'. Not right: file textures are released only by explicit Rml::ReleaseTexture(source) / ReleaseTextures(), or at RenderManager teardown (RenderManager.cpp:19,41,257-260 -> TextureDatabase.cpp:168-181). NOT on document close or element destruction. Correct wording is 'retired at render-manager teardown'. Nothing leaks either way (4 bytes RGBA + one 1x1 RHI texture per broken source), but the reasoning is load-bearing for the 'keep the placeholder on decode failure' decision, so it has to be accurate.

2. WaitForTextureDecodes() is a documented test-only method carrying VACUUSRENDER_API on a production class. A #if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS guard around the declaration costs nothing and turns a comment-only footgun into a compile-time one.

3. The 'placeholder in frame N, payload in N+1' framing is the common case, NOT an invariant. LoadTexture is reachable out-of-frame: AdoptDocument -> Document->Show() runs during DrainCommands, before the record loop, so RmlUi's lazy FileTextureDatabase::EnsureLoaded (TextureDatabase.cpp:118-129) can fire with bInFrame == false, and GetPending() lazily creates the buffer the NEXT BeginFrame also drains into. A fast small PNG can therefore overwrite its own placeholder in the SAME buffer. Benign -- the buffer then carries only the real payload and the placeholder never reaches the RHI -- but the test's 'Second->Generation > First->Generation' assertion is only deterministic because the test never loads out-of-frame, and that should be stated in the test.
acceptance_criteria: Wording corrected, test-only API compile-guarded, and the same-buffer case documented at the drain site and in the test.

description: Shows up in every git status in the plugin clone. Decide: gitignore it or commit it. Trivial, but it has been noise in every task report since M2 started.
close_reason:
Landed in Task 13 (23f3181 exact-EOF Tell, a117ba7 private VaCuusRml dep, df2164b task-10 follow-ups, c82a2ce task-12 follow-ups, 5d0a36b self-correction). 31/31 tests green; both the editor and the MONOLITHIC game target rebuilt Succeeded, and the monolithic target genuinely recompiled Module.VaCuusRender.cpp so the dependency change was exercised rather than assumed.

6.1: verified the clamp at UnixPlatformFile.cpp:177 (FileOffset = NewPosition >= FileSize ? FileSize - 1 : NewPosition) before coding. Rml::FileHandle now carries handle + logical position + cached size; Seek moves only the position and Read re-syncs the handle. RmlUi's contract was checked in the vendored header rather than assumed POSIX. Restore-the-bug: reverting Tell() to the handle gave 4 failures (Tell 15 instead of 16; empty-file EOF reporting 18446744073709551615), and reverting the whole pre-fix pair gave 6, adding 'a read returns 0, not the last byte again'. NEW FACT WORTH KEEPING: the exact-EOF clamp is UNIX-ONLY -- both Windows read handles accept InPos == FileSize and report it -- so this fix makes Unix agree with Windows rather than inventing a third contract.

6.4: premise confirmed before acting -- zero RmlUi includes anywhere under VaCuusRender/Public/, and in fact no Build.cs in the plugin or the host project even names VaCuusRender.

6.32 (task-12 spec review): D1's stated fix WAS WRONG AND THE FINDING IS WORSE THAN STATED. A uint32 between Type and Geometry occupies offsets 4-7 and shifts nothing: sizeof stays 112 and every other member keeps its offset, so offsetof is structurally incapable of seeing it. Verified by building it both ways. What catches it is a MEMBER COUNT check -- FVaCuusCommand is an aggregate, so brace-initialising it with one initialiser too many is ill-formed inside a requires-expression. The four offset clauses were kept anyway for a different reason: they catch REORDERING (swapping Texture with Translation leaves both sizeof and the member count intact). Restore-the-bug: the padding-slot field now fails compilation with 'FVaCuusCommand gained or lost a field'; with the pre-change assert it compiled clean. D2 also got an unrequested restore-the-bug -- the exact copy-paste slip named in review now fails, and passed the whole file before.

6.23: gitignored in the canonical repo.

title: vacuus.M1HUD: no inline fallback when VFS file exists but fails to load
description: Dev-only robustness gap from Task 9 review: corrupt m1_hud.rml silently no-ops the toggle instead of degrading to inline probe doc.
close_reason: Landed in m2-ui-thread a714a7b (Task 4): process-wide UI thread owned by FVaCuusModule + per-view contexts via UVaCuusSubsystem/UVaCuusView (6.10 structural, proven by new VaCuus.Threading.MultiView test); module now stops the thread it owns before engine teardown, ForceShutdownAll demoted to last-resort (6.11); vacuus.M1HUD retries with the inline document when a VFS file load fails, reported through FVaCuusViewStatus (6.7). Spec §4/§13 amended: RmlUi's global state makes per-subsystem threads impossible.

title: Spike (variant B validation): Linux opaque-FD GL<->Vulkan shared texture into UE 5.8.1
description: 1-day spike, all prerequisites verified on this machine (RTX 3090 Ti, NVIDIA 610.43.03): allocate exportable VkImage (OPAQUE_FD) on UE VkDevice via IVulkanDynamicRHI, wrap with RHICreateTexture2DFromResource, import into a surfaceless GL context via GL_EXT_memory_object_fd + glTexStorageMem2DEXT, render gradient, sync via exported semaphore, sample in a Slate widget. Success: correct pixels, no validation errors, no game-thread wait. Protocol details in docs/research/2026-07-29-webui-middleware.md and agent report (cef-3).
notes: DEFERRED: user chose variant A (RmlUi). Keep as backlog for a possible future browser-grade tier on Servo; all prerequisites verified on this machine.
close_reason: Closed 2026-08-03 by triage, need never materialized. Variant B (Linux opaque-FD GL<->Vulkan shared texture) was the fallback if the recorder/replay architecture could not reach the required performance. It did: variant A shipped through M1-M6 with the passport filled — game thread 0.008-0.012 ms/frame, composite 0.002-0.003 ms, the idle gate withholding publication at 1 in 6,910 frames on a static HUD, and a 1,732-node reference HUD running at 1.05 ms on the dedicated UI thread. A tree-wide search found no opaque-FD / GL_EXT_memory_object / glTexStorageMem / external-memory work anywhere in M5 or M6, and nothing in the M5 world-space or M6 bundle work revived the need. If a future tier (e.g. a Servo-class engine, bead akj.3's sibling context) ever needs a foreign GL surface, that will be its own spike against that engine's constraints, not this one.
